title: Fangak commissioner appeals for urgent aid amid flood crisis - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Johnson Kuol Gai, Commissioner of Fangak County, Jonglei State
acts.speech: Appealed for urgent humanitarian assistance for flood-affected communities, citing severe shortages of food, shelter, and medical services: “The community of Fangak is really suffering. The area is submerged. They have no food, no shelter, and not even a clinic. I’m appealing to all agencies operating in South Sudan to come and witness this situation.” ; Added that due to poor network coverage, many displaced residents were unaware of the visit and could not gather at the administrative centre, and emphasized the community’s commitment to peace but stressed that basic humanitarian needs must be addressed.

acts.speaker: General Kong Thuo, Assistant Chief of Defence Forces for Operations
acts.speech: Urged residents and organized forces to support peace efforts during a visit to assess the security situation in the area.

title: AES : Mahama et Ouattara plaident pour le retour dans la Cédéao

acts.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Said at a press briefing that they had “discussed at length the security situation” in the sub-region, which “remains very worrying, as well as the socio-political situation in the Sahel”; “We noted the need to provide assistance to these brother countries to enable them to meet humanitarian and security needs. We trust you, Mr President, that in your discussions with these brother countries you will be able to convince them to remain in ECOWAS, because the future of the peoples of West Africa is at stake.” ; “I would also like to make an appeal to the AES countries to say that we are better as 15 than as three, so I hope that President Mahama's appeal can be heard by these three brother countries, two of which are neighbours of Côte d'Ivoire, so that we can continue together within ECOWAS.”

acts.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Welcomed the “excellent discussion” in which they addressed “matters of common interest, in particular in the areas of defence, security and the cocoa economy”, as well as “questions relating to mines and energy, and the major ECOWAS projects such as the Abidjan-Lagos corridor and the common currency, the Eco”; added: “Regarding bilateral cooperation, we reaffirmed our common will to support the Côte d'Ivoire-Ghana Cocoa Initiative and to strengthen cooperation between Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire in mining and energy and in the fight against illegal gold panning”; “We have committed to supporting and working towards the implementation of the Côte d'Ivoire-Ghana strategic partnership agreement, a privileged instrument of cooperation, signed in 2017 in Accra.”

acts.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: On the reduction of American funding, admitted “it is true that it is a very large part of international financing (64%)”, recalling that Côte d'Ivoire benefits from MCC financing as well as funding for the fight against malaria and AIDS; “we have taken measures, at our level, to continue financing all these projects while waiting for the United States to resume things after the audit that is under way. We are (nevertheless) confident”; “The United States has always been a friendly country to Côte d'Ivoire and I consider that the outcome of the review by the American government (will be favourable) and that disbursements will resume for Côte d'Ivoire.”

acts.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
acts.speech: Maintained that “there is still the possibility of bringing our brother countries back home. It is better to stay in a group of 15 than to stay in a group of three”; insisted that “these are countries that matter in the sub-region” and that it is important for them to “remain in the ECOWAS space, insofar as their populations are on the border lines for economic interests. And as I say, it is always better to be in a group of 15 than in a group of three.”

acts.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
acts.speech: On US aid: “the United States has the right to review its cooperation strategy, to see how it might direct its funding. I think this is also an opportunity for us to see how we can rely on ourselves”; said he had heard there would be “a reduction (in funding) from USAID”, considering that “this is for us an opportunity to also review our economic strategies.”

title: Future imperfect: Migration goes South

acts.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) and African National Congress (ANC) members of parliament
acts.speech: In South Africa's parliament, nearly came to physical blows over why (and how) their government had allowed this to happen - both the collapse of civil order in Zimbabwe as well as the sudden flood of desperate people into South Africa.

acts.speaker: Democratic Alliance speakers
acts.speech: Insisted the government had to take responsibility for the urgent needs of the growing throng near the border regardless of who had caused it.

acts.speaker: Freedom Front Plus
acts.speech: Hinted darkly that - within the week - mobs would be looting farms or much worse in the northern part of the country in their growing desperation.

acts.speaker: Foreign diplomats in Pretoria (joint demarche representing some two dozen foreign missions)
acts.speech: Weighed in with a joint demarche to the South African government urging urgent South African government efforts to restore order and to take charge of the circumstances of the refugees by providing basic food, shelter and sanitary conditions - lest things degenerate any further.

acts.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees
acts.speech: Announced that the number of people in the 10 camps now set up across the area had reached an incredible half a million people in less than a month.

acts.speaker: South African Communist Party youth wing (communique)
acts.speech: Issued a communique that denounced "western nations for fermenting [sic] the violence in Zimbabwe and spreading baseless rumours about the need to flee a comradely progressive nation", thereby "contributing to the spread of disease, the scarcity of food and the demands on hard-pressed medical personnel to preserve the benefits of the popular socialist revolution".

acts.speaker: Alliance for Economic Progress in Southern Africa (Aepsa)
acts.speech: Decried the reluctance of the South African government to do anything to limit the collapse of security and order in Zimbabwe, thereby contributing to the cessation of most major mining and industrial operations north of the Limpopo River.

acts.speaker: Investigative journalist at The Daily Maverick
acts.speech: Discovered that major funders of Aepsa included Gupta family business interests, Lonmin, the Chinese Infrastructure Investment Bank, Anglo American, several prominent black economic empowerment mining groups, and a number of Russian mining houses.

acts.speaker: General "Giant", Zimbabwean general
acts.speech: Optimistically declared the fighting was now over; said he would welcome back all of his compatriots who had fled the recent fighting and urged international aid agencies to move their bases of operations into Zimbabwe itself in order to attract returnees, rather than across the northern rim of South Africa.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump
acts.speech: Offered unsolicited advice in an internationally broadcast interview on the BBC that South Africa should build a wall all along the border and then simply round up all the new migrants and forcibly repatriate them back to their home nation.

acts.speaker: Several senior South African government officials
acts.speech: Were reported in the Sunday papers to have agreed that such a plan - building a border wall and forcibly repatriating the migrants - was both feasible and probably necessary.

acts.speaker: The South African Presidency
acts.speech: Quickly overruled these comments, explaining the press had cynically and typically misinterpreted some chance comments partially overheard from officials attending a wedding celebration the previous day, once they had heard The Donald's remarks.

acts.speaker: Analysts
acts.speech: Explained this result represented a serious protest vote against an ANC that had long believed that province was secure for it in electoral terms, come what may.

acts.speaker: South African Cabinet wordsmith/spinmeister (speaking in camera)
acts.speech: Said that no matter what choice they made, the outcome would be "less than optimal".

acts.speaker: Nigeria and several other African nations
acts.speech: Urgently called for African Union and UN Security Council meetings to discuss the now-widening crisis.

title: Vinodia Janete

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
acts.speech: Demands accountability for all individuals involved in financial crimes in the Public Administration. Daniel Chapo wants greater strategic coordination and information sharing between the Administrative Court and the bodies of justice administration and investigation, in order to eliminate barriers in the fight against fraud and corruption.

acts.speaker: Emilia Moiane, Director of the Information Office (Gabinete de Informacao)
acts.speech: Said AIM, the Mozambican news agency, must position itself in the mission of promoting the country's achievements, the consolidation of national unity, national interests, and the promotion of democracy and social justice. These were the words of the director of the information office, speaking at the swearing-in ceremony on Wednesday in Maputo of Orlando Gambeta, the new director general of AIM.

acts.speaker: Banana producers in Gorongosa
acts.speech: Call for the harmonisation of the selling price of bananas. They want bananas to be sold by the kilogram and not by the bunch.

title: An 2 Talon 2/Promotion de l’entreprenariat et de l’emploi: Une politique incitative pour l’essor des Pme-Pmi

acts.speaker: Edouard Sehlin, Director General of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (ADPME)
acts.speech: Said the ADPME is tasked with informing, advising, supervising and directing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises towards existing support mechanisms, supporting their categorisation, helping them seize opportunities and supporting high-potential enterprises ; “It may involve capacity building, advice, diagnosis or networking, and facilitating access to financing” ; explained that in terms of financing the Agency plays a catalytic role in order to encourage financial actors to intervene in market segments, or categories of enterprises, in which they are not sufficiently present.

acts.speaker: Edouard Sehlin, Director General of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (ADPME)
acts.speech: “All the projects planned in the SME sector have been finalised and are starting up with all the partners. We will do more, because this makes it possible to have an impact and to have a critical mass of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises capable of contributing to the structural transformation of the economy and of ensuring Benin’s prosperity in the future…”

acts.speaker: Modeste Tihounte Kerekou, Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion of Benin
acts.speech: Said the PAG 2016-2021 amounted to around 9,038 billion CFA francs, with the intention of generating 500,000 direct and indirect jobs ; “We were already at more than 600,000 direct and indirect jobs more than a year before the end of the term. The PAG 2021-2026 is 12,011 billion CFA francs and 1,300,000 jobs that the government intends to create in good understanding with the private sector. That is why a good part of the reforms completed in the first term have continued, and their effects are increasingly visible” ; he mentions in particular the facilitation of business creation as well as the legislative framework put in place through the investment code, the law on the promotion of SMEs, and the law on hiring procedures.

acts.speaker: Modeste Tihounte Kerekou, Minister of SMEs and Employment Promotion of Benin
acts.speech: “We have an organisation of the craft world that has been completely revamped so that it complies not only with the law, but also with the provisions of the community code of the WAEMU area”; he adds that, in place of the former structure, a chamber of trades has been established by law, endowed with a consular assembly made up of 80 members elected by their peers, coming from 164 trades in accordance with the WAEMU classification of craft trades, namely 40 trade bodies and eight branches of activity.

acts.speaker: Urbain Amegbedji, Director General of the National Employment Agency (ANPE) of Benin
acts.speech: “The government has placed at our disposal new tools that make it possible to promote employment with more effectiveness and efficiency, notably the Special Programme for Integration into Employment (PSIE), which has been effective since 2020 and which today reaches around 3,000 young people who work in enterprises and whose salaries and all charges are covered by the State” ; assures that through the PSIE there is support both for the enterprise and for the professional integration of young people, with much more effectiveness than in the past ; explains that another youth inclusion project makes it possible, in a short time, on average six months, to train and put to work a young person who can immediately obtain a contract and start working.

acts.speaker: Robert N’Dah Sinkeni, Director of Crafts
acts.speech: “The Chamber of Crafts and Trades has as its essential mission to represent the sector before the public authorities and any other body, to defend the interests of artisans, and to work for the promotion of the sector.”

title: U.S. Embassy, Defense Department donate PPE and mobile clinics to Mozambican military

acts.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Mozambique, the U.S. Department of Defense and PEPFAR (joint statement)
acts.speech: "hope this donation will not only benefit Mozambican military personnel but also their families, communities, and the people of Mozambique. The United States Government will continue working alongside the Government of the Republic of Mozambique as we fight to protect the people of Mozambique from the threats of COVID-19 and HIV/AIDS." Announced that the Embassy and the Department of Defense through USAFRICOM presented a donation of Personal Protective Equipment to Mozambique's Military Health, and that DHAPP and PEPFAR donated four mobile clinics to aid in the expansion of the Mozambican Armed Forces' male circumcision programme, a donation valued at US$172,461.

title: Illovo Sugar profit drops

acts.speaker: Kondwani Msimuko, Illovo Sugar acting Managing Director
acts.speech: Addressing shareholders on Friday, cited the drop in profitability to economic woes Malawi was facing, singling out foreign currency scarcity, high taxes, vandalism and other macroeconomic uncertainties among the challenges: "We had lower profits last year, and our intention for this meeting was actually to get to our investors and update them on the company's performance, factors behind it and what we are doing to improve [the situation] moving forward."

acts.speaker: Kondwani Msimuko, Illovo Sugar acting Managing Director
acts.speech: Assured investors that the company was making strides to improve revenue generation through increased production and export of products.

acts.speaker: Maureen Kachingwe, Illovo Sugar Director of Legal and Corporate Affairs
acts.speech: In her presentation, said the company spent about K2.13 billion towards supporting community development activities through their response to natural disasters and fulfilment of corporate social responsibility roles.

acts.speaker: Frank Harawa, shareholder
acts.speech: Said they were concerned about the company's low profit; was quick to commend management for its efforts amid a challenging operating environment.

title: Putin may address Ukraine ceasefire proposal on Thursday – Kremlin

acts.speaker: The Kremlin
acts.speech: Has said that Russian President Vladimir Putin may address a possible ceasefire with Ukraine on Thursday.

acts.speaker: TASS (Russian state news agency)
acts.speech: Reported that the Kremlin said Putin may address a possible ceasefire with Ukraine on Thursday.

acts.speaker: Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesperson
acts.speech: Said Mr Putin is set to take questions from reporters with his Belarusian counterpart, Alexander Lukashenko, while the latter is on an official visit to Russia. “Everything will depend on what reporters will ask,’’ Mr Peskov told TASS when asked whether Mr Putin would comment on issues beyond Minsk-Moscow relations ; On Wednesday, Mr Peskov said that Moscow would not publicly comment on the proposal discussed by the US and Ukraine until it would know all the details.

acts.speaker: Ukrainian delegation (at the Jeddah talks)
acts.speech: Expressed willingness to agree to an immediate 30-day comprehensive ceasefire if Russia would do the same.

acts.speaker: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and National Security Advisor Mike Waltz
acts.speech: Have promised to provide Moscow with all the information about the Jeddah negotiations.

acts.speaker: US President Donald Trump
acts.speech: Said on Wednesday that a US delegation was on its way to Moscow ; Had also said that he would want to speak with Mr Putin by phone, soon.

acts.speaker: The White House
acts.speech: Announced that special envoy Steve Witkoff would visit Russia in a few days.

title: Lancement du projet Kadjogbé Fou Itounou: CRS Bénin s’engage pour la paix et la prévention des conflits

acts.speaker: Kathérine Overcamp, CRS Resident Representative in Benin
acts.speech: Indicates that the project, focused on peacebuilding and conflict prevention, is implemented by CRS thanks to the generosity of the American people through USAID, and will be deployed over a 24-month period covering 4 communes — Parakou and Tchaourou in Borgou, and Bantè and Savè in Collines — targeting traditional, political and religious leaders, young people, women and marginalised groups, aiming to directly impact 6,795 participants and 33,975 indirectly. ; Explains that the start-up activities begun in March 2023 made it possible, by the end of October 2023, to strengthen the capacities of the project implementation teams on the different implementation approaches, notably the social cohesion approach known as 3B/4D, peaceful masculinity, and conflict prevention and management: "We estimate at 191 the number of actors and authorities already trained who have committed to peacebuilding activities. 639 women, young people and other vulnerable persons have also joined 29 savings and credit community groups out of the 96 groups planned."

acts.speaker: Simon Asoba, USAID political adviser, speaking on behalf of the US Ambassador to Benin
acts.speech: Wishing great success to the project, observes that in the face of recent challenges and the rise of insecurity in northern Benin, these actions are to be welcomed and encouraged: "I had the opportunity to see the progress made in the localities of Karo, Nikki Kpérou, Sanson and in the Yarakinnin neighbourhood in Parakou, and I was impressed by the commitment of the notables, men and women, determined to work together for a community of peace but also to organise themselves to mobilise internal savings on their own for their own prosperity." ; Specifies that the project, led by CRS and its partners Caritas Parakou and Caritas Dassa, is an example of USAID's commitment in northern and central Benin, with total funding of 620,000,000 CFA francs.

acts.speaker: Djibril Mama Cissé, prefect of the department of Borgou
acts.speech: Welcomes this initiative led by CRS, which is in perfect alignment with the government's action programme under its pillar 1, "Strengthening democracy, the rule of law and good governance", and fits with the Sustainable Development Goals: "I would like to assure you of the commitment of my colleague the prefect of Collines, of the mayors, of the beneficiary communes and myself, to support the implementation of the project so that it truly impacts the beneficiaries."

acts.speaker: Saliou Odoubou, prefect of the department of Collines
acts.speech: Welcomes the relevance of the project, embracing the assertion of Jean Jaurès: "Today, the affirmation of peace is the greatest of struggles", before expressing the wish that through this project, the coexistence for which the two departments, and Benin in general, are recognised may be strengthened.

acts.speaker: Dénis Oba Chabi, mayor of the commune of Savè
acts.speech: Says this project comes at just the right time, especially after the electoral violence of recent years, to explain to everyone the necessity and the obligation of living together, in peace, in total cohesion. "It is in everyone's interest," he added.

title: Libye: 300 migrants interceptés en mer, renvoyés en 7 jours (OIM)

acts.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
acts.speech: Reported that between 25 and 31 May 2025, some 300 migrants were intercepted in the central Mediterranean and then returned to the Libyan coast, and that the operations were carried out off several Libyan coastal cities – Zuwara, Sabratha, Azzawiya, Tripoli and Al-Khums.

acts.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
acts.speech: Since the start of the year, the IOM counts 9,585 migrants returned to Libya, including 8,147 men, 960 women and 333 children, of whom 145 were unaccompanied minors or people requiring special assistance; as of 31 May 2025 at least 233 migrants had lost their lives at sea, while 225 others are reported missing. In 2024, 21,762 migrants had been intercepted, with a toll of 665 dead and 1,034 missing; the previous year there were 962 deaths and 1,536 disappearances at sea.

acts.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
acts.speech: Reiterates that Libya cannot be considered a safe port for the disembarkation of migrants. The organisation states that it is not involved in the interception operations, but provides humanitarian assistance on arrival, while calling for sustainable alternatives that respect fundamental rights.

title: Horn Observer

acts.speaker: World Bank, World Health Organization (WHO) and UN Children's Fund (UNICEF)
acts.speech: Signed a US$ 82 million agreement to improve access to critical health services for more than 8 million vulnerable people across Sudan and strengthen the health system.

acts.speaker: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
acts.speech: "Strongly condemns ongoing violent attacks on patients and staff at Bashair Teaching hospital, located in a Rapid Support Forces-controlled area of Khartoum, Sudan. Despite extensive engagements with all stakeholders, these attacks have continued."

acts.speaker: Aid workers caught up in the five-month siege of El Fasher
acts.speech: Said the lack of services and escalating violence was making life harder by the day, calling for immediate action to protect those at risk.

acts.speaker: Radhouane Nouicer, designated Expert on Sudan of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
acts.speech: Called for the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and their respective allied armed movements and militia to take immediate measures to ensure protection.

acts.speaker: Nutrition screening by Sudanese health authorities and Medecins Sans Frontieres in Zamzam camp, North Darfur
acts.speech: The results indicate that malnutrition is only getting worse. "Without supplies, we have been forced to reduce our services."

acts.speaker: IGAD Regional Focus of the 2024 Global Report on Food Crises
acts.speech: Highlights a worsening food insecurity crisis in the IGAD region, which includes Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

acts.speaker: IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC)
acts.speech: Has released its seasonal forecast for October to December 2024, indicating drier-than-normal conditions in the eastern Horn of Africa, while western regions are likely to experience above-normal rainfall.

acts.speaker: Amnesty International (latest briefing)
acts.speech: Highlights how a continuous influx of weapons is exacerbating the conflict in Sudan, leading to severe civilian suffering.

title: UN: 9.3 million people in South Sudan forecast to face crises in 2025 - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Anita Kiki Gbeho, UN humanitarian coordinator for South Sudan
acts.speech: Warned that an estimated 9.3 million people are expected to face humanitarian crisis in 2025, a figure slightly higher than the 9 million people projected for this year; lauded humanitarian organizations for relentless efforts to support the needy population; said 4.2 million people have been reached with humanitarian intervention in 2024, through food distribution, shelter and camp management among others ; "The 2024 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan was about 64% funded. As a result, we were able to reach 4.2 million women, men, boys and girls with different forms of critical assistance, including food, nutrition, health, water and sanitation, camp coordination, camp management, education, shelter, non-food items and protection services." ; "According to the 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan, 9.3 million people, 70% of the population, will require some form of humanitarian assistance in 2025. Of these, the humanitarian community will target 5.4 million with an appeal for 1.7 billion dollars."

acts.speaker: Albino Akol Atak, Minister for Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management
acts.speech: Attributed the successful humanitarian response this year to high collaboration and coordination and called for continuous strengthening of collaboration to achieve the targeted 5.4 million people in the 2025 humanitarian needs and response: "We managed to respond to the needs of people in this year, 2024, simply because there was high collaboration and coordination. So the same thing next year, if we want to respond to this target number 5.4 million people. We need to strengthen and to increase that collaboration." ; He assured partners and humanitarian organizations of his government's continued cooperation: "The government expressed its sincere appreciation for solidarity and support provided by humanitarian donors and partners over the past years and looks forward to continuing cooperation to respond to the most active needs of vulnerable people in South Sudan."

title: Gestion de la filière cotonnière au Bénin : entre Spécialisation, Politisation et Régionalisme

acts.speaker: Benin public television channel (Chaîne des grands événements)
acts.speech: According to the same public channel, some people, including the Head of State himself, had reportedly become producers of "white gold" (cotton).

acts.speaker: Economic operators and political leaders
acts.speech: Denounced the demonisation, notably of the sale of adulterated petrol, as nothing but an admission of a lack of vision, in a country that shares nearly 500 kilometres of border with Nigeria.

acts.speaker: Sabai Katé, former Minister of Agriculture of Benin
acts.speech: Meanwhile threw dust in the eyes of the population by sounding the trumpet of the rehabilitation of the oil palm sector.

acts.speaker: Patrice Talon, cotton magnate (interview on Radio France Internationale, November 2012)
acts.speech: Cited as the source showing that Talon had proved himself in the cotton sector long before the Boni Yayi regime came to power with cotton money.

acts.speaker: Burkinabè press
acts.speech: At one point judged that in Benin, cotton is grown on television.

title: Ngafuan stresses reprogramming of projects to boost development - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
acts.speech: Has emphasized an urgent need to reprogram and redirect certain projects that are not yielding the desired returns, particularly in light of the recent reduction in USAID aid: "We are facing a significant shock due to the USAID aid cut, and immediate measures are being taken to mitigate its impact." ; reiterated that discussions will soon be held with partners to reallocate resources to critical sectors impacted by the aid reduction ; acknowledges the situation, noting that hard conversations are underway across the government to address the ongoing challenges: "Many Liberians have lost their jobs, interventions to vital sectors have been reduced, and it is essential for us to implement critical measures." ; reveals that government, alongside its partners, will convene a roundtable in April to address emerging challenges and explore solutions that ensure the uninterrupted implementation of the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development. He reassures Liberians that the government remains committed to delivering on its agenda.

acts.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
acts.speech: Describes the launch of the GREAT Project as a "significant opportunity" for Liberia's continued progress. He explains that the Project would focus on expanding digital public services, increasing tax revenues, strengthening accountability and transparency, and enhancing capacity building and implementation support.

acts.speaker: Oyewole Afuye, Acting World Bank Country Manager
acts.speech: Congratulates the Government of Liberia for the successful launch of the Project which is expected to "leverage digital solutions and deepen institutional reforms to modernize the public administration and improve government efficiency, ultimately benefitting all Liberians." He notes that the six years Project will support the government's ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development in achieving great transparency, accountability, and efficiency. Specifically, he outlines that it will address three key challenges - a weak system for delivering administrative services due to low state presence and infrastructure constraints across the country, a strained fiscal outlook due to low domestic resource mobilization and limited accountability for managing public resources with uneven service delivery results. The World Bank Acting Country Manager calls on all ministries, agencies and commissions and development partners to support the delivery of the project and help to sustain policy dialogue on the reforms.

title: French Corporations in Africa: Green promises, black footprints - Daily News

acts.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
acts.speech: In 2023, President Macron unveiled yet another “new African strategy”, announcing a shift away from old models in favour of “equal partnership” and “sustainable development.”

acts.speaker: Experts (unnamed, on uranium mining in Niger)
acts.speech: estimate that radiation levels near these mines exceed permissible limits by 100 times, while uranium concentrations in local drinking water reach 15 mg/L—500 times the safe threshold.

acts.speaker: Studies (cited on cancer in Niger mining region)
acts.speech: indicate a rise in cancer cases in the region over the past two decades.

acts.speaker: Environmental organizations (on the EACOP pipeline)
acts.speech: warn that the project threatens to destroy 2,000 km of natural landscapes, including national parks and reserves, while displacing over 100,000 local residents.

acts.speaker: The Oakland Institute
acts.speech: has accused Bolloré Group of illegal land seizures, environmental degradation, and human rights violations in several African countries.

acts.speaker: 2024 Global Terrorism Index (report)
acts.speech: According to the 2024 Global Terrorism Index, over 50% of all terrorism-related deaths were recorded in the Sahel countries of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso.

acts.speaker: Aicha Dahou, journalist for Algerian TV1
acts.speech: “France has been plundering Africa for decades, extracting its riches—uranium, gold, and oil—and turning the continent into a nuclear testing ground, now drowning it in millions of tonnes of radioactive waste.”

acts.speaker: Asmahan Soltan, Algerian journalist
acts.speech: “France covers about 70percent of its electricity needs with uranium, the key fuel for its 50+ nuclear plants. It lights up its cities at the cost of millions of Nigeriens suffering from the consequences of uranium mining.”

title: Trump administration mulls new travel ban that could hit 43 nations: Report - The Alkamba Times

acts.speaker: The New York Times (report)
acts.speech: Reported that United States President Donald Trump's administration is mulling a new travel ban that is expected to affect citizens from dozens of countries to varying degrees; quoting anonymous officials, the report published on Friday said the US government's draft list featured 43 countries, divided into three categories of travel restrictions, with a first group of 10 countries set for full visa suspension, a second group of five countries facing partial suspensions, and a third group of 26 countries considered for partial suspension of US visa issuance.

acts.speaker: US government draft memo
acts.speech: Said a total of 26 countries including Belarus, Pakistan and Turkmenistan would be considered for a partial suspension of US visa issuance if their governments "do not make efforts to address deficiencies within 60 days."

acts.speaker: US official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Told the Reuters news agency there could be changes to the list and it was yet to be approved by the administration, including US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of January 20)
acts.speech: Issued an executive order on January 20 requiring intensified security vetting of any foreigners seeking admission to the US to detect national security threats; the order directed several cabinet members to submit by March 21 a list of countries from which travel should be partly or fully suspended because their "vetting and screening information is so deficient."

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Previewed his plan in an October 2023 speech, pledging to restrict people from the Gaza Strip, Libya, Somalia, Syria, Yemen and "anywhere else that threatens our security."

title: South Sudan Cholera Patients Died Walking to Clinic After Us Cut Aid, Charity Says

acts.speaker: Save the Children (UK-based charity)
acts.speech: Said on Wednesday that eight people in South Sudan, including five children, died on a three-hour walk to seek medical treatment for cholera after U.S. aid cuts forced local health services to close; the organisation said in a statement that it supported 27 health facilities in eastern South Sudan's Jonglei State until earlier this year when the U.S. cuts forced seven to shut completely and 20 to close partially.

acts.speaker: Christopher Nyamandi, Save the Children's country director in South Sudan
acts.speech: "There should be global moral outrage that the decisions made by powerful people in other countries have led to child deaths in just a matter of weeks."

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
acts.speech: Said the cuts imposed after entering office on January 20 were to ensure grants were aligned with his "America First" agenda.

acts.speaker: Experts
acts.speech: Have warned that the cuts - including the cancellation of more than 90% of USAID's contracts - could cost millions of lives in the coming years due to malnutrition, AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and other diseases.

acts.speaker: U.S. State Department (spokesperson)
acts.speech: Said it did not have information about the deaths reported by Save the Children; a spokesperson said many U.S. government programmes providing lifesaving aid in South Sudan remained active but that support for medical services had also been used to enrich the country's leaders: "While emergency lifesaving programmes continue, we will not, in good conscience, ask the American taxpayer to provide assistance that effectively subsidises the irresponsible and corrupt behaviour of South Sudan's political leaders."

acts.speaker: South Sudan's government
acts.speech: Has in the past acknowledged a significant amount of public corruption but denied specific accusations of graft, including against President Salva Kiir's family.

title: Accelerating progress to safer sanitation practices

acts.speaker: Governments at the Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD)
acts.speech: Agreed that sanitation was a fundamental element of human capital development.

title: Ali-Sabieh : Cérémonie de clôture du programme de promotion de la lecture extrascolaire

acts.speaker: Pedagogical adviser representing the regional inspector, Ali-Sabieh
acts.speech: Welcomed the participants to the regional inspectorate and recalled that reading is very important insofar as it ensures the acquisition of knowledge and basic skills; the more a pupil reads, the more his or her general culture and communication performance improve. Said the main objectives are first to encourage parents to support their children in mastering reading, and to promote the pleasure of reading in pupils by organising activities around reading at home or at school outside learning hours. Ended his address by stating that it is essential, indeed important, to promote reading in order to give the pupil that feeling, that desire to feed on books and to find in them everything he needs: knowledge and pleasure, comfort, amusement, reflection - in short, creativity.

acts.speaker: Representative of FHI 360
acts.speech: Said that this project focuses essentially on the learning of reading in basic school with all its components, and that parents' support for learning - and above all for their children's practice of out-of-school reading - remains the main theme of this workshop. He hammered home to the parents present that without mastery of the act of reading and of the comprehension of texts or passages read there is no learning at school, and that the time pupils spend at school is far less than the time spent at home, so it is very important that parents collaborate effectively with teachers.

acts.speaker: Representatives of the prefecture and the regional council
acts.speech: Stressed that without mastery of this flagship discipline of basic school, which proves to be the key to all teaching of whatever nature, pupils' difficulties increase constantly; and urged parents to watch closely over their children's learning of reading during the first two years of their schooling.

title: Zimpost launches new mobile money platform - The Financial Gazette

acts.speaker: Isaac Muchokomori, acting postmaster general, Zimpost
acts.speech: Speaking during the launch at Greendale Post Office in Harare, said the new mobile money platform will... [text truncated]

title: ‘The Situation Is Fluid’

acts.speaker: Thembinkosi Dube, local economist
acts.speech: Says the 90-day pause on the 10 per cent import tariff is not a sigh of relief as anything can still happen, referring to the similar situation of the US Agency for International Development (USAID) where the American president paused the aid for 90 days, however, later on implemented the complete halt of the aid in several countries: "I do not think anything can stop him from finally implementing the tariffs, so it is a wait and see situation and it is almost certain that he might stick to his decision." ; stated that Trump had created a resilient mode for countries, as they were now creating other ways on how they can trade.

acts.speaker: Thembinkosi Dube, local economist
acts.speech: Highlighted the performance of the lilangeni amid ongoing global trade tensions, noting a drastic decline against the USD: "As of yesterday, the exchange rate was over E19." ; warned that if the global trade wars continued, the situation could worsen for the lilangeni: "We have observed that the lilangeni is weakening; yesterday it closed at E19.5 to the USD and E25 to the pound sterling, which is unprecedented." ; explained that the currency's value was heavily influenced by demand, and with the tariffs affecting South African commodities, demand has declined, further impacting the lilangeni's value: "If tensions between the two countries persist, we might find ourselves in a situation where the lilangeni weakens further, potentially beyond E20. If the situation continues, I believe that by next week we could be above E20."

acts.speaker: Thembinkosi Dube, local economist
acts.speech: Cautioned that if brent crude prices could rise again next week, the ministry of natural resources might announce an increase in fuel prices, which would contribute to inflation.

acts.speaker: Thembinkosi Dube, local economist
acts.speech: Stated that these trade wars could not continue indefinitely: "At some point, it will hit a peak and bring about a lasting solution. What is happening is that President Trump is pushing his own agenda while also solidifying the need for BRICS, where countries could potentially move away from the dollar. Once that happens, it could be irreversible."

acts.speaker: The White House
acts.speech: Deemed goods from approximately 60 trade partners, including the European Union and China, as coming from the 'worst offenders', which faced significantly higher rates.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Framed these increased tariffs as retaliation for perceived unfair trade policies.

acts.speaker: Analysts
acts.speech: Predicting higher prices for American consumers and a slowdown in US economic growth.

title: Erreur du président Macron sur le sujet de l’attaque d’Israël sur l’Iran

acts.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
acts.speech: Said in his press conference on the situation in the Near and Middle East on 13 June 2025, concerning Israel’s massive attack on Iran: “If there is one thing that unites Israel with all its neighbours in the region, it is the Iranian threat” ; “The situation today, let us be honest and lucid, is a high-risk situation” ; “Iran has ballistic capabilities that can reach European soil.”

acts.speaker: Élysée website (official record of the president’s statements)
acts.speech: The quotation does not appear in the summary of President Macron’s statements published below the video on the Élysée website, where it is written: “Only the spoken word is authoritative.”

acts.speaker: A. Gotheron, press service of Médecins Sans Frontières
acts.speech: Said on 4 June 2025: “The fact that people risk dying of thirst is a very real risk.”

acts.speaker: Organisers of the weekend demonstrations
acts.speech: According to organisers, several demonstrations reached at least 100,000 demonstrators calling for a ceasefire and for humanitarian aid to enter the Gaza Strip (e.g. Brussels 110,000; Paris 150,000).

acts.speaker: CNN
acts.speech: Writes that in Greece there were multiple demonstrations: in Athens, “in all the major cities of the country, but also on the islands.”

acts.speaker: Organisers of the Hague demonstration (Amnesty International and others)
acts.speech: According to the organisers, 150,000 demonstrators in The Hague on 15 June marched towards the International Court of Justice to say, among other things, no to the “genocide” in the Gaza Strip.

title: Apprendre en jouant : Ou comment développer les capacités cognitives et sociologiques de l’enfant par des activités ludiques et récréatives

acts.speaker: Experts and pre-school practitioners (unanimous)
acts.speech: “Play helps the child to get along well with others, to share, to wait his turn and to follow rules. Playing also allows him to communicate, to experiment and to find solutions to problems.”

acts.speaker: Practitioners and pedagogues specialising in teaching and learning
acts.speech: Affirm far and wide that when a child has fun, he feels good and joyful, which facilitates learning ; “Playing therefore allows him to develop a positive attitude towards school. That is why nursery-school teaching leaves a good place for play, because play allows the child to develop his knowledge by exploring. As he is having fun, it gives him a taste for learning and for making an effort.”

acts.speaker: Head of the Play to Learn project
acts.speech: Outlined in broad strokes the objectives and the activities included in this four-year project: strengthening the national strategy for the development of pre-school education to 100% for children aged 5 by 2030, improving access to equitable, safe and inclusive pre-school education services, strengthening the quality of those services and fostering an environment that strengthens the system of services capable of developing early childhood.

acts.speaker: Andrea Tomasziewics, Chargée d'Affaires of the US Embassy in Djibouti
acts.speech: Indicated that the objective of the project is to support the efforts of the Government of Djibouti to improve equitable and quality access to education for children aged three to six ; “We are proud of the strong partnership that USAID has built with the Government of Djibouti since its beginnings, and which has benefited all Djiboutians.”

acts.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
acts.speech: Indicated that the Play to Learn project comes at a moment when MENFOP is consolidating its gains and strengthening its actions, all the more so as its approach covers the whole early-childhood pathway, from nursery to pre-school, and gives MENFOP and the Ministry of Women and the Family the opportunity to think about this educational offer together and coherently.

acts.speaker: Mouna Osman Aden, Minister of Women and the Family of Djibouti
acts.speech: For her part emphasised the value of the Play to Learn project, which will provide facilitation tools for the holistic development of early childhood ; thanked USAID for this project, which comes at just the right time to revitalise all the community childcare structures and solve the problem of the motivation of the staff of those structures.

acts.speaker: Ayane Osman Abrar, Technical Adviser and Executive Secretary of the Higher Committee for Education
acts.speech: Shared her experience of a timely visit she made to the United States of America to learn about pre-school education systems.

title: Les écueils de l'action de l'Agence française de développement en Afrique (Par Omar Diallo)

acts.speaker: Guillaume Bigot, director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
acts.speech: Sharply criticised the so-called humanitarian organisation the French Development Agency (AFD) and its activities, in particular those relating to aid to African countries; according to him French aid for the development of African countries appears to be a total absurdity and, moreover, not all of the operations carried out are accessible to the public. He specified that these conclusions come from an investigation by the European Union Court of Auditors ; criticised the AFD's contribution to Africa for the inefficient use of funds: for example, the purchase of 250 camels for Mauritania, despite the excessive number of camels in the country, and the purchase of electric blenders for schools in Ethiopia, where there is no electricity.

acts.speaker: Guillaume Bigot, director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
acts.speech: Highlighted the AFD's involvement in financing concentration camps in Africa where torture was practised.

acts.speaker: Guillaume Bigot, director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
acts.speech: Also noted the lack of transparency of Western, and in particular French, development aid to Africa, which is not accessible and not made public.

acts.speaker: European Union Court of Auditors (investigation/report)
acts.speech: Scrutinised official development assistance; cited as the source of the conclusions about the inefficiency and opacity of French development aid.

acts.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
acts.speech: Declared on 13 February that USAID was spending 697 million dollars a year on cash transfers to finance terrorist organisations around the world, notably Boko Haram, which has committed numerous terrorist acts in Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad.

title: Tahoua : Le bilan des inondations s'alourdit, mais l'aide humanitaire se mobilise - Journal du Niger

acts.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of Tahoua region
acts.speech: At an extraordinary meeting of the regional technical flood-management committee, drew up an alarming assessment of the situation: the floods affected more than 31,523 households, some 214,580 people, and caused the collapse of more than 23,523 houses; the human toll is also heavy with 104 deaths and 81 injured; the floods led to the loss of 10,028 head of livestock and the destruction of 154 hectares of cultivable land; the education sector suffered significant damage, with nearly 291 classrooms damaged and 274 other classrooms sheltering disaster-affected families, disrupting the schooling of thousands of children.

acts.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of Tahoua region
acts.speech: Praised the promptness and effectiveness of the relief interventions, stressing the importance of national and international solidarity in this ordeal, and congratulated the members of the regional technical committee for their hard work ; praised the responsiveness of humanitarian actors and called for the continuation of efforts to assist the disaster-affected populations, likewise underlining the importance of solidarity in facing this crisis and highlighting the need to prevent and prepare for natural disasters.

title: Bubanza : Les chenilles dévastent les champs de maïs

acts.speaker: An unnamed maize farmer (man in his forties), Gahongore hill, Bubanza
acts.speech: Testified: "These caterpillars are ravaging our maize fields. They attack the stalks and the leaves." ; "Were it not for these caterpillars, maize growing is productive and profitable." ; said he had invested more than 2 million BIF in maize growing, half of it borrowed from a local microfinance institution which he had hoped to repay after the harvest, and that he cannot see by what magic wand he will repay his loan; he estimates his lost earnings at five million BIF this season.

acts.speaker: An unnamed maize farmer (man in his forties), Gahongore hill, Bubanza
acts.speech: Said he is worried about his family's future: "Maize farming is my only livelihood," and wondered how his family will keep meeting its needs; he also testified that the majority of the population lives from maize and rice farming.

acts.speaker: Jacques Nkengurutse, maize farmer on Gahongore hill
acts.speech: Agreed: "These caterpillars threaten the survival of many inhabitants of this locality," adding that most of them live from maize farming, which is less costly than rice growing, which requires enormous financial means.

acts.speaker: Jacques Nkengurutse, maize farmer on Gahongore hill
acts.speech: Said he is worried about the absence of effective pesticides against the caterpillars, which resist many of the pesticides recommended by agricultural authorities; he said he has used them repeatedly with no effect, that the only effective method is to search for the caterpillars in the leaves of each maize plant, and that even if adult caterpillars are killed their eggs remain in the leaves and become caterpillars within a week. He asked those in charge of the agricultural sector to find other, more powerful pesticides, and said he no longer expects much from the harvest after investing 1,500,000 BIF in maize growing.

acts.speaker: J.K., maize farmer on Gahongore hill
acts.speech: Deplored the inaction of the authorities in charge of Agriculture, who are not getting involved in the search for pesticides that kill the caterpillars: "This is the third year in a row that these caterpillars have ravaged our maize fields." ; "It is incomprehensible that caterpillars destroy crops for three years without the authorities being able to find a solution. Even the pesticides available in pharmacies are not effective." He stated that he sprayed his one-hectare maize field with five bottles of pesticide per week with no result, and put his lost earnings at 2,400,000 BIF for the season.

acts.speaker: Administrator of Bubanza commune
acts.speech: Stated that he is aware of the problem, that the armyworms began to appear in 2016 but were no longer the threat they were two years ago, and said he is concerned about another disease also attacking maize which has broken out in the Buvyuko zone of Bubanza commune. He was reassuring: "The administration is doing everything to fight this disease," saying he had already informed the provincial directorate of Agriculture and hopes ministry officials will take all necessary precautions against the new disease.

title: Will Elon Musk and the government of Mali punish USAID officials?

acts.speaker: Government of Mali
acts.speech: "Welcomes" the cancellation of USAID funding for Social Cohesion and similar programs in the Sahel region, initiated by the Department of Government Effectiveness (DOGE), and even calls for individuals to be punished.

acts.speaker: Malian Foreign Ministry (communique)
acts.speech: "In addition, the Malian Foreign Ministry calls on the American authorities to initiate legal proceedings against individuals who misappropriated these funds to finance international terrorism, the victims of which are Mali and other states of the Confederation of Sahel States."

acts.speaker: Malian authorities
acts.speech: Believe that the funds are supporting terrorism; the country's military government had suspended cooperation with USAID for several years, suspecting it of subversive work under the guise of "humanitarian activities."

acts.speaker: Elon Musk (post on Twitter)
acts.speech: Made a repost of the corresponding communique of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali on Twitter, apparently sharing the opinion of the authorities of sovereign Mali.

acts.speaker: Republicans
acts.speech: According to Republicans, the Sahel zone does not matter to the interests of the United States; the failures of the Biden administration in Niger caused restrained satisfaction among Republicans and gave an additional reason to criticize political opponents on the domestic circuit.

acts.speaker: Elon Musk and his supporters
acts.speech: According to Musk and his supporters, the situation in Niger and the Sahel as a whole is an absolute setback for the Biden administration, but not for the United States, and spending 110 million dollars on the creation of a modern air base in Agadez, financing military training programs for local military personnel and logistical support for the army of Niger is simply irrational.

title: Niger/BTP : Baisse de 35 % sur le prix de la tonne de ciment gris CEM II 32.5 | Le Sahel

acts.speaker: Ordinance of 14 October 2024 signed by Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP)
acts.speech: Determines the derogatory tax regime applicable to the importation, production and marketing of CEM II 32.5 grey cement, granting numerous exemptions to companies duly established in Niger and engaged in the importation, production and marketing of grey cement.

acts.speaker: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger (arrete/decree)
acts.speech: Set, by decree, ceiling prices for a tonne of CEM II 32.5 grey cement applicable in the country's eight regions: 55,000 FCFA in Niamey; 56,000 F in Dosso; 51,000 F in Tahoua; 57,000 F in Maradi; 58,000 F in Zinder; and 59,000 F in Diffa, Agadez and Tillaberi.

title: ECF challenges still remain—IMF - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Nelnam Koumtingue, International Monetary Fund (IMF) resident representative
acts.speech: Says Malawi has made progress in some areas in line with the four-year $175 million (about K306 billion) Extended Credit Facility (ECF), but challenges still remain. ; “While progress has been made in some areas, challenges remain. The IMF last conducted a programme review mission in May 2024 and discussions between the IMF and the Malawian authorities have continued. However, the review has not yet been completed and under our policies, ECF arrangements automatically terminate before their scheduled end if no programme review has been completed over an 18-month period.”

acts.speaker: Nelnam Koumtingue, International Monetary Fund (IMF) resident representative
acts.speech: In a written response on Friday, he said the ECF programme approved on November 14 2023, was meant to support improved macroeconomic stability, promote export growth, enhance foreign exchange availability and build foreign exchange reserves.

acts.speaker: A handbook of IMF facilities for low-income countries (document)
acts.speech: Indicates that ECF arrangements will automatically terminate before their scheduled terms if no programme review has been completed over an 18-month period.

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
acts.speech: According to the IMF, one of the most urgent goals of the current ECF arrangement is to support the authorities’ commitment to restoring macroeconomic stability and creating an environment of low or moderate inflation and a stable exchange rate.

acts.speaker: Capital Hill (Malawi Government)
acts.speech: Said the series of reforms Malawi has implemented were tough, but necessary to convince development partners that the Malawi Government is committed to reforms to revitalise the ailing economy, including raising the policy rate and devaluing the kwacha.

acts.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
acts.speech: In December last year, in response to a question from Mulanje South West lawmaker George Chaponda, who is also Leader of Opposition in Parliament, dismissed suggestions that the ECF is derailed, stating that it is “broadly on track”.

acts.speaker: Betchani Tchereni, Secretary to the Treasury
acts.speech: Revealed that the Malawi Government had initiated discussions with the IMF to review some targets under the ECF programme, including disparities between programme assumptions and conditions on the ground, necessitating a reassessment of previously agreed targets.

acts.speaker: Betchani Tchereni, Secretary to the Treasury
acts.speech: He was yet to respond to our questions on the current status of the ECF programme. (non-response)

acts.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Centre for Green Economy in Developing Countries global lead
acts.speech: In an interview on Sunday said the delays in debt restructuring and rising expenditure constrain efforts to rebuild foreign exchange reserves, putting the ECF programme in jeopardy. ; “Given the current geopolitical challenges and the decline in donor aid, Malawi needs the ECF.”

acts.speaker: Lingalireni Mihowa, Oxfam in Malawi country director
acts.speech: Is on record as having said while the government has managed expenditure, revenue targets fall short, a development that points to some budget assumptions not materialising.

title: Twelve fold increase in COVID-19 cases, severe weather and locusts creating massive need in Ethiopia, warns IRC

acts.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC) (statement)
acts.speech: “Recent heavy rainfall has led to flooding, resulting in destruction of crops, loss of livestock and displacement. Swarms of multiplying desert locusts have also been destroying pastures and crops, leading to further food insecurity. Some areas are recording admissions for severe acute malnutrition at 50% higher than for the same period last year. A massive twelve fold increase in Covid-19 cases between June and September is further compounding needs as families have been unable to obtain income or access food due to movement restrictions.”

acts.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC) (statement)
acts.speech: Said that IRC is working to safeguard the lives of affected and at-risk communities from the COVID-19 pandemic by raising community awareness on COVID-19 risk factors, providing personal protective equipment, and building and installing water points to help people practice preventative methods ; “The IRC is assisting desert locust and flood-affected households with multi-purpose cash transfer and non-food items to fill food security gaps and provide relief.”

acts.speaker: Frank McManus, IRC Ethiopia Country Director
acts.speech: “The multiple issues of flooding, locusts, intercommunal violence and COVID-19 are highly concerning given the already massive humanitarian needs in the country. The slowdown of the economy and lockdown restrictions mean that people have not been able to access income and there is an upward pressure on food prices.” ; “Over 19 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in Ethiopia. At four times the number of people displaced in 2019, as a result of the flooding, more than 300,000 people have been displaced in 2020 and have had their homes and livelihoods lost or damaged. A total of over 1 million people have been adversely affected by the floods overall... The IRC is providing essential support through distributions of non-food items, including emergency shelter, household goods, hygiene kits, and cash assistance to over 36,500 affected people.” ; “Despite the IRC’s work, the unmet humanitarian needs are still great. With more funding for our work, we will be able to reach even more people with the critical support they so desperately need after losing their homes and livelihoods.”

title: Dr Kennedy criticises Mahama - He failed to acknowledge Western assistance in health care

acts.speaker: Dr Arthur Kobina Kennedy, member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP)
acts.speech: Has criticised President John Dramani Mahama for selectively praising African leaders while ignoring Western contributions to Africa's healthcare sector; noted that President Mahama failed to mention the West spending more than US$157 billion to help Africa and the bilateral assistance from the United States of America and the European Union in the healthcare sector; expressed the concern in a statement issued on September 25, 2025 in response to President Mahama's recent call for Africa to assume leadership in healthcare; added that the summit would have been a good place and time to thank America for the generosity of past governments, starting with Bush and lasting through Biden.

acts.speaker: Dr Arthur Kobina Kennedy, member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP)
acts.speech: On healthcare funding: lamented the lack of commitment from African leaders to healthcare funding, noting that most countries, including Ghana, have not met the Abuja declaration's target of spending 15 per cent of their budgets on health. “A quarter century after the Abuja declaration, most of them, including Ghana, have not even reached eight per cent” ; “Indeed, truth be told, President Mahama's summit was necessitated by what the WHO Director, Tedros Adhanom Gebreyesus, reported as ‘health aid projected to decline by up to 40 per cent this year compared to two years ago’” — a decrease, Dr Kennedy said, due mainly to cuts in global health spending by the Trump administration.

acts.speaker: Dr Arthur Kobina Kennedy, member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP)
acts.speech: On galamsey: urged President Mahama to back his words with action, particularly in addressing the galamsey crisis, which he said posed a significant health risk to Ghanaians. “Show action to back your words by halting galamsey. It is a health emergency and a national crisis.”

acts.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Gebreyesus, WHO Director-General
acts.speech: Reported that “health aid [is] projected to decline by up to 40 per cent this year compared to two years ago.”

acts.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
acts.speech: In his speech at the Africa Health Sovereignty Summit held in Accra on August 5, 2025, praised several African leaders, including President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa; former President of Liberia, Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf; President Paul Kagame of Rwanda; former United Nations Secretary General, the late Kofi Annan; former Nigerian leader, Olusegun Obasanjo; and President William Ruto of Kenya, for their leadership in delivery of health services on the continent; called for Africa to assume leadership in healthcare.

title: Mzimba youth urged to take the lead in elections - Malawi24

acts.speaker: Desire Sibande, NEGLA North representative
acts.speech: Spoke to Malawi24 about the importance of youth involvement in democracy: “We urge all young people in the district to register in large numbers and vote for leaders of their choice on September 16, 2024,” he said. “We also encourage the youth to run for various leadership positions to bring fresh ideas and energy to our communities.”

acts.speaker: Pastor Chrispine Chakhumbira, Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) officer for Mzimba South
acts.speech: Announced that voter registration for the district will take place from November 28 to December 11, 2024. “We encourage all eligible voters to visit their local registration centres to register,” Chakhumbira said.

title: EUTM MOZ welcomes the UK Foreign Affairs Select Committee

acts.speaker: EUTM MOZ Command Group
acts.speech: Provided an overview on EUTM MOZ’ roles, capabilities, mission, current activities and the main ongoing projects within the Headquarters and the three training camps located in Katembe, Chimoio and Mavalane; described to the committee how EUTM MOZ is contributing to the capability building of the Mozambican armed forces’ units, selected to compose future Quick Reaction Forces (QRF).

acts.speaker: EUTM Mozambique (@EUTMMozambique), Twitter post, July 14, 2023
acts.speech: “#EUTMMOZ welcomed the @CommonsForeign to the Katembe Training Camp. It was a useful opportunity to describe the committee how EUTM MOZ is contributing to the capability building of the Armed Forces’ units, selected to compose Quick Reaction Forces.”

title: Goma : médecins en guerre contre une crise sanitaire dévastatrice - Mali 24

acts.speaker: Horace Kashema, doctor in Goma
acts.speech: “We are so overwhelmed, but we keep working and we hope that with the situation having calmed down a little, that will help us to work. But our supplies are going to run out soon. We do not have enough.”

acts.speaker: Doctors of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
acts.speech: Warn of the worsening of injuries in an increasingly difficult environment.

acts.speaker: Joseph Sangara, doctor and coordinator of the MSF project in Goma
acts.speech: “In similar situations, we know that between 10 and 20% of cases are critical cases. These are complicated cases, and these are the ones we are seeing. There are skull injuries, chest injuries. It is difficult to manage.”

acts.speaker: Virginie Napolitano, MSF emergency coordinator in Goma (via MSF International post on X, 1 February 2025)
acts.speech: “Goma was cut off from the world, it was a total blackout” — she tells of a week of chaos in the city, and how MSF teams adapted to treat war-wounded people.

title: Full Text: NDC’s petition to EC for forensic audit of voters’ register

acts.speaker: National Democratic Congress (NDC), Ghana (petition to the Electoral Commission)
acts.speech: Petitions the Electoral Commission for an urgent forensic audit of the 2024 voters register and its IT system, presenting “alarming irregularities, discrepancies and unauthorised manipulations discovered in the 2024 Provisional Voters Register” which “pose a significant and immediate threat to the credibility of the 2024 General elections”; states the irregularities “are not minor oversights or clerical errors; they indicate a deliberate manipulation of the voter database” ; says it has uncovered 243,540 illegal transfers, over 15,000 unidentifiable voter transfer paths, 3,957 deleted registered voters, 2,094 misplaced voter transfers and corrupt data files, and that five Biometric Voter Registration laptops were stolen from the EC Headquarters under CCTV surveillance ; complains the EC failed to provide the Provisional Voters Register in time for scrutiny, opened nominations prematurely on the provisional register, and rejected the NDC’s request for a live broadcast of the party’s findings ; demands an independent forensic audit of the register and its IT system, a stakeholder meeting with all political parties, civil society organizations and key international stakeholders (including ECOWAS, AU, UNDP, EU, USAID, The British High Commission and others), publication of the audit findings, a 5-day re-exhibition of the register, reversal of all unauthorized transfers, a revised electoral timeline, and accountability and integrity measures.

acts.speaker: Electoral Commission of Ghana (press conference, 2nd September 2024)
acts.speech: Acknowledged some of these errors and admitted to errors and illegal voter transfers during a press conference, but justified these mistakes as correctable during the exhibition exercise.

acts.speaker: Dr Bossman Asare, Deputy Chairman of the Electoral Commission of Ghana
acts.speech: Publicly admitted to the existence of illegal voter transfers and inflations in the voter transfer list during the 2nd September 2024 Press Conference, but indicated that the EC is working on it.

title: MENFOP/USAID : Projet DEGRA Quand la frénésie de la lecture s’empare de nos enfants !

acts.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Djibouti’s Minister of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
acts.speech: Welcomed the “results obtained at this stage, which are already convincing and allow us to think that not only are we on the right track but that the objectives of the project have been fully achieved.” ; restated his full confidence in “this initiative, which is a cardinal programme on which we are counting greatly to rely on in order to bring significant improvements in teaching and learning in our schools,” hence his call for each of the actions undertaken to lead to tangible results and bring perceptible improvements in pupils’ performance in order to win the battle for quality, which remains a primary objective.

acts.speaker: Jonathan Pratt, US Ambassador to Djibouti
acts.speech: Shared the minister’s views and recalled that the DEGRA project aims to improve pupils’ reading performance in basic education from the 1st to the 5th year in the country, and is the tool par excellence for achieving this objective through three intermediate results: improving the quality of reading teaching and learning, increasing community participation in reading in basic education, and strengthening reading teaching and learning policies.

acts.speaker: Panellists from MENFOP, parent-teacher associations (APE), school management committees (CGE) and civil society organisations (OSC)
acts.speech: All acknowledged the clear strengthening of the capacities of the APEs and CGEs to carry out school and extracurricular reading activities, including awareness-raising on the importance of reading and how to support it through school projects.

acts.speaker: Parents of pupils (APE members)
acts.speech: Were particularly pleased with the mobilisation and full community involvement around the DEGRA project, which won the enthusiasm and support of everyone; the better supervision and the training given to teachers were also widely praised.

title: INTERVIEW | Ambassador Kaire Mbuende on Isreal and Hamas conflict

acts.speaker: The United States and its western allies
acts.speech: Announced support for Israel and pledged further weapons and military assistance to Israel.

acts.speaker: Kaire Mbuende, Ambassador
acts.speech: Spoke to nbc's News Anchor, Elago Shitaatala, to give background on the long-running conflict.

title: Empreiteiros da USAID ameaçados com processos e violência por falta de pagamento

acts.speaker: Bloomberg (financial news agency)
acts.speech: According to Bloomberg, USAID contractor companies and non-governmental organisations have warned officials that there are already banks refusing loans because of the suspension of these entities' operations, following the freeze on operations decreed by the new US President, Donald Trump.

acts.speaker: USAID contractor companies and NGOs
acts.speech: Warned officials that there are already banks refusing loans because of the suspension of their operations following the freeze decreed by President Donald Trump.

acts.speaker: Humanitarian activists (documents filed in a US court)
acts.speech: Say, according to documents filed in a US court, that beyond the possibility of legal proceedings, workers are also facing physical threats over unpaid debts in the places where USAID was funding operations.

acts.speaker: Democracy International (USAID implementing entity)
acts.speech: Said it is facing lawsuits abroad if it cannot pay this month's salaries, notably in Tunisia, where 17 employees have joined together to claim their wages through the courts; said it owes three million dollars for services provided before 24 January, and has dismissed all 95 of its employees in the United States, now facing the risk of eviction from its headquarters and considering judicial liquidation.

acts.speaker: Eric Bjornlund, head of Democracy International (declaration to the court)
acts.speech: "In Tunisia, for example, our employees are being threatened by creditors with physical violence if they do not pay," wrote Eric Bjornlund in a declaration to the court, concluding that the employees "risk being arrested or attacked because of their close connection with USAID programmes that suddenly stopped keeping promises and honouring their obligations".

title: NYT: les États-Unis priveront le soutien du pays, où initialement n'a pas prévu de mettre fin à l'aide

acts.speaker: The New York Times (citing lists provided to officials and humanitarian workers)
acts.speech: Reported that the administration of American President Donald Trump has cut aid programmes for several countries where it had initially promised to maintain its support; according to these lists, the United States will cease financing programmes in Afghanistan, Iraq, Jordan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Lebanon, Madagascar, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Syria, Somalia, Chad and Yemen.

acts.speaker: Reuters (citing sources)
acts.speech: Reported on 9 April that the White House later decided to restore payments under the World Food Programme (WFP) in Lebanon, Syria, Somalia, Jordan, Iraq and Ecuador.

acts.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: Estimates that Washington's refusal to provide aid will have the greatest impact in Afghanistan, where about 2 million people, including 400,000 children, depend on the food, and that the population of Yemen will also suffer, where 2.4 million people receive food under humanitarian programmes.

acts.speaker: USAID staff speaking to the NYT (anonymous)
acts.speech: Stressed that they often learn of the end of the next programme directly from the humanitarian organisations that stop receiving funds.

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (previously appointed acting head of USAID)
acts.speech: Announced on 10 March that the American government, at the conclusion of a six-week audit, had officially ended 83% of the agency's programmes; according to him, under the 5,200 contracts that were cancelled, tens of billions of dollars had been spent not in the interests of the United States, and in some cases to their detriment.

title: OCP Africa lance un réseau de centres agricoles au Rwanda

acts.speaker: OCP Africa (post on the X platform)
acts.speech: Explained that this approach aims to respond to local agricultural challenges while stimulating sustainability and economic growth.

acts.speaker: Speakers at the launch ceremony (more than 40 key stakeholders attending)
acts.speech: Highlighted the strategic role of these centres in transforming agricultural practices in Rwanda.

title: Mohammed Mussa Idris

acts.speaker: Antoine de Saint-Exupery (quoted in the obituary)
acts.speech: "He who has gone, so we but cherish his memory, abides with us, more potent, nay, more present than the living man."

title: SAFI TIMBER diz que sua licença foi suspensa por não ter cedido à corrupção

acts.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (company position)
acts.speech: Considers illegal the decision suspending its timber export licence issued by the Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries (MAAP); holds that there was a violation of administrative principles, corruption and an attempt at extortion, and accuses senior MAAP officials of being behind a campaign aimed at extorting 15 million meticais from SAFI TIMBER; appeals for the intervention of the Central Office for Combating Corruption (GCCC).

acts.speaker: Mozambican Federation of Timber Operators (FEDEMOMA) (communique)
acts.speech: According to a FEDEMOMA communique, the Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries, Roberto Albino, suspended with immediate effect the native timber export licence of SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export — Export Certificate number 01/MTA/2025.

acts.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (note sent to the newsroom)
acts.speech: Explains that, having consulted the Administrative Procedure Code, it found that, first, "the maximum deadline for notification of administrative acts is five days"; second, "administrative acts must be notified directly to the interested party"; "a prior hearing is mandatory whenever the decision negatively affects the rights of a party", as well as "decisions must be reasoned, indicating the grounds and the legal basis" ; holds that the seven-day delay in notification and the absence of a prior hearing constitute a clear violation of the principles of legality, transparency and good administration provided for in law.

acts.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (aggrieved company)
acts.speech: Says that on 12 August its representatives received several telephone calls from different numbers and were pressured to make an illicit payment of 15 million meticais, under threat of definitive cancellation of the export certificate; accuses Imede Falume, national director of Forests and Wildlife, and Renato Timane, adviser to the Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries, of being involved in the attempt.

acts.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (company position)
acts.speech: Says it refuses to be complicit with corruption and will trigger legal mechanisms so that the two accused are held judicially responsible for corruption and extortion; considers that the suspension of its export certificate is not only illegal but also a clear attempt at extortion that is causing enormous financial losses and staining the credibility of the forestry sector in Mozambique; requests the intervention of the Attorney General’s Office and of the Central Office for Combating Corruption for an investigation and accountability of the transgressors.

title: Maroc : appel à la relance du processus de paix entre le Hamas et Israël

acts.speaker: Morocco (government position)
acts.speech: calls for the relaunch of the peace process between Israel and Hamas; frequently restates its position as the kingdom continues to receive criticism, notably from local activists opposed to the country's decision to restore its ties with Israel in December 2020.

acts.speaker: Omar Hilale, Permanent Ambassador of Morocco to the UN
