acts.speech: reiterated the country's satisfaction with the ceasefire agreement between Hamas and Israel, speaking on Monday in New York during a meeting devoted to the situation in the Middle East, notably in Palestine; described the ceasefire as a decisive step forward for the reconstruction of what was destroyed by the disastrous and genocidal Israeli campaign launched in October 2023 ; "The ceasefire agreement should pave the way for the reconstruction of what was destroyed by the war, as well as for the launch of a genuine peace process, allowing the establishment of a Palestinian State within the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side and in peace with Israel," he declared before the Security Council ; noted that Morocco welcomes the progress made towards halting hostilities and attacks on civilians, hoping that the ceasefire agreement will be fully respected through the release of hostages and detainees and the return of displaced persons ; recalled King Mohammed VI's commitment to the Palestinian cause, adding that his defence of this position has been constant and clear given that the creation of a Palestinian State is the cornerstone of peace and stability in the Middle East ; "Gaza must be an integral part of the independent Palestinian territories, where legal and political jurisdiction belongs to the Palestinian National Authority," he declared, adding that the continuation of unilateral Israeli acts in Al Quds exacerbates tensions.

acts.speaker: Qatar
acts.speech: echoed Morocco's call, reiterating the need to respect the ceasefire in Gaza; also called for the adoption of a binding resolution supporting the full implementation of the ceasefire.

title: SADC Ministers urged to take bold steps to address energy and water insecurity

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: Made the call for member states to urgently adopt collaborative and innovative strategies to tackle the growing energy and water insecurity that threatens economic growth and social development across the region, underscoring the critical need for regional integration and accelerated infrastructure development to meet rising demand and climate-related pressures: “Energy and water are the lifelines of our communities, economies and ecosystems. Insecurity in either will undermine production, weaken economic resilience and hinder growth.” ; Said that over 172 million people in SADC remain without access to electricity and only 40 percent of the population has adequate sanitation, and that compounded by population growth, urbanization, aging infrastructure, vandalism, and underinvestment, both energy and water sectors are under strain.

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: “In Zimbabwe alone, we lose approximately US$4 million annually to transformer theft and related damage. These criminal acts disrupt both power and water supply and demand a regional crackdown through tougher laws, technology deployment, and community awareness.”

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: Said that although Zimbabwe's installed generation capacity stands at nearly 3 000 MW, only 1 200–1 600 MW is currently achievable, far short of peak demand estimated at 2 000 MW, a situation which has led to periodic load shedding and increased reliance on imports.

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: Noted progress in renewable energy deployment, saying Zimbabwe is ramping up solar and hydro investments, including projects backed by pension funds such as the 25 MW Centragrid Nyabira Solar PV Park and the upcoming 100 MW Munyati Solar Plant: “We have developed our National Energy Compact with a goal to install 1.2 million solar home systems and solarize 35 000 villages by 2030 under the Presidential Rural Development Program.”

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: Called for urgent completion of interconnection projects to allow all SADC mainland countries, particularly Angola, Malawi and Tanzania, to join the Southern African Power Pool (SAPP), thus enabling greater electricity trade and improved grid stability ; urged member states to capitalise on solar potential, particularly in countries like Botswana, Namibia, Zimbabwe, and South Africa, and called for increased regional manufacturing and market creation for clean energy technologies.

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: Warned that El Niño-induced droughts, pollution, and underutilised irrigation are undermining access and sustainability, as currently only 71 percent of the region's population has access to safe drinking water: “This is a serious indictment. We must scale up water infrastructure investment and prioritize sanitation resilience, particularly as climate impacts worsen.”

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: Applauded countries like Tanzania for rapidly increasing electricity access, connecting 8 million people in two years, and encouraged member states to share best practices and scale up investments.

acts.speaker: July Moyo, Zimbabwean Minister of Energy and Power Development
acts.speech: “If we don't act decisively now, the SADC Industrialization Strategy and Roadmap will remain a pipe dream. Let this meeting be a turning point for the region. We must move from plans to action.”

title: Salon international de l’artisanat: Brice Hondi présente sa vision de l’artisanat

acts.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO and promoter of the Communication Platform of the African Network of Artisans (speech at the 6th Salon international de l’artisanat des Comores, SIACOM)
acts.speech: “Craftsmanship is not a sub-sector. It is not a fallback alternative. Craftsmanship is the silent cradle of our economies. It is the beating heart of our identities. It is the universal genius of our know-how. Alas, it is still one of the most underestimated sectors of our continent.” ; “The observation is blunt: artisans without up-to-date training. Workshops without suitable tools. Masterpieces sold at charity prices. Talents smothered in the informal sector, without social protection or visibility. Meanwhile, our countries import more than 15 billion dollars of craft products every year… WHICH OUR HANDS KNOW HOW TO MAKE BETTER THAN ANYONE. And Africa is impoverished — not for lack of talent, but through neglect.”

acts.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
acts.speech: Said that the Communication Platform of the African Network of Artisans, created more than a decade ago, works tirelessly to make the voice of the continent's artisans heard, and that, present in several countries, this initiative carried by the NGO CLUB EXCELLENCE ADECO acts daily to structure, train, connect and promote professionals of the sector: “This platform was not conceived for us, but for you — governments, decision-makers, public actors. Because the challenges of craftsmanship are structurally similar across all our countries. And because only a continental, coherent and sustainable response can meet this challenge.” ; recalled the training cycles initiated in several countries on digitalisation, craft transformation and youth integration, and the events organised to restore artisans' dignity — La Nuit des Artisans since 2014, the Day of African Women Leaders since 2020, and FIMEC since 2024 — announcing that the 2025 edition of FIMEC becomes an international festival with four dimensions: the 2nd FIMEC, the 11th Nuit des Artisans, the 5th Journée des Femmes Leaders Africaines, and the first edition of SIJA (International Symposium of African Youth).

acts.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
acts.speech: Addressing Heads of State and Government, saluted the efforts they are already making, but suggested: “Why not devote to craftsmanship a ministry in its own right, with substantial budgets and a continental vision? Why not integrate craft trades into school and university curricula, as a genuine bridge between knowledge and know-how? Why not create an African fund to support craftsmanship and youth entrepreneurship? Why not establish a structural alliance between tourism and craftsmanship, so that what we create finally finds showcases worthy of its genius?” ; “Africa cannot become great by importing its identity. It will become great when it understands the value of what it creates. And that requires that those who create are finally recognised… and taken seriously.”

acts.speaker: Dr Brice Hondi, President of the Board of Directors of the NGO Club Excellence ADECO
acts.speech: Appealed to the technical and financial partners present or listening: “Support this vision. Join us. This is not an event project. It is a transformation project. A project that touches three vital sectors: craftsmanship, women, youth. To support that is to choose impact, innovation and sustainability.” ; “We seek neither glory nor the spotlight. What we want is that tomorrow a young hairdresser from Burkina, a fashion designer from Malawi, a jeweller from the Comoros… can live with dignity from their art.” ; “What we do not raise up always ends up dying out. Let us not let African craftsmanship die out. Let us make it a torch. A torch of economy, dignity and sovereignty. We have dreamed Africa enough. It is time to build it with our hands.”

title: La Chine accélère sa coopération pour faire progresser l’Initiative pour le développement mondial

acts.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
acts.speech: Solemnly proposed the Global Development Initiative on 21 September 2021 during the general debate of the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly, bringing China's wisdom and strength to solving global development problems.

acts.speaker: China (at the High-level Dialogue on Global Development, June 2022)
acts.speech: Announced pragmatic measures to implement the initiative, notably transforming the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund into the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund, increasing its contribution to the UN Peace and Development Trust Fund, creating a Global Development Promotion Centre and a Global Development Knowledge Network, and publishing a Global Development Report.

acts.speaker: Stephen Bainous Kargbo, representative of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in China
acts.speech: Said the Global Development Initiative has helped mobilise resources, establish cooperation mechanisms and advance practical cooperation, and that the major progress achieved in areas such as poverty reduction, food security and health has demonstrated China's determination and capacity to contribute to global well-being and common prosperity.

acts.speaker: Carlos Maria Correa, executive director of the South Centre
acts.speech: Noted that the Global Development Initiative aligns with the priorities of developing countries, emphasising the sustainable development goals and providing stronger and more targeted support to these nations.

acts.speaker: Dennis Francis, President of the 78th session of the United Nations General Assembly
acts.speech: Stressed that the objectives of the Global Development Initiative are consistent with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and have great potential to benefit countries around the world; the vision championed by the Initiative embodies the spirit of true multilateralism and will build a fairer and more sustainable world for all.

title: Mali : opération militaire d'envergure à Sébabougou

acts.speaker: General staff of the Malian armed forces (etat-major general des armees)
acts.speech: The provisional toll communicated by the general staff reports five wounded soldiers, treated by the medical services, and twenty-one terrorists neutralised; a significant quantity of military equipment, communication equipment, vehicles and logistics was recovered in the locality.

acts.speaker: General staff of the Malian armed forces (etat-major general des armees)
acts.speech: Gave assurances that all measures will be taken to secure the area durably, protect civilians, facilitate free movement and prevent any attempt by armed groups to re-establish themselves in the region.

acts.speaker: General staff of the Malian armed forces (communique)
acts.speech: In its communique, paid tribute to the professionalism and courage of the soldiers engaged, while stressing that the struggle for the stabilisation of central and northern Mali requires constant and determined action.

acts.speaker: Testimonies gathered from reliable local sources (cross-checked by several Malian media outlets)
acts.speech: Reported that living conditions in Sebabougou had become extremely precarious: supply cuts, movement restrictions, violence and constant threats.

title: Pres. Boakai Reassures US of Openness to Strategic Partnership…

acts.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
acts.speech: has reassured the United States of Liberia's openness to strategic partnership in the areas of trade, energy, infrastructure, agriculture, technology, and entrepreneurship, among others; announced that his administration is building a foreign policy architecture that seeks not only to deepen political alliances but also to create strategic economic partnerships ; "The goal is to promote Liberia as a viable and attractive destination for investment, innovation, and sustainable development." ; his administration stands committed to creating a stable, transparent, and enabling environment for business ; recognized the critical role of the U.S. Private Sector and expressed optimism about the creation of pathways that foster increased engagement between Liberian and American businesses.

acts.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
acts.speech: extolled the historical ties between Liberia and the U.S., while calling for a stronger economic partnership between both countries, and underscored the unique and enduring relationship between Liberia and the U.S., highlighting a shared history that spans over two centuries: "The U.S. has remained a steadfast ally, supporting Liberia in its democratic journey, providing development assistance, strengthening institutions, and most importantly, standing with Liberia during moments of national challenge."

acts.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
acts.speech: described the celebration of the United States' 249th Independence Day as the birth of an enduring idea that freedom, democracy, and opportunity should be the bedrock upon which nations are built.

title: Grand Kru Technical College needs US$400,000 - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Authorities of the Grand Kru Technical College
acts.speech: Are pleading with local and international partners, including USAID, UNDP, UNESCO, the Chinese Embassy in Liberia, and the Government of Liberia, to help construct the building that will house the college in the county.

acts.speaker: Professor T. Dan Jah Bestman, Vice President for Administration, Grand Kru Technical College
acts.speech: Says the College needs about 12 million United States Dollars to construct its campus; said that about 50 acres of land have already been secured in Grand Kru County, and they need about Four Hundred Thousand United States Dollars ($400,000) to jump-start construction ; said the college does not have the mobility to transport materials to the county, thus it stocks equipment at its Monrovia office ; revealed that the College signed an MOU with the Ministry of Agriculture local office in the county to use its premises for about five years, but they fear that they may be thrown out as the Ministry of Agriculture embarks on strengthening its sub-offices across the country.

acts.speaker: Professor T. Dan Jah Bestman, Vice President for Administration, Grand Kru Technical College
acts.speech: Lauded the County Legislative Caucus and the Acting President of Grand Kru Technical College, Josephus M. Gray, for the level of support and cooperation they are receiving for the college’s forward match ; lauded the government and the Grand Kru County Legislative Caucus for transitioning from TEVT to Grand Kru Technical College (GKTC), which he noted is highly welcoming.

acts.speaker: Professor T. Dan Jah Bestman, Vice President for Administration, Grand Kru Technical College
acts.speech: Pointed out that the college currently has about 3,300 students for its first Semester of 2024/2025, surpassing Tubman University’s enrollment when it first opened in Maryland County in 2009.

title: Ethio-Aid: Softening the blow from US aid cut

acts.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
acts.speech: Tuesday announced the launch of a new initiative dubbed “Ethio-Aid”, aiming to substitute the assistance being withheld by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); it is a national disaster response mechanism intended to soften the blow caused by the aid cut and address emergencies using domestically mobilised resources.

acts.speaker: Draft proclamation on disaster risk management (presented to parliament)
acts.speech: According to the draft, 3 percent of the national budget will be allocated annually to a dedicated disaster response fund; the draft proclamation specifies that both governmental and non-governmental entities will be part of this national contribution effort.

acts.speaker: Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission
acts.speech: recently told legislators that the goal of Ethio-Aid is to enhance the country’s capacity to respond to natural disasters, conflict-related emergencies, and other crises, and that in addition to addressing domestic needs, the initiative is also intended to support neighbouring countries during times of hardship.

acts.speaker: Officials from the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission
acts.speech: indicated that the funds collected will be used to build a permanent, well-resourced disaster response institution.

title: Namibia's GDP reaches 2.8% in third quarter of 2024

acts.speaker: Namibian Statistics Agency (NSA)
acts.speech: Indicated the economy's size in the third quarter of 2024 reached N$61.6 billion, marking an increase of N$5.3 billion compared to the N$56.3 billion recorded in the third quarter of 2023.

acts.speaker: Mirijam Shihepo, NSA spokesperson
acts.speech: Noted, “In real terms, the domestic economy grew by 2.8% during the third quarter of 2024 compared to 3.1% growth registered in the parallel quarter of 2022.”

title: WFP urges $404M to secure food aid for South Sudan in 2025 - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: is appealing to donors to provide early funding of $404 million for next year’s humanitarian operations in South Sudan to enable the agency to secure enough food to reduce hunger through 2025 ; In a press statement on Friday, WFP said it currently has no food supplies in South Sudan to preposition for next year’s humanitarian response and needs US$404 million to frontload assistance ; added that failure to do so will leave WFP reliant on expensive airdrops later in the year to reach isolated communities who are facing the most severe levels of hunger and depend on humanitarian food assistance ; the statement said funds received before the end of this year will enable WFP to preposition food by road in remote hunger-hit areas during the brief dry season window from December to April.

acts.speaker: WFP-FAO Hunger Hotspots report
acts.speech: warns that South Sudan is facing a combination of crises that continue to push the country towards new levels of severe food insecurity; it said the situation has left nine million people in urgent need of humanitarian assistance and protection, worsening the already dire living conditions across the country; the report underscored that South Sudan is facing unprecedented floods, impacting more than 1.3 million people nationwide, with Unity, Jonglei, Abyei Administrative Area, Western Bahr el Ghazal, and Lakes States being the most affected.

acts.speaker: Shaun Hughes, WFP’s Acting Country Director for South Sudan
acts.speech: “It can take months to turn pledged donor funds into food in the hands of hungry people in South Sudan. The country’s limited road networks are impassable for much of the year – particularly in the east and central parts of the country where food insecurity is highest” ; “Airdrops are always last resort for WFP. Every dollar spent on planes is a dollar not spent on food for hungry people. But there is a simple solution: get food to communities by road before they are cut off by heavy rain and flooding.”

acts.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: said it had to double the amount of food delivered by airdrops during the lean season of 2024 to meet hunger needs, adding US$30 million to overall operational costs reportedly because food aid did not arrive in the country in time ; said it was able to reduce airdrops by 70 per cent in 2019 when prepositioning was optimized due to generous donor contributions and the timely arrival of food ; said acute food insecurity in South Sudan – where 56 per cent of population already faces crisis (IPC3) or worse levels of hunger – is likely to worsen as the 2025 lean season approaches, typically starting in May.

title: Gvt to lower taxes, retirement age to boost youth employment - Lesotho Times

acts.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
acts.speech: Announced a series of bold initiatives aimed at reducing unemployment in Lesotho, with a particular focus on creating opportunities for young people; said during a media briefing this week that by encouraging civil servants aged 50 and above to take early retirement, the government could create more space for young people to enter the workforce: “The government will also explore ways to reduce taxes, making it easier for businesses to hire more youths.”

acts.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
acts.speech: Instructed ministries that are able to do so to allocate two percent of their annual budgets to the Youth Development Fund: “This contribution will help us combat unemployment by directly supporting youth initiatives.”

acts.speaker: Bureau of Statistics / Lesotho Labour Force Survey 2024
acts.speech: Cited by the Prime Minister as showing that 50 percent of the population is currently unemployed, with youths making up less than half of this number.

acts.speaker: Dr Retšelisitsoe Matlanyane, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Lesotho
acts.speech: Said in February this year during her 2025-2025 budget speech in parliament that 38.9 percent of youth in Lesotho were unemployed, with young women bearing the brunt at 41 percent.

acts.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
acts.speech: Pointed to international factors, including U.S. executive orders and the withdrawal of Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) aid, as having worsened the unemployment situation.

acts.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
acts.speech: Said the government aimed to “significantly reduce unemployment and provide more opportunities for Lesotho's youth”, and emphasized his personal commitment to ensuring the success of his plans, stating he “will spend time each week visiting projects to monitor progress”.

title: Gaza : des agences de l’ONU condamnent le plan israélien visant à utiliser l’aide comme un "appât "

acts.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
acts.speech: According to UNICEF, the Israeli proposal to open a handful of aid centres exclusively in the south of the Gaza Strip would create an "impossible choice between displacement and death."

acts.speaker: UNICEF spokesperson (James Elder), at a press briefing in Geneva
acts.speech: Said the plan "contravenes fundamental humanitarian principles" and appears designed to "reinforce control over vital goods as a means of pressure" ; "It is dangerous to ask civilians to go into militarised zones to collect rations... humanitarian aid should never be used as a bargaining chip" ; maintained that Gaza's most vulnerable people - the elderly, disabled children, the sick and the wounded who cannot travel to the designated distribution areas - would face "terrible challenges" in collecting aid ; insisted that the 60 aid trucks a day foreseen by the plan, "one tenth of what was delivered during the ceasefire," is "far from enough to meet the needs of 1.1 million children and 2.1 million people" ; "There is a simple alternative: lift the blockade, let humanitarian aid in, save lives."

acts.speaker: Humanitarian workers (aid agencies in Gaza)
acts.speech: Have repeatedly warned that food, water, medicine and fuel were beginning to run out, with the Palestinian enclave under a total aid blockade for more than two months.

title: Liberia stands ready to overcome USAID obstacles - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
acts.speech: Says the country is prepared to brace the direct and indirect impact of what he terms as "USAID obstacles" ; "Liberia's is resilient and will surely overcome this latest obstacle", Minister Ngafuan told the Voice of America's Day Break Africa program Wednesday, February 19, 2025.

acts.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
acts.speech: Says the lead cancelled project, for local accountability and decentralization, is US$17 million, which was mainly helping the country in domestic resource mobilization: "We have set an ambitious agenda to increase domestic revenue through the Liberia Revenue Authority and USAID was the main partner assisting us to rollout this new tax system from what we call goods and services tax (GST) to Value Added Tax by 2026"; notes the project comes with training, investment assistance and that USAID has been providing support for the government's tax database system or E-tax, which has been assisting in improving government revenue collection in local terrains.

acts.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
acts.speech: Says other projects in education, health and governance, and support to the elections commission which USAID has been supporting through international and local NGOs, are all being affected by the cancellation; acknowledges that there are direct and indirect impacts, noting that other international organizations that had been supported by USAID have scaled down support, with USAID being Liberia's second largest donor next to the World Bank; and recalls USAID support to Liberia from 2021-2029 totaling US$422 million, with an agreement concluded to receive more than US$100 million to support education, health, agriculture and other key areas before everything halted by President Donald Trump.

acts.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberia's Finance and Development Planning Minister
acts.speech: Asked what Liberia is doing to mitigate the obstacles, says the government has accepted the decision of the United States Government, and discloses that the Ministry of Finance has just concluded and will be submitting to President Boakai and the 55th Legislature short and long-term impacts and what is to be done to address the shocks ; "We will be engaging into some fiscal tightening, mopping up our resources mobilization, among other things. We are going to make sure we reduce losses and abuses, and we will also be engaging our partners in regional organizations; there are conversations in our block on what we are to do to reduce the impact of this cancellation", he assures.

acts.speaker: Government of Liberia
acts.speech: Says it is prepared to brace direct and indirect impacts of obstacles posed by the departure of USAID.

acts.speaker: U.S. Ambassador to Liberia (reported by Minister Ngafuan)
acts.speech: Paid Minister Ngafuan a courtesy call and told him that the project for local accountability and decentralization is among several projects that were cancelled under the USAID aid cancellation program.

title: Message de la ministre en charge de la Population à l’occasion de la Journée Mondiale de l’Aide Humanitaire : Pour une action humanitaire ancrée dans la souveraineté nationale | Le Sahel

acts.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: Delivered a message in which she encouraged all actors to continue their efforts with rigour and humanity, respecting the principles of transparency, accountability and above all the dignity of the country's people. ; Stressed that, since 19 August 2003, hundreds of other humanitarian workers around the world have been victims of violence, injured or killed while working tirelessly to assist vulnerable populations in contexts of war, forced displacement, epidemics or climate disasters.

acts.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: Noted that this edition is being held in a global context still marked by complex security crises, forced displacement of populations, and increasingly frequent climate shocks; said that in regions such as the central Sahel, and particularly in the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), lawless armed terrorist groups attack civilians gratuitously every day, disrupting community life and compromising their access to security, education, health and livelihoods. ; "Persistent insecurity, particularly in certain border areas, continues to cause displacement of refugees and internally displaced persons and makes access to basic services difficult for many families."

acts.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: Rejoiced that, by the grace of God and unlike previous years at the same period, the 2025 floods have so far not reached the alarming toll recorded last year, the result of unprecedented prevention efforts made possible by key measures: reconstruction and rehabilitation of waterways in cities such as Niamey and Maradi; intensive awareness campaigns via radio, television and community relays; early mobilisation of local actors and technical services; and active collaboration of populations living in flood-prone areas.

title: Leão Lopes marca presença na 3ª edição dos Encontros do Património Audiovisual em Moçambique

acts.speaker: Associação dos Amigos do Museu do Cinema em Moçambique (AAMCM) (press statement)
acts.speech: In a statement, the organisation confirmed that Leão Lopes, author of Cabo Verde’s first feature film, “Ilhéu de Contenda”, will bring his vast experience to one of the central debates of the gathering, which brings together specialists from Cabo Verde, Germany, Angola, Brazil, Cuba, the United States, France, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique and Portugal ; “Among the most eagerly awaited moments is the debate ‘The power of cinema in political propaganda’, which will feature specialists from Cuba, France, Portugal and Brazil.”

title: A lottery that's changing lives in Uganda

acts.speaker: Eric Mabuza Jnr, General Manager, ITHUBA Uganda (opinion column)
acts.speech: Writes that when the Uganda National Lottery was launched a few months ago, “we didn't simply introduce a game. We introduced a promise—a promise of fairness, opportunity, and national progress. And today, I can confidently say: that promise is already coming to life.” ; Says at ITHUBA the mission has never been just about creating winners but about creating impact, and that what excites him most is that “this transformation is funded not by debt or foreign aid—but by Ugandans themselves. Every UGX 600 DAILY LOTTO ticket or UGX 1,000 POWERBALL play becomes a small act of nation-building.” ; Says he has witnessed firsthand how a National Lottery can drive real, measurable development, noting ITHUBA has channelled more than $650 million from ticket sales into good causes over the past decade ; Says the company has invested heavily in systems that ensure integrity, that every game is fully digital and operations are 100% regulated by the NLGRB, and that ITHUBA encourages responsible gaming and has partnered with counselling organisations ; Says jobs have been created, small businesses are benefiting and communities are gaining access to new resources: “This is what it looks like when a National Lottery becomes more than entertainment. It becomes an economic engine.” ; “So, the next time you buy a ticket, know that you're not just playing for a chance to win. You're joining a movement—one that's transforming communities, supporting dreams, and building a better Uganda.”

acts.speaker: National Lotteries and Gaming Regulatory Board (NLGRB)
acts.speech: Has already identified the upcoming AFCON 2027 tournament as a flagship beneficiary of Uganda National Lottery proceeds, supporting the construction of world-class stadiums and training facilities.

title: Projet de l’employabilite de la main d’œuvre djiboutienne de l’USAID ; Cérémonie de remise de certificats pour 475 jeunes djiboutiens formés

acts.speaker: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh, Director General of ANEFIP (Djibouti's National Agency for Employment, Training and Professional Integration)
acts.speech: At the certificate award ceremony, encouraged jobseekers to seize every opportunity to gain experience in the world of work, even if it is only a small amount of experience, and to register with ANEFIP's agencies.

acts.speaker: Laura Dillon-Binkley, head of the PED (Djiboutian Workforce Employability) project
acts.speech: Urged them to move forward and to take their own initiatives in searching for work.

acts.speaker: Moussa Abdillahi, USAID representative
acts.speech: Congratulated the participants on having completed the training and wished them good luck.

acts.speaker: A female participant from the Gabode centre (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said that “to go out into the field you have to be armed. And for me, this training is my weapon.”

acts.speaker: A participant from the Tadjourah region (anonymous)
acts.speech: Shared that “before the training, I blamed everyone else for my situation. Now I am convinced that I am the sole master of my own future.”

title: USAID’S DEVELOPMENT INNOVATION VENTURES accepting new applicants

acts.speaker: US Agency for International Development (USAID) (program announcement)
acts.speech: Announced that it is accepting new applications for the Development Innovation Ventures (DIV) program, that anyone, anywhere can apply at any time, and set out the tiered funding stages and separate evidence grants; stated that since 2010, DIV has invested in over 190 solutions across 46 countries and all sectors in which USAID invests, has directly affected more than 30 million lives, that over half of DIV grantees had never received USAID funding before, and that DIV has mobilized USD4.60 of external funding for every USD1 from the American people.

title: Le Niger dit avoir demandé le remplacement de l'ambassadeur de l'UE, rappelé à Bruxelles -

acts.speaker: Nigerien authorities / government
acts.speech: Accused the EU of having "unilaterally" redistributed 1.3 million euros of EU humanitarian aid to foreign NGOs operating in Niger without their having been informed beforehand; said they were carrying out an audit and called on the EU to do the same; said Niger had requested the replacement of the EU ambassador before his recall.

acts.speaker: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
acts.speech: Said it had summoned Mr Da Franca on 14 October to "put an end to the operations" of delivering the aid, before "noting" that they continued; said the government concluded that "collaboration" with Salvador Pinto da Franca was "no longer possible" and officially requested "his recall and replacement as soon as possible"; stated that Niger "has never issued an appeal for international humanitarian aid following the floods" ; "The announcement of this unsolicited aid appeared on social media two weeks before the Nigerien authorities were officially informed, which is contrary to diplomatic practice."

acts.speaker: European Union
acts.speech: Expressed its "profound disagreement" after the challenge to the aid management arrangements and announced the recall of its ambassador to Niger, Salvador Pinto da Franca, for "consultations" in Brussels; stated that it "wishes to continue supporting the population."

title: Ministry of Information presents certificate of appreciation to welfare organization, Tallo-wadaag

acts.speaker: Mohamed Nor Indhos, Chief Executive Officer of Talla-Wadaag
acts.speech: "We have received a certificate of appreciation from the Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism of Somalia, this recognization to our services for our community here, encourages us to continue the social services" ; added that different parts of the Somali Community in Columbus, Ohio participated the event.

title: Over 88m in east, central Africa food insecure – Report

acts.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) (joint report)
acts.speech: Said that more than 88 million people in East and Central Africa faced food insecurity and required urgent humanitarian assistance in June 2025, of whom 57.1 million were in seven of the eight IGAD member states, namely Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda: "Levels of acute food insecurity across the region remained concerning, with ongoing or approaching lean seasons compounding the effects of conflict, climatic shocks, and macroeconomic challenges in many countries." ; The two organisations noted that countries battling conflict are the worst affected as the crises continue to disrupt livelihoods and undermine food security across the region, including Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the last three being the worst affected.

acts.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
acts.speech: Said an estimated 23.8 million people had been forcibly displaced across the region as of the end of June, including 18 million internally displaced persons and 5.8 million refugees and asylum seekers; they observed that conflict, insecurity, and climatic shocks remained the primary drivers of displacement, and that Sudan accounted for over half of the region's total IDPs, at 10.1 million, 2.4 million displaced before the start of the ongoing conflict, and 7.7 million after.

title: Pelo menos 38 feridos em aterragem de emergência de avião na Nigéria - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) (statement)
acts.speech: Announced that at least 38 people were injured, six of them seriously, in the emergency landing of a United Airlines plane in Lagos; said the Boeing 787-800 took off from Murtala Muhammed International Airport at 23:59 local time on Thursday bound for Washington, was forced to make an "emergency return" and landed "safely" at 03:22 local time on Friday with 245 adults and 11 crew members on board: "Four passengers and two crew members suffered serious injuries, and 27 passengers and five crew members suffered minor injuries," adding that "the aircraft itself did not suffer significant damage."

acts.speaker: Leslie Scott, United Airlines spokeswoman
acts.speech: Told CNN that six of the injured had already been discharged from hospital and that the reason for the plane's return was not severe turbulence, and that the airline is "working with US and Nigerian aviation authorities to understand the cause" of the incident.

acts.speaker: Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA)
acts.speech: Confirmed that it is investigating the case, which occurred over Ivory Coast's airspace.

acts.speaker: Michael Achimugu, NCAA Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection (statement)
acts.speech: "We are investigating the incident. We have received the flight data records in order to determine exactly what happened."

title: Starvation alert as children fill Kenya refugee ward after US aid cuts - Daily News

acts.speaker: United Nations official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Told the BBC that hundreds of thousands of people are “slowly starving” in Kenyan refugee camps after US funding cuts reduced food rations to their lowest ever levels.

acts.speaker: Medic at Kakuma’s Amusait Hospital (anonymous)
acts.speech: Tells the BBC that the wrinkled, peeling skin and angry patches of red on the baby Hellen are the result of malnutrition.

acts.speaker: Agnes Awila, refugee from northern Uganda
acts.speech: “The food is not enough, my children eat only once a day. If there’s no food what do you feed them?”

title: United States Govt Partners FCMB To Strengthen Nigeria’s Private Health Sector

acts.speaker: Melissa Jones, USAID Mission Director (Nigeria)
acts.speech: Affirmed the U.S. government’s commitment to strengthen Nigeria’s health sector and private sector resilience with a new partnership agreement. “As demonstrated by this partnership, the United States government is eager to continue collaborating with the financial sector to improve access to credit for underserved borrowers, including small and medium enterprises in the health sector, and thereby stimulate economic growth.” ; “In addition to supporting FCMB’s increased lending in the health sector, we are committed to work with FCMB to disburse loans to the agriculture and renewable energy sectors through our existing partnerships.”

acts.speaker: Mrs. Yemisi Edun, Managing Director, First City Monument Bank (FCMB)
acts.speech: “I commend the DFC for its commitment to improving local access to quality healthcare. This partnership will help close the gap in healthcare financing. This means more Nigerians will have access to better healthcare facilities.” ; “First City Monument Bank welcomes the opportunity to collaborate with healthcare providers and SMEs nationwide to build a healthier, more productive future for our nation.”

title: La maison russe en RCA : un acteur humanitaire discret mais essentiel pour les Centrafricains

acts.speaker: Dmitry Sytyi, director of the Russian House in Bangui
acts.speech: Stressed that these actions are part of a broader approach. “We have already provided humanitarian aid to more than twenty African countries,” he said. According to him, these initiatives, though little publicized, attest to Russia’s growing commitment to humanitarian cooperation on the continent ; “Western media often remain silent about these actions, but for us, the essential thing is to respond to the needs of local populations,” he added.

acts.speaker: Dmitry Sytyi, director of the Russian House in Bangui
acts.speech: Explained, on the institution’s cultural and educational role: “Our mission is not limited to culture. We want to contribute to the human and social development of the CAR.”

acts.speaker: President of the Central African Republic
acts.speech: Hailed this initiative, calling Russian support “a source of hope for hundreds of families.” He also expressed his government’s desire to strengthen cooperation with Russia, particularly in the areas of health and social development.

title: Asia’s Strongest Storm In 2024 Hits Myanmar, Leaves Over 220 Persons Dead, Others Missing

acts.speaker: Time Magazine (report)
acts.speech: According to Time Magazine, tens of thousands of people had fled to safer grounds, including 438 relief camps nationwide, as water inundated more than 158,000 homes and destroyed 2,116 more.

acts.speaker: Government of Myanmar
acts.speech: Said that tens of thousands of people had fled to safer grounds, including 438 relief camps nationwide, as water inundated more than 158,000 homes and destroyed 2,116 more.

acts.speaker: Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar junta chief (quoted by state media)
acts.speech: Made a rare request for foreign aid: "Officials from the government need to contact foreign countries to receive rescue and relief aid."

acts.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (report)
acts.speech: Estimated 631,000 people were likely affected, and "multiple sources indicate that hundreds of people have died, with many more missing," the U.N. agency said in a report ; said evacuation and rescue efforts in Myanmar are ongoing, oftentimes hampered by damaged infrastructure, ongoing clashes and the lack of funds.

acts.speaker: Thailand's disaster prevention department
acts.speech: According to the department, at least 45 have died from flooding and related incidents since mid-August, while about 28,000 households remain affected by the floods across 13 provinces.

acts.speaker: Major General Zaw Min Tun, Myanmar junta spokesman
acts.speech: Said a thorough assessment of the damage will be made to provide support accordingly.

acts.speaker: Myanmar's meteorology department
acts.speech: Asked people near the river banks in three towns to flee to safer ground as the Sittaung River has exceeded its danger level by about five feet ; forecast heavy rains in three provinces including war-torn Rakhine State in the next 24 hours.

title: Dead Aid: Why the uproar now? - Nation Online

acts.speaker: US President Donald Trump (Executive Order)
acts.speech: Has decided to freeze all Aid to foreign countries except Israel and Egypt, and has introduced tariffs; exceptions that are free are funds meant for life saving medicines, ARVS and other. His Executive Order comes in the footsteps of another order withdrawing the USA from the World Health Organisation.

acts.speaker: Leonce Ndakumana, Burundian Professor of Economics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst
acts.speech: Has studied the Politics of Aid and found that in fact instead of being a net recipient of Aid, as it is said, Africa is a net creditor to America and the world through its corrupt leaders.

acts.speaker: ActionAid studies (“Real Aid”)
acts.speech: Studies by Action Aid called Real Aid reached similar conclusions.

acts.speaker: The wise men of Tongaland (proverb)
acts.speech: Say, a fool says or does things before swallowing his own saliva.

title: PR diz que nova Lei de Terras deve resolver problemas da população - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: Says the new Land Law, currently under public consultation, opens the way for the elimination of idle land and of the arbitrary allocation of land for mining exploration in the country ; defended the need for a profound revision of land legislation, stressing that "the land belongs to all of us, as Mozambican citizens, and belongs to the Mozambican people," within the framework of strengthening sovereignty and building the country's economic independence.

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: Praised the advances already achieved, namely the approval of the new Land Policy in 2022, and highlighted the forum as "a space for consultation in the process of consolidating the policy and the regulatory framework for access to and use of land," essential to guarantee the sustainable and fair use of natural resources ; "In this sense, the Land Consultation Forum, by constituting itself as a space for consultation in the process of consolidating the policy and regulatory framework for access to land use, seeks to translate, in concrete terms, our commitment to continue making land one of the weapons of our people in asserting our economic independence, whose foundations we are now laying for our Mozambican people."

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: Highlighted the symbolism of the meeting at a time when Mozambique is preparing to celebrate 50 years of National Independence: "The June sun allowed the recovery of the land by the Mozambican people," recalling that land was one of the pillars of the liberation struggle ; greeting peasants, community leaders, women, young people and other actors present, reiterated the importance of inclusion and popular participation in the process of revising the Land Law: "To all of you, thank you very much for your presence at this very inclusive forum."

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: "On this occasion, we want to praise the main achievements of the governance of the mandate that preceded us, which consisted of leading the public consultation process for the revision of the national land policy and the respective legal framework, and the consequent approval of the current land policy and its 2022 implementation strategy, and bringing to debate the present draft Land Law. That is why we are very pleased to see here the former Minister of Land and Environment, Ivete Maibasse, who did an extraordinary job in getting us to this point."

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: "By taking shape as a platform for inclusive debate on issues relating to land administration and management in the country, the Land Consultation Forum allows us to analyse the results achieved on the basis of the national consensuses cemented over some 28 years of implementation of the Land Law in force" ; stressed that it "opens the way for us to adapt and adopt a more robust and predictable Land Law, one that responds to challenges such as the consolidation of market structures, population growth, the increase in the population living in cities and towns without the provision of infrastructure and basic services, combined with the country's vulnerability to the effects of climate change."

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: Detailed the main innovations of the draft Land Law, including the elevation of the Right to Use and Benefit from Land (DUAT) to a basic human and property right, special protection for women, and the prohibition of practices that could result in the emergence of shadowy land markets or the exclusion of local communities ; called for a determined fight against criminal practices associated with land, such as corruption and the illegal sale of plots, stating: "We must, as a nation, eradicate these harmful practices that undermine the development of our communities and of the country."

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
acts.speech: Expressed recognition of the Commission for the Revision of the National Land Policy for the breadth and depth of the consultation process, and thanked international partners for their support, such as the World Bank, the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the embassies of friendly countries ; encouraged participants to put forward proposals that strengthen gender equity in access to land and help make the new legislation an effective instrument for economic development and social justice: "We also await contributions that clarify the meaning and practical effect of the Right to Use and Benefit from Land within the framework of the market economy."

title: Lutte contre la malnutrition dans l’espace Cedeao: L’Alliance régionale de fortification alimentaire en gestation à Cotonou

acts.speaker: Francoise Sybille Assavedo, Deputy Director of Cabinet of the Minister of Health of Benin
acts.speech: Recalled, opening the proceedings, that this meeting follows the one held in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, in June 2023, and stressed that it serves as a framework for taking stock of the implementation of large-scale food fortification programmes in West Africa and for sharing good practices and the lessons learned in each country.

acts.speaker: Francoise Sybille Assavedo, Deputy Director of Cabinet of the Minister of Health of Benin
acts.speech: "Food and nutrition problems remain a brake on development in West Africa and persist because of their complex determinants, at once cultural, social and economic"; she developed that the deficiency in key micronutrients, notably iron, vitamin A, folic acid, zinc and iodine, remains at an alarming level among both children and women of childbearing age.

acts.speaker: Dr Keita Namoudou, West African Health Organisation (WAHO/Ooas)
acts.speech: Indicated that the workshop allows participants to carry out a SWOT analysis (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats) of existing projects and interventions, and that the aim is to identify methodological approaches, the limits and the paths for improving public-private partnership and sub-regional governance for the sustainability of fortification efforts, in order to prevent nutrient deficiencies and improve the overall health of the populations of West Africa.

acts.speaker: Dr William Bosu, West African Health Organisation (WAHO/Ooas)
acts.speech: Added that one woman in two of childbearing age is anaemic, with severe deficiencies in micronutrients indispensable to the proper functioning of the organism; that one child in three under five is stunted; and that 15% of infants have a low birth weight in the region.

acts.speaker: Lassane Kabore, representative of ECOWAS
acts.speech: Said it is important to propose actions to be replicated and advocacy avenues for the sustainability of the fortification strategy in West Africa in order to free populations from the tyranny of hunger and poor nutrition.

title: Uuministeli gwuuhaku wa pewa Oombulansa

acts.speaker: Lisa Johnson, United States Ambassador to Namibia
acts.speech: “This assistance came from a programme called ‘Defense’s humanitarian assistance’ of the United States. Such assistance is given in order to help wherever there is a need to fight the Covid-19 disease across the whole country.”

acts.speaker: Ben Nangombe, Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
acts.speech: Confirmed that all the donations were given to the hospitals that are truly in need.

acts.speaker: Eric Dziuban, head of the U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention in Namibia
acts.speech: Said their agency is working together with the Namibian government to fight the disease ; “We are prepared to fight the Covid-19 disease, and the advice we give to the public is only that citizens should wash their hands all the time and keep away from places where many people gather.”

title: Opinion – Basic income grant: benefit or burden?

acts.speaker: Economists
acts.speech: Argued that the [2008 Omitara-Otjivero BIG] pilot was too small-scale and short-term to assess the long-term economic impacts.

acts.speaker: Namibian gender ministry
acts.speech: Late last year announced the conversion of the Food Bank Programme and Marginalised Communities Special Feeding initiative into a monthly household cash payout of N$600 ; according to the ministry, 8 238 households currently receive the BIG payout nationwide.

acts.speaker: Data collected in 2023
acts.speech: Revealed that approximately 12 699 additional households qualify for registration.

title: Israel ameaça destruir Gaza se Hamas não aceitar condições para cessar-fogo - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli Defence Minister
acts.speech: Says that the city of Gaza may be destroyed if Hamas does not accept the conditions imposed by Israel to bring an end to the war.

acts.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
acts.speech: Announced that he will give final approval for the occupation of Gaza City and, at the same time, begin negotiations with Hamas to return the hostages and end the war.

acts.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (data)
acts.speech: Since 8 August, more than 50 residential structures have been attacked in the enclave's capital, causing the death of 87 Palestinians.

title: La Turquie réaffirme son soutien à la position algérienne sur le Sahel - amap

acts.speaker: Hakan Fidan, Turkish Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Reaffirmed Ankara’s support for Algiers’ position on the Sahel, stressing the importance of Algerian-Turkish cooperation in fighting terrorism and extremism: “Regarding the Sahel region, we consider that in order to resolve the problem of terrorism and extremism, we will continue to work together. We support the Algerian position, which perceives the resolution of regional issues with clarity and discernment.” ; Welcomed Algeria’s role on the UN Security Council, where it “successfully makes the concerns of our region heard.”

acts.speaker: Hakan Fidan, Turkish Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: On Gaza, insisted on the need to “intensify consultations” in order to deliver humanitarian aid and establish an immediate ceasefire.

acts.speaker: Ahmed Attaf, Algerian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Described the Algerian-Turkish partnership as “strategic”, highlighting the desire of the two countries to strengthen their cooperation: “The decision of our two Presidents to found this commission as an institutional space makes it possible to address common priorities and to remove the obstacles to their realisation.”

title: Violência sexual usada como meio de punição aos civis no Sudão - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: The United Nations denounces collective sexual violations in Sudan, following the civil war in the country.

acts.speaker: United Nations report / UN fact-finding mission (report)
acts.speech: A report by the Organization says that the violence has been used as a means of terrorising and punishing civilians ; the mission concluded that the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces committed large-scale violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, many of which may constitute war crimes and/or crimes against humanity.

acts.speaker: Mohamed Chande Othman, President of a United Nations fact-finding mission
acts.speech: Revealed on Tuesday that the escalation of sexual violence committed in Sudan is staggering, in a context in which the country has been at war since April 2023 between the Sudanese army (SAF), under the command of the country's de facto ruler Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), led by his former vice-president Mohamed Hamdan Daglo ; accuses the paramilitaries in particular of committing such acts.
