title: China warns Philippines over Taiwan remarks amid rising tensions - Daily News

acts.speaker: Ferdinand Marcos Jr, Philippine President
acts.speech: Suggested his country would be drawn into a potential conflict between China and the United States over Taiwan; during a state visit to India, said the Philippines' geographic proximity and the large Filipino community in Taiwan meant the country would be forced to get involved in the event of war ; "If there is an all-out war, then we will be drawn into it. There are many, many Filipino nationals in Taiwan and that would be immediately a humanitarian problem."

acts.speaker: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
acts.speech: Issued a strongly worded statement on Friday, warning Manila not to "play with fire" and urging it to uphold the one China principle ; "Geographical proximity and large overseas populations are not excuses for interfering in others' internal affairs." ; dismissed Marcos's justification as undermining both international law and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations charter, saying his comments risk destabilising regional peace and harming the interests of the Philippine people.

acts.speaker: Philippine officials
acts.speech: Earlier this week condemned the launch of a Chinese rocket, which they said dropped suspected debris near a western province, alarming residents and threatening local ships and aircraft.

acts.speaker: Washington (United States government)
acts.speech: Has reaffirmed its commitment to defend Filipino forces, including coastguard personnel, aircraft and public vessels, should they come under attack anywhere in the South China Sea.

title: RDC : L’ONU et le PAM alertent sur une catastrophe humanitaire à Goma - Mali 24

acts.speaker: United Nations and World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: According to the United Nations and the World Food Programme, the humanitarian situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo is reaching a critical level; in Goma, a strategic city for humanitarian aid, basic services are paralysed, threatening millions of people displaced by the conflict.

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: Is also worried about the situation in South Kivu, where the M23 is advancing rapidly toward the city of Bukavu, further aggravating the crisis. Faced with this dramatic situation, the UN is calling for urgent intervention to secure the delivery of humanitarian aid and protect civilian populations.

acts.speaker: Shelley Thakral, spokesperson for the World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: Warns of critical shortages and describes a dramatic situation: "People cruelly lack food, drinking water, medical supplies and that is very worrying. The supply chain is no longer assured at the moment, because everything is closed, whether road access or air access. Our first priority is of course the safety of staff. We will resume our activities as soon as security allows us to."

title: No elephants poached in Niassa Reserve since 2018

acts.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
acts.speech: Declared on Thursday that no elephants have been poached since 2018 in the Niassa Special Reserve, the largest conservation area in the country: “The investments and the legal reforms we have been undertaking in the conservation areas have brought a new dynamic and important gains for the Reserve” ; said poaching had been reduced through the recruitment of more rangers, who now used boats and aircraft as well as conventional means of land transport.

acts.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
acts.speech: Thanked the defence and security forces for their cooperation with the Niassa rangers, and added that the increase in the number of partners and “the healthy coexistence between the various operators, alongside the government and the communities” had also contributed to a healthy environment for the development of the Reserve.

acts.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
acts.speech: “The Mozambican state will continue to do its part by investing in a programme of monitoring, through placing collars and satellite tracking of the iconic animals of the Reserve… ensuring their continued protection and the integrity of their habitats” ; “This is a re-affirmation of our commitment to the conservation of biodiversity, and of emblematic species in particular… This is an activity we promise to follow and to honour, in defence of our entire planet, our collective home.”

acts.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID director in Mozambique
acts.speech: Said that American support had played a determinant role in the fight against poaching: “Support from the US Government’s Aerial Vigilance Programme has allowed monitoring, and also the deployment of patrols… This has led to a reduction in the cases of illegal mining and logging in the reserve, as well as cutting to zero the poaching of elephants since 2018.”

acts.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID director in Mozambique
acts.speech: Stressed that the preservation of biodiversity is a necessity in a world facing the threats of climate change and environmental degradation.

title: Pendant le ramadan en pleine chaleur : Quel sort l’Energie du Mali réserve-t-elle aux citoyens ?

acts.speaker: Minister of Energy of Mali
acts.speech: Speaking to the press last week, assured that a plan is in place to minimise cuts in the coming days; without going into details, he promises significant efforts to ensure a better service.

acts.speaker: Director General of Energie du Mali (EDM-SA)
acts.speech: Also gave reassurance that all arrangements have been made to ensure the success of Mali's load-shedding programme, called “Plan Unique”, which provides for coverage of 80% of Malians' energy needs per day, that is, 19 hours of electricity per day out of 24.

title: AVCA Conference Strategises On How To Power Next 20 Years Of Africa’s Growth

acts.speaker: Abi Mustapha-Maduakor, Chief Executive Officer, AVCA
acts.speech: introduced the flagship forum by noting that despite a challenging macroeconomic environment in recent years, "Africa's private capital industry has remained resilient and will continue to rise." She reflected on AVCA's theme for the conference - "embracing change and shaping the next era of Africa's prosperity."

acts.speaker: Phuthuma Nhleko, Chairman and Co-Founder, Phembani Group
acts.speech: followed with an instructive keynote address rallying private investors to back innovative businesses to drive prosperity at scale. Reaffirming the region's competitive edge, he highlighted the imperative for policymakers, business leaders and investors to harness the fourth industrial revolution, powered by artificial intelligence (AI) and the digital economy ; argued: "the size of population generates 50 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP). By 2050, we will have 2.5 billion Africans that constitute over a quarter of humanity, with over forty per cent of youth below the age of 18. By this time, Nigeria's population is expected to be bigger than the US."

acts.speaker: 'Tokunboh Ishmael, Co-founder and Managing Director, Alitheia Capital
acts.speech: described the exponential growth witnessed throughout the second decade of private capital expansion in Africa.

acts.speaker: Wale Adeosun, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Kuramo Capital Management
acts.speech: aligned that Africa's private capital industry remains a nascent ecosystem with immense potential ; commented on the benefits of bringing institutional investors from the U.S into Africa.

acts.speaker: Vincent Le Guennou, Chief Executive Officer, Africa50's Infrastructure Acceleration Fund
acts.speech: proposed that the traditional private equity model replicated in the continent needs to be adapted and advocated for proactive efforts to attract the US$ 2.3 trillion of domestic capital in Africa that needs to be unlocked. He said: "This needs to be a key objective for the next 10 years."

acts.speaker: Dieynaba Kamara, Partner and Chief Operating Officer, Joliba Capital
acts.speech: expressed that most pension funds needed "education on investing in private equity as an asset class", especially in Francophone Africa where pension funds prioritise hard assets such as real estate.

acts.speaker: Jerry Parkes, Chief Executive Officer, Injaro Investments
acts.speech: re-emphasised the need to tap local pools of capital, drawing on Injaro's launch of Ghana's first private equity fund, anchored by Ghanaian pension funds.

acts.speaker: Laurent Demey, Managing Partner, Amethis
acts.speech: suggested that historically, "The big difference between liquidity in Africa and Europe or the US, has been that if you have a good business, you can sell it. In Africa, it has been a different story" ; he noted a shift in the industry with far more African companies and investors from emerging markets, such as the Gulf states or Turkey, making deals compared to traditional investors from the Global North.

acts.speaker: Patrice Backer, Partner and Chief Investment Officer, AFIG Funds
acts.speech: discussed the secondary market as a viable solution to liquidity constraints in African markets - attracting private finance yet to invest on the continent.

acts.speaker: John Owers, Director and Head of Funds Solutions, British International Investment
acts.speech: "A functioning private capital ecosystem needs to provide options for exits for Limited Partners (LPs), and that is what the secondary market does."

acts.speaker: African Private Capital Association (AVCA)
acts.speech: announced the winners of the association's 20th Anniversary Conference Awards, celebrating the outstanding firms and individuals championing private capital in Africa.

title: SEM Retieb Kamel, le nouvel Ambassadeur de l’Algérie au Mali : ‘’La coopération militaire et dans le domaine du renseignement, n’a pas été occultée de cet effort, l’Algérie ayant apporté au Mali… ‘’

acts.speaker: H.E. Retieb Kamel, new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
acts.speech: Delivered a speech paying vibrant tribute to the martyrs of the 1 November 1954 Revolution and taking stock of the cooperation between his country and Mali. He explained that in triggering this glorious Revolution the National Liberation Front (FLN) was not placing its struggle solely in the quest for national independence against the French colonial regime, but wanted above all to be a symbol of defiance and self-determination for oppressed nations throughout the world; that the Revolution subsequently inspired numerous revolutionary movements across Africa, Asia and Latin America; that "the Algerian Revolution was not only crucial for its own people, but also served as a model for anti-colonial movements the world over", and that Algeria's success encouraged other nations, from Angola to South Africa, to challenge the colonial powers and assert their sovereignty.

acts.speaker: H.E. Retieb Kamel, new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
acts.speech: Said that in the field of bilateral cooperation his country continues to affirm its leadership role in North Africa by actively engaging in regional diplomacy and the promotion of peace and stability; that Algeria, under the presidency of Abdelmadjid Tebboune, continues to favour constructive diplomacy and promotes solidarity within the Arab, African and Mediterranean communities; and that as a key member of the African Union and of the Non-Aligned Movement, Algeria remains a fervent defender of the right of nations to govern themselves without outside interference.

acts.speaker: H.E. Retieb Kamel, new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
acts.speech: On Mali, he said that, grateful for the active solidarity Algeria received from its partners during the years of struggle for independence, foremost among them Mali, independent Algeria has striven to develop good-neighbourly relations with all the countries with which it shares borders. Besides the annual offer of scholarships, of which 270 for Mali for the 2024-2025 academic year, making it the leading beneficiary of Algerian government scholarships worldwide, Algeria has always been present in difficult times and in situations of natural disaster, providing support and diversified humanitarian aid: "Military and intelligence cooperation has not been left out of this effort, Algeria having provided Mali with multifaceted technical support; transfers of various military materials and equipment; and military training at all levels, in the various institutes, specialised higher schools, the Staff College and the Cherchell school." He added that Algeria, favouring the mixing of populations with African countries, has agreed with seven of them, including Mali, not to place barriers on the free movement of persons and not to impose a visa requirement.

title: Relocated people from flood-prone area in Nsanjes appeal for an irrigation scheme

acts.speaker: Group Village Head (GVH) Kalonga, Milton Village, TA Mbenje, Nsanje District
acts.speech: Appealed to government to construct an irrigation scheme so that the relocated people can be food secure, asking for this life-changing facility on behalf of her subjects ; said despite their settling at the upper land, her subjects have been hit hard by hunger following last year’s dry spell: “We have farmland at Makhanga but it is in water due to rising levels of water in Shire River.” ; added that once the scheme is constructed, families will be able to grow crops more than once a year, contributing to food security at household level.

acts.speaker: Group Village Head (GVH) Kalonga
acts.speech: Assured the delegation that the community will never go back to Makhanga after going through devastating floods every year, and praised a non-governmental organisation called Give Direct for supporting the community with startup cash which the community used to build houses at the new settlement area.

acts.speaker: Olympia Wereko-Brobby, British Deputy High Commissioner in Malawi
acts.speech: Commended the community for using the donation wisely: “I am impressed the way the community build its resilient following the effects of Cyclone Freddy.”

acts.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Commissioner for Disaster (DoDMA)
acts.speech: Said the government was putting in place sustainable systems to ensure food security in the country: “Such systems include irrigation schemes just like what we have seen at Chimwala mbango scheme which is gravity fed”, while assuring the community that the government will continue supporting them with systems that will enhance food security in Nsanje.

title: Dissolution de l’Usaid: Déclic pour des systèmes de financement innovants

acts.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
acts.speech: According to OECD data, sub-Saharan Africa absorbed nearly 40% of USAID's annual budget.

acts.speaker: The White House
acts.speech: According to the White House, USAID's missions will from now on be integrated directly into a Directorate-General for Cooperation and Development attached to the US State Department; officially the aim is to streamline the structure, limit administrative duplication and strengthen the alignment between development aid and the diplomatic priorities of the United States.

acts.speaker: World Bank
acts.speech: recalls that the agency was among the top five bilateral donors for the Sustainable Development Goals relating to health, education and gender equality.

acts.speaker: Government Accountability Office (GAO) report
acts.speech: underlines that USAID managed more than 1,300 projects in 80 overseas missions, sometimes with duplication between federal agencies.

acts.speaker: US administration
acts.speech: presents the dissolution as a measure of sound management of public funds and defends a refocusing on major diplomatic priorities, in a context of increased rivalry with China over investments in Africa and Asia.

acts.speaker: Several US officials
acts.speech: find that USAID's strength lay precisely in its operational autonomy and its technical expertise; according to them, the technical expertise accumulated over decades by USAID's teams could be diluted, or even lost, within a broader diplomatic apparatus in which aid risks becoming a mere instrument of geopolitical influence.

acts.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa
acts.speech: "Aid can no longer be regarded as a reliable or sustainable solution. Time is short. We must act now, with you, our heads of state, who are leading reforms, creating an enabling environment and mobilising domestic resources. Together, we can fulfil the promise of Agenda 2063 and the SDGs," he stated recently at the eleventh session of the Africa Regional Forum on Sustainable Development held in Kampala, Uganda.

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, statistician-economist, specialist in economic policy management
acts.speech: "Efforts must be made to diversify sources of financing by turning to regional and international financial markets and to innovative financing. The most predictable and most sustainable resources are domestic public resources."

title: Mozambique: $10M Compact Development Funding (CDF) Agreement signed with Millenium Challenge Corporation - AIM report

acts.speaker: Mozambican Ministry of Economy and Finance (press release)
acts.speech: said that, with the signature of the revised CDF agreement, 10.75 million dollars will be allocated to the preparation of Compact II, which is expected to benefit the entire country, but with a geographical emphasis on the central province of Zambezia.

acts.speaker: Max Tonela, Mozambican Minister of Economy and Finance
acts.speech: said his signature represents an important commitment leading towards the qualitative design of Compact II, and that the compact will contain projects in areas such as the promotion of investments in commercial agriculture; rural connectivity and transport; and the integrated management of climate and coastal development ; “I would like to reiterate the commitment of the Mozambican government to strengthen the capacity of our institutions to implement solid economic policies and fiscal reforms, which will improve the cornerstones of the social and economic development of Mozambique.”

acts.speaker: Fatema Z. Sumar, MCC Deputy President for Compact Operations
acts.speech: “We are pleased to take the next step in our partnership with the Mozambican government” ; “The signing of the Revised Agreement on the Compact Development Fund will continue to mark progress towards a successful MCC Mozambique Compact” ; “With the funding that will be made available, the MCC and the Mozambican government will work to identify investment projects to reduce poverty and to speed up inclusive and sustainable economic growth.”

title: South Africa Doesn't Receive Funding From US Except For HIV/AIDS Programme — President Ramaphosa Replies To Donald Trump’s Threat

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Vowed to cut off all future funding to South Africa, citing concerns over "land expropriation and alleged discriminatory treatment" of some residents, particularly foreigners in the country; in a post shared on his Truth Social on Sunday he condemned the situation, stating that the country is "confiscating land, and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY", and accused the "Radical Left Media" of ignoring the issue, which he described as a "massive Human Rights VIOLATION": "South Africa is confiscating land, and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY. It is a bad situation that the Radical Left Media doesn't want to so much as mention. A massive Human Rights VIOLATION, at a minimum, is happening for all to see. The United States won't stand for it, we will act. Also, I will be cutting off all future funding to South Africa until a full investigation of this situation has been completed."

acts.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
acts.speech: In a statement issued on Monday morning, said his country is a constitutional democracy rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality; clarified that his government has not confiscated any land as claimed by Donald Trump; said the recently adopted Expropriation Act is a constitutionally mandated process aimed at ensuring public access to land in an equitable and just manner; noted that expropriation laws are not unique to South Africa; and expressed willingness to engage with the Trump administration: "South Africa is a constitutional democracy that is deeply rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality. The South African government has not confiscated any land. The recently adopted Expropriation Act is not a confiscation instrument, but a constitutionally mandated legal process that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner as guided by the constitution. South Africa, like the United States of America and other countries, has always had expropriation laws that balance the need for public usage of land and the protection of rights of property owners. We look forward to engaging with the Trump administration over our land reform policy and issues of bilateral interest. We are certain that out of those engagements, we will share a better and common understanding over these matters. The US remains a key strategic political and trade partner for South Africa. With the exception of PEPFAR Aid, which constitutes 17% of South Africa's HIV/Aids programme, there is no other funding that is received by South Africa from the United States."

title: Huge U.S military exercise comes to Botswana

acts.speaker: Van Vranken, US Ambassador to Botswana
acts.speech: Said in his opening remarks at the US Africa Command (AFRICOM) African Chiefs of Defense Conference 2024 in Gaborone that Botswana is "a steadfast partner of the United States."

acts.speaker: Van Vranken, US Ambassador to Botswana
acts.speech: Announced to the Conference that Botswana will soon host AFRICOM's flagship military exercise, Southern Accord 2024.

acts.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, head of Niger's ruling Conseil National pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP)
acts.speech: Has given the US up to September 15th, 2024 to have completed withdrawal of troops.

acts.speaker: Niger and Chad (governments)
acts.speech: Have already called for withdrawal of US troops.

title: Le Royaume de Belgique fait don des médicaments et consommables médicaux à trois structures sanitaires de la région de Tahoua - Agence Nigérienne de Presse

acts.speaker: Abou Hamed Saley, Representative of the international NGO Médecins du Monde (MDM)
acts.speech: In handing over the donation to the Governor of the Tahoua Region, recalled that for more than 10 years MDM Belgium in Niger has worked alongside communities to guarantee equitable access to care, notably for the most vulnerable people—women, children, unaccompanied minors and populations on the move ; stressed that this donation aligns with the priorities of the Government of Niger in matters of public health, with a view to contributing to the protection of populations and the reduction of morbidity and mortality ; took the opportunity to thank the authorities of Tahoua and all the actors present who work tirelessly to improve access to health care for target groups, and reaffirmed his institution's commitment to supporting Niger in strengthening its health system through permanent and quality support for the benefit of the population.

acts.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of the Tahoua Region
acts.speech: In receiving the donation, expressed his deep gratitude to the generous donor; on behalf of the highest Nigerien authorities, conveyed his encouragement and congratulations to the NGO Médecins du Monde for this support, so important for health facilities, which comes at a time when the CNSP military authorities have lowered the fees for patient care services and in a context of refoundation ; gave assurances that this donation will go directly to the beneficiaries.

title: DoDMA to continue with maize distribution to vulnerable households - Usi - Malawi24

acts.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
acts.speech: Says the government, through the Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA), will continue with the Lean Season Food Insecurity Response programme to provide relief food to households that are affected by natural disasters such as drought and cyclones.

acts.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
acts.speech: Asked those who are charged with the responsibility to register beneficiaries to be honest when identifying and registering recipients of humanitarian assistance.

acts.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
acts.speech: Appealed to communities to stop cutting down trees carelessly, saying this contributes to climate change, whose effects are so devastating.

acts.speaker: Charles Kalemba, DoDMA Commissioner
acts.speech: Said hunger will remain, and the department will continue with Lean Season Food Insecurity Response programmes to cushion people.

acts.speaker: Reinhard Chavula, District Commissioner for Zomba
acts.speech: Hailed the government through DoDMA for responding to the situation in the district ; disclosed that 1,760 households were affected by drought while 788 households were affected by the recent Cyclone Chido in Zomba.

acts.speaker: David Mwanyali, recipient of relief food
acts.speech: Commended the government for responding to the plight of hunger-affected households.

title: Washington suspend son aide à Prétoria contre le VIH/Sida

acts.speaker: US Agency for International Development (USAID), correspondence seen by APA
acts.speech: Justified the termination of the grants by “reasons of convenience” and “the interest of the American government”, in accordance with a directive of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, acting administrator of USAID ; ordered the beneficiaries to immediately halt all activities linked to the funding and to inform their partners and subcontractors ; also ordered other USAID-supported health programmes, although not directly linked to HIV, to cease their activities.

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and acting administrator of USAID (directive)
acts.speech: Issued the directive in accordance with which the South African PEPFAR grants were terminated.

title: As South Sudan's allies shut embassies, activist faults leaders' failure to deliver peace - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Edmund Yakani, Executive Director of Community Empowerment for Progress Organization (CEPO)
acts.speech: Said the closure of embassies and consulates by South Sudan's traditional allies reflects their disappointment with lack of commitment from the country's political leaders to deliver lasting peace; in a statement shared with Eye Radio said the trend of closure of diplomatic missions in South Sudan is an expression of great disappointment, and stated that the main concern the foreign nations may not have expressed is the sluggish efforts by South Sudanese leaders in transitioning the country from chronic violence to peace. "I take this opportunity to amplify my voice loudly to the attention of the leaders in South Sudan on a new trend that we have seen." ; "Our traditional friends from other parts of the world are now deciding to close down their embassies under the pretext that they are closing their embassies because they want to cut down their foreign spending." ; "I'm quite sure the message of where the traditional friends of South Sudan are closing their diplomatic mission in South Sudan is an expression of great disappointment. Why the great disappointment? Because as a country, we have seen dragging of feet in transitioning the country from violence to peace without any clear commitment and a will from our leaders." ; Suggested a need for South Sudan to have a change of strategy and approach with regard to the political transitional process: "Dragging feet to transition the country from violence to peace, may lead us to a situation of isolation by our traditional friends."

acts.speaker: Edmund Yakani, Executive Director of CEPO
acts.speech: "On a separate note, I would like to alert every South Sudanese. Whoever you are with whatever power you hold, please abstain from weaponizing information to meet your own political objective." ; "Weaponizing information with loaded hate speech, hostile propaganda, fake news, disinformation, with misinformation, is a crime. And we have seen a trend where some South Sudanese are start weaponizing information."

acts.speaker: Cabinet of the Kingdom of the Netherlands
acts.speech: Approved on April 17 a proposal by the country's foreign minister to close embassies in South Sudan and other parts of the world, reportedly as part of a broader budget reduction policy and to reshape its global diplomatic presence.

acts.speaker: German Federal Foreign Office
acts.speech: Decided to let its diplomatic mission in South Sudan temporarily operate from Berlin, although it added that the mission may resume operations in Juba as soon as conditions permit.

acts.speaker: Michael J. Adler, United States Ambassador to South Sudan
acts.speech: Said on April 29 that the Embassy in Juba remains operational although the staff number has been severely reduced.

acts.speaker: Media reports (April 15)
acts.speech: Reported that Washington was weighing closing nearly 30 overseas embassies and consulates including in South Sudan, as it eyes significant changes to its diplomatic presence abroad.

acts.speaker: Jok Madut Jok, renowned South Sudanese academic
acts.speech: Said should Washington proceed with the plan, it would be bad news for South Sudanese and undermine America's ability to monitor and address negative developments in the country.

title: Somalia’s federalism is at a vital crossroads - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: Abdirashid Fidow, Deputy Chief Executive of the Anti-Tribalism Movement, political analyst and social justice campaigner (opinion piece)
acts.speech: writes that more than a decade after Somalia adopted federalism as a post-conflict solution, the system remains at odds with the realities on the ground, and that unless urgently reformed or replaced, Somalia’s federal experiment may deepen the very fragmentation it sought to prevent; argues that Somalia’s federalism is largely clan-based and has reinforced exclusionary politics, that without a finalised federal constitution federalism remains based on conflicting interpretations, that Al-Shabaab has stepped into the cracks of fragmented authority, and that federalism has become a stage for foreign ambitions: “Unless federalism is reimagined through a Somali-led, inclusive, and sovereign framework, the very idea of a unified Somalia risks fading into history.”

title: UNICEF pledges collaboration with Tanzania to protect children - Daily News

acts.speaker: UNICEF
acts.speech: Has reaffirmed its commitment to collaborating with Tanzania to uphold the universal right of every child to protection, enabling them to grow free from violence.

acts.speaker: Ms. Sheema Sen Gupta, UNICEF Global Director for Child Protection
acts.speech: "No matter the circumstances, every child has the right to be protected from violence. Child protection systems connect children to vital social services and fair justice systems-starting at birth" ; "Together with our partners, we are dedicated to enhancing child protection systems in Tanzania, ensuring that every child grows up free from violence and has the support they need to thrive."

acts.speaker: Ms. Sheema Sen Gupta, UNICEF Global Director for Child Protection
acts.speech: Noted that despite significant progress in Tanzania, societal norms still endorse practices such as child marriage and corporal punishment in schools, and that a large number of children lack birth registration, making them vulnerable to violence and abuse; praised Tanzania for simplifying birth registration services, which have significantly increased registration rates for children under five, from 12 per cent in 2013 to 68 per cent in 2023; highlighted that the child protection sector is often overlooked and underfunded, leading to persistent challenges: "Rates of violence and abuse remain alarmingly high across the world" ; said that with the support of partners funding UNICEF's Global Child Protection Thematic Fund, UNICEF has been continuously assisting the government of Tanzania in strengthening child protection systems.

title: Eight dead as flood wreaks havoc in Ebonyi community - Official

acts.speaker: Timothy Nwachi, Chairperson of Afikpo Local Government Area, Ebonyi State
acts.speech: Confirmed the incident to reporters, according to a statement on Sunday by Sunday Nkama, a media aide; consoled the families of the deceased and assured them that the local government council will do everything to prevent a recurrence; urged the people still residing in flood-prone areas to relocate to safer ground: "We are deeply sad over the unfortunate incident, and we are using this medium to extend our condolences to the families who lost their loved ones." ; "As a government, we will support them and pledge to collaborate with relevant state and federal agencies to provide humanitarian assistance and timely relief to those affected"

acts.speaker: Francis Okpani, Councillor representing Itim Ward in the Afikpo Legislative Council
acts.speech: Said out of the eight people who lost their lives, three bodies have been recovered, while five were still missing, and that three of the victims who died in the flood were children; recalled that the Federal Ministry of Environment had predicted that Afikpo was one of the areas in Nigeria likely to experience flooding: "I had earlier implored the people of Afikpo to incorporate climate change projections into flood-risk management plans" ; also urged residents of the area to ensure that they have effective drainage systems and keep their drains and waterways free from debris to prevent blockages.

acts.speaker: Federal Ministry of Environment
acts.speech: Had predicted that Afikpo was one of the areas in Nigeria likely to experience flooding.

acts.speaker: Ebonyi State Government
acts.speech: Has warned residents that massive flooding continues to destroy farmlands in several local government areas.

acts.speaker: Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET), 2025 seasonal climate prediction
acts.speech: Listed Ebonyi as a high-risk flood zone.

acts.speaker: Felix Ezeaka, a resident whose farmland was submerged in Abakaliki
acts.speech: Appealed to the Ebonyi State Government for support: "We are begging the state government to do something about it. If we plant rice, the same thing, the flood will cover it. If we plant cassava, the flood will cover it. We don't have anything to do about it"

acts.speaker: Victor Chukwu, Ebonyi State Commissioner for Environment
acts.speech: Blamed the current situation in the capital city of Abakaliki partly on an incomplete drainage project by the Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP), and said the halted project has worsened the impact of rainfall in the capital city: "The second phase of the NEWMAP is called EIB NEMAP. So, we have designed the sites because the issue is that the water that is supposed to discharge to the river flows back to the city because the river appears to be higher than the slope of the discharge of water that is collected in the city. So, we have designed the sites. The state has also paid the counterpart fund. Our government has graciously approved the payment of the counterpart fund for the EIB NEWMAP" ; said the state government was now conducting public awareness campaigns and holding town hall meetings to guide residents on flood prevention steps, and that people living in low-lying, flood-prone zones are advised to relocate to safer locations as the rains continue.

title: UA pede reforma financeira mundial para libertar potencial de África - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
acts.speech: Called for urgent reforms of the global financial system to unlock Africa's full potential, saying that with the reforms it is possible to build a financial architecture that benefits everyone: "Let us align capital with our development priorities and build a 21st-century financial architecture that benefits everyone," he stated in a speech at the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4) in Seville.

acts.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission (per an African Union statement)
acts.speech: Stressed that business and private finance "are not simply complementary, but catalysts of inclusive growth, job creation and the green transition."

acts.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
acts.speech: Noted that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which aims to create the world's largest single market for goods and services, represents a "radical change" for the continent, and argued for greater support for foreign direct investment; concluded: "Africa is young, resource-rich and ready."

title: SORTIE DE L’ANCIEN PRESIDENT CONGOLAIS SUR LA CRISE SECURITAIRE DANS L’EST DE LA RDC : Joseph Kabila tombe-t-il le masque ? - Editions Le Pays

acts.speaker: Joseph Kabila, former President of the Democratic Republic of Congo
acts.speech: Broke his silence on 23 February, from outside the country, to give his reading of the security crisis in eastern DRC, saying the solution to the conflict is not a military one; said the roots of the crisis are at once "political, social and institutional" and originate in the rupture of the political process in 2021, when his clan was excluded from power by the current head of state.

acts.speaker: Joseph Kabila, former President of the Democratic Republic of Congo
acts.speech: Accused Félix Tshisekedi of having established a "tyrannical" regime, characterised by "intimidation, arbitrary arrests, summary and extrajudicial executions, repression of the opposition, censorship of the media, as well as the forced exile of numerous opponents, journalists and opinion leaders, including religious leaders"; accuses his successor of being at the origin of all the DRC's misfortunes.

acts.speaker: Félix Tshisekedi, President of the Democratic Republic of Congo
acts.speech: On 13 February did not mince his words in accusing his predecessor, Joseph Kabila, of being behind the armed opposition to his regime.

acts.speaker: Corneille Nangaa, former president of the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) and head of the Congo River Alliance (AFC)
acts.speech: According to him, President Félix Tshisekedi made a deal with Joseph Kabila in order to accede to power under the conditions that are known.

title: Mozambique: The killing floods

acts.speaker: Stela Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique (press conference)
acts.speech: Told a press conference that the bodies of a teenager and a woman were found floating in the Buzi river following flooding in the region; said the 16-year-old girl lived in the district of Buzi, in the central province of Sofala, but the woman's origin and age are not known.

acts.speaker: Stela Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique
acts.speech: Says the floods that have hit the province since Wednesday (12.02) have already caused the removal of 70,070 people - 15,755 families - to accommodation centres or family homes located in safe areas; "We want to salute the solidarity of the many individuals who are hosting family members and others. Less than 50% of those affected are staying in accommodation centres"; added that thirty camps were created to accommodate the victims of the floods.

acts.speaker: Stela Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for Sofala province, Mozambique
acts.speech: "We expected to provide assistance to approximately 150,000 people, and in this case we have only 71,000 people affected, which is still within our contingency plan"; said there was capacity to provide humanitarian assistance to all victims of floods.

acts.speaker: Local authorities in Sofala province
acts.speech: Consider the affected area to be as large as 8,000 hectares.

acts.speaker: National Institute for Disaster Management (INGC) of Mozambique
acts.speech: According to the INGC, the current rainy season in Mozambique, from October to April, has already killed 54 people and affected around 65,000, many of whose homes were flooded.

title: In Africa, meager expectations and some hopes for a second Trump presidency - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
acts.speech: In the wake of Trump's win, said his country “stands ready” to deepen its ties with Washington.

acts.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
acts.speech: spoke of a second Trump administration ushering in an era of “earnest, beneficial, and reciprocal” cooperation.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
acts.speech: once described African countries as “shithole countries.”

acts.speaker: Charles Ray, chair of the Foreign Policy Research Institute’s Africa Program
acts.speech: said U.S. foreign policy has not made Africa a priority for a long while — beyond seeing the continent through the lens of countering rivals such as Russia and China. Africa “will be at the very bottom of (Trump's) list of priorities” and any U.S. action on the continent would likely be driven by his “transactional, ego-driven leadership style,” Ray added.

acts.speaker: Charles Ray, chair of the Foreign Policy Research Institute’s Africa Program
acts.speech: said countries that undermine U.S. interests under trade programs “will be treated as pariahs.”

acts.speaker: Murithi Mutiga, program director for Africa at the Crisis Group
acts.speech: says the president-elect is “a committed isolationist and clearly wants to pull back” on various fronts across the world.

acts.speaker: Murithi Mutiga, program director for Africa at the Crisis Group
acts.speech: says “the problem historically has been that the U.S. and the West viewed Africa as a problem” to be solved. China and others “saw it as an opportunity to be grasped.” ; “The question is often, what will Washington do, but, really, what is Africa’s interest?” ; “We’re in an age of transactional global relations and unless Africa can engage in a way that articulates its own interests, America’s (interests in Africa) will continue to be determined by geopolitical competition with its rivals,” he said.

acts.speaker: J. Peter Pham, Trump's former special envoy to Africa's Great Lakes and Sahel regions
acts.speech: says the next Trump presidency may look for a “win-win” situation in Africa. That could include a renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which grants eligible African countries duty-free access to U.S. markets, Pham said during a Voice of America broadcast. ; However, U.S. lawmakers have been asking questions about whether African countries are complying with conditions under the program — or if they are undermining U.S. foreign policy interests and national security, Pham said. ; Basically, you don't “kick America in the teeth” in ways that raise questions about compliance with such deals, Pham said.

acts.speaker: Reuben Brigety, U.S. Ambassador [to South Africa]
acts.speech: accused South Africa in 2023 of providing weapons and ammunition to Russia for its war in Ukraine and brought its professed neutral stance on the war into question.

acts.speaker: Valentine Damitoni, a mother at 18 who visits a U.S.-funded clinic in Harare, Zimbabwe
acts.speech: “The situation is already bad for girls (and) it will turn into a disaster without these services,” she said.

acts.speaker: Max Primorac, former acting deputy administrator of USAID (in Project 2025, Heritage Foundation blueprint)
acts.speech: criticized some of the agency's programs in Project 2025, a 900-page blueprint proposed by the conservative-leaning Heritage Foundation to reshape the federal government. In particular, Primorac criticized USAID programs that “promote abortion, climate extremism and interventions against perceived systematic racism.”

acts.speaker: Kiron Skinner, head of policy planning at the U.S. State Department during Trump’s first term (in Project 2025 document)
acts.speech: recommends in the document that in Africa, America should “focus on core security, economic, and human rights” rather than impose “radical abortion and pro-LGBT initiatives.”

acts.speaker: Biden administration
acts.speech: announced last December that it had invested at least $22 billion in Africa and promised to do more.

acts.speaker: Isah Mohammed, a fruit seller in Nigeria's capital, Abuja
acts.speech: “Trump ... is not going to save us from hunger caused by our government,” he said.

acts.speaker: Assabah newspaper (Morocco), editorial
acts.speech: “The return of the friend of Morocco to the White House,” proclaimed the country's Assabah newspaper in its editorial.

acts.speaker: Rashid Abdi, analyst at the Nairobi-based Sahan Research think tank
acts.speech: predicts Trump will likely cut funding to Somalia and engage more with Somaliland.

acts.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
acts.speech: had said the African Union’s admission to the G20 as a permanent member was “a long time in coming.”

title: Le Soudan en flammes : deux ans de guerre qui ont détruit le pays

acts.speaker: United Nations (UN)
acts.speech: According to the UN, more than 60% of Sudanese now live below the poverty line, and no clear plan for economic recovery exists as long as the war persists.

acts.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
acts.speech: Have repeatedly warned that, without immediate intervention, Sudan could experience one of the worst health crises of the 21st century.

acts.speaker: World Food Programme
acts.speech: Warned that Sudan is on the brink of famine and that millions of people risk dying of hunger in the coming months.

acts.speaker: Many experts
acts.speech: Agree that to stop the war it is necessary to have: a lasting ceasefire through international mediation (UN, African Union, Arab League); direct dialogue between the Sudanese authorities and the RSF, possibly with civil society; strong international pressure, with sanctions against parties violating truces and an arms embargo; a fight against foreign interference, limiting the role of mercenaries and halting outside support (weapons, financing); the opening of humanitarian corridors and delivery of food and medicine, as well as increased support for refugees (more than 8 million displaced); and an inclusive political settlement, with the restoration of a civilian government and negotiations involving all regions (Darfur, South Kordofan, etc.).

title: Région d’Ali-Sabieh : Lancement du projet d’appui à l’engagement de la société civile dans le processus du développement local à Daasbiyo

acts.speaker: Hamid Khaireh Darar, President of the Association for the Promotion of Tourism and Social Development of Daasbiyo (APTDSD)
acts.speech: Said that “the information collected from some forty families will help us implement our project to improve access to water in our village.”

acts.speaker: APTDSD survey leaders
acts.speech: Urged the mothers to cooperate with the association’s surveyors by providing only accurate and truthful data, informed them that their answers would remain confidential and that each of their answers is crucial to the success of the survey, and encouraged them to answer honestly with accurate and detailed responses.

title: India's Patrol Vessel Sachet makes port call at Maputo, delivers 20 metric tonnes of HADR Material to Mozambique

acts.speaker: Government of India (statement)
acts.speech: “As part of India's humanitarian outreach, ICGS Sachet is carrying 20 metric tonnes of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) material, including medical stores and medicines, to be handed over to Mozambican authorities,” read a statement issued by the Indian government.

acts.speaker: India in Mozambique (@IndiainMoz), Indian High Commission social media post
acts.speech: “Gifting of medicines and equipment to Mozambique (11 Oct 2025) ... gifted medicines and equipment to [Mozambique], which will augment healthcare capabilities. The first tranche of medicines and equipment, brought by ICGS Sachet, was handed over to the Hon'ble Health Minister in Maputo.”

title: Somalia, IMF open fourth review to assess reform progress - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund
acts.speech: Praised Somalia's reform momentum but warned that the country's economic outlook has weakened, with growth projected to slow to 3 percent in 2025, down from 4 percent the previous year, weighed by foreign aid cuts, climate shocks and global uncertainty; stressed the need to press ahead with customs modernization, the new income tax law and civil service pay and pension reforms to ensure fiscal sustainability.

acts.speaker: Bihi Iman Egeh, Somalia's Finance Minister
acts.speech: Opened the fourth review meeting of the country's Extended Credit Facility program with the IMF in Nairobi on Sunday, speaking as senior officials from the Federal Government of Somalia looked on, with discussions focused on fiscal reforms and economic progress tied to IMF support.

title: Zimbabwe battles aid shortages as drought bites

acts.speaker: Enny Nyashanu, an 83-year-old grandmother and WFP food aid beneficiary in Buhera, Manicaland
acts.speech: “Our region is prone to drought. Aid agencies come to our rescue each year when crops fail. We cannot continue to rely on aid,” says Nyashanu.

acts.speaker: Enny Nyashanu, an 83-year-old grandmother and WFP food aid beneficiary in Buhera, Manicaland
acts.speech: Says climate proofing and construction of dams for small scale farmers could be an immediate solution to wean her community off donor aid. Nyashanu told DW: “Local solutions are now needed more than ever.”

acts.speaker: Tomson Phiri, Regional spokesperson for the WFP
acts.speech: Said the agency would run operations for eastern and southern Africa from Nairobi. “The goal is to stretch every dollar and target maximum resources to our frontline teams,” he told DW, adding the closure would not affect country operations in Southern Africa.

acts.speaker: Tomson Phiri, Regional spokesperson for the WFP
acts.speech: “It is clear the region is going to experience more frequent droughts. There is need to invest more in irrigation infrastructure to allow people to grow food regardless of change in climate.”

acts.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: Says overall, more than 60 percent of the food it procures is used in operations in the same region it was purchased.

acts.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: Warned the “scale of this disruption underscores the far-reaching consequences of the funding pause on global food assistance efforts” and added it was still assessing the impact of vulnerable beneficiaries.

acts.speaker: World Bank assessments
acts.speech: According to World Bank assessments, countries like Zimbabwe are projected to record 6 percent economic growth driven by the anticipated agriculture recovery in 2025.

title: Pfumvudza/Intwasa inputs distribution underway

acts.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
acts.speech: Said in a weekly post-Cabinet briefing that distribution of inputs under the Presidential Pfumvudza/Intwasa programme for the 2024/25 summer cropping season is currently ongoing in all parts of the country and that the move dovetails with the government thrust to increase productivity ; "Meanwhile, distribution of Presidential Inputs including cotton has commenced. Progress with the Silo expansion project is on course at the following depots, Kwekwe, Mutare Grain, Mhangura, Mvurwi, Timbermills, Lupane and Rutenga. On cotton, a total of 427 550 farmers will be supported through contract farming with a target covering an area of 278 750 hectare."

acts.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
acts.speech: Said the government aims to increase production of cereals to 3 274 200 metric tons from 744 271 metric tons in the 2023/24 season ; "The overall production volumes of major crops are expected to increase by 347 percent. The plan is to produce enough to feed the nation and to replenish the Strategic Grain Reserve. The country expects to receive normal to above normal rainfall during this season."

acts.speaker: Dr Anxious Masuka, Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development Minister
acts.speech: Said following rains received recently, planting has started across the country ; "A few areas that have not received sufficient rain to start planting, but this is just isolated patches throughout the country. So this whole sector has mobilised resources, particularly for the Presidential Input programme. 58 percent of the fertilisers are available and of that fertiliser 75 percent has been distributed. 90 percent of the maize seed has been received and of that 80 percent has already been distributed." ; "Similarly, for cotton inputs we have received over 80 percent of those inputs and distribution is ongoing. So countrywide farmers are naturally excited."

acts.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
acts.speech: Said national grain stocks at the Grain Marketing Board (GMB) stand at 253 665 metric tons ; "Cabinet highlights that a total of 1 036 721 metric tonnes, comprising 852 260 metric tonnes of maize, 184 121 metric tonnes of wheat and 340 metric tonnes of wheat flour were imported by the private sector as at 20 November, 2024. To date, 885 import permits have been issued to 423 companies to import 4 430 280 metric tonnes of maize against the deficit of 1 million metric tonnes. Government continues to monitor volumes of imports, stocks at millers, import prices, and import sources ahead of the festive season in order to eliminate arbitrage opportunities."

acts.speaker: Partners (Nigeria and Niger, at the political level)

title: Drone strikes pound Port Sudan, putting aid deliveries at risk

acts.speaker: A witness in Port Sudan (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said explosions and fires rocked Sudan's main port city and wartime capital Port Sudan on Tuesday, part of a days-long drone assault, and that blasts had been heard from other areas though it was not clear exactly where else had been hit.

acts.speaker: Reuters (video and @Reuters social media post, 6 May 2025)
acts.speech: A Reuters video showed a massive column of black smoke billowing from the area around the port; the Reuters post stated: "Explosions and fires rocked Sudan's wartime capital Port Sudan, a witness said, part of a days-long drone assault that has torched the country's biggest fuel depots and damaged its primary gateway for humanitarian aid in a major escalation."

acts.speaker: Sudan's electricity company
acts.speech: Said a substation in the city was also hit, causing a complete power outage, part of a systematic assault on infrastructure.

acts.speaker: Military sources (anonymous)
acts.speech: Have blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) for the attacks on Port Sudan since Sunday.

acts.speaker: Rapid Support Forces (RSF)
acts.speech: Has not yet claimed any responsibility for the strikes.

acts.speaker: Witnesses (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said one of the targets was a major hotel near the residence of Sudan's military leader, General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.

acts.speaker: A military source (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said the army had destroyed an aircraft and weapons depots in the RSF-controlled Nyala airport in Darfur, the main stronghold of the paramilitary group.

acts.speaker: Egypt and Saudi Arabia
acts.speech: The attacks have drawn condemnation from neighbouring Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: Expressed concern over the attacks; the UN has called the situation in Sudan the world's biggest humanitarian disaster.

acts.speaker: UN experts

acts.speaker: United Arab Emirates

acts.speaker: International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Said on Monday it could not rule in a case in which the Sudanese government accused the UAE of fuelling genocide.

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: According to the UN, the war, triggered by a dispute over a transition to civilian rule, has displaced over 12 million people and pushed half the population into acute hunger.

title: Commune Rurale de Tanda : Une économie locale basée à 80% sur l’agriculture et les activités liées à la pêche | Le Sahel

acts.speaker: 2012 RGP/H (General Population and Housing Census) and INS (National Institute of Statistics) data
acts.speech: According to the 2012 RGP/H, the population was estimated at 49,973 inhabitants; it is projected at 86,340 inhabitants in 2025 and 104,020 in 2030, according to INS data.

acts.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
acts.speech: "The local economy, like that of the other communes of the department of Gaya, is doing relatively well despite the sanctions unjustly imposed on the country by ECOWAS" ; specified that in Tanda agriculture and fishing-related activities represent more than 80% of economic activity ; "The state, through its technical and financial partners such as UNDP, the Millennium Challenge Corporation and the Millennium Challenge Account (MCC/MCA-Niger), has supported women's farmers' organisations in Tanda and Sia in the processing and marketing of groundnut by-products."

acts.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
acts.speech: Noted that, like the majority of the rural communes of the Dosso region, Tanda has no hygiene and sanitation service: "However, to ensure the upkeep of certain public places, the commune organises collective works with the support of youth and women's structures. The rubbish collected is then used by certain agricultural producers. As for the disposal of waste water or run-off water, the commune has no facilities provided for that purpose", he regretted.

acts.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
acts.speech: Indicated that the main resource on which the commune relies is the municipal tax, whose mobilisation rests essentially on the commitment of village and tribal chiefs in collaboration with the municipal revenue collector: "However, since the appearance of armed bandits who carry out sporadic attacks in the area, the commune has been struggling to collect this tax. It is now limited to the revenues from market taxes and the subsidies granted by the state to ensure its functioning."

acts.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
acts.speech: Issued an appeal to the population, inviting them to cultivate patriotism in order to foster genuine economic, social and cultural development of the commune.

title: IN FULL | Professor Malcolm Shaw says SA's genocide case misrepresents the facts and is wrong in law | News24

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Told the International Court of Justice that South Africa's case was misleading and should be rejected on the basis of law and precedent, while Israel's response to the 7 October attack by Hamas did not constitute genocide. On context: "the immediate and proximate context for the specific allegations of genocide claimed by South Africa lies in the events of 7 October, when Hamas militants and other armed groups and individuals stormed into the internationally recognized sovereign territory of Israel and committed acts of barely credible atrocity... Indeed, such acts may be seen as the real genocide in this situation." ; "Armed conflict, even when fully justified and conducted lawfully, is brutal and costs lives... Not every conflict is genocidal... if claims of genocide were to become the common currency of armed conflict, whenever and wherever that occurred, the essence of this crime would be diluted and lost."

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
acts.speech: On prima facie jurisdiction and the existence of a dispute: argued that "Unilateral assertion does not suffice. There needs to be some element of engagement between the parties... A dispute is a reciprocal phenomenon." Said South Africa "cites no relevant exchange between the Parties" and that "There is no evidence of 'positive opposition' as required by the Court"; "This is not a dispute, it is a 'unispute' - a one-sided clapping of hands." Argued South Africa's Application incorrectly stated Israel had not responded to its Note Verbale, that Israel responded that very day and repeatedly offered meetings, and that "South Africa did not give Israel a reasonable opportunity to engage with it on the matters under consideration before filing its no doubt long-prepared Application."

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
acts.speech: On intent: "What determines the existence of the crime of genocide is the intention to destroy, in whole or in part, a particular group, as such... To consider the acts alone as listed in Article II, with no reference at all to the intent criterion, is thus to denude the crime of its very essence: Hamlet without the Prince; a car without an engine." ; "there is little beyond random assertions to demonstrate that Israel has or has had the specific intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinian people, as such." ; Argued that Israel's targeting practices, mitigation of civilian harm and facilitation of humanitarian assistance "all demonstrate the precise opposite of any possible genocidal intent", and that South Africa "presents a distorted picture" and "misunderstands the nature and provenance of certain comments made by some Israeli politicians"; to produce random quotes not in conformity with government policy "is described as misleading at best".

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
acts.speech: On plausibility and the rights to be protected: "plausibility is an elusive concept. Simply declaring that claimed rights are plausible is insufficient." ; Said "Provisional measures are intended to constitute a shield and not a sword. To preserve not undermine rights", and that "the Court needs to consider the relevant respective rights of both Parties, Respondent as well as the Applicant", chief among them Israel's inherent right of self-defence.

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
acts.speech: On Hamas and South Africa's role: "if there has been any genocidal activity in this situation, it was the events of 7 October"; argued that States "that supported, condoned, praised or glorified the events of 7 October... stand guilty of a violation of Article III (e) of the Convention as being complicit in genocide" and that "South Africa has given succour and support to Hamas. At the least."

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
acts.speech: Conclusion: "Allegations have been made which verge on the outrageous. The attack by Hamas on 7 October, with its deliberate commission of atrocities, clearly falls within the statutory definition of genocide. Israel's response was and remains legitimate and necessary... There is no genocidal intent here. This is no genocide." ; "South Africa tells us only half the story."

acts.speaker: South Africa's Application to the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Declares that "it is important to place the acts of genocide in the broader context of Israel's conduct towards [the] Palestinians during its 75-year-long apartheid". The Application further states that "Israel has not responded directly to South Africa's Note Verbale"; it also stated that "the dispute is plainly not capable of resolution by way of a bilateral meeting".

acts.speaker: President of the European Commission
acts.speech: As the President of the European Commission put it on 19 October: "There was no limit to the blood Hamas terrorists wanted to spill. They went home by home. They burned people alive. They mutilated children and even babies. Why? Because they were Jews. Because they were living in the State of Israel. And Hamas' explicit goal is to eradicate Jewish life from the Holy Land. These terrorists, supported by their friends in Tehran, will never stop. And so, Israel has the right to defend itself in line with humanitarian law."

acts.speaker: International Court of Justice (case law and orders cited)
acts.speech: Emphasised in its Order of 2 June 1999 that the threat or use of force cannot in itself constitute an act of genocide within the meaning of Article II of the Genocide Convention; reaffirmed in the Myanmar case that "[i]t must be shown that the claim of one party is positively opposed by the other" and that "the function of provisional measures... is to protect the respective rights of either party pending its final decision"; referred in the Marshall Islands cases to the need that the Respondent should not "be deprived of the opportunity to react before the institution of proceedings"; made clear that "claims against a State involving charges of exceptional gravity must be proved by evidence that is fully conclusive"; and in its Order of 16 March 2022 in Ukraine v. Russia stated that the power to indicate provisional measures "has as its object the preservation of the respective rights claimed by the parties in a case, pending its decision on the merits thereof."

acts.speaker: Professor John Dugard, counsel for South Africa
acts.speech: Explains that South Africa had voiced its concerns in the Security Council and in public statements, and had further referred the matter to the International Criminal Court; at that point, he says, it became clear there was a serious dispute between the two States. Concludes that "Israel must have been aware from South Africa's public statements, d[é]marche and referral to the International Criminal Court of Israel's genocidal acts that a dispute existed between the two States", and declares that "special considerations" apply to the existence of disputes concerning Article IX of the Genocide Convention.

acts.speaker: Judge Greenwood (in the Border Area case)
acts.speech: Emphasised that "[w]hat is required is something more than assertion but less than proof; in other words, the party must show that there is at least a reasonable possibility that the right it claims exists as a matter of law and will be adjudged to apply to that party's case."

acts.speaker: Judge Tomka
acts.speech: Has noted that sometimes statements are made which are "nothing more than a part of the recent war-time rhetoric intending to put the blame and shame on the other side".

acts.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel
acts.speech: Publicly declared on 28 October that "the IDF is doing everything possible to avoid harming those not involved", and on 18 November declared that "first of all, and above all else, Israel acts according to the laws of war. This is how our army works." ; On 10 January: "Israel has no intention of permanently occupying Gaza or displacing its civilian population. Israel is fighting Hamas terrorists, not the Palestinian population, and we are doing so in full compliance with international law. The IDF is doing its utmost to minimize civilian casualties, while Hamas is doing its utmost to maximize them by using Palestinian civilians as human shields... Our goal is to rid Gaza of Hamas terrorists and free our hostages." ; On 23 November: "Any civilian death is a tragedy. Any one. And to avoid them, what you do is first, you try to get the civilians out of harm's way. And that's exactly what we did." ; Statement of 28 October: "We are now entering the second phase of the war, which its objectives are clear: destruction of the military and governmental capabilities of Hamas and the return of the hostages back home... Remember what Amalek has done to you. We remember, and we are fighting... The IDF is the most moral army in the world, the IDF does everything to avoid harming the uninvolved..."

acts.speaker: Israeli Ministerial Committee on National Security Affairs, 29 October (internal cabinet decisions, tab 1A)
acts.speech: Instructions from the Prime Minister stating: (i) "The Prime Minister stated time and again . . . we must prevent a humanitarian disaster"; (ii) "The Prime Minister indicated the possible sorts of solutions that will ensure required supply of water, food and medicine: increasing the amount of trucks entering, [with] the necessary inspections"; (iii) "[P]romoting the construction of field hospitals in the south of the Gaza Strip".

acts.speaker: Minister of Defence of Israel
acts.speech: Publicly stated on 29 October that "we are not fighting the Palestinian multitude and the Palestinian people in Gaza" and declared on 13 November that "[o]ur war is against the Hamas terrorist organization, not the people of Gaza".

acts.speaker: President of Israel
acts.speech: Declared on 12 October that "we are working, operating militarily according to rules of international law. Period. Unequivocally."

acts.speaker: Operations Directorate of the Israel Defense Forces (daily operational directive, tab 1B)
acts.speech: Stating that "[a]ttacks will be solely directed towards military targets, while adhering to the principles of distinction, proportionality and the obligation taking precautions in attacks in order to reduce collateral damage"; that "the laws of armed conflict allow destruction to civilian property only when there is a military necessity to do so, and prohibit harm to property for deterrence purposes only or for the purpose of punishment (individual or collective)"; and that it "is necessary to treat enemy civilians with respect, they should not be treated in a humiliating manner and civilians should not be used for the purpose of performing activities that might put them under risk to their life or their body".

acts.speaker: Professor Vaughan Lowe, counsel for South Africa
acts.speech: Sought to maintain yesterday that Israel has no right to self-defence in this situation.

title: UN marks 80 years, calls for continued support to South Sudan’s peace and stability - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
acts.speech: Says the UN remains committed to supporting South Sudan’s journey toward lasting peace and stability; speaking during the United Nations Day commemoration in Juba, said this year’s event is marked under the global theme “Building Our Future Together”, and noted that the UN is celebrating 80 years since its founding, following the devastation of the Second World War.

acts.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
acts.speech: Highlighted the progress South Sudan has made through the partnership between the United Nations, the government, and the people: said adult literacy has improved from 27 percent in 2008 to just over 34 percent in 2022, while maternal deaths have fallen from about 2,000 in 2006 to around 1,200 per 100,000 live births in 2023; added that several roads and bridges have been constructed, new institutions established, and women’s representation in parliament has risen to 32 percent, up from 26 percent in 2013.

acts.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
acts.speech: Noted that insecurity and conflict continue to hinder the country’s progress; said renewed clashes and economic shocks have worsened displacement, with more than 320,000 people newly displaced this year alone, that an estimated 9.3 million people across South Sudan are in need of humanitarian assistance, and that more than 1.2 million people have crossed into the country since the outbreak of the Sudan conflict.

acts.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
acts.speech: Reaffirmed the UN’s long-standing partnership with South Sudan, recalling its support since Operation Lifeline Sudan, the Comprehensive Peace Agreement, the 2011 referendum, and the Revitalized Peace Agreement of 2018.

title: MSF reduces operations around Yei due to rising insecurity - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) / Doctors Without Borders (statement of Tuesday)
acts.speech: Announced indefinite reduction of its outreach medical activities in Yei County of Central Equatoria State due to "increased insecurity" ; "Due to increased insecurity, Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) has made the difficult decision to reduce outreach activities around Yei, Central Equatoria State, South Sudan until further notice" ; said it is deeply concerned about the impact this reduction will have on vulnerable communities; urged all parties to the conflict to ensure the protection of civilians and guarantee unhindered access to medical and humanitarian assistance for all people.

acts.speaker: Emmanuel Taban, Commissioner of Yei River County, Central Equatoria State
acts.speech: Reported that a woman was killed and two others were injured during an attack on a civilian vehicle along the Yei-Umbasi road on Saturday, April 26; said the vehicle was carrying civilian passengers from Yei to Umbasi, and added that the assailants are yet to be identified and arrested; revealed that the perpetrators fled the scene; reassured the public, stating that the situation has returned to normal, and the road is now safe for travel.

acts.speaker: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
acts.speech: Urged an immediate end to hostilities and restoration of calm in Morobo and Yei counties, Central Equatoria State, following renewed clashes between government forces and the SPLA-IO that displaced thousands of civilians; appealed to the warring factions to refrain from conflict, prioritize the protection of civilians, resolve differences through dialogue, while ensuring unimpeded access for peacekeepers to reinforce security; added that it was engaging with authorities, security actors, faith-based groups, traditional leaders, youths, civil society and community leaders to prevent the situation from deteriorating.

title: From an Activist State to Economic Liberalism. Welcome!

acts.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
acts.speech: Outlined the content of his government's economic reform agenda, the "Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda," before representatives of the international community (members of the Development Assistance Group), acknowledging past accomplishments, soberly admitting "the limit to the road traveled to date" and rolling out the way forward.

acts.speaker: Ricardo Hausmann, Center for International Development at Harvard University
acts.speech: Equates the reform blueprint with "endodontic therapy" — a dental procedure where the doctor removes structures before subsequently cleaning, shaping and decontaminating the hollow with tiny files and irrigated solutions — based on his study of the bottlenecks of growth in Ethiopia.

acts.speaker: Ethiopian government (official narrative)
acts.speech: That there has been "fast and sustained growth" — a narrative the article says was not persuasive enough for a young population that continued to press with demands for more jobs and a response to income inequality among citizens and disparity between regional states.

title: ICC Arrest Warrants: Netanyahu Is Certainly A Criminal, But … – The Standard Newspaper | Gambia

acts.speaker: International Criminal Court (ICC) (press release)
acts.speech: Issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his former defence minister, Yoav Gallant, "for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed from at least 8 October 2023 until at least 20 May 2024". ; Among the war crimes charges against Netanyahu and Gallant are that "both individuals intentionally and knowingly deprived the civilian population in Gaza of objects indispensable to their survival, including food, water, and medicine and medical supplies, as well as fuel and electricity, from at least 8 October 2023 to 20 May 2024". ; The ICC has "found reasonable grounds to believe" that both Netanyahu and Gallant "each bear criminal responsibility as civilian superiors for the war crime of intentionally directing an attack against the civilian population".

acts.speaker: International Criminal Court (ICC)
acts.speech: Stopped short of calling Israel out on genocide, instead specifying that the court "could not determine that all elements of the crime against humanity of extermination were met".

acts.speaker: United Nations committee
acts.speech: Recently found Israel's methods of warfare in the Gaza Strip to be "consistent with genocide".

acts.speaker: Israel (Israeli establishment position)
acts.speech: In the eyes of Israel, the ICC decision constitutes a horrifying display of anti-Semitism and even support for "terror".

acts.speaker: Fatou Bensouda, then-ICC prosecutor (2019 ICC announcement)
acts.speech: The court announced in 2019, after nearly five years of "preliminary investigation", that then-prosecutor Fatou Bensouda was "satisfied" that there was a "reasonable basis to initiate an investigation into the situation in Palestine", having established that there was a "reasonable basis to believe that war crimes have been or are being committed in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip".

title: Mouneissa Tandina, batteuse : un talent oublié par les célébrités - Mali 24

acts.speaker: Mouneissa Tandina, Malian drummer
acts.speech: "My brother played with the Super Biton. He was Salif Keïta's drummer. He died in Ségou; I remember the song titled Mandjou, on which he was the drummer."

acts.speaker: Mouneissa Tandina, Malian drummer
acts.speech: "My mother was my first supporter. She saved all my earnings. Through the Super Biton orchestra, alongside Yéyé Koumba, I was spotted by several music personalities such as the late Toumani Diabaté, the late Mangala Camara, the late Ali Farka Touré, Cheick Tidiane Seck, etc."

acts.speaker: Mouneissa Tandina, Malian drummer
acts.speech: Expresses her regrets: "Indeed, after more than 30 years of a career in the service of music, I have still not received any distinction from the Malian authorities as a sign of recognition. Most of the famous artists with whom I began my career seem to have forgotten me. I fought against prejudice and played with so many celebrities who have cast me into oblivion. I did 17 concerts with Oumou Sangaré; I have always been at Cheick Tidiane Seck's side. The late Toumani Diabaté had promised me many things, but after his death I cannot get hold of his son Sidiki Diabaté. I have even performed in the theatre. The Germans made a documentary about my career and visited me at home; they were even astonished about me," she admits with a wounded heart.

title: Harmonize hana deni kwa msanii yeyote Konde Music!

acts.speaker: Harmonize, Tanzanian musician and owner of Konde Music Worldwide
acts.speech: Came out and said there was no need to go to the National Arts Council (Basata) for arbitration over an artist whom he himself had brought out, and that he therefore wishes Ibraah all the best.

title: Eswatini loses about E1bn US funding in 2 years

acts.speaker: foreignassistance.gov, official US data
