acts.speech: According to official data published by foreignassistance.gov, Eswatini's total US foreign assistance allocation dropped from USD 76.6 million (about E1.38 billion) in 2024 to USD 20.9 million (about E378 million) in 2025 - a 72.7% decrease ; according to foreignassistance.gov, between 2022 and 2024, the majority of US funding went toward HIV/AIDS, health systems, and related social support programmes.

acts.speaker: Khanya Mabuza, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Health of Eswatini
acts.speech: Assured that the country was planning to take over funded programmes by 2030 and outlined an operational plan agreement with the US detailing how Eswatini would sustain services if partner support ended: "Eswatini is among the African states planning to procure its own HIV treatment by 2030. Currently, partners are only providing line two and other drugs, while the government pays for line one, which is in high demand." ; "The roadmap states that in two years, the country will contribute 60%, with partners covering 40%. By 2030, the government would sustain HIV programmes on its own."

acts.speaker: Khanya Mabuza, Principal Secretary, Ministry of Health of Eswatini
acts.speech: Asked if the government was ready to sustain programmes like rural home visits, health services, and gender-based violence interventions, the PS said plans were being developed to incorporate them into government systems: "The country has integration plans for different programmes, as some will be fitted into the various ministries."

acts.speaker: Ministry of Health of Eswatini, 2025/26 first quarter report
acts.speech: The impact of the US Government's Stop Work Order, issued on January 25, 2025, was acknowledged; it has already significantly impacted HIV services, leading to a downturn in HIV testing from 27,334 individuals in April to 18,801 by June.

acts.speaker: Local NGOs in Eswatini
acts.speech: Report fewer community health visits, and some outreach activities have been halted entirely; clinics supported by US partners report fewer resources to conduct testing and outreach.

title: Egypt, Qatar, US urge Israel, Hamas to finalise Gaza truce deal

acts.speaker: Qatar, Egypt and the United States
acts.speech: called on Hamas and Israel to finalise an agreement that embodies the principles outlined by US President Joe Biden on May 31, 2024.

acts.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
acts.speech: said there are almost no health services remaining in Rafah after the city's last partially functioning hospital, the al-Helal al-Emirati Hospital, shut down amid the ongoing hostilities.

acts.speaker: Thousands of Israeli protesters
acts.speech: took to the streets urging Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to strike a deal with Hamas and free the captives held in Gaza.

acts.speaker: Far-right ministers in the Israeli government
acts.speech: threatened to topple his government if he accepts such an agreement.

title: Cidadãos árabes em Israel protestam contra Fome na Faixa de Gaza - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Arab citizens in Israel (protesters in Lod)
acts.speech: Warn that all Palestinians in Gaza are going hungry, with children the most affected, because of the months-long Israeli blockade, which has cut off the supply of infant formula and other vital supplies ; appeal to the Israeli government to end the hunger by allowing humanitarian aid into the Gaza Strip ; accuse the government of using hunger as a weapon of war ; recall that some journalists died during the attacks carried out by Israeli forces.

title: IMF, World Bank and their Russian roulette with Nigeria, By Umar Farouk Bala

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
acts.speech: Has raised alarms, projecting that by 2026, the Federal Government could spend nearly 100 per cent of its revenue just on servicing its existing debts.

acts.speaker: Bismarck Rewane, CEO of Financial Derivatives
acts.speech: Has been vocal in highlighting the negative impact of this debt burden. He pointed out that debt servicing is so consuming that it has crippled the government's ability to invest in infrastructure and essential services. For instance, the N8 trillion spent on debt servicing in 2023 could have been used to build 5,000 kilometres of dual carriage roads, 1,600 schools, 80,000 healthcare centres, or generate 5,000 MW of solar power.

acts.speaker: World Bank
acts.speech: Has attempted to reassure global stakeholders by describing Nigeria's debt as “statistically sustainable.” However, it has also cautioned that the country's debt remains “vulnerable and costly.”

title: Alake Calls For End To Africa’s Raw Minerals Export, Urges Shift To Industrialization

acts.speaker: Dr. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairman of the African Minerals Strategy Group (AMSG)
acts.speech: Has called for a bold new vision to make minerals the fulcrum of Africa's transformative industrialization. “Africa's minerals have powered industrialization elsewhere while our own economies remain under-industrialized. This paradox must end. Our vision must be clear: to move from extractive dependence to transformative industrialization,” Dr. Alake declared in a statement issued on Sunday, October 5, 2025, in Abuja ; delivering the keynote address at African Mining Week in Cape Town, the minister emphasized that Africa must no longer be content as a supplier of raw minerals but must become a global hub for mineral processing, innovation, and green industrialization, and noted that the continent is blessed with some of the world's richest mineral deposits, key to clean energy, digital technologies, advanced manufacturing, and global security ; “Our youth should no longer seek jobs abroad while opportunities lie buried beneath their feet. The time to industrialize is now. Let us set the stage for an Africa that is not just a participant in the global minerals economy, but a driver of its future,” Alake asserted.

acts.speaker: Dr. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development (represented by Permanent Secretary Dr. Farouk Yabo)
acts.speech: Highlighting Nigeria's ongoing reforms in the mining sector, said the nation is incentivizing local beneficiation from gold refining to lithium processing, revoking dormant licenses to encourage serious investment, and strengthening transparency to attract credible global partners; added that Nigeria is also developing a National Critical Minerals Strategy and investing in digital systems for data accessibility and mineral traceability ; reiterated Nigeria's commitment to creating a $1 trillion economy by 2030 through solid minerals development: “We are investing in digitizing mining processes from data accessibility to mineral traceability. We are also focusing on bequeathing strong institutions and the right policies to drive reforms. Hence, the ongoing efforts to amend the 2007 Minerals and Mining Act to provide a more robust legislative framework that will propel investments in the mining sector” ; emphasized that Nigeria's minerals will henceforth be traceable, originating only from licensed operators or formalized artisanal and small-scale miners.

acts.speaker: Dr. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairman of AMSG
acts.speech: Urged African nations to prioritize mapping their mineral resources to understand their true potential. “After national mapping, it is the duty of countries to ensure only licensed operators are mining. We must also build adequate capacity for effective supervision,” he said.

acts.speaker: Dr. Farouk Yabo, Permanent Secretary, Nigeria's Ministry of Solid Minerals Development
acts.speech: During the Country Spotlight Session, presented investment opportunities in the solid minerals sector, showcasing reforms, incentives, and a synopsis of the nation's mineral endowments.

title: 2025 Financial Times Africa Summit to Tackle Trump-Era Policies as Malawi Reels from Visa Bond, Aid Cuts - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Financial Times
acts.speech: Announced that the 12th edition of its flagship Africa Summit will take place in London on October 21-22, 2025, under the theme "Africa in a Changing World," bringing together African Heads of State, policymakers, CEOs, investors and next-generation entrepreneurs to explore the continent's place in an era of geopolitical upheaval, economic uncertainty and rapid technological change.

acts.speaker: Financial Times (statement)
acts.speech: "The dramatic changes to America's foreign policy in Donald Trump's second term and his upending of the decades-old global trading system present challenges, uncertainties and risks for Africa as other outside powers intervene." ; notes there may also be opportunities if Africa can pivot toward trade and investment over aid.

title: Solidarité nationale : Le gouvernement et ses partenaires mobilisés pour les sinistrés des inondations de la région de Kayes

acts.speaker: United Nations Resident Coordinator in Mali
acts.speech: Took the opportunity to emphasise the importance of providing "support to the populations affected by these natural disasters."

acts.speaker: Nicolas Simard, Canadian Ambassador to Mali
acts.speech: Spoke of his country's commitment in the areas of health and education in Mali's first administrative region and announced humanitarian aid of one million dollars, or nearly 437,879,840 CFA francs.

acts.speaker: Assa Badiallo Touré, Malian Minister of Health and Social Development
acts.speech: Recalled that the floods had affected 792 households and caused six deaths in the region, and that material aid (food, shelter kits) and financial assistance had been distributed to help the victims ; also mentioned the creation of a unified social registry to better coordinate aid to vulnerable populations.

acts.speaker: Religious and traditional notables of Kayes
acts.speech: Expressed their gratitude to the government for this assistance and supported the ongoing efforts to help the flood victims.

title: Rights Group Raises Alarm Over Alleged Fulani Jihadists’ Plot To Impose Empire On Nigeria

acts.speaker: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), human rights group
acts.speech: Has raised alarm over alleged Fulani Jihadists plot to impose Sultanate in Nigeria by 2075.

acts.speaker: Emeka Umeagbalasi, chairman of Intersociety, and other leaders of the group (special report)
acts.speech: Said already Nigeria is headquartering 22 Islamic terror groups in Africa seeking to obliterate Christianity and indigenous cultural heritage to achieve this purpose with world Jihad fund.

acts.speaker: Intersociety special report
acts.speech: Stated that the terror groups, presently using Nigeria as their ‘safest haven’, are also seeking to obliterate or wipe out an estimated 112 million Christians and 13 million traditional religionists across the country, particularly in South-East and South-South by the year 2075 or in 50 years' time ; “The groups to achieve the objectives, had so far massacred 7,087 Christians and abducted 7,800 in 220 days of 2025, mostly Christians from South East, South South, who are either killed or incarcerated alongside thousands of liberal Muslims particularly across core Northern Muslim States dominated” ; “They have killed 185,009 defenseless Nigerians since 2009 (16 Years) including 125,009 Christians And 60,000 liberal Muslims during Which 19,100 churches were razed, and more than 1,100 Christian communities sacked” ; “20,000 square miles of their lands were taken-over and over 600 Christian clerics abducted including abduction of 250 Catholic priests and 350 pastors and killing of dozens. They have forced out estimated 12m-14m Christians out of their homes to become IDPs and millions of others fled” ; said the Islamic terror groups are using violence and genocidal means to obliterate or wipe out Nigeria's indigenous ethnic groups and their identities especially the 3,475-year-old Igbo cultural heritage put in place since 1450BC.

acts.speaker: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), human rights group
acts.speech: Believed that even the far-reaching punitive measures by US, EU, UK, and Canadian leaders were not only belated and long overdue, and that “all the first-class Fulani Muslims and top Islamic clerics and leaders, including those of the MACABAN, must be banned from traveling to these religious freedom compliant and respectful countries” ; also wants world leaders and respecters of human rights to review hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of annual humanitarian, democracy, military, and development assistance to Nigeria.

title: Intra-Africa Trade Stands at 15% of Total African Trade, Says Former Ethiopian Prime Minister

acts.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
acts.speech: Highlighted the slow pace of intra-Africa trade, which currently accounts for just 15% of the continent's total trade, and pointed out the stark contrast with other continents such as Asia, where intra-regional trade stands at over 50%; he noted that while Africa's total merchandise exports surged by 200% between 2017 and 2023, intra-Africa trade only increased by 27% during the same period, growing from $140 billion to $190 billion.

acts.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
acts.speech: "The political commitment to AfCFTA is strong, and we are beginning to see more African goods being exchanged," Desalegn remarked, emphasizing that trade under the AfCFTA has become more encouraging, especially between 2017 and 2023; he also lauded the progress made toward the formation of a single African market, describing the launch of the AfCFTA five years ago as a landmark moment for the continent, and stressed that with a population of 1.2 billion people and a combined GDP of $3 trillion the potential for economic growth and prosperity through increased regional trade is immense.

acts.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
acts.speech: Pointed out the long-standing challenges that continue to hinder trade within Africa, including inadequate trade infrastructure and colonial-era legacy systems that were not designed for regional integration: "We have seen the export of raw materials like gold, cocoa, and coffee, only for these to return to Africa as processed goods. Our infrastructure, built by colonial powers, remains a major barrier to implementing AfCFTA fully."

acts.speaker: Hailemariam Desalegn Boshe, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia and board chair of Trademark Africa
acts.speech: Emphasised the importance of Africa navigating the challenges carefully to ensure successful implementation of AfCFTA, and remained optimistic: "While there have been frustrations along the way, the achievements of AfCFTA remain undeniable. Africa's exports are projected to grow faster than any other region, with the World Trade Organization forecasting a 5.3% increase in 2024, up from 3.1% in 2023." He expressed confidence in the future of African trade integration and urged governments, businesses, and regional bodies to continue working together to overcome the obstacles and fully realize the economic potential of the AfCFTA.

acts.speaker: World Trade Organization (forecast, cited by Desalegn)
acts.speech: Forecasting a 5.3% increase in Africa's exports in 2024, up from 3.1% in 2023.

title: Ein palästinensischer Arbeiter erlag seinen Verletzungen, nachdem er von den Besatzungstruppen im besetzten Jerusalem verfolgt worden war - Union der Nachrichtenagenturen der Organisation für Islamische Zusammenarbeit

acts.speaker: Abdullah Hammad, brother of the deceased Palestinian worker Raafat Abdul Aziz Abdullah Hammad
acts.speech: Said the family had refused the occupation authorities’ demand to carry out an autopsy on the body, and pointed out that the occupation is still withholding his body under the pretext of an “identity verification” ; added that the martyr’s body would be buried in his home town of Silwad, east of Ramallah, as soon as it arrived, and pointed out that the martyr was the father of three children (the eldest six years old, the youngest one year old).

acts.speaker: Jerusalem Governorate (official statement)
acts.speech: Stated that this crime stands “in the context of a systematic policy of the occupation forces against Palestinian workers, who are forced to take on the risk of jumping over the apartheid wall, while the forces continue to shoot directly at them or fire tear gas and stun grenades at them, which in recent months has led to the martyrdom and injury of dozens of people.”

title: BREAKING: Robbers Burgle Retired Nigerian Supreme Court Justice Dattijo’s Official Quarters In Abuja

acts.speaker: Sources privy to the incident (anonymous)
acts.speech: Told SaharaReporters that the home was stripped bare as the burglars “took everything from the house”; “The burglary took place at the quarters for Supreme Court justices in Maitama. It occurred over the Christmas holidays and Dattijo was travelling out of the country at the time.”

acts.speaker: Muhammad Dattijo, retired Justice of the Supreme Court of Nigeria
acts.speech: Described the apex court as rotten and characterised by filth, lamenting that it had been pervaded by bribery and perversion of justice, and adding that it was dangerous for two out of the six geopolitical zones of the country to be excluded from the bench of the Supreme Court hearing appeals on the presidential election ; lamenting that the appointments of judicial officers have been political, selfish and sectional, he said: “It is asserted that the process of appointment to judicial positions is deliberately conducted to give undue advantage to the children, spouses and mistresses of serving and retired judges and managers of judicial offices. At the Court of Appeal, it is asserted, presiding justices are now being appointed out of turn. And there is the further issue of the unpredictable nature of recent decisions of the courts as well. A number of respected senior members of the bar inter alia, citing Ahmed Lawan, the former President of the Senate and Imo governorship appeals, claim that decisions of even the apex court have become unpredictable. It is difficult to understand how and where, by these decisions, the judicial pendulum swings. It was not so before, they contended. In some quarters, the view is strongly held that filth and intrigues characterise the institution these days. Judges are said to be comfortable in companies they never would have kept in the past. It is being insinuated that some judicial officers even campaign for politicians. It cannot be more damnifying.” ; said that some years ago “appointment to the bench was strictly on merit. Sound knowledge of the law, integrity, honour and hard work distinguished those who were elevated”, and continued: “Lobbying was unheard of. I never lobbied, not at any stage of my career, to secure any appointment or elevation. As much as possible, the most qualified men and women were appointed. That can no longer be said about appointments to the bench. The judiciary must be uniquely above board. Appointments should not be polluted by political, selfish and sectional interests. The place of merit, it must be urged, cannot be overemphasised. Public perceptions of the judiciary have over the years become witheringly scornful and monstrously critical”, and called for urgent reform in the judiciary to correct the alleged anomalies.

title: As Trump Wields His Sledgehammer on Immigrants

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Riding to power for the second time on the mantra of "America First," vowed to shut the country's borders to illegal migrants; even since the time of his first presidential campaign in 2016, Trump has strongly and repeatedly emphasized a need to safeguard the interests of the US by adopting policies that would firmly place "America First".

acts.speaker: Trump's detractors
acts.speech: Are condemning his deportation strategies, pointing out that they could usher in an era of human rights violations as well as large-scale trauma which could affect families and communities more likely to be targeted by mass deportations.

acts.speaker: Some experts
acts.speech: Argue that mass deportations could benefit American workers by raising wages and improving job conditions.

acts.speaker: Other experts
acts.speech: Have warned that plans to remove millions of working immigrants have the potential to hasten economic instability, especially as cheap immigrant labour helps key sectors like agriculture and hospitality.

acts.speaker: Migration Policy Institute (database)
acts.speech: Cited as the source for the figures that Biden carried out deportations with about 271,000 immigrants flown out to approximately 192 countries in just 2024, and a total of 1.5 million illegal immigrants deported during his four years as the 46th President.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: In a televised moment during one of his debates with then Democratic presidential candidate and former Vice President Kamala Harris, blamed a wave of Haitian immigrants for the deaths of domesticated animals in Springfield, Ohio; although this claim was refuted as baseless and false, Trump has not backed down from constantly pointing out that illegal immigration poses a huge threat not just to the economy of the US, but to the security of its cities and citizens.

acts.speaker: Punch Newspaper (report)
acts.speech: According to a recent report by Punch Newspaper, US-based Nigerians have gone into hiding amid Trump's deportation crackdown. Many have stopped going to churches, mosques, and even their workplaces, fearing they could be the next targets.

acts.speaker: A Life Bencher, Body of Benchers, Nigerian Law School (unnamed)
acts.speech: Echoed the sentiment that this country is all we have, at a recent law dinner with the Body of Benchers at the Nigerian Law School, Bwari.

title: Nitiwul’s US$8.8 million Soviet-Scrap armoured vehicles put Ghanaian Soldiers in danger

acts.speaker: Military insiders (anonymous)
acts.speech: Describe these vehicles as "death traps", posing a serious risk to the lives of Ghanaian soldiers deployed on international peacekeeping missions.

acts.speaker: Technical reports and confidential military documents obtained by The Herald
acts.speech: Reveal that the APCs, now over 50 years old, are plagued with mechanical and structural deficiencies - oil and lubricant leakages, frequent engine overheating after limited use, malfunctioning brake and clutch systems, blurred vision blocks, missing side mirrors, and defective rear cameras - and that they lack intra- and inter-vehicle communication systems, leaving troops effectively isolated during operations.

acts.speaker: Sources within the Ghana Army (anonymous)
acts.speech: Describe the APCs as unfit for purpose; many arrived immobile and had to be transported from Tema Port to Burma Camp on low-loader trailers, and despite superficial refurbishment efforts most remain non-operational.

acts.speaker: Soldiers who spoke to The Herald (anonymous)
acts.speech: Revealed that seven of the vehicles were shipped to Ghana's UN peacekeeping battalion in Abyei (UNISFA) in 2024.

acts.speaker: Military mechanics (anonymous)
acts.speech: Report that while the original petrol engines of the BTR-70s were replaced with diesel variants, critical accompanying components such as radiators and hoses were not upgraded accordingly.

acts.speaker: Insiders (anonymous)
acts.speech: Disclosed to The Herald that the APCs were effectively salvaged from a scrapyard in Azerbaijan.

acts.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
acts.speech: Further allege that Major General Thomas Oppong-Peprah, who served as Army Commander at the time and has since become CDS, was heavily involved in the transaction and is reported to have personally travelled to Azerbaijan alongside the suppliers to inspect and finalise the deal.

acts.speaker: Confidential documents reviewed by The Herald
acts.speech: Show that the GAF repeatedly sought waivers and expedited clearances to facilitate the vehicles' entry into Ghana; in letters addressed to Customs and Port Authorities dated between January and March 2023, military officers cited "budgetary constraints" and "urgent operational needs" to justify bypassing standard procedures.

acts.speaker: Captain F.A. Amin, 1 Forces Movement Unit (memo)
acts.speech: Requested a 100 percent waiver on state warehouse rent fees, citing an inability to pay GHS 4,800.

acts.speaker: Captain E. Owusu-Acheampong (letter)
acts.speech: Applied for release of the consignment before full customs processing was complete, stressing the "sensitive nature" of the shipment.

acts.speaker: Defence analysts and military insiders
acts.speech: Are now calling for a full value-for-money audit to assess the wisdom of the purchase and prevent similar embarrassments in future.

title: Migration volontaire : La Côte d’Ivoire affine sa stratégie nationale de réintégration

acts.speaker: Dr Gaoussou Karamoko, Director General of the DGIE (Directorate-General for Ivorians Abroad)
acts.speech: Set out several key points to be addressed at the workshop in his opening remarks, saying the reintegration of migrants is a reality linking Côte d'Ivoire to Europe, a global issue, and that migrants form a link connecting the two regions, while stressing that "now, it is up to Côte d'Ivoire to fully complete this reintegration process."

acts.speaker: Anne-Catherine Claude, representative of the European Union
acts.speech: "The MPRR project is being revised to add additional financial resources which it currently lacks."

acts.speaker: David Preux, Head of Mission of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Stressed the need for a coordinated approach through a national consultation framework, noting that such an initiative would help strengthen efforts to further structure support for returning migrants.

title: #Mali : Rétrocession du camp de l’entité de liquidation de la Minusma : Le Ministre Diop salue le patriotisme du personnel malien

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: "I would like to reiterate my words of appreciation, with a special thought for the Malian staff of MINUSMA. These staff lived through the government's decision to request the withdrawal of the UN Mission in the interest of our country... who experienced this withdrawal as a social and financial trauma, but who also received this decision with a sense of dignity and responsibility that I wanted to salute," he stated. ; For him, this final phase is full of symbolism, lessons and opportunities for better envisaging the appropriate format for United Nations intervention in our country.

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: "MINUSMA had symbolised in the eyes of Malians what the international community, through the United Nations, had best to offer: peace and stability," recalled the head of Malian diplomacy. And he stressed that the handover of MINUSMA's last site coincides with the anniversary of the recapture of Kidal by the FAMa.

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: "It thus became obvious that the Mission, in its form, did not meet the requirements on the ground," regretted Minister Diop, who added that while the Mission, in its first year, contributed to consolidating the FAMa's hold over areas liberated from terrorist occupation, successive developments showed the limits of its intervention.

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Pointed out that the end of MINUSMA's presence does not mean the end of cooperation between Mali and the United Nations. "Cooperation between our country and the United Nations existed before MINUSMA's arrival and continues at least as much, if not better, since its departure, thanks to the experience and expertise of the United Nations country teams in Mali," he noted. ; "MINUSMA was an important mechanism in Mali's cooperation with the United Nations, but I am happy to acknowledge and salute the excellent articulation between the government's vision and the actions on the ground of the United Nations Funds, Agencies and Programmes operating in Mali," he acknowledged.

acts.speaker: Atul Khare, UN Under-Secretary-General for Operational Support
acts.speech: announced that a new chapter focused on humanitarian affairs would be opened. "We are closing one chapter and opening another... a chapter focused on strengthening United Nations support to Mali in the areas of humanitarian aid and development. The United Nations remains committed alongside Mali during this transition and to support Mali's continued efforts towards development and prosperity," indicated Atul Khare.

title: Journée Mondiale de l’Aide Humanitaire : Poursuivre le plaidoyer et agir ensemble pour les causes humanitaires et sécuritaires | Le Sahel

acts.speaker: Pr Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: In her introductory remarks, stressed the commitment of the Government of Niger to all the initiatives put in place to guarantee security. She also recalled the importance of this day, which honours the memory of the humanitarian workers who were victims of the attack on the United Nations house on 19 August 2003 in Baghdad, and the praiseworthy actions carried out by them to save and improve the lives of many people, as well as the importance of community participation in achieving the predefined objectives. "Humanitarian aid accompanies, but it is the communities that initiate, guide and shape the responses to their challenges. It is important to respect dignity, beyond relief, because it is the women, the men and the children who resist crises every day," she said. By supporting projects arising from community-led initiatives, she added, collective resilience and appropriate responses are built in connection with government action.

acts.speaker: Pr Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: Stressed that terrorist acts constitute a brake on Niger's development, forcing many people to live in conditions of high precariousness and thereby accentuating forced displacement, epidemics, malnutrition, floods, social psychosis and food insecurity in several areas of the country and in the AES Confederation area.

acts.speaker: Kinday Samba, interim Humanitarian Coordinator
acts.speech: Explained that the choice of this year's theme is a call to decision-makers to use their position and influence to put an end to human atrocities, relying on human rights legal instruments, international humanitarian law and all available means. She also mentioned the missions assigned to humanitarian workers and their concrete impact on the lives of local communities. "Through this day, we aspire to continue advocacy for the protection of civilians and humanitarian workers, to promote respect for international humanitarian law and for the principles that guide humanitarian action," she said. She also mentioned the importance of humanitarian workers, which consists in relieving suffering, strengthening community resilience and fostering sustainable responses guided by the real needs of the populations.

acts.speaker: Kinday Samba, interim Humanitarian Coordinator
acts.speech: Noted that the humanitarian situation in Niger remains worrying despite all the efforts made by the authorities, because of the violence perpetrated in the three-borders area, generating additional humanitarian needs.

acts.speaker: Kinday Samba, interim Humanitarian Coordinator
acts.speech: Stresses that several advances have been recorded thanks to humanitarian aid combined with government efforts, notably better control of the impact of floods thanks to preventive measures put in place, an improvement in the food and nutrition situation thanks to the availability of cereals on the market, moderate-price sales operations and the positive impact of the vast irrigation campaign. She praised the efforts of the authorities, who continue to establish a climate of security and peace allowing the various operations to be carried out and challenges to be met. "This requires increased mobilisation, a strengthened commitment from all stakeholders. Anticipatory actions can help prevent natural disasters, because acting before a foreseeable shock is not only more effective but also less costly than the traditional humanitarian response. We must promote sustainable solutions for greater community self-reliance," she suggested.

acts.speaker: Mme Lafuente Nena, Representative of the Technical and Financial Partners
acts.speech: Praised the noble and constant work of humanitarian workers to save the lives of vulnerable people, often at the expense of their own. "In 2024, 383 humanitarian workers were killed, compared with 265 humanitarian workers who lost their lives in 2025," she lamented. She then launched an appeal to all parties to guarantee the protection and security of civilians and humanitarian workers. "On this day, let us commit to protecting our workers and all act for humanity," she maintained.

acts.speaker: M. Issoufou Soumana, Representative of national and international NGOs
acts.speech: Praised the noble and constant work of humanitarian workers to save the lives of vulnerable people, often at the expense of their own ; recalled the constant effort of NGOs to mobilise funds in order to continuously assist millions of people in Niger despite the challenges they face. He also reaffirmed the commitment of NGOs alongside the populations and the Government to preserve human dignity and strengthen the resilience of communities.

title: Tanzania’s tax-to-GDP ratio soars to 14pc in 2024/25 - Daily News

acts.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
acts.speech: Said the tax-to-GDP ratio remains low, rising from 12.0 percent in 2001/02 to 14.9 percent in 2024/25, despite good progress in tax collection, and called for more systemic and policy-driven action ; emphasized that a stable and transparent tax regime is a key driver of economic growth and public welfare ; urged participants, including stakeholders from both public and private sectors, to develop strategic approaches for increasing domestic revenue, enabling the government to deliver better services to citizens and reduce reliance on foreign aid ; directed ministers across various sectors to actively contribute ideas through open discussions and digital platforms aimed at expanding national revenue streams.

acts.speaker: Dr Philip Mpango, Vice President of Tanzania
acts.speech: Reiterated the Sixth Phase Government’s commitment to enhancing Tanzania’s business and investment environment by strengthening security, maintaining peace, and ensuring a fair and equitable tax system ; outlined several government initiatives on tax reform, including the increased use of ICT in tax collection, the development of a comprehensive taxpayer database, and the reduction of non-productive tax exemptions.

acts.speaker: Saada Mkuya, Minister of State for Finance and Planning (Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar)
acts.speech: Reported that the government has already scrapped over 380 nuisance charges and continues to expand the use of digital platforms to simplify tax payment processes.

acts.speaker: Angelina Ngalula, Chairperson of the Tanzania Private Sector Foundation (TPSF)
acts.speech: Stressed the importance of tax education among both small and large-scale business owners to help broaden the taxpayer base; noted that Tanzania’s approximately two million registered taxpayers is still low relative to the country’s economic potential.

title: President Mbumba calls on UNGA to support ICJ decision on Gaza

acts.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
acts.speech: "has appealed to the United Nations General Assembly to support the modalities to actualize the advisory opinion rendered by the International Court of Justice regarding the ongoing conflict in Gaza": "Prolonged occupation does not justify or make acceptable the hardships and injustices endured. This is particularly true for the people of Gaza, who continue to be brutally massacred. As a country that has endured genocide, Namibia believes that Israel, by intent and by action, is committing genocide. Namibia continues to call for a ceasefire and for humanitarian assistance to flow unhindered into Gaza."

acts.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
acts.speech: Repeated Namibia's call for the lifting of decades-old US blockades against Cuba and Zimbabwe: "Economic hardships continue to affect the sister Republic of Cuba, in stark contrast to the ideals of inclusivity and the goal of leaving no one behind. Namibia calls for the end of the economic, financial, and commercial blockade against Cuba. Namibia also reiterates its call for the immediate and unconditional lifting of illegal sanctions against Zimbabwe, which hinders the country's capacity to achieve Sustainable Development Goals."

acts.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
acts.speech: Said the quest for self-determination for the Sahrawi people remains a matter the world body should help intensify, and reminded the Assembly that continued disenfranchisement of the people of Western Sahara is an affront to the UN Charter, its purposes and principles, and that this year's session must change this.

acts.speaker: International Court of Justice (advisory opinion)
acts.speech: "stated that Israel's continued occupation of the Gaza Strip and West Bank is a violation of international law" and "further outlined that Israel end the war".

title: Tension and Anticipation in Lilongwe as MEC Prepares to Announce Final Election Results

acts.speaker: Malawi Congress Party (MCP)
acts.speech: Reacted defiantly, staging what it termed a “victory march” in Lilongwe city.

acts.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
acts.speech: Has strongly condemned the MCP’s demonstration, describing it as an “unholy act” that undermines the integrity of the electoral process.

acts.speaker: MEC officials
acts.speech: Have urged all political parties to remain patient and await the official announcement of results through formal channels.

title: Tempête à Washington : Zelensky s'écharpe, la diplomatie vacille - Journal du Niger

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Lectured Zelensky, reproaching him for a lack of gratitude for American aid: "You're gambling with World War Three and you dare to talk to me like that?" he is said to have thrown out, according to witnesses.

acts.speaker: JD Vance, US Vice-President
acts.speech: Reportedly drove the point home, denouncing a "disrespectful" attitude.

acts.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
acts.speech: "I do not negotiate with a killer," he declared, implicitly targeting Vladimir Putin, while demanding an "unavoidable bulwark" to guarantee peace ; refuses to sell off his subsoil, castigating a first draft of the agreement that he described as "old-fashioned plunder".

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: For weeks has been multiplying his attacks, accusing Zelensky of having "triggered" the war and portraying him as an autocrat; sees the Ukrainian rare earths as an opportunity to "make profitable" the colossal aid given to Kyiv.

acts.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
acts.speech: In return has branded his counterpart a victim of a "Russian disinformation fog".

acts.speaker: Senator John Curtis (Republican)
acts.speech: Praised Zelensky's "admirable tenacity" in the face of Russian aggression.

acts.speaker: Senator John Cornyn (Republican)
acts.speech: Brushed aside the label of "dictator" pinned by Trump on the Ukrainian leader.

acts.speaker: X users (anonymous social media posts)
acts.speech: "Trump literally reduced Zelensky to shreds in front of everyone," marvelled one internet user ; "It's a diplomatic detonation live on air," added another.

acts.speaker: Witnesses (anonymous)
acts.speech: According to witnesses, Trump said to Zelensky: "You're gambling with World War Three and you dare to talk to me like that?"

title: Uganda’s minority groups face rising fear as US aid halts

acts.speaker: Pius Kennedy, Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
acts.speech: “Some donors are now going to pull out resources because they were also receiving from the similar funding baskets to sub grant to us” ; according to Kennedy, the funding cuts mean reversing years of gains in the country ; said USAID had been the biggest funder of HIV programs, with around 20 million people receiving drugs and testing services through associated organisations.

acts.speaker: Pius Kennedy, Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
acts.speech: Amid uncertainty on the future of US funding, underscored the immediate impact on at-risk individuals in the world’s poorest communities, decrying that survivors of gender-based violence have nowhere to turn for medical or psychological support.

acts.speaker: Pius Kennedy, Ugandan LGBTQ+ rights activist and employee of the Africa Queer Network
acts.speech: Expressed concern about the impact of tougher conditions on asylum seekers and fears that LGBTQ+ people under threat in Uganda will no longer be able to claim asylum in the US ; “I’m looking at this not as an issue that affected Uganda or that affected East Africa, it’s an issue that has affected the global citizenship.”

title: UBA África à procura de áreas de investimento em Moçambique - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Abiola Bawuah, CEO of UBA Africa
acts.speech: After holding a meeting with the management of Caminhos de Ferro de Moçambique (CFM), assured that in the coming days agreements would be signed with CFM with the aim of driving the expansion of rail and port infrastructure: "In the coming months, perhaps one or two months from now, we should close a partnership agreement to see how we can support this enormous infrastructure and extension work they are about to carry out. Thus, we will give prominence to their expansion programme. We may partner with the Government to ensure that they expand the port and then perhaps renovate some equipment, locomotives that are old."

acts.speaker: Abiola Bawuah, CEO of UBA Africa
acts.speech: "We have more than 60 million dollars in aid, which we use to support SMEs. Mozambicans are not excluded, they are part of it. And most of this happens in Africa. So SMEs have the right to support trade in Africa. So we have more than 60 million that we are using to support this. And this is a unique relationship between us and Africa."

acts.speaker: Abiola Bawuah, CEO of UBA Africa
acts.speech: Explained, regarding her closed-door meeting with the investment administrator of the Bank of Mozambique, which she considered a moment of market assessment: "I think Mozambique is a very beautiful country. I saw that it is a major exporter of cashew. I also saw the beautiful hospitality industry. And then, as a bank, I think there is a great local opportunity. And that is part of the reason why I am here today. And this is to support all the people who want to invest in the main sectors of the economy."

title: Youth make clarion call for economic indepenence

acts.speaker: Tlohang Sekhamane, Speaker of the National Assembly of Lesotho
acts.speech: Described youth unemployment as a national emergency that requires urgent and united action from the government and all sectors of society: "Poverty is what Lesotho has been used to for the past 200 years. This country was formed on poverty. But we cannot solve the problem of poverty with the same mind-set that created it."

acts.speaker: Tlohang Sekhamane, Speaker of the National Assembly of Lesotho
acts.speech: Criticized the culture of complacency among the youth, saying the youth of this country are in their comfort zone; they do not take action against poor decisions being made today. Basotho cherish poverty, it is time the youth become the solution, as the future of Lesotho depends on them.

acts.speaker: Kananelo Boloetse, one of the lead organizers of the Youth Dialogue on Economic Independence
acts.speech: Announced that young people were working on an Independence Charter, a manifesto that will outline practical steps and policies aimed at achieving economic self-reliance. He stated that this document will serve as a roadmap for the youth and the entire country to move away from dependency on foreign aid and start building their own future.

acts.speaker: Tumelo Moteuli, organizer of the Youth Dialogue on Economic Independence
acts.speech: Emphasized the importance of learning from the past: "Back in the day, our leaders had strong strategies to unite nations and boost the economy. This dialogue is about reviving those strategies and applying them to today's generation, we need to stop depending on other countries and make sure Lesotho stands on its own feet economically." ; He further explained that the realization that foreign aid is not a sustainable solution was a driving force behind the dialogue, as countries that are poverty-stricken can no longer rely on foreign aid, so they must take charge of their own future.

acts.speaker: Mohau Mabetha, representing the voices of the youth
acts.speech: Echoed similar sentiments, saying the dialogue serves as an opportunity for young people to brainstorm and develop job creation strategies, stating that the youth need to unite, identify opportunities, and work together to overcome the high unemployment rate, and only then can they improve Lesotho's economy and future.

title: China’s boasts of creating over 1.1 million jobs in Africa - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
acts.speech: Says China's cooperation with Africa continues to yield visible and tangible results: "China remains one of Africa's largest trade partners for over sixteen years. My African brothers and sister, China Africa Corporation is visible, tangible and truly a vision" ; "In the past three years alone, Chinese enterprises created more than 1.1 million new jobs in Africa."

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
acts.speech: Argued that the China-Africa cooperation is a strategic partnership that is built on the aspiration of transforming livelihood, advancing industrialization and agricultural modernization ; explained that China-Africa cooperation aimed at raising Africa's voice and representation at the international level, adding that China's foreign policy stands firmly on international justice and opposes power politics and hegemony ; stated that China's foreign policy also focuses on advancing a cooperation with a shared future inherited in people-centered governance and advancement of the livelihood of people.

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
acts.speech: Said Africa is experiencing a new awakening, and countries should support it in exploring this new development.

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
acts.speech: Disclosed that this year marks the beginning of implementing the outcome of the Forum on China Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit: "Also, this year marks the 20th anniversary of FOCAC. Over the past twenty-five years, China has helped Africa build nearly one hundred kilometers of roads and more than ten thousand kilometers of railways" ; "China stands ready to deliver on the ten partnership action that China and Africa seek to jointly advance modernization, including supporting Africa in accelerating its industrialization, agriculture modernization, implementing zero tariff treatment for 100% tariff free, fostering new sanitary life with new growth to harvest like digital green, and AI industry and promoting one thousand small and beautiful projects, enhancing governance experience sharing and rising representation on voice of Africa in international office."

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
acts.speech: Stated that this year the D20 summit will be held on the African continent for the first time, adding that the summit supports Africa in carrying out its duties as G20 President and in leading a proper African mark in global governance.

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
acts.speech: Described China and Africa as good friends, saying they are brothers that shared a single future, and noted that under the guidance of China President Xi Jinping and African leaders, the China Africa relationship is now at its best in history ; said China has established strategic partnerships with all African countries that have diplomatic ties with it, and the China Africa Community with the Shared Future has been elevated ; indicated that Africa is a third tier of the twenty-first century and there will be no global modernization without Africa's modernization, asserting that the stability of development is quite in true humanity and the world must listen to Africa and heed its concerns.

title: U.S Congressmen Reed and Amo Underline Importance of Sustained Investment in Liberia’s Edu. Sector

acts.speaker: U.S. Senator John "Jack" Reed and U.S. Representative Gabriel Felix Kofi Amo
acts.speech: Have emphasized the importance of sustained investment in Liberia's Education Sector, and made a firm commitment to advocate for continued support to the country's Education Sector during a one-day visit to the Ministry of Education to assess the impact of USAID's support; they expressed their desire to learn as much as possible about the impacts of the recent cuts, while also hearing directly from local leaders about areas of progress.

acts.speaker: Nekpeh Forkpa, Deputy Education Minister for Administration of Liberia
acts.speech: Thanked the U.S. government for its longstanding support to Liberia's Education Sector and highlighted the critical role USAID has played in strengthening Liberia's education system, particularly through teacher training programs and institutional capacity building: "USAID's support enabled thousands of students to pursue education locally and abroad, while also helping to establish systems for data collection and analysis that inform national education policy" ; noted that the recent adjustments to USAID programming have forced Liberia to make internal shifts, including reallocating resources and assuming direct responsibility for initiatives such as school feeding.

title: Let’s establish laws to protect women in fisheries sector — Director

acts.speaker: Sarah B.M. Bamie, Upper East Regional Director of the Fisheries Commission
acts.speech: Underscored the need for a comprehensive legal framework to address the unique challenges faced by rural women in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors, including ensuring that women had equal access to resources such as land, credit and training: "By establishing laws that protect women's rights and promote gender equality, we can foster an environment where women can thrive as entrepreneurs and leaders within the fisheries value chain."

acts.speaker: Sarah B.M. Bamie, Upper East Regional Director of the Fisheries Commission
acts.speech: Called for the implementation of gender-responsive policies through which the needs and perspectives of women would be integrated into all fisheries management and development programmes, indicating that such a move would enhance women's participation in decision-making processes, thereby ensuring that their voices and contributions were heard and valued.

acts.speaker: Zinabu Abdulai, Director, Resilience and Social Inclusion, USAID-funded Market Systems and Resilience (MSR) Activity
acts.speech: Said under the MSR activity, a series of entrepreneurship initiatives have been rolled out to empower women to run their businesses effectively: "We are assisting women to do their respective trades better by adopting best practices to produce commodities and products on a large scale to meet the growing demands of the larger market."

title: US senators exempt HIV/Aids funding from initial spending cuts - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Republicans in the US Senate
acts.speech: Have said they will spare the US-backed HIV/Aids programme Pepfar from cuts, amid a larger effort to reduce government spending; senators said they would end a plan to cut $400m (£300m) from the President's Emergency Plan for Aids Relief programme, leaving total proposed cuts at $9bn.

acts.speaker: BBC
acts.speech: Reported that Republicans in the US Senate have said they will spare the US-backed HIV/Aids programme Pepfar from cuts.

acts.speaker: Multiple senators from both parties
acts.speech: Had expressed concern with cuts to Pepfar, which was launched under President George W Bush and has been credited with saving tens of millions of lives around the world.

acts.speaker: John Thune, Republican Senate majority leader
acts.speech: Said there had been a “lot of interest” in keeping the Pepfar funding intact.

acts.speaker: Susan Collins, Republican Senator from Maine
acts.speech: Told reporters after a White House lunch on Tuesday that she was “very pleased” that the cuts would be removed. Prior to the amendment, Collins had been vocal against the bill. She has not said whether the changes are enough to secure her support.

acts.speaker: Russell Vought, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director
acts.speech: Told reporters that the White House was on board with the Senate amendment, meaning that in its current form President Donald Trump would be willing to sign it.

title: Red flag hangs over HPX deal - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Critics (of the HPX deal)
acts.speech: Argue that HPX's shift toward demanding access to existing infrastructure undermines efforts to establish an equitable railway policy that allows multiple users.

acts.speaker: South Africa's Special Investigating Unit (SIU)
acts.speech: According to the SIU, Gumede orchestrated an overpriced contract worth nearly R600 million (approximately $33.6 million) through Red Roses Africa, a company closely linked to him; the investigation found that Red Roses Africa dramatically inflated the price of essential goods—selling 25-litre containers of hand sanitizer to the South African Police at a 370% markup, generating nearly R400 million ($22.4 million) in excessive profits.

acts.speaker: Robert Gumede, South African businessman and CEO of Guma Group
acts.speech: Has denied any wrongdoing.

acts.speaker: Mamaka Bility, Liberian Minister of State without Portfolio
acts.speech: Announced the deal involving the importation of 285 units of earth-moving equipment for road maintenance in Liberia, which was allegedly conducted without proper procurement procedures.

acts.speaker: Lawmakers and transparency advocates
acts.speech: Have raised concerns about the lack of legislative oversight and the potential for backdoor dealings.

acts.speaker: Senator Amara Konneh, Chair of the Liberian Senate's Public Accounts and Audit Committee
acts.speech: Has called for a thorough review of the government's engagement with foreign investors; in a social media post, Konneh questioned why the administration would enter into informal agreements with politically connected businessmen without proper due diligence.

acts.speaker: John Morlu, former Auditor General of Liberia
acts.speech: Echoed these concerns, arguing that the government should acknowledge its missteps and subject such agreements to proper legislative scrutiny. "Government business cannot be conducted based on friendships and gentleman's agreements," Morlu said. "Transparency and accountability must be the guiding principles of Liberia's economic decisions."

acts.speaker: Bronwyn Barnes, President and CEO of High Power Exploration (HPX)
acts.speech: In an August 23, 2024, communication, proposed providing budgetary support for the formation of a National Rail Authority: "We are prepared to provide budgetary support to the Government of Liberia for the formation and initial operations of the National Rail Authority. This demonstrates our commitment to ensuring that the rail management system operates under the highest international industry standards and with full transparency."

acts.speaker: Analysts and government insiders
acts.speech: Believe this "budgetary support" is merely another form of financial inducement aimed at securing favorable terms for HPX; critics point out that this commitment comes as HPX seeks to finalize its Access Agreement with the government, raising suspicions that the offer is a strategic attempt to circumvent established procurement laws.

acts.speaker: Guinean authorities
acts.speech: Have reportedly stated that they will not permit their ore to be transported through Liberia.

source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
title: Communiqué du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 05 mars 2025 - amap

acts.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
acts.speech: At the start of the session, prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died, offered his condolences to their families and wished a prompt recovery to the injured, following the tragedies that occurred at the gold-panning sites at Kokoyo, in the village of Danga, Kangaba Cercle, and at Bilalikoto, Kenieba Cercle. He instructed the Government to strengthen measures to avoid human and environmental tragedies in the country.

acts.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
acts.speech: Further instructed: the repeal of the appointment orders of the administrative officials directly involved in the occurrence of the said incidents (Prefect, Sub-prefects, heads of the Security Forces - Police, Gendarmerie, Guard - of the local Water and Forestry services, the Sanitation and Pollution and Nuisance Control services, and the sub-regional Geology and Mines services); the revision of certain legal texts in order, among other things, to put an end to settlements in the environmental field, to facilitate the recovery of equipment involved in gold panning and its transfer to state property; the suspension of artisanal mining exploitation permits granted to persons of foreign nationality; and the launch of the procedure to dissolve the communal council of Dabia.

acts.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
acts.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted draft texts relating to the ratification of the budget support agreement including a loan, signed in Bamako on 26 February 2025 between the Government of the Republic of Mali and the Qatar Fund for Development, under which the Fund grants Mali budget support of 50 million US dollars, about 31.4475 billion CFA francs, comprising a loan of 45 million US dollars; this budget support will help sustain the humanitarian aid, economic development and health sectors, notably the supply of foodstuffs, the construction of water points, the rehabilitation and construction of infrastructure and the strengthening of the means of action of the Administration and local authorities.

acts.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
acts.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordinance amending Law No. 06-067 of 29 December 2006, as amended, on the General Tax Code, modifying articles 240 and 425 to adapt the General Tax Code to the new Mining Code, extending the scope of the Special Tax on Certain Products to marble, gold ingots and other mining products, reducing the minimum rate of that tax for those products from 5% to 3%, and extending stamp duty on export intentions to all mining products.

acts.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
acts.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree setting the deadlines and procedures for concluding agreements between the National Health Insurance Fund and health providers; a draft decree approving the standard management-delegation agreements under the Universal Health Insurance Scheme; and a draft decree setting the principles of preferential pricing and the coverage rates for health care services under the Universal Health Insurance Scheme.

acts.speaker: Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of Mali's participation in the "High-Level Segment" on the human rights situation, held from 24 to 26 February 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland, where Mali addressed the Human Rights Council with strong messages: reaffirmation of the Government's determination to implement all the recommendations accepted during the Universal Periodic Review and the commitments made at the high-level event "Human Rights 75"; the remarkable improvement in the overall security situation thanks to the efforts of the Armed and Security Forces and their strategic partners; the pooling of defence resources by the Heads of State of the Alliance of Sahel States in order to fight terrorism effectively; the appropriation of the endogenous resolution of multidimensional crises through the ongoing drafting of the National Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation; the Government's determination to fight impunity in all its forms; the reiteration of the appeal to the international community to avoid the politicisation and instrumentalisation of human rights; and the reaffirmation of the Government of Mali's willingness to continue its cooperation with all human rights promotion and protection mechanisms, in strict respect for its sovereignty and the vital interests of the Malian people. On the margins of the High-Level Segment, the minister had an audience with the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights on Mali's efforts and progress in human rights and the resumption and strengthening of cooperative relations between Mali and the Office of the High Commissioner.

acts.speaker: Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his mission to Timbuktu from 25 to 27 February 2025, whose objectives included assessing the state of progress of the operationalisation of the University of Timbuktu, exchanging with administrative, customary and educational authorities, and visiting the site earmarked for the construction of the University's infrastructure. He reported that the department had appointed a Coordinator in charge of operationalisation activities, renovated certain administrative and teaching premises and held the first session of the Board of Directors of the Ahmed Baba Institute of Higher Islamic Studies and Research of Timbuktu, and that the mission noted with interest and satisfaction the progress of the operationalisation process and the involvement of the actors concerned.

acts.speaker: Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers about the student meetings called "Citizen Masterclass", organised with the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research as a mission of civic and citizenship education, personal development and patriotic engagement to make students "model and responsible citizens", consisting of the minister delivering modules on citizenship in public or private universities during the 2025 academic year in order to strengthen the role of students in the refoundation of Mali.

acts.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his participation in the 19th edition of the National Cereals Exchange, launched officially from 19 to 21 February 2025, whose objective was to contribute to the promotion and valorisation of locally produced cereals; the 2025 edition recorded the signing of 61 contracts for a total of 1,184,410,000 CFA francs, against 261 contracts worth 1,070,988,394 CFA francs for the 2024 edition, and recommendations were formulated for the Ministry of Agriculture, the Food Security Commission and the Permanent Assembly of Chambers of Agriculture of Mali.

acts.speaker: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the launch of the recruitment process for unemployed young graduates for the 14th contingent of the vocational training internship programme of the Agency for the Promotion of Youth Employment, with the recruitment of 2,500 new interns beginning with a call for applications on 13 February 2025 and the opening of application submissions on 17 February 2025; by the closing date of 22 February 2025, 15,021 applications had been registered nationwide, comprising 6,791 male applications (45.22%) and 8,230 female applications (54.78%), with new interns to be assigned to the Institutions of the Republic, ministerial departments, local authorities, consular and umbrella organisations and non-governmental organisations.

acts.speaker: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of a field mission to the Gao Region from 27 February to 1 March 2025 to convey to local populations the message of comfort, reassurance and solidarity of the Transition Authorities and to gather their priority needs in skills development and socio-professional integration, particularly for young people and women; activities included the inauguration of a new building for the Regional Directorate of Employment and Vocational Training, the opening of three Youth Guidance Spaces, the launch of the "driving licence" operation and the handover of integration kits to training beneficiaries. The mission also gathered the expectations of local actors, which include the continuation of peace and security initiatives, adapting training provision to labour market needs, specific support for young people and women, and the introduction of concrete measures to reduce unemployment.

acts.speaker: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the holding in Mali of the 1st edition of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation's Africa Investment Forum, decided at the 47th Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers held on 27 and 28 November 2020 in Niger, with Mali selected to host the 2025 event at the 50th Session held in August 2024 in Yaounde, Cameroon. The forum, on the theme "Unlocking investment potential in Africa", aims to strengthen economic cooperation within the OIC and attract investors to Africa, will address themes such as investment financing, insurance and gender issues, and offers Mali an opportunity to promote its economic attractiveness and mobilise public and private investment.

acts.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
acts.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the country's epidemiological situation, marked by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with the previous week.

acts.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
acts.speech: Called on the population to strictly respect the measures for the prevention of and fight against dengue.

title: The Aid Paradox: How Malawi Can Turn the US Aid Suspension into an Economic Opportunity

acts.speaker: President Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
acts.speech: The order said the “foreign aid industry and bureaucracy are not aligned with American interests and in many cases antithetical to American values” and “serve to destabilize world peace by promoting ideas in foreign countries that are directly inverse to harmonious and stable relations internal to and among countries.” Trump declared that “no further United States foreign assistance shall be disbursed in a manner that is not fully aligned with the foreign policy of the President of the United States.”

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
acts.speech: Told members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during his confirmation hearing last week that “every dollar we spend, every program we fund, and every policy we pursue must be justified with the answer to three simple questions.”

title: Global Economic Downturn Looms From Iran-Israel Conflict

acts.speaker: Kabalano Rampa, international trade expert
acts.speech: In a televised interview on Monday, stated that Botswana is unlikely to feel the immediate effects of the impending fuel crisis: "We will definitely not experience the effects immediately in regards to our fuel prices going up as there are delayed and buffer effects." ; "We will experience them at a later time. It gives us an opportunity to start acting and preparing now."

acts.speaker: Kabalano Rampa, international trade expert
acts.speech: Noted that the proposed joint oil refinery deal between Namibia and Botswana could prove critical in the long run but said that it will be some time and cost before it is in place; he added that Botswana has the capacity to switch to solar and wind energy as alternative sources of fuel, and recommended intra-African trade as a means to mitigating the economic effects of the war.

acts.speaker: Iran (government threat)
acts.speech: In response to airstrikes by the United States early Sunday, has threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz through which 20 percent of the world's oil supply of 20 million barrels pass per day.

title: Don’t misuse resources,cyclone survivors told - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Davie Mlose, Zomba City Council director of administration
acts.speech: Has warned Cyclone Jude survivors in Zomba against misusing resources they receive from well-wishers; said relief funds from non-governmental organisations (NGOs) are meant to help survivors get back to their feet and rebuild their homes; said failure to utilise the money will push more people into poverty. “Invest the funds in sustainable activities that can restore your previous livelihoods.”

acts.speaker: Blessings Mlowoka, Self Help Africa humanitarian committee coordinator
acts.speech: Said the funds are meant to help households build their resilience against climate shocks. “The funds should boost the survivors’ capacities and buy utensils and repair their houses. Stable families are essential to development.”

acts.speaker: Esinala Kumtembwe, a beneficiary from Mpunga Township
acts.speech: Said part of her house collapsed and destroyed utensils and foodstuffs. “I will, therefore, use the funds for its intended purpose, to repair my house and buy utensils.”

acts.speaker: Esinala Kumtembwe, a beneficiary from Mpunga Township
acts.speech: Appealed to other well-wishers to emulate the example set by Self Help Africa and reach out to the survivors with humanitarian assistance.

title: Cyclone Chido death toll reaches 13, 29 injured - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma) (update/statement signed by Commissioner Charles Kalemba)
acts.speech: Said in an update that 227 people have been displaced while the number of injured persons has also increased from 16 to 29, and that the number of affected households has risen from 7 721 to 10 159; the death toll from Cyclone Chido has reached 13 from seven reported on Tuesday.

acts.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
acts.speech: Clarified in an interview that the figures reported on Monday and Tuesday were preliminary while yesterday's report was the final one: "It means we have collected all the information that we needed to collect from councils."

acts.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
acts.speech: Said Dodma has not opened evacuation camps for the displaced people since they are staying with their relatives in their villages.

acts.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Dodma Commissioner
acts.speech: On humanitarian assistance, said the needs are within Dodma's contingency plan and delivery of relief items in Southern Region districts was expected to be completed yesterday while Central Region districts will receive items today.

acts.speaker: Martin Chiwanda, Machinga District Council spokesperson
acts.speech: Said in an interview that the district has recorded two deaths and five injuries with 557 households affected: "The people have received psychosocial support, but we are yet to provide them with food and other relief items as we are still mobilising the resources."

acts.speaker: Faith Khamula, Blantyre District Council disaster risk management officer
acts.speech: Said the council has already started distributing a 50 kilogramme bag of maize to each of the affected 502 households in the district.

title: Chakwera hails organisations for food support

acts.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
acts.speech: Expressed his appreciation to local organizations and development partners for their unwavering support and dedication in ensuring food availability to Malawians during this period of food security crisis ; recognised significant contributions that Malawi has received from various development partners through the World Food Programme (WFP) ; specifically commended partners such as Good Neighbors Malawi, Nkhoma Synod, Emerging Donor March Fund, Save the Children, United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), BHA, FAO, Mary's Meals, USAID, JBJ Foundation, ISRAID, and Caritas partners for their steadfast support ; urged the partners to continue their efforts in mobilising support for Malawi from across the globe to alleviate the lives of Malawians.

acts.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
acts.speech: Stressed the importance of seeking international support to address the humanitarian crisis the country is currently grappling with.

acts.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
acts.speech: Said WFP will publicly disclose the details of how and where the aid has been distributed.

acts.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
acts.speech: Pointed out that Malawi has received substantial financial support from governments around the world through the World Food Program (WFP), including 11.8 million dollars from Sweden and the Netherlands, 7 million dollars from the United States, 3.8 million dollars from the United Kingdom, 1.9 million dollars from Japan, 1.6 million dollars from France, 1.5 million dollars from South Korea, and 1.07 million dollars from Germany; additionally, Norway and Iceland contributed 950,000 dollars, Denmark provided 750,000 dollars, Ireland donated 556,000 dollars, Switzerland contributed 500,000 dollars, and the African Development Bank donated 1 million dollars.

title: 19.2 million Nigerians use health insurance - Official

acts.speaker: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
acts.speech: says 19.2 million citizens have enrolled on health insurance schemes surpassing its 2024 target.

acts.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
acts.speech: disclosed that 19.2 million citizens have enrolled on health insurance schemes; said this feat was a significant milestone in the NHIA's efforts to expand access to healthcare for Nigerians under the health insurance scheme, that the achievement surpasses the 2024 target and places the nation at 95 per cent of its ambitious 2027 presidential coverage goal, and attributed the success to strategic policy reforms, effective collaborations with stakeholders, and an unwavering commitment to universal health coverage: "We are proud to announce that 19.2 million Nigerians have been covered by health insurance. This surpasses our 2024 target and places us within striking distance of achieving 95 per cent of the 2027 presidential target."

acts.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
acts.speech: said that the NHIA had worked tirelessly to implement innovative strategies: "This includes the expansion of the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund (BHCPF) and partnerships with state health insurance agencies to ensure affordable and accessible healthcare for all Nigerians, especially the most vulnerable populations." ; said the milestone reflects the federal government's commitment to delivering quality healthcare as outlined in the National Health Act.

acts.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
acts.speech: urged state governments and private sector stakeholders to intensify efforts to sustain the momentum and bridge the remaining gaps in health insurance coverage.

acts.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
acts.speech: said that the achievement came amid ongoing challenges in Nigeria's healthcare sector, including funding limitations, infrastructure deficits, and inadequate human resources, but expressed optimism, noting that the agency's strategic roadmap for 2025-2027 includes scaling up digital enrollment processes and integrating informal sector workers into the insurance scheme.

acts.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
acts.speech: "With the theme of this year's UHC Day, health should reflect the type of government the country has and must make decisions that represent its aspirations. We should prioritise Primary Health Care (PHC) as the bedrock of our health system."

acts.speaker: Muhammad Lawal, Commissioner for Health in Yobe
acts.speech: said that UHC was a reality and we must work towards it ; said that there should be no negotiation for the health of the people, especially the vulnerable segment of the population.

acts.speaker: Bolanle Olusola-Faleye, USAID LHSS Project
acts.speech: said that it was a remarkable time to celebrate 2024 UHC Day with the presence of reforms such as the Sector Wide Approach (SWAP) ; said that SWAP had shown evidence of success in the states through the harmonised Annual Operational Plan (AOP), ensuring alignment of priorities.

acts.speaker: Public health advocates
acts.speech: have lauded the progress, describing it as a significant step toward achieving UHC in Nigeria.

acts.speaker: Garfa Alawode, Co-convener of the UHC2023 Forum
acts.speech: said that it was a commendable accomplishment; however, said that more needed to be done to ensure that every Nigerian could access affordable, quality healthcare services, and called for sustained political will, increased funding, and effective monitoring: "This is to ensure that the gains are not only maintained but also translated into improved health outcomes for all citizens."

acts.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
acts.speech: reports that the roundtable was part of the activities lined up for the commemoration of the 2024 UHC Day ; recalls that UHC Day is a global advocacy day to raise awareness about the importance of equitable, affordable, and accessible healthcare for all individuals without financial hardship.

title: TRIBUNE : La diplomatie humaniste et son impact sur le renforcement des relations internationales

acts.speaker: Dya-Eddin Bamakhrama, Ambassador of Djibouti to Riyadh (opinion column)
