acts.speech: Argues that alongside conventional diplomacy there exists second-track diplomacy, including humanist diplomacy and popular diplomacy or “soft power”, and that humanist diplomacy is one of the strongest and most effective diplomatic fields, capable of changing the reality on the ground and accomplishing actions sometimes inaccessible to conventional diplomacy ; says that states and decision-making centres continue to play a decisive role in removing the obstacles facing national and international humanitarian organisations, placing their action in an institutional and legal framework and protecting them from security and political infiltration and from corruption ; cites the Republic of Djibouti, which took an early interest in assisting refugees and preserving their dignity - welcoming those fleeing the 1977 Ogaden war despite the modesty of its resources, and today receiving and housing tens of thousands of Yemeni refugees under the personal attention and follow-up of President Ismail Omar Guelleh - and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as a leader in humanist diplomacy, particularly through the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre ; calls for working together to remove obstacles hindering humanitarian action, promote access to zones of conflict, offer more guarantees of protection to humanitarian personnel including diplomatic and political immunities, give increased attention to dialogue and cooperation between humanitarian workers and local authorities, organise forums and workshops for diplomats and humanitarian agents, and give broader space to academic and research efforts to lay the scientific foundations of humanist diplomacy.

title: M1 rehabilitation faces setback - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Katawa, group village head
acts.speech: Said in an interview yesterday that people around Kakoloha have been blaming the cracks in their houses on the blasts and are demanding compensation.

acts.speaker: Report by Robert Chidothe, Rumphi Community Development officer
acts.speech: Shows that communities wanted the company to construct a proper drainage system, rehabilitate access roads and provide building materials for a local primary school: "For instance, the potable water system installed was placed near a sewer area. The marketplace was described as too small and poorly built. The community expressed deep disappointment and a sense of betrayal."

acts.speaker: He Chuanfeng, project manager for China Henan International Cooperation Group (Chicco)
acts.speech: Said people were failing to understand that development assistance is not obligatory: "As a contractor, it is not obligatory to provide assistance to the local community, if this is done it is done for social upliftment and a gesture from the company."

acts.speaker: Engineer Ammiel Champiti, Roads Authority chief executive officer
acts.speech: Said the issues for Lot 4 were identical to Lots 1, 2 and 3, but added that people around Lot 4 are motivated by "baseless demands" as efforts being made by people are criminal in nature.

title: News and Periodicals Enterprise (NPE)

acts.speaker: Local journalists and media analysts (interviews conducted in May 2024 and February 2025)
acts.speech: Indicate that over 80% of NPE's funding is drawn directly from the state budget.

acts.speaker: Local journalists interviewed in May 2024 and February 2025
acts.speech: Affirm that the organization's editorial mission is to promote the policies, positions, and narratives of the state.

acts.speaker: Ministry of Information of Myanmar
acts.speech: According to the Ministry of Information, NPE's core mandate is to "focus on publishing newspapers that are in line with the vision of the Ministry of Information to inform, educate and entertain."

acts.speaker: Maung Maung Ohn, Union Minister for Information
acts.speech: In July 2025, visited NPE's Yangon offices and urged staff to report with "open eyes and ears," to remain accurate, and to understand state policies thoroughly. He emphasized the Prime Minister's high regard for print media as a source of "trustworthy and reliable information."

title: Binwell calls for national unity amid USAID funding halt

acts.speaker: Binwell Mpundu, Nkana Independent Member of Parliament (Zambia)
acts.speech: Made a passionate appeal for unity following the US government's decision to halt all USAID-funded programmes for 85 days, and expressed deep concern about the impact on people living with HIV and AIDS and others dependent on US-sponsored projects. "The situation has become dire, especially for those living with HIV and AIDS." ; "Can you imagine how many of our brothers and sisters are employed through these projects?"

title: Electric Grid Distribution Code Draws to Close

acts.speaker: Hailu Assefa, member of the (Transmission Grid Code) Review Committee
acts.speech: Said that though the Authority has finalised nearly the entire process for the Distribution Code, it is still working on the Transmission Code: “We want to table them for approval together. It’ll take another month to wrap up the inputs and get it finalised by consultants.”

acts.speaker: Bahru Oljira, competency certification & technical regulation director at the Ethiopian Electric Authority
acts.speech: Said the Code was supposed to be tabled for approval to the Authority in the last fiscal year, but the pandemic has slowed down the process: “Transmission and distribution are dealt with in different codes for simplicity.”

acts.speaker: Mekdes Mezgebu, consultant and attorney at law at Mesfin Tafesse & Associates
acts.speech: Said the Code has been eagerly anticipated for a long time and its formation will bring predictability to the playing field: “Private players will know what the requirements are to join the sector. This will, in turn, boost investor confidence.”

title: Jinsi ya Kuwasaidia Watoto Kupunguza Matumizi ya Vifaa vya Kidijitali Wakati wa Likizo - The Chanzo

acts.speaker: American Academy of Pediatrics (research)
acts.speech: Research by the American Academy of Pediatrics shows that excessive screen use can weaken memory, concentration, and the ability to solve and cope with challenges.

title: PNUD/ Djibouti : Un partenariat pour la reprise socio-économique

acts.speaker: Ilyas Moussa Dawaleh, Djiboutian Minister of Economy and Finance in charge of Industry
acts.speech: Stated that "Should new resources be mobilised through this partnership, modifications may be made. By signing a single document, we will be able to have a programme approach rather than a project approach." ; welcomed the good collaboration existing between Djibouti and the UNDP, which supports the government in many areas focused on socio-economic development: "Social entrepreneurship is our priority, with the aim of creating as many jobs as possible."

acts.speaker: Fatima Elsheikh, UNDP Resident Representative in Djibouti
acts.speech: Congratulated the President of the Republic on his inauguration at the head of the country for a new term ; recalled that the signing of this portfolio will have as its mission to respond to several projects focused on local micro-enterprises in order to mitigate the impacts of Covid-19 and recover quickly from the socio-economic crisis.

title: Cerca de 50 civis mortos em ataques no Burkina Faso desde Maio

acts.speaker: Human Rights Watch (statement)
acts.speech: “The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), affiliated with Al-Qaeda, attacked the town of Djibo, in the Sahel region, on 11 May, and the village of Youba, in the northern region, on 3 August, killing at least 40 civilians” ; “The Islamic State in the Sahel (IS) attacked a civilian convoy delivering humanitarian aid to the besieged town of Gorom Gorom, in the Sahel region, on 28 July, killing at least nine civilians.”

acts.speaker: Residents of the village of Youba
acts.speech: Explained to HRW that the extremists wanted to “punish the local community for not having obeyed GSIM’s instructions to abandon certain crops.”

acts.speaker: GSIM (Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims), in a response to HRW on 15 August
acts.speech: Maintained that it had “never intentionally targeted civilians,” speaking of “unfounded allegations” or “at most, incidents caused by stray bullets,” of which it says it has no knowledge.

acts.speaker: Ilaria Allegrozzi, Human Rights Watch Sahel researcher
acts.speech: Considers that “the authorities must guarantee better protection for all civilians in danger.”

acts.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, head of the junta
acts.speech: On taking power at the end of September 2022, promised to restore security within a few months.

acts.speaker: Human Rights Watch
acts.speech: Asks the authorities to “investigate the abuses, particularly those committed by the military and allied militias, and prosecute those responsible”; observes that “the Government has increasingly attacked civilians during” counterterrorism operations.

acts.speaker: Acled (organisation that counts conflict victims worldwide)
acts.speech: Reports more than 26,000 people killed in terrorist attacks — civilians and military — since 2015 in Burkina Faso, more than half of them in the last three years.

title: "We're not talking this lightly." - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Says it does not take lightly the potential strict travel restrictions on Liberia by United States diplomats and security officials.

acts.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Termed the potential visa ban a complete surprise while urging Liberians to remain calm as the government engages the US State Department to ascertain the facts surrounding the matter; argued that since taking office she has worked with the U.S. government to address some of the requirements outlined in the potential visa ban through formal letters and meetings in Washington, D.C. ; "The information received in the news and social media was a surprise. When the information came out, we contacted the U.S. Embassy in Monrovia, and they said that they had no information in relation to this report" ; "This was also reported in the New York Times newspaper. We are not taking this lightly whether it's true or misleading."

acts.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Monrovia
acts.speech: Said that they had no information in relation to this report (as recounted by Minister Beysolow-Nyanti).

acts.speaker: International reports (unnamed)
acts.speech: According to international reports, U.S. diplomats and security officials have developed a plan to impose strict travel restrictions on citizens from 43 countries, including Liberia, categorizing them into red, orange and yellow lists; the report further indicated that the proposed restrictions stem from concerns over weak or corrupt governance and security challenges in the affected nations.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
acts.speech: Signed an executive order upon taking office in January instructing officials to compile the lists within 60 days, and described the list as necessary to protect the US from potential security threats.

acts.speaker: Liberian government officials (non-response)
acts.speech: Have yet to comment on this development; The New Dawn searched official U.S. government sources but found no confirmation of the policy.

title: Mozambique: Committee on Budgets of the European Parliament visits EUTM MOZ

acts.speaker: Colonel Daniele Pepe, EUTM MOZ Deputy Mission Force Commander
acts.speech: Briefed the Committee on EUTM MOZ' roles, capabilities, mission, current activities and the main ongoing projects within the Headquarters and the three training camps located in Katembe, Chimoio and Mavalane.

title: La Russie se prépare à combler le vide laissé par l’USAID

acts.speaker: The National Interest (British newspaper article)
acts.speech: Reported that, unlike Washington, which centralised its aid through USAID, Moscow relies on a more flexible and multipolar model, mobilising more than a dozen ministries and public organisations, and that these entities run various programmes in the fields of development, culture, education and humanitarian assistance in the event of disaster.

acts.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
acts.speech: Estimate that Russia's annual aid reached more than one billion dollars before the war in Ukraine.

acts.speaker: Evgeny Primakov, Director of the Rossotrudnichestvo agency (Russian Cooperation)
acts.speech: In an interview, gave an overview of Russia's future foreign aid apparatus, indicating that the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs is preparing a new architecture for foreign aid, inspired by the USAID model but adapted to Russian realities, with the aim of grouping efforts under a structured entity and of increasing its funding.

acts.speaker: Evgeny Primakov, Director of the Rossotrudnichestvo agency (Russian Cooperation)
acts.speech: Acknowledged that, in a context marked by a costly war, priorities are being readjusted, but nevertheless insisted on the need to target concrete and measurable socio-political results, stressing that foreign aid must serve the country's interests — not as a simple act of charity, but as a strategic, win-win lever.

acts.speaker: Evgeny Primakov, Director of the Rossotrudnichestvo agency (Russian Cooperation)
acts.speech: Also mentioned competition with China in certain areas, notably in the matter of student scholarships ; “For now, we hope to be able to compete with a country like Finland,” he indicated.

acts.speaker: Certain Western media (unnamed)
acts.speech: Have attempted to discredit Rossotrudnichestvo's activities by accusing it of serving as a front for propaganda and intelligence operations.

acts.speaker: European Union
acts.speech: Sanctioned the agency in 2022, because of what it claims was the launch of a network of “agents of influence” to mobilise support for the war in Ukraine.

title: Protesters accuse govt of blocking LEC price hike march

acts.speaker: Balefe Sekhamane, leader of the march organizers
acts.speech: "We were asked to go to the office of the prime minister to inquire if he would be available on the day that we are intending to hand him the letter, when we got there we were told to come back last week Thursdays for negotiations." ; said that at the negotiations at the premier's office they were told to write "a fully detailed letter and bring it back to the office", and that the response to their letter could not be guaranteed since "the office of the prime minister is very busy"; said they left the prime minister's office without reaching an agreement because they believe the office was merely trying to frustrate the planned march. ; "We presented the letter as written, but they told us to go back and submit a more detailed one. It felt like a waste of time - just a tactic to postpone the march, which was supposed to happen on June 18." ; "The officers couldn't help us or approve our request."

acts.speaker: Balefe Sekhamane, leader of the march organizers
acts.speech: "Since the Prime Minister's office refuses to confirm when they will respond - what if they take two years? We have advised ourselves to approach the courts." ; "The police asked us to confirm whether the prime minister's office would be present during the letter handover. It felt like we were being forced to seek their permission." ; "It's clear they are deceiving us, making us rewrite a letter with no guarantee of a timely response." ; "The march will proceed once the court intervenes." ; "We won't be silenced. If the prime minister won't listen, we will take our demands to the streets - and the courts."

acts.speaker: Balefe Sekhamane, leader of the march organizers
acts.speech: "First, they delay our protest. Then, they ignore our demands. It's clear they're shielding the powerful."

acts.speaker: Protesters / march organizers (Disgruntled Basotho)
acts.speech: claim authorities are deliberately obstructing their planned protest to the Prime Minister's office and allege these demands are unnecessary hurdles to silence dissent over LEC's mismanagement and rising costs; demand a 30 percent reduction in domestic electricity tariffs and accountability for alleged embezzlement at the LEC, with stolen funds recovered from fraudsters; allege that the prime minister's office is protecting LEC leadership rather than addressing corruption. "People are tired of corruption. If the government doesn't act, protests could escalate."

acts.speaker: An LEC insider who requested anonymity
acts.speech: "Money meant to maintain infrastructure and keep prices stable has been looted. Now, ordinary Basotho pay the price through higher bills and unreliable supply."

acts.speaker: Lineo Khoarai, caller on a local radio station's phone-in morning talk show
acts.speech: "If there's nothing to hide, why no investigation? The longer this goes unchecked, the more it looks like a cover-up."

title: Burkina Faso : Les défis de la réhabilitation minière au cœur de la SAMAO 2025 à Ouagadougou

acts.speaker: Doulaye Sanou, president of the SAMAO 2025 organising committee
acts.speech: Said this edition will constitute a framework for exchanging experiences between public and private actors from various countries for the sustainable management of mineral resources. ; "It will serve as a platform for mining industry actors to discuss the issue of the rehabilitation and closure of mines, with the future of local communities as the backdrop." ; Indicated that at least 2,000 participants from Burkina Faso, the sub-region and the rest of the world are expected at SAMAO, at the Ouaga 2000 International Conference Centre; added that a session will be devoted to presenting innovations for more environmentally friendly mining, and that the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) will be honoured through a session dedicated to their achievements in mine rehabilitation.

acts.speaker: Doulaye Sanou, president of the SAMAO 2025 organising committee
acts.speech: Explained that the pre-SAMAO workshop aims to contribute to the development of local materials in Burkina Faso's cement industry. ; "It will thus make it possible, among other things, to make known the existing potential of quarry substances that can be used in cement manufacturing and to explore the economic and industrial opportunities linked to the exploitation of local resources in order to reduce dependence on imports and strengthen the capacity of national industries."

title: Private sector engagement crucial for sustainable healthcare in Tanzania - Daily News

acts.speaker: Dr Rashid Mfaume, Director of Health, Social Welfare and Nutrition Services at the President's Office (Regional Administration and Local Government Authority)
acts.speech: Said that currently about 85% of health care services in Dar es Salaam are provided by private health care facilities ; ‘The government has shown political will and implemented policies that create a conducive environment for private sector stakeholders to work towards achieving their goals while collaborating with the government’

acts.speaker: Dr Denis Mzaga, Director of Strategic Information for USAID Afya Yangu Southern
acts.speech: ‘USAID Afya Yangu is providing support to 752 Health Facilities (HFs) in 6 regions. Of the supported HFs, 145 (19.3%) are from private with 80,329 (27%) clients on ART which is more than any of the supported regions (Iringa is the largest with 65,468 clients)’

acts.speaker: Kenneth Chima, Deputy Chief of Party for USAID Kizazi Hodari Southern Zone
acts.speech: Said despite these achievements, the projects still faces challenges due to limited funding and competing from the government priorities.

acts.speaker: Godfrey Nyombi, USAID Tanzania Head of System Strengthening
acts.speech: Said that USAID works in supporting government health projects that touches lives of Tanzanians from grassroots level with an aim of improving lives. "USAID is very proud of this health forum which highlight the achievements of projects that we have been funding. We will continue working and collaborating with the Tanzania government for purpose of making lives of Tanzanians and especially those living in rural areas better."

title: Consultative Meeting between Somali Religious Leaders and the Somali Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)

acts.speaker: Mohamud Ma'alin, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)
acts.speech: Opened the meeting by emphasizing the importance of engaging religious scholars and the community in SoDMA's decision-making processes; highlighted that since its inception in 2022, SoDMA has consistently valued the insights of religious scholars; also addressed the current vulnerabilities caused by the extremist group Al-Shabaab, which has disrupted farming and displaced hundreds of thousands, exacerbating the humanitarian crisis.

acts.speaker: Abdirahman, Member of Parliament
acts.speech: Commended SoDMA's efforts, noting the significant benefits that have accrued to the population since the agency's re-establishment two years ago; stressed the importance of providing security as a prerequisite to effective humanitarian assistance.

acts.speaker: Ali Hagi Dahir, Chair of the Parliamentary Committee on Justice and Religious Affairs
acts.speech: Emphasized Somalia's rich agricultural potential and urged religious leaders to raise awareness about farming; called on SoDMA to facilitate agricultural activities to enhance self-sufficiency.

acts.speaker: Sheikh Ali Wajis, prominent religious leader
acts.speech: Reinforced the need for humanitarian efforts, suggesting the imposition of a 2% salary contribution for such causes; proposed that business communities should also pledge regular contributions and recommended that the President be accompanied by humanitarian teams, led by SoDMA, during official visits; also advocated for relocating IDP camps from the capital to allow displaced individuals to return home.

acts.speaker: Faduma Adle, Chair of Somali Women Religious Scholars
acts.speech: Advocated for the integration of religious leaders into SoDMA's framework, suggesting the establishment of a dedicated department for them.

title: The Impact of Hate Speech on the Electoral Integrity in The Gambia - The Alkamba Times

acts.speaker: Merriam-Webster online dictionary
acts.speech: Categorizes hate speech as a noun referring to speech that expresses hatred toward a particular group of people.

acts.speaker: Cambridge online dictionary
acts.speech: Defines it as public speech that expresses hate or encourages violence toward a person or group based on characteristics such as race, religion, sex, or sexual orientation.

acts.speaker: United Nations Strategy and Plan of Action on Hate Speech
acts.speech: Defines hate speech as “any kind of communication in speech, writing or behaviour, that attacks or uses pejorative or discriminatory language with reference to a person or a group on the basis of who they are, in other words, based on their religion, ethnicity, nationality, race, colour, descent, gender or other identity factor.”

acts.speaker: Council of Europe
acts.speech: Hate speech is understood as all types of expression that incite, promote, spread or justify violence, hatred or discrimination against a person or group of persons, or that denigrates them, by reason of their real or attributed personal characteristics or status such as “race”, colour, language, religion, nationality, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, sex, gender identity and sexual orientation.

acts.speaker: Article 19
acts.speech: Describes hate speech as an “emotive concept [with] no universally accepted definition”; a term used to describe broad discourse that is extremely negative and constitutes a threat to social peace.

acts.speaker: Pippa Norris (2014)
acts.speech: Emphasizes the importance of maintaining political legitimacy and adhering to global democratic standards, noting that deviations can undermine the integrity of democratic systems.

acts.speaker: Steven Levitsky and Daniel Ziblatt (2018), “How Democracies Die”
acts.speech: Discuss how political actors who treat rivals as enemies and intimidate the free press contribute to the weakening of democratic institutions.

acts.speaker: UN Report (2011)
acts.speech: Documented that Kenya's 2007–2008 post-election violence resulted in the deaths of over 1,100 people and the displacement of more than 600,000 others, with targeted killings, sexual violence and destruction of property as ethnic rivalries were exacerbated by inflammatory rhetoric from political leaders ; that Côte d'Ivoire's 2010–2011 post-election crisis led to the deaths of approximately 3,000 people, the raping of over 150 women and the displacement of more than one million, with hate speech playing a central role in fuelling tensions ; and that Rwanda's 1994 genocide, in which radio broadcasts and political propaganda encouraged ethnic hatred, culminated in the mass killing of over 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus in just 100 days.

acts.speaker: Yahya Jammeh, former President of The Gambia
acts.speech: At a political rally in Tallinding in June 2016 referred to the Mandinka ethnic group as “enemies, foreigners” and threatened to kill them one by one, vowing to place them “where even a fly cannot see them”; frequently used public platforms to brand political opponents as “traitors” and “enemies of the state”, often targeting specific ethnic groups to stoke fear and loyalty among his supporters.

acts.speaker: Human Rights Watch (2016)
acts.speech: Documented Jammeh's June 2016 Tallinding rally remarks describing the Mandinka ethnic group as “enemies, foreigners” and threatening to kill them one by one.

acts.speaker: Amnesty International (2016)
acts.speech: The 2016 death of Solo Sandeng, an opposition activist arrested and killed in custody after leading a protest for electoral reform, underscores the “lethal consequences of Jammeh's regime and its hate-driven propaganda.”

acts.speaker: Paradigm Initiative (2021 report)
acts.speech: Confirmed that much of the hate speech in The Gambia, which is usually ethnic or political in nature, occurs on social media platforms like Meta (Facebook) and WhatsApp, and highlighted how political supporters use these platforms to target opponents with derogatory language, false accusations and incitements to violence, often under the cloak of anonymity.

acts.speaker: Malagen (2023 media monitoring report)
acts.speech: Underscored the prevalence of hate speech on social media, noting that political supporters frequently use these platforms to disseminate inflammatory content.

acts.speaker: International Republican Institute (2021)
acts.speech: Reported that during the 2021 presidential election campaign supporters of the ruling National People's Party (NPP) and the opposition United Democratic Party (UDP) engaged in online vitriol, with some posts inciting violence against perceived political or ethnic adversaries.

acts.speaker: African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance (ACDEG) (African Union, 2007)
acts.speech: Underscores the responsibility of member states to prevent incitement to violence and discrimination, particularly during electoral processes, as a means of safeguarding democracy and human rights.

acts.speaker: United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Promotion and Protection of Freedom of Opinion and Expression (UN Human Rights Council, 2017)
acts.speech: Highlighted the dangers of weaponizing speech to erode democratic governance, warning that unchecked hate speech can contribute to polarization, political instability, and even mass atrocities.

acts.speaker: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM, 2014) and the Global Network Against Hate Speech (2020)
acts.speech: Documented instances where inflammatory rhetoric has preceded violence, as seen in the Rwandan genocide and ethnic conflicts in the Balkans.

acts.speaker: International IDEA (2021)
acts.speech: The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) possesses regulatory mechanisms to oversee campaign rhetoric, but enforcement has been inconsistent, largely due to political considerations and institutional weaknesses.

acts.speaker: Gambia Information and Communications Act (2009)
acts.speech: The country's media regulatory framework lacks explicit provisions on hate speech in digital spaces, thereby allowing unregulated online discourse to flourish.

acts.speaker: Center for Democracy and Development (CDD) in West Africa (2022 study)
acts.speech: Highlighted the increasing use of digital platforms to propagate hate speech in the region, often exacerbating ethnic and political tensions.

acts.speaker: Kenya National Cohesion and Integration Act (2008)
acts.speech: Criminalizes hate speech and includes provisions allowing for the electoral disqualification of candidates found guilty of inflammatory rhetoric.

acts.speaker: South Africa Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act (PEPUDA, 2000)
acts.speech: Enforces strict provisions against hate speech in political contexts, offering a legal framework that balances free speech with the need to prevent harmful rhetoric.

acts.speaker: UNESCO (2021)
acts.speech: Empirical evidence from countries that have implemented such measures suggests that proactive legal intervention, combined with public awareness campaigns and independent regulatory bodies, can effectively mitigate the spread of divisive rhetoric and enhance social cohesion.

acts.speaker: International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES, 2020)
acts.speech: Emphasizes that clear legal frameworks are essential in countering hate speech during elections, making such a bill a necessary measure.

acts.speaker: Council of Europe (2019 toolkit on combating hate speech during elections)
acts.speech: Highlights the importance of equipping electoral management bodies with the authority to enforce such regulations effectively.

acts.speaker: United Nations (2019)
acts.speech: Underscores the role of education in fostering inclusive societies and reducing the spread of hate speech, making civic education an essential tool for electoral integrity.

acts.speaker: German Ministry of Justice (2017) / Germany's Network Enforcement Act (NetzDG)
acts.speech: Requires social media platforms to remove hate speech within 24 hours of reporting.

title: Business support key to AfCFTA success

acts.speaker: Myriam Montrat, Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
acts.speech: Has stressed the African Continental Free Trade Agreement's (AfCFTA) capacity to enable economies to scale and position Africa as a more competitive player in global value chains; said its success depends on translating policy goals into tangible business support systems: "AfCFTA provides a unique platform to now further reduce trade barriers and harmonise regulations. It also provides a platform to enable economies of scale and position Africa as a more competitive player in global value chains. However, unlocking its full benefits will require bridging the gap between policy and practice. It has to ensure that entrepreneurs have the tools, the financing, and market intelligence to be able to seize cross-border opportunities." (in a speech read on her behalf by Senior Trade Commissioner Andrew Maharaj)

acts.speaker: Myriam Montrat, Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
acts.speech: Affirmed Canada's commitment to deepening trade and investment ties with Africa in three key ways - business-to-business connections facilitated by the Trade Commissioner Service, partnerships with local business associations, and development cooperation supporting private sector growth: "Canadian companies are actively collaborating with African partners. We have multiple projects across renewable energy projects, responsible mining, innovative agri-tech solutions that not only scale businesses but also deliver value and social and environmental benefits. I'm particularly pleased by Canada's funding of $19.7 million over four years to the trademark Africa-led project titled: Making Trade Work for Women in West Africa. This funding, in partnership with AfCFTA Secretariat as well as ECOWAS Secretariat, is improving trade across the board of six countries in West Africa, namely Burkina Faso, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire, Togo, Guinea, and Nigeria."

acts.speaker: Myriam Montrat, Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
acts.speech: Urged African entrepreneurs to view Canadian companies as innovation partners rather than merely suppliers or investors, highlighting their global expertise, long-term commitment, and respect for local knowledge; further encouraged foreign companies to engage with Africa's integrated market, describing the opportunities as real and the potential as vast.

acts.speaker: Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff at the Office of the President of Ghana
acts.speech: Explained that government would maintain strict fiscal discipline while channeling investments into critical growth sectors, and said such measures were essential to protecting growth momentum and strengthening Ghana's competitiveness in regional and global markets: "Our government continues to prioritise trade facilitation and infrastructure to ease the movement of goods and services across borders, macroeconomic stability, and reforms to ensure that Ghana remains a safe and attractive investment destination."

acts.speaker: Mohammed Adam Sukparu, Deputy Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations
acts.speech: Emphasised the pivotal role of technology in advancing Africa's economic integration under the AfCFTA; stressed the need for Africa to transition from being a consumer of technology to a producer and innovator, which he said required robust collaboration between governments, the private sector, and academia; urged entrepreneurs to adopt digital tools and investors to deepen partnerships with Africa's growing tech ecosystem; affirmed the Ministry's commitment to driving digital transformation across the continent: "the future of Africa's business lies not just in its markets, but in its innovation. If we digitize Africa, we globalize Africa."

title: Health ministry comments on US funding crisis

acts.speaker: Ministry of Health of Botswana (statement)
acts.speech: Stated that in the health sector, this aid comprised funding for direct service delivery and technical support, which has over the years been instrumental to the growth of the health sector of this country; that through support from PEPFAR, USAID and the CDC, the US has been part and parcel of the Botswana health story; that since the introduction of PEPFAR in 2003, the health sector has cumulatively benefited support amounting to more than One Billion Pula; and that the US support has been instrumental in helping Botswana to be one of the first countries in the world to reach and exceed the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets well ahead of time, as a result of which many people living with HIV/AIDS in Botswana are able to live long.

title: Mozambique - Escalating violence and displacement (DG ECHO, UN OCHA, IOM) (ECHO Daily Flash of 1 October 2025)

acts.speaker: DG ECHO, UN OCHA and IOM (ECHO Daily Flash of 1 October 2025)
acts.speech: reported that between 26 August and 24 September, Cabo Delgado province has experienced a sharp rise in non-state armed group violent episodes, heavily affecting civilians in Ancuabe, Balama, Macomia, and Mocimboa da Praia; that 519 attacks have been recorded since January 2025, the highest number since the conflict began, with incidents including abductions, looting and killings; that over 20,000 people were displaced, including some 10,000 children, adding to the 57,000 people already displaced by attacks between late July and early August; that child protection risks are escalating, with many unaccompanied children lacking birth registration, restricting access to services and increasing exposure to harm, and reports also citing child killings and maiming due to improvised explosive devices as well as growing child marriage risks in displacement settings; that growing insecurity has also disrupted humanitarian operations, causing temporary aid suspensions in several areas; and that partners are assisting displaced populations in Mueda, Muidumbe, Ancuabe, Balama, and Montepuez through the NGO-led rapid response mechanism supported by DG ECHO, but others remain without support due to limited resources.

title: HIV alarm in Uganda as anti-gay law forces LGBTQI+ 'lockdown' | News24

acts.speaker: Staff at the HIV/AIDS treatment centre in Kampala
acts.speech: Say the usual daily influx of around 50 patients has all but dried up, with antiretroviral drugs piling up unused.

acts.speaker: Andrew Tendo, resident medical officer at the US-funded clinic in Kampala
acts.speech: Warned that new waves of HIV infections were forming even as vulnerable people stayed away from treatment centres, afraid of being identified and arrested under the new laws: “The LGBT community in Uganda is on lockdown now. They don't have preventive services. They cannot access condoms ... they cannot access ARTs (antiretrovirals)” ; said that now, when patients do come in, it's often out of absolute necessity, adding that the HIV cases presenting had become more severe as people skipped treatments.

acts.speaker: Andrew Tendo, resident medical officer at the Kampala clinic run by Icebreakers Uganda
acts.speech: Said he understood the fears of LGBTQ people in Uganda who often endured painful lives, featuring rejection by their families and arrests: “The majority of these people, like transgender or queer people, have gone through a lot already. They wouldn't want to be in a place where they can be raided or detained at any time.”

acts.speaker: Uganda AIDS Commission (state-run)
acts.speech: According to the commission, 1.4 million people in Uganda live with the virus and 17 000 die a year as a result of its ravages.

acts.speaker: US official (unnamed)
acts.speech: Suggested that the law would reverse the country's gains fighting HIV/AIDS.

acts.speaker: Uganda's Health Minister
acts.speech: Disputed a suggestion from a US official that the law would reverse the country's gains fighting HIV/AIDS, saying last week that the government would ensure that prevention programmes would remain accessible to those that needed them.

acts.speaker: Ugandan health ministry
acts.speech: Declined to comment for this article.

acts.speaker: Mary Borgman, country director for the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)
acts.speech: Said the trend of HIV patients staying away from treatment centres is being mirrored on a national level, and that fear had increasingly been deterring people from coming in for treatment ever since the anti-gay bill was introduced in parliament in March ; said the American government was acutely aware of the impact any funding cuts would have on vulnerable communities, including LGBTQ Ugandans: “The review is around whether we can operate within the environment that we are provided with”, without elaborating on specific legal concerns.

acts.speaker: 27-year-old gay man, patient at the Kampala clinic (anonymous, asked not to be identified for fear of being targeted by authorities)
acts.speech: Said he despaired at the new legislation: “I felt so sad when the law was enacted because we fear PEPFAR will cut off funding for the free services we have been receiving.”

acts.speaker: PEPFAR (programme estimates)
acts.speech: Estimates its support for the scale-up of antiretroviral treatments in Uganda helped avert nearly 600 000 HIV-related deaths between 2004 and 2022.

acts.speaker: Lillian Mworeko, East African regional coordinator for the International Community of Women living with HIV/AIDS
acts.speech: Said some providers feared that offering medical services to LGBTQ patients could be classed as “promoting” homosexuality, an offence punishable by 20 years in prison under the new law.

title: US President Trump’s clear messages on aid suspension, illegal immigrants deportation

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: "God has blessed your country. Go back and hold your corrupt leaders accountable. Stop loitering in the streets of America. If Americans were docile and refused to initiate Revolution, then you would never see such an amazing nation like USA... Stop depending on WHO for subsidized drugs. At your age, you ought to have home-made drugs for common ailments. On that ground, America has left WHO... Go and hold your ruling class accountable for rots in health care delivery. When they are sick, they run to USA for treatment with your national resources... America belongs to Americans not indians, Nigerians, Chinese, Mexicans, and other nationals who want good life and escaped to USA... Return to your country and change the narratives. No more running to America with your heavily pregnant wives. You want them to give birth in America and automatically become citizens of America. That is revoked immediately... Remain in your country and enjoy the consequences of being docile."

title: “La situation est extrêmement dramatique” en Syrie, selon le chef de l’aide humanitaire de l’ONU

acts.speaker: Tom Fletcher, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: Said on Monday that Syria needed a "massive flow of aid" after the fall of President Bashar al-Assad ; "The situation is extremely dramatic" ; said the UN wished to "surge massive aid into Syria and rapidly scale up" its operations ; "Things are moving very, very fast" ; "the important thing is that the Syrian people now hold their destiny in their own hands" ; "The international community must stand alongside them" ; "seven out of ten Syrians need aid now" ; said the UN wanted to "do things on a grand scale" to provide "food, medicine, shelter, but also funds to develop a Syria in which the population can believe again" ; OCHA has "ambitious plans" for Syria ; "That will depend a great deal on the talks we will have here with the authorities."

acts.speaker: Tom Fletcher, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: Asked whether he would encourage the lifting of sanctions, replied that it was "still very early" ; "It is a very fluid time. Things are moving and we have to be flexible."

acts.speaker: HTS (former Syrian branch of Al-Qaeda)
acts.speech: Claims to have broken with jihadism.

title: Vinodia Janete

acts.speaker: Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM)
acts.speech: Promises to build houses for young people, jobs and an increase in the subsidy for the elderly.

acts.speaker: Lutero Simango, MDM presidential candidate
acts.speech: Promises to raise the elderly subsidy from the current 600 to 1,200 meticais and to mobilise investors to build small units for processing and preserving fresh produce - promises made this Monday to the population of Nhamatanda district, Sofala province.

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Frelimo presidential candidate
acts.speech: Promises the establishment of farms in Maringúe to capitalise on the district's agricultural potential and generate employment ; in Gorongosa, Sofala, promised to build a peace monument, an operating theatre at the local hospital and secondary schools for young people.

acts.speaker: Renamo (in Maputo City)
acts.speech: Promises to build decent schools and to pay maintenance pensions for the elderly, should Issufo Momade win the elections.

acts.speaker: Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM), campaigning in Laulane, Kamavota Municipal District, Maputo City
acts.speech: Promised jobs for young people and an improvement in the quality of education in the country, should it win the 9 October elections.

acts.speaker: Joaquim Chissano, former President of the Republic of Mozambique
acts.speech: Says that all vital forces must be guided by tolerance and serenity in the ongoing electoral process ; welcomed the order and calm that have characterised the election campaign so far.

acts.speaker: Maputo City Council
acts.speech: Promises to change the situation in which around five thousand stalls stand empty in the city's municipal markets while hundreds of people trade on the pavements around them.

title: City Receives Donations Worth 36m Br

acts.speaker: Addis Abeba City Administration
acts.speech: Said the assistance, received by Deputy Mayor Takele Uma, will directly go through as cash support to sustain the households for three months.

title: Finance Minister proffers collaboration as booster to SMEs success in Ghana's economy

acts.speaker: Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana (speech read on his behalf)
acts.speech: Emphasised the need for the collective responsibility of all stakeholders to ensure the success of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) in Ghana; said SMEs are the lifeblood of the country's economy and therefore the need to create an enabling environment for SMEs to thrive; said that through the SME GO programme the Ministry would bind the public and private sectors together to create a better ecosystem for SMEs.

acts.speaker: Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana
acts.speech: Noted that Ghana's growth model must evolve beyond heavy reliance on foreign direct investment and raw material exports, which could be volatile and expose the country to external shocks.

acts.speaker: Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana
acts.speech: Said government supported the GEA and GEXIM with a total of 700 million cedis, while Development Bank Ghana committed about 1.2 billion cedis to support SMEs and the International Finance Corporation committed to support SMEs with 400 million dollars through financial institutions.

title: Aide: L’ONU débloque $110 millions pour compenser les coupes

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: Announced on Thursday the release of $110 million to offset "the precipitous decline" in funding devoted to humanitarian aid worldwide, particularly in Africa ; said one third of the allocated funds will go to supporting the humanitarian response in Sudan, plunged into civil war since April 2023 and currently experiencing the world's worst humanitarian crisis, as well as in neighbouring Chad, which hosts a large number of refugees fleeing the violence, with funds also distributed among countries such as Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Honduras, Mauritania, Niger, Somalia, Venezuela and Zambia ; said the recent funding cuts are creating a global funding crisis that threatens the lives of millions of children.

acts.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: Said the emergency funds of $110 million from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) aim to strengthen life-saving assistance in ten of the most underfunded and neglected crises, notably in Africa, Asia and Latin America ; warned that although more than 300 million people worldwide are expected to depend on humanitarian aid in 2025, funding is declining every year and "This year's levels are expected to reach a historic low."

acts.speaker: Tom Fletcher, Emergency Relief Coordinator and head of OCHA (statement)
acts.speech: "For countries hit by conflict, climate change and economic turmoil, brutal funding cuts do not mean that humanitarian needs disappear."

acts.speaker: Catherine Russell, Executive Director of UNICEF
acts.speech: "Millions of children are affected by conflict, must be vaccinated against deadly diseases such as measles and polio, and must be educated and kept healthy."

acts.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
acts.speech: Warned that funding cuts, particularly the freeze on American disbursements decided by the Trump administration, threaten the progress made in the fight against tuberculosis, the world's deadliest infectious disease; said global efforts against tuberculosis have saved more than 79 million lives over the past two decades but these gains are now threatened by budget cuts, with Washington having traditionally provided about $200 to $250 million a year to fight the disease.

title: Diffa : Lancement de la campagne de démoustication pour lutter contre le paludisme - Agence Nigérienne de Presse

acts.speaker: Major General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma, Governor of the Diffa Region
acts.speech: In his address, recalled the scale of malaria in Niger, particularly in the Diffa region, where the disease remains one of the leading causes of illness and death: "Malaria is a major public health problem in Niger and ranks first in terms of cause of morbidity and mortality. In 2024, the Diffa region recorded 90,650 confirmed cases with 172 deaths, against 77,381 cases and 94 deaths between January and September 2025." ; stressed that this situation has serious health and socio-economic repercussions, affecting above all vulnerable groups such as children, pregnant women, people with disabilities, as well as displaced and refugee populations.

acts.speaker: Major General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma, Governor of the Diffa Region
acts.speech: Regarding collective protection, insisted on the importance of dusting insecticides along the main thoroughfares, sanitation of living environments (disposal of waste water, drainage of rainwater), as well as on community awareness-raising and the seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) campaign.

acts.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
acts.speech: According to the WHO, malaria is an acute febrile parasitic disease, potentially fatal, transmitted to humans by the bite of infected female anopheles mosquitoes; although curable and preventable, it can lead to serious complications and even death if not treated quickly.

title: US-based Malawian ‘Cha Cha’ generosity turns to budding talent - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’), US-based Malawian socialite and owner of Cha Cha Care Home
acts.speech: Says that much as she left Malawi for the US in 2001, she has always remained connected to her motherland: “I left Malawi in 2001 when my father was an influential cabinet minister in the Bakili Muluzi administration as well as owning a newspaper giant, Nation Publications Limited. I did not leave Malawi as an economic migrant to the US but wanted to experience new challenges in life.”

acts.speaker: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’)
acts.speech: Says she earned her nursing license and ran a care home for a lady for ten years before setting up her own business, which she says has been success epitomized: “My business has become extremely successful and I can attribute that to God’s grace, resilience and hard work.”

acts.speaker: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’) (Facebook post)
acts.speech: Says she has decided to support as much budding talent in the country as her team deems fit, announcing that she would fully support 14-year-old comedian Ndaziona from Chirimba Township in Blantyre by taking care of her tuition and other essential needs: “From now onwards, I have decided to assist a young comedian, Ndaziona, with her education. I feel that it is proper if I send her to a boarding school, where I will be providing all the support,” posted Cha Cha on her Facebook page ; “Talent without good education can sometimes deter one from reaching their utmost potential.”

acts.speaker: Ndaziona, 14-year-old comedian from Chirimba Township, Blantyre
acts.speech: Expressed her gratitude saying it is a dream come true: “I promise to work hard.”

title: MEC to visit Tembisa after residents leave trail of destruction over 'skyrocketing' cost of services | News24

acts.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
acts.speech: says the violent protests that rocked the township are far from over ; says they will keep protesting until their grievances are attended to ; Addressing the media in Hospital View, said residents would continue protesting until the Ekurhuleni Municipality attended to their grievances.

acts.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
acts.speech: added many could not afford to pay their rates and taxes. "We are spending a lot of money on electricity. Our tariffs are skyrocketing. Our municipal rates are too high and we can't afford them. The municipality has cancelled the free units they used to give us." ; "We are pulling hard. We then decided to write a letter of demand to the mayor. We need lower rates. We need a flat rate. The municipality has to reinstate the indigent policy."

acts.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
acts.speech: blames Mayor Tania Campbell for the protests ; She said the protests escalated after residents felt Mayor Tania Campbell failed to address them when asked.

acts.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
acts.speech: "We are peaceful. We won't harm anyone. We are not violent. We managed to convince the police that we are not violent. I don't condone what happened in parts of the township."

acts.speaker: Letlhogonolo Moseki, Community Safety MMC
acts.speech: said the province had deployed more than 100 Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Police Department officers to Tembisa ; added they would be monitoring the situation.

acts.speaker: Lebogang Maile, Gauteng Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs MEC
acts.speech: claimed he wanted to establish the cause of the violent protests.

title: AfDB, World Food Programme Support Nigeria to Tackle Northeast Food Crisis

acts.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB source)
acts.speech: Said the African Development Bank has contributed $1 million from its Special Relief Fund to provide emergency food assistance to flood-affected communities in northeastern Nigeria.

acts.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP's Country Director in Nigeria
acts.speech: “The African Development Bank’s support is timely and comes as a lifeline for those struggling to feed themselves amidst rising food prices and economic turmoil” ; “Communities which, after years of conflict and violence, started rebuilding their lives were struck by the floods and once again displaced, meaning more and more people cannot support themselves and their families.”

acts.speaker: Cadre Harmonisé food security analysis (November 2024, 26 states and the federal capital)
acts.speech: Projects that 33 million people in Nigeria will face food insecurity by August 2025.

acts.speaker: Abdul Kamara, African Development Bank Director General in Nigeria
acts.speech: “I hope that this additional funding will mitigate the suffering of vulnerable people on the brink of acute hunger at a time when more Nigerians than ever need humanitarian assistance” ; “I commend the Federal Government of Nigeria and WFP for the continuous efforts to operate in such a challenging environment to improve the lives of Nigerian families.”

title: Mozambique: U.S. Embassy launches program to include people with disabilities in climate action

acts.speaker: United States / U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
acts.speech: Announces a new program to provide information on climate change advocacy tools for persons with disabilities in Mozambique. The goal of this project is to make information about emergency preparedness and climate change systems accessible to those who are blind, deaf, or other forms of disability.

acts.speaker: UNICEF
acts.speech: According to UNICEF, persons with disabilities are usually left out of discussions about policies, plans, and programs that prepare communities for and respond to these climate events at the national and subnational level.

acts.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID Mission Director
acts.speech: “The United States is dedicated to helping all people with disabilities to participate actively in Mozambique’s public life. Inclusivity improves decision-making and strengthens communities.”

title: From America first to America alone: The lab meets the street, By Azu Ishiekwene

acts.speaker: Mark Steyn, Canadian newspaper columnist, author of America Alone: The End of the World as We Know It
acts.speech: Thought demographic shifts, cultural decline, and Islam would ruin Western civilisation, and that the only redeeming grace was American exceptionalism; his book title extolled America as the last bastion of civilisation as we know it.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Accused Mexico and Canada of not doing enough to control the flow of fentanyl, a potent synthetic opioid analgesic more than 50 times more powerful than morphine, into the US ; apart from his perennial accusations against China of stealing US technology and other unfair trade practices, also accused Beijing of sending ingredients for making fentanyl to Mexico.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (second inaugural address)
acts.speech: Said that his "proudest legacy will be that of a peacemaker and unifier."

acts.speaker: Adam Smith, economist
acts.speech: Once described a trade war as "beggar-thy-neighbour."

acts.speaker: Analysts
acts.speech: Before the one-month tariff pause between the US and its neighbours, forecast the tariffs would hinder US GDP growth by approximately 0.25 per cent to 0.3 per cent, that the tariffs on Canada and Mexico alone could decrease overall economic output by around $45 billion, with potential losses escalating to $75 billion following retaliatory measures.

title: Under pressure, Syria agrees to Arab League plan to end violence

acts.speaker: Arab League (statement)
acts.speech: Announced that the Syrian government had accepted a proposal by the League to halt violence in Syria, and said in a statement following a meeting in Cairo, “The Arab League welcomes the Syrian government's agreement to the Arab plan”, adding that it “emphasised the need for the immediate, full and exact implementation of the articles in the plan”.

acts.speaker: Syrian state news report
acts.speech: Claimed on Monday that Syrian authorities had agreed to terms with an Arab League ministerial committee on a plan to end the violence.

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: Says the number of people killed in the seven-month-old uprising has surpassed 3,000.

acts.speaker: Syrian government
acts.speech: Throughout the uprising has defended its actions with the claim that terrorists had killed hundreds of security personnel.

acts.speaker: Bashar Al-Assad, Syrian President
acts.speech: Admitted to Britain’s Sunday Telegraph that his security forces had indeed made “some mistakes”.

acts.speaker: Syrian activists
acts.speech: Claimed at least 34 people were killed in the restive provinces of Homs and Hama ahead of the Arab League’s announcement on Wednesday.

acts.speaker: Syrian Revolution General Commission (SRGC)
acts.speech: Said it rejected the Arab League plan; for them only a toppling of the regime would be acceptable.

acts.speaker: Representatives of the Arab League
acts.speech: Indicated to the media that if the plan was not implemented, the Arab foreign ministers would reconvene to “reconsider further steps”.

title: Minister Calls for Innovative Ways to Teach Integrated Farming in Eswatini

acts.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
acts.speech: Has urged for innovative approaches to teaching integrated farming, suggesting starting with a few crops first and incorporating livestock. He emphasized minimal ploughing and very low fertilizer usage, encouraging farmers to integrate livestock for manure production. "Integration means having compost and manures, like the East is doing, whether using animal waste from goats, cows, or chickens for the manure."

acts.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
acts.speech: With Africa's population rising and land holdings shrinking, stressed the need for strategic small-scale agriculture. "Less than half of agriculture land on SNL is cultivated every year which has potential. How do you make a one-hectare piece of land commercial and have a farmer manage it all year round?" he questioned. He noted that Eswatini had adopted a Western commercial approach, while Eastern countries had successfully cracked integrated farming.

acts.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
acts.speech: Proposed that 100,000 homesteads participate in a tree-planting scheme, with each homestead planting 20 trees, creating a large-scale, small-farmer-driven project. The minister highlighted the need for public-private partnerships (PPPs) to provide ready financing or credit guarantee schemes for farmers.

acts.speaker: Neal Rijkenberg, Minister of Finance of Eswatini
acts.speech: "We need a fund of over E1 billion so that when that farmer needs finance, we provide it—whether to buy seeds, farming inputs, or sows." He emphasized involving financial institutions, agro-processors, exporters, and the supply chain, ensuring farmers have guaranteed markets, including for pork processing and potential exports. "So when we start producing more pork than the country can use, we are ready to export."

title: Mais de 60 mil congoleses fugiram para o Burundi devido a escala de violência - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: UNHCR (UN Refugee Agency)
acts.speech: Praises Burundi’s decision to grant refugees prima facie status, ensuring that they receive immediate protection and critical humanitarian assistance.

title: Mca-Bénin II Akassato doté d’un terrain aux normes de la Fifa

acts.speaker: Brian Shukan, United States Ambassador to Benin
acts.speech: Welcomed the entry into service of the facility, the fruit of cooperation between Benin and the United States: “MCA-Benin II is the best symbol of the cooperation between Benin and the United States, which has lasted for 60 years.”

acts.speaker: Gabriel Dégbègni, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin II
acts.speech: Says he is proud to take stock of the new infrastructure the country is benefiting from: “It is a source of pride for the staff of MCA-Benin II, who overcame a good number of challenges to achieve the objectives.”

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State in charge of Development and Coordination of Government Action and Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
acts.speech: Welcomed the implementation of MCA-Benin II, which impacts 12 million Beninese and opens prospects for Benin’s economic development thanks to the availability of electricity: “The Compact is the best development financing tool.”

title: Comparing Chibok AndYazidi Girls: Ten Years After, The Freed And Not Freed (2)

acts.speaker: President Barack Obama of the United States
acts.speech: Has now apologised for the unfortunate and sad incident at the Kunduz hospital.

acts.speaker: Carrie P. Snow, philosopher
acts.speech: “When you think of the long and gloomy history of man, you will find that more hideous crime has been committed in the name of obedience than have ever been in the name of rebellion.”

acts.speaker: President Muhammadu Buhari of Nigeria
acts.speech: Presumed, in his address to USA lawmakers during his maiden state visit to Washington DC, that Western superpowers who fail to assist in providing weapons to rout Boko Haram are vicariously guilty of collusion with or are acquiescing with terrorists to kill and maim innocent Nigerians.

acts.speaker: A Yazidi girl (15-year-old captive, interviewed by PBS NewsHour)
acts.speech: “They brought everyone to a school, put the women upstairs, and drove the men away. I didn’t want to let my mother go, but they were pulling us from our mothers and beating us. The children were all put in cars. They said, ‘We’re going to sell you to others, and you will have sex with them.’” ; told how she and her siblings were captured, separated, and, for four months, she was shuttled between towns and cities hundreds of miles apart, even being sent to Syria.

acts.speaker: Marcia Biggs, PBS NewsHour special correspondent (report ‘Freed And Not Freed’)
acts.speech: Reported that in the months that followed the kidnap, a network of activists sprung up throughout Northern Iraq, an underground railroad of sorts, coordinating rescue efforts, and that their phone numbers quickly spread among captive girls, who used smuggled phones to call for help and give their location; stated that “At times, the Kurdish regional government has stepped in to grease the wheels,” and that KRG envoy Dr. Nouri Othman told her about two girls who escaped their captors in Raqqa and ran to a nearby house but were turned away by the owner, too scared to take the chance; reported that about 400 Yazidi women and girls are now free.

acts.speaker: Dr. Nouri Othman, Envoy to Internally Displaced Persons, Kurdish Regional Government
acts.speech: Said he called the house owner and pleaded with him to keep the two girls at his home for a couple of days, and that he had to promise to pay him: “Nobody is going to risk their life without getting something in return. You have to pay them.” ; revealed that “Some families are raising money to buy back their girls, racking up thousands of dollars in debt.”

acts.speaker: Dr. Nouri Othman, Envoy to Internally Displaced Persons, Kurdish Regional Government
acts.speech: On whether the government funds a programme to buy back the girls: “I’m not buying them, no. Maybe I’m paying some people. They are helping me get them back… The important thing is I want these people to be back. They are my responsibility.” ; told PBS that his government has spent over $1.5 million to rescue the girls, and on the ethical question responded: “Well, I’m not—not paying ISIS fighters. This is one. Second thing, these are Kurdish citizens. And I don’t care where the money goes personally. I care how to rescue the people.”

acts.speaker: The Punch Newspaper of April 15
acts.speech: Reported that 187 Chibok girls have been rescued.

title: China, Zambia, and Tanzania to Sign $1.4 Billion investment Deal for CCECC to Operate TAZARA for 30 Years - The Chanzo

acts.speaker: Bruno Ching’andu, TAZARA Chief Executive Officer
acts.speech: Announced during the Zambia International Mining and Energy Conference (ZIMEC 2025) in Kitwe, Zambia that investment negotiations are in their final stages and that with CCECC’s $1.4 billion investment the company will operate TAZARA for 30 years ; “The investment from CCECC will not only restore our railway infrastructure but also position TAZARA as a key enabler of trade and economic growth between Tanzania and Zambia.”

title: Alex Mould takes over as MiDA CEO from Michael Asare Bediako

acts.speaker: Millennium Development Authority (MiDA) (announcement)
acts.speech: Announced Alex Mould as its new Chief Executive Officer, following the departure of Michael Asare Bediako.

acts.speaker: Michael Asare Bediako, outgoing Chief Executive Officer of MiDA
acts.speech: As he stepped down, expressed gratitude for the support he received, stating his confidence in MiDA's continued success under its new leadership.

acts.speaker: Michael Asare Bediako, outgoing Chief Executive Officer of MiDA
acts.speech: Has assured a smooth transition, having already engaged Mr Mould in discussions to ensure the continuity of strategic initiatives, and remains optimistic about MiDA's future and its impact on Ghana's development.

title: Preserve Bingu’s Legacy: Stop the Political Exploitation

acts.speaker: Political analysts and citizens
acts.speech: Have expressed outrage at Chimombo's actions, arguing that they undermine the very essence of Bingu's legacy.

acts.speaker: A prominent political commentator (anonymous)
acts.speech: "If Bingu were alive today, he would not have allowed his name to be politically exploited in this manner" ; "We must protect his legacy from those who seek to tarnish it for their own ambitions."

title: L'OMS tente d'empêcher le départ des USA

acts.speaker: Michael Ryan, WHO Deputy Director-General
acts.speech: Is indignant: "I remind you all that the United States government is not leaving a building in Geneva. It is not leaving a secretariat in Geneva. It is leaving a community of nations. It is essentially... it is essentially a break with you, not with me. And that must be taken into account by the 193 member states represented here today."

acts.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
acts.speech: "Nevertheless, it will be very important to invest in the return of the United States. And on this point, I think each one of you can play, can play, a role."

acts.speaker: An analyst (unnamed)
acts.speech: Worries that interventions in the Middle East, in Ukraine and in Sudan are threatened, not to mention hundreds of millions of dollars lost by the polio eradication and HIV programmes since the announcement of the freeze on American development aid worldwide.

title: Djibouti, 48 ans après : l’indépendance confisquée ? - La Voix de Djibouti

acts.speaker: Thomas Sankara (quoted)
acts.speech: "The slave who does not take charge of his own revolt does not deserve pity for his fate."

title: TZ, US join forces in battle against rabies - Daily News

acts.speaker: Dr Stanford Ndibalema, Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
acts.speech: Said there is need for collaboration in combating rabies: "The partnership between USAID and the Tanzanian government is crucial in our fight against rabies." He added that by working together, the government of Tanzania and USAID can ensure the communities are educated about the risks of rabies and properly empowered to take proactive steps in protecting themselves and their pets.

acts.speaker: Dr Stanford Ndibalema, Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
acts.speech: Underscored the critical need for vaccination and community awareness campaigns: "Every vaccinated dog is a step toward to having a rabies-free community."

acts.speaker: Revina John, a mother of three from Mwanza
acts.speech: "Before the campaign, I had no idea how dangerous rabies could be." She added: "After we learnt about the importance of vaccinating our dogs, we took immediate action. Now, I feel much safer allowing my children to play outside."

title: Trump administration asks US Supreme Court to halt foreign aid payments

acts.speaker: US Department of Justice (emergency filing to the Supreme Court)
acts.speech: Asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday to intervene in the administration's efforts to withhold billions of dollars from foreign aid organizations and lift an injunction that is forcing it to keep making payments; noted in the emergency filing that a 2-1 panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit earlier this month ruled the injunction should be overturned.

acts.speaker: Trump administration (Supreme Court filing)
acts.speech: Said the congressionally appropriated funds subject to the injunction comprise tens of billions of dollars, some $12 billion of which would need to be spent by the U.S. Department of State before September 30, when they expire; said that without the justices' intervention, it will be forced to keep making payments before the expiration date, "overriding the Executive Branch's foreign-policy judgments regarding whether to pursue rescissions and thwarting interbranch dialogue."

acts.speaker: AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition and Journalism Development Network (litigation)
acts.speech: Brought litigation alleging Trump's funding freeze was unlawful.

acts.speaker: Lawyers for the plaintiffs
acts.speech: Did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

acts.speaker: Amir Ali, US District Judge (Washington-based)
acts.speech: Ordered the Trump administration to pay nearly $2 billion in outstanding aid to its humanitarian partners worldwide; rejected on Monday a request to put his injunction on hold.

acts.speaker: Karen Henderson, US Circuit Judge, writing for the D.C. Circuit panel majority
acts.speech: Ruled that the nonprofit groups failed to satisfy the requirements for an injunction, saying only the U.S. Government Accountability Office, a watchdog agency, could challenge Trump's efforts to withhold the funding.

title: Mali : des réformes face à la crise alimentaire de 2025

acts.speaker: 21st ordinary session of Mali's National Food Security Council (CNSA), chaired by Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maiga
acts.speech: Called on the Food Security Commission to continue the reforms, in particular through the creation of the Food and Nutrition Security Monitoring and Early Warning Agency (AVASAN), which will play a central role in the preventive management of crises.

title: CHR de Fada N'Gourma : Le Premier ministre au chevet des soldats blessés

acts.speaker: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
acts.speech: Words addressed by the Head of Government to the wounded soldiers: "I have come to inquire about your state of health and to wish you a speedy recovery. I have come to express to you our admiration for your spirit of sacrifice which allows our country to remain standing."

acts.speaker: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
acts.speech: Declared to the medical staff: "I thank you for all the efforts you are making to care for our wounded soldiers. I salute your individual and collective commitment, despite the difficult working conditions. When one looks at the state of the wounded and above all the quality of the care they receive, which today allows us to hope that they may recover their health, one can only salute you. It is a state of mind that the Government salutes. Everything is being done to improve your working conditions. Continue to perform miracles."

title: Malawians champion community-led development over foreign aid

acts.speaker: Study published in World Development Perspectives
acts.speech: According to the study, Malawians prefer community-led initiatives over traditional top-down approaches often tied to foreign aid. The research, conducted in nine rural Malawian communities, found that community leaders possess the necessary knowledge and skills to spearhead development projects.

acts.speaker: Frank Kasonga, Executive Director of Mudzi Connect and co-author of the study
acts.speech: Emphasized the importance of community participation in development projects: "Community-led development prioritizes the community's participation in contrast to external contractors or organizations at every level of a project."

acts.speaker: A study participant (anonymous)
acts.speech: "Community ownership of development projects is key to sustainability of development as it brings a sense of responsibility to the community."

title: EWADE entrusted to deliver food sovereignty – minister

acts.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister for Agriculture of Eswatini
acts.speech: Says government has placed a monumental task before EWADE Chief Executive Officer Dr Samson Sithole to lead the country towards food sovereignty; speaking to the Times Business Desk, said the ministry's expectations for EWADE are immense following the renewal of Dr Sithole's contract for another three years, and noted that the parastatal's track record in uplifting rural communities through agriculture has demonstrated its ability to deliver on major national objectives. "EWADE is entrusted with many government projects and the expectation is huge. Our vision is to fight hunger and reach a stage where emaSwati are able to feed themselves, instead of relying on imports. That is the ultimate measure of food sovereignty."

acts.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister for Agriculture of Eswatini
acts.speech: Praised the impact of EWADE under Dr Sithole's leadership, citing tangible changes in the lives of rural farmers: "The work of this parastatal is felt and seen by many. It speaks volumes about the CEO's leadership, which is rooted in strong work culture and ethical practices."

acts.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister for Agriculture of Eswatini
acts.speech: Described the Mkhondvo Ngwavuma Water Augmentation Programme (MNWAP) as a game-changer for the Shiselweni Region: "The MNWAP will transform livelihoods by ensuring water access for irrigation and opening up new agricultural opportunities. This project is central to our national food security goals." He said these initiatives, together with SAPEMP and a World Bank-funded youth empowerment project, collectively form the backbone of the country's push towards food sovereignty and rural economic transformation.

title: Can the real Monetary Policy Committee stand up! - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama), as espoused by its president Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
acts.speech: Called for urgent action to achieve fiscal discipline, export-led recovery and reform of foreign exchange markets to avert a deeper balance-of-payments crisis ; said Malawi will require a combination of monetary tightening to curb speculation and long-term investment in export growth to restore macroeconomic stability, cautioning that the widening trade gap is fuelling forex shortages, driving transactions underground and worsening inflationary pressures.

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) statement
acts.speech: Showed that Malawi's net international reserves (NIR) were projected to fall to negative $2.03 billion (about K3.55 trillion or 18.9 percent of gross domestic product) by the end of this year; projected that Malawi's net international reserves - or what the Reserve Bank of Malawi can actually use after deducting liabilities - will deteriorate from -$1.02 billion in 2023 to -$2.03 billion in 2025.

acts.speaker: Bloomberg
acts.speech: Reporting that part of Malawi's external debt total includes almost $500 million owed to Africa Export and Import Bank (Afreximbank) and about $400 million with the Trade and Development Bank.

acts.speaker: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
acts.speech: Maintained the policy rate at 26 percent in a move some economists described as a 'cautious' approach that takes into account the existing inflation risk, especially on rising maize prices.

acts.speaker: MacDonald Mafuta-Mwale, Reserve Bank of Malawi Governor
acts.speech: Said in February, barely a month in office, that the central bank had finalised the process of formulating measures aimed at crushing the parallel market foreign exchange supply as a key price stabilisation strategy.

title: Liberia’s Ambassador Designate to France Commits to Economic Diplomacy, Development Goals

acts.speaker: Dr. Teeko T. Yorlay, Sr., Liberia's Ambassador Designate to France
acts.speech: Committed to advancing Liberia's interests on the global stage through targeted collaborations and proactive representation, emphasised the transformative potential of strong bilateral relations with France and its European partners and highlighted the need to prioritise development goals, particularly in education, infrastructure, and trade. “Our partnership with France is an untapped reservoir of opportunities. As ambassador, my goal will be to translate these opportunities into tangible benefits for our country.”

acts.speaker: Dr. Teeko T. Yorlay, Sr., Liberia's Ambassador Designate to France
acts.speech: Underscored economic diplomacy as the cornerstone of his strategy, describing it as a tool to attract foreign direct investments (FDIs) and boost local industries, and cited France's role as a major global economy and its potential as a key partner for Liberia in trade, agriculture, and industrial development. “I intend to position Liberia as an attractive destination for French investors.
