The Russian government has allocated the necessary financing to the program for the supply of domestic food to Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan. However, due to the sanctions imposed by Washington in November 2024 against Russian financial institutions, funds have not been transferred yet.”

acts.speaker: T.E. Dovgalenko, Director of the Department of Partnership with Africa of the Russian Foreign Ministry
acts.speech: On education cooperation: “We give priority attention to the issues of training highly qualified personnel among Africans, who are called upon to ensure, among other things, the economic and technological sovereignty of their countries. More than 34,000 African students study in Russia, of which about seven thousand are funded by the federal budget.”

title: Pressure Mounts on Chakwera to Concede as Defeat Looms - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Reverend Billy Gamah, chairperson of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
acts.speech: Declared that, based on the partial presidential results announced by the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC), “the table cannot change to deliver victory” for Chakwera ; “A public statement by the President acknowledging defeat would not only be an act of statesmanship but also a powerful gesture to encourage his supporters to accept the outcome peacefully.” ; “We believe that conceding early, even before the official announcement, will show maturity, promote peace, and help the nation move forward without violence or unnecessary tension.”

acts.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
acts.speech: Says the responsible path for Chakwera is to publicly concede and call for calm among his supporters.

acts.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former president of Malawi
acts.speech: Confirmed that he had personally urged Chakwera to concede and call Mutharika to congratulate him; argued that doing so would defuse political tensions and safeguard Malawi’s democratic stability, reminding Chakwera that “there is life after State House.”

acts.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
acts.speech: Announced the partial presidential results last night, showing former president Peter Mutharika commanding an unassailable lead in 21 out of the 24 councils tallied.

title: L'ambassade des États-Unis à Bangui pourrait être fermée prochainement

acts.speaker: Internal document of the US State Department
acts.speech: According to it, the Trump administration is considering closing nearly 30 embassies and consulates abroad; the document recommends the closure of 10 embassies and 17 consulates, most of them in Europe and Africa, including the embassies of Malta, Luxembourg, Lesotho, the Republic of Congo, the Central African Republic and South Sudan.

acts.speaker: Central African social media users
acts.speech: Have already expressed their joy at the planned closure of the United States embassy in Bangui.

acts.speaker: Media reports (unspecified media and social networks)
acts.speech: Have already reported on several occasions on dubious American activities in the Central African Republic, and have provided what the article calls irrefutable evidence of the involvement of PMC Bancroft and other American actors in attacks on employees of Chinese mining companies operating in the CAR.

acts.speaker: Pedro Campo-Boué, foreign service officer of the US State Department based in Bangui
acts.speech: In a telephone conversation leaked by the French mobile operator Orange in April 2024, asked Paul Crescent Beninga to organise another, much larger demonstration in Bangui against the Bangui regime, against the backdrop of the GTSC’s successful anti-government demonstration on 12 April.

acts.speaker: Paul Crescent Beninga, spokesman of the GTSC
acts.speech: In the leaked telephone conversation, accepted and asked for more money and other facilities.

acts.speaker: Anthony Odom, press officer of the Central African opposition party MLPC (WhatsApp audio message)
acts.speech: On 17 April 2024 sent an audio message to a party member on WhatsApp, later leaked to a well-known blogger, revealing the links between the MLPC and the United States: that opposition leader Martin Ziguele had not only met the Americans but had also received the assurance of a grant of 56,000 dollars from USAID.

acts.speaker: Abdou Ali (article author)
acts.speech: Argues that such work by the American embassy in Bangui could not fail to attract the attention of the new American authorities, who wanted to put an end to this illegal activity at the expense of American taxpayers’ money, and that the Central African Republic can only benefit from this decision because the embassy in its current format is more a place for planning and implementing geopolitical games than for establishing productive and warm relations between the two countries.

title: TRA Yatangaza Msamaha wa Adhabu kwa Wenye Magari Haya Yenye Changamoto za Kikodi - The Chanzo

acts.speaker: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
acts.speech: Has announced a waiver of penalties for vehicles in use and present in the country but which have various tax problems; the waiver, which began on August 01 and ends on December 31, 2025, will cover vehicles brought in under temporary importation that have remained in the country, vehicles that entered Tanzania Mainland from Zanzibar without following customs procedures, transit vehicles retained in the country, vehicles granted tax exemption whose ownership was transferred to persons not entitled to the exemption, and transit vehicles whose permitted period expired without an extension.

acts.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, TRA Commissioner General (statement)
acts.speech: In a statement issued by the TRA Commissioner General, Yusuph Mwenda, the Authority explained that it has been facing challenges in managing these vehicles on which duty and taxes were not paid at the time of importation, and so TRA has officially announced an amnesty period from August 01, 2025 to December 31, 2025, during which the owners of the vehicles concerned will be required to come forward to pay duty and taxes while all interest and penalties are waived. ; "In accordance with section 70(1) of the Tax Administration Act, Chapter 438, and Section 249 of the East African Community Customs Management Act of 2004, the Commissioner General of the Authority grants a tax waiver to owners of the types of vehicles mentioned… which were brought into the country knowingly or unknowingly without the relevant duty and taxes having been paid." ; "During the amnesty period, the owners of the vehicles concerned will be responsible for paying the relevant amount of duty and taxes; the interest and penalties will all be waived."

acts.speaker: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
acts.speech: TRA stated that vehicles in the listed categories that are seized after 31 December 2025, and on which duty and taxes have not been fully paid, will be dealt with in accordance with the law, including criminal prosecution, with those involved required to pay the duty and taxes, together with penalties and interest.

title: Année scolaire 2025-2026 dans les Tannouyan: le gouverneur sonne la cloche de la rentrée

acts.speaker: Badabouè Florent Bazié, Governor of the Tannounyan region, Burkina Faso (representing the Minister of Basic Education)
acts.speech: In his address, he insisted on the need for all actors in the education system to redouble their efforts in order to build a school system that is stronger, more accessible and more equitable ; "Every enrolment, every classroom opened, every teacher mobilised is a national victory," the governor recalled, while saluting the determination and courage of teachers who, he said, despite the security challenges, continue to carry out the mission of transmitting knowledge.

acts.speaker: Badabouè Florent Bazié, Governor of the Tannounyan region, Burkina Faso
acts.speech: Took the occasion to invite pupils to discipline and hard work, while inviting parents of pupils to accompany their children in their school careers; he further urged teachers to maintain their patriotic and professional commitment in the service of the Nation.

acts.speaker: Jacques Sosthène Dingara, Minister of Basic Education, Literacy and the Promotion of National Languages of Burkina Faso (message conveyed by the governor)
acts.speech: The minister's message also highlighted the major reforms marking this school year, namely the progressive generalisation from this year of the teaching of English, which will extend to the CE2, CM1 and CM2 classes, the transformation of classic schools into bilingual schools, the promotion of school councils, and the transparent and equitable management of human and financial resources.

title: Tsumeb Municipality to raise water tariffs

acts.speaker: Manuel Pedro, engineer of the Tsumeb Municipality
acts.speech: told Nampa in an interview that consultations are underway with the Ministry of Rural and Urban Development in this regard. “Currently, water is priced at approximately N$8.40 per liter. We are looking to increase that amount in July 2025.” ; He explained that the new plant will improve water quality for Tsumeb residents, addressing long-standing issues such as calcium build-up in appliances, and that the facility treats underground water to reduce its hardness and eliminate clostridium.

acts.speaker: Stella Nangolo-Imalwa, spokesperson of the Tsumeb Municipality
acts.speech: confirmed that the revised tariffs will also account for ongoing maintenance expenses associated with the plant. “The new tariff will be determined through council meetings.”

title: Téléphonie mobile : TERIATEL en projet dans l’espace AES

acts.speaker: Nam Waya Rahouf Ouedraogo, head of the TERIATEL project delegation
acts.speech: "We came to present our project to the minister. It is a project to set up a mobile telephone network, called TERIATEL" ; specified that "the objective is to offer concrete and reliable telecommunications solutions to the three countries of the Alliance of Sahel States, and more particularly to Burkina Faso."

acts.speaker: Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabane, Minister of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications
acts.speech: Welcomed their approach and promised to organise working sessions with the technical services of her department to better understand the details of the project.

title: Afin de soulager les populations nécessiteuses contre l'insécurité alimentaire au Mali : 6200 kits alimentaires distribués par l'ONG Al Farouk à 43 400 bénéficiaires !

acts.speaker: Ibrahim Traoré, military doctor and president of the special delegation of Commune IV
acts.speech: took the floor to salute this fine initiative and this surge of solidarity towards the disadvantaged: “We sincerely thank the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for this gesture, which comes at just the right time. It is in difficult moments that one recognises one's friends. And Saudi Arabia has just proven it to us through this donation of food baskets.”

acts.speaker: A. Cheick Ibrahim Kontao, director of the NGO Al Farouk-Mali
acts.speech: addressed the audience with religious exhortations: “Those who spend their wealth in the path of God are like a grain that sprouts seven ears, in each ear there are a hundred grains. God multiplies blessings for whom He wills. God is great and wise.” ; recalled the saying of Muhammad, son of Abdallah: “Whoever relieves a Muslim of a hardship of this world, God will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection.”

acts.speaker: A. Cheick Ibrahim Kontao, director of the NGO Al Farouk-Mali
acts.speech: said of the response to the floods: “the State was among the first to intervene in order to alleviate the suffering of the victims by providing precious resources and by calling on its partners to collaborate. In response to this appeal, the NGO Al Farouk mobilised its partners. By the Grace of God, the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Aid stood by our side, adopting a brotherly approach and always on the front line of this humanitarian mission, with kindness and compassion. Today, we celebrate together the launch of a project to assist several families in Bamako, Koulikoro, Segou and Mopti.” ; said each food kit is made up of 25 kg of rice, 10 kg of noodles, 5 kg of sugar and 5 litres of oil.

acts.speaker: A. Cheick Ibrahim Kontao, director of the NGO Al Farouk-Mali
acts.speech: expressed, on behalf of the NGO Al Farouk, his deep gratitude to King Salman bin Abdulaziz and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for this important donation: “I also wish to thank the team of the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Aid, led by Dr. Rabia and his collaborators, in particular our brothers who travelled long distances to Mali to serve their brothers in God, for their remarkable efforts aimed at promoting security, stability and well-being throughout the world and particularly in the Islamic world. I also thank His Excellency the Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and all the members of the embassy for their availability and their contribution to our country. I cannot conclude without expressing my gratitude to the government of Mali, under the leadership of the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, for all the facilities granted to the Al Farouk organisation so that it may carry out its mission. I pray to God to grant them success in leading this country towards a serene future.”

acts.speaker: Abdullah Saleh Saber, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali
acts.speech: saluted the fraternal and historic relations between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the sister Republic of Mali in various fields, in confirmation of the Kingdom's willingness to stand by the brotherly Malian people ; “I thank the government of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques for the humanitarian aid it provides. I also cannot fail to thank the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre for its efforts in the area of food aid. I also thank the Minister-Commissioner for Food Security for the efforts and the cooperation you have deployed to implement this programme, and my thanks go to the highest authorities for all the facilities that have been provided to us.” ; thanked the NGO Al-Farouk for its valuable efforts in organising this launch ceremony.

acts.speaker: Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali, Minister-Commissioner for Food Security of Mali
acts.speech: saluted all the actors who contributed to the realisation of this purely humanitarian action: “It is with great satisfaction that I note the completion of a project on which we worked with the NGO Al-Farouk. We involved the governors of the regions concerned, namely the district of Bamako and the regions of Koulikoro, Ségou and Mopti, to produce the lists of all the beneficiaries, with eligibility criteria that were determined by common agreement with the NGO Al Farouk and its partners. Thank you to each and every one for the completion of this noble action; it is never a happy thing to see fellow citizens in need of assistance. We must all work together to create living conditions worthy of our fellow citizens in situations of food difficulty.”

acts.speaker: Beneficiaries of the food kits
acts.speech: did not stop thanking King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for this generous donation.

title: Africa to react: Is Trump ushering in a new era of self-reliance? - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: Institute for Security Studies (data modelling)
acts.speech: Projects catastrophic outcomes: 5.7 million additional Africans will fall into extreme poverty (<$2.15/day) by 2026 if Trump's administration succeeds in its aid-reduction ambition.

acts.speaker: John Mearsheimer, realist scholar
acts.speech: Asserted that "great powers always act in ways that maximize their relative power advantage."

acts.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
acts.speech: Announced the closure of its office in South Africa following the Trump administration's recent foreign aid cuts; the agency will consolidate its southern and East Africa operations into a single regional office in Nairobi, Kenya, while shutting down its Johannesburg office, citing a worsening donor funding outlook that has necessitated an acceleration of a restructuring plan initiated in 2023.

acts.speaker: Abdirahim Mohamed Hassan, independent researcher and author
acts.speech: Argued that Trump's policies reinforce a realist worldview and have validated dependency theory's core critique that North-South aid architectures perpetuate extractive relationships, and that Africa must respond with strategic foresight by rethinking its dependency on external actors and strengthening intra-African trade, security collaboration and independent policymaking; he wrote that "as the ruins of USAID are cleared, the foundations for a self-reliant Africa must rise in their place."

title: Appui au secteur de la santé:Le Bénin signe un protocole d’accord de 53 milliards F CFA avec 20 PTF

acts.speaker: Dorothée Kindé Gazard, Minister of Health of Benin
acts.speech: reiterated during the meeting with the technical and financial partners (PTF) the government's commitment to carry out major actions with these resources. According to her, this signing marks the materialisation of the Beninese government's commitment to work for the improvement of the health of the population ; stressed that, managed on the basis of the results-based financing approach, this compact will make it possible to coordinate effectively the actions of the PTFs at departmental and national level ; "The year 2015 is a year of great challenges and of consolidating the gains," she assured.

acts.speaker: Dorothée Kindé Gazard, Minister of Health of Benin
acts.speech: emphasised, regarding the record of actions in the health sector: "All of which improved the rate of coverage of staffing needs from 66.06% in 2013 to 74.05% in 2014" ; according to her, the contingency plan against the Ebola and Lassa haemorrhagic fever epidemics worked perfectly and the conclusions are reassuring.

acts.speaker: Kevin Armstrong, Director of USAID, lead of the technical and financial partners (PTF)
acts.speech: said Benin has recorded a great deal of progress in the health sector. "We stand by your side to achieve the results," he said on behalf of the international and non-governmental organisations that are parties to the agreement ; the spokesman of the health sector PTFs said he was convinced that the approach would serve to improve the MDG indicators.

acts.speaker: The Beninese side (government)
acts.speech: also welcomed the fact that the signing of this compact will allow a consensual process of monitoring the tools, approaches, mechanisms and indicators for tracking the integrated annual work plan.

title: Niger/sécurité alimentaire : ouverture ce mardi à Niamey d’une rencontre de capitalisation du ‘’programme Hamzari’’ | Le Sahel

acts.speaker: Maria Barron, USAID Niger Mission Director
acts.speech: Support from the Hamzari program enabled more than 17,000 farmers to learn and apply improved production techniques, allowing them to increase their agricultural production ; the project also enabled more than 58,000 people to have better access to drinking water, improving their quality of life and reducing the risk of water-related diseases ; in total, the Hamzari project directly benefited more than 104,000 people, 62% of whom were women, reaching 106% of its initial target.

title: USAID’S DEVELOPMENT INNOVATION VENTURES accepting new applicants

acts.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
acts.speech: Announced that it is accepting new applications for the Development Innovation Ventures (DIV) program, that anyone, anywhere can apply at any time, and set out the tiered funding structure – Stage-One grants (up to USD200,000), Stage-Two grants (USD200,000 to USD1,500,000), Stage-Three grants (USD1,500,000 to USD5,000,000) and separate evidence grants (up to USD1,500,000); it stated that since 2010, DIV has invested in over 190 solutions across 46 countries and all sectors in which USAID invests, has directly affected more than 30 million lives, that over half of DIV grantees had never received USAID funding before, and that DIV has mobilized USD4.60 of external funding for every USD1 from the American people.

title: Taxes douanières américaines: Les implications économiques pour le Bénin

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said the resurgence of protectionism observed on the part of the United States since President Donald Trump's return to power constitutes a major economic event that deserves in-depth analysis, and that the decision can be considered a calling into question of the tariff preference granted by the United States to certain countries, including Benin, through AGOA. "Although the share of the United States in our exports is still fairly small (a little less than 2% between 2021 and 2023), it is showing a very marked upward trend." ; "The abandonment of AGOA and the establishment of a 10% customs duty will inevitably lead to increased competition for the products we export to that country. This may contribute to a reduction in our exports to the United States. The consequence must be a worsening of the deficit in Benin's trade balance, which is structurally in deficit."

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said that despite the relative weakness of the share of Beninese sales on the American market, the measure could have notable repercussions on several macroeconomic indicators: "One can notably expect a contraction of investment in sectors oriented towards export to the United States, a fall in the incomes of the producers concerned, as well as a decrease in the volume of goods transiting through Benin bound for the American market. This last development could also negatively impact the country's port activities."

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said on the Glo-Djigbé Industrial Zone (Gdiz) textile sector that "it is too early to have a fairly precise estimate of the impact on the activities of the textile factories installed at the Gdiz," but that since conquering the American market is among investors' objectives there, "there is a risk of a slowdown in foreign investment," while adequate trade facilitation measures could improve competitiveness and attract investors ; "From my point of view, the situation should not be dramatised... our capacity to react can prevent our economy from suffering a significant slowdown in its growth rate."

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Argued that the response "must not be limited to seeking a short-term readjustment," because obtaining new unilateral preferences through bilateral renegotiation "will always expose Benin to the possibility of an abrupt reversal in the future"; urged continuation of the policy of diversifying export products and markets and the elimination of all practices and measures that obstruct competitiveness, so as to make the country "more resilient in the face of trade policy shocks from its partners."

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said on the fate of AGOA that the United States has, since President Trump's return, taken measures suggesting it is "no longer in a logic of special and differential treatment for developing countries — I am speaking of the suspension of the programmes managed by USAID," and that clarifications must be given by the American side ; proposed that the authorities assume AGOA will not be renewed after September 2025 and begin taking measures so as not to be excluded from the American market through lack of competitiveness.

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gildéric Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said such shocks create the conditions for a readjustment of economic strategies and that countries must avoid building their entire strategy on preferential agreements, since "unilateral preferences can be called into question at any time"; pointed to the AfCFTA as a mechanism for better access to the African market, and noted that Benin's membership of WAEMU, ECOWAS and the AU requires a concerted trade policy approach, since "the regional approach also increases our negotiating power."

title: NAB board engages Zambezi producers and traders

acts.speaker: Dr. Fidelis Mwazi, Chief Executive Officer of the Namibian Agronomic Board (NAB)
acts.speech: Outlined the NAB's five-year plan, emphasising its alignment with the recently launched sixth National Development Plan (NDP 6) by President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah ; noted that while Namibia has achieved 100% production in certain food categories, there are limitations in others.

acts.speaker: Ruth Masake, Deputy Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform
acts.speech: Encouraged farmers to voice their challenges, emphasising that such meetings are crucial for informing the ministry on how to best support the agricultural sector.

title: Visite de Joy Basu au Bénin: La sous-secrétaire séduite par les investissements économiques

acts.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
acts.speech: "I am here to understand how things work economically in Benin and to find out how the United States can be a better and very good partner." ; "What explains my visit to Benin is mainly the fact that the economic connection is very important between the United States and Africa, especially as concerns the Biden administration."

acts.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
acts.speech: Assured: "I had the opportunity to listen to companies, members of civil society, entrepreneurs, to visit facilities such as the Autonomous Port of Cotonou and the GDIZ, and this allows us at the State Department level to see what form to give our economic cooperation to ensure that it is beneficial for both parties."

acts.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
acts.speech: Congratulated the Beninese government for its work in making the business environment more attractive through investments and measures such as digitalization, improved transparency and the fight against corruption; said she was impressed by the investments made towards an economy evolving very fast so as to have a positive impact on people's lives.

acts.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
acts.speech: Declared: "We also had the opportunity to meet the Minister of Industry and Trade and the Secretary of State for Energy. The round table with companies, civil society and other actors allowed us to learn more about the business environment in Benin, about what works and how the USA can work to strengthen economic cooperation and have a positive impact."

acts.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
acts.speech: "At the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, the first thing that struck me was its scale, its size, which shows how much it is a hub of trade, and it was really impressive to see the machines, the many containers that ensure the movement of goods which impact not only Benin but also its neighbours. At the GDIZ, it was really impressive to see everything that is being done in terms of processing products such as cashew nuts, cotton into textiles; it is relentless work that is very promising for Benin's economic development."

acts.speaker: Joy Basu, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of African Affairs for Economic and Regional Affairs
acts.speech: Said she was happy to see that American taxpayers' money, through the energy transformers installed under the second MCC compact, has served to improve the lives of the Beninese people.

title: Frères et sœurs jumeaux de Tori Bossito

acts.speaker: Head of State of Benin
acts.speech: Affirms the will to establish where responsibility lies (for the Tori-Bossito tragedy).

acts.speaker: Birago Diop, Senegalese writer
acts.speech: Convinced us that: in Africa, the dead are not dead, the dead have never gone away.

title: Watu milioni 14 hatarini kufa, kisa kusitishwa misaada ya USAID

acts.speaker: New study published in the scientific journal The Lancet
acts.speech: Explains in detail how the gains made over the past two decades in reducing child and adult deaths could collapse following the formal closure of USAID; reports that between 2001 and 2021 USAID assistance helped reduce malaria and neglected diseases by more than 50 percent worldwide, that USAID funding reduced child deaths by 44 percent and deaths overall by an average of 15 percent, and that a total of 91 million deaths were averted, including 30 million deaths of children under five.

acts.speaker: Researchers (authors of the Lancet study)
acts.speech: "Our estimates show that, if the funding-cut measures announced and implemented in the first half of 2025 are not reversed, a large number of avoidable deaths could occur by 2030," the researchers said. ; "Our estimates are often higher because they take into account not only the direct effects of USAID health projects, as earlier studies did, but also the broader effects of USAID aid. These effects may have contributed greatly to this agency's success in reducing deaths," they explained.

acts.speaker: Scientists (authors of the Lancet study)
acts.speech: Said that between 2000 and 2023 deaths of children under five fell from 10.1 million to 4.8 million; however, they warn that halting USAID assistance could disrupt those gains and make it difficult to reach the Sustainable Development Goal of reducing child deaths to below 25 per 1,000 children by 2030.

acts.speaker: Researchers (authors of the Lancet study)
acts.speech: Warn that the effect of cutting off that aid is equivalent to a global pandemic or a major war, the difference being, they say, that this catastrophe can be prevented through a change of policy.

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
acts.speech: Announced the decision to close USAID through a 900-word speech titled "Make Foreign Aid Great Again", saying American citizens should not continue to pay taxes to support governments that do not work in faraway nations.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Ordered the suspension of USAID's operations, under which much of the aid, largely in the health sector, has been halted.

title: An III du rétablissement des relations Burkina Faso-Chine : L’ambassadeur, LI Jian, appelle à la construction d’un avenir commun

acts.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
acts.speech: In a speech delivered live on Facebook on Wednesday 26 May 2021, on the occasion of the third anniversary of the restoration of Sino-Burkinabè relations, argued for the deepening of cooperation between the two countries: “It is a great pleasure to meet you on the occasion of the third anniversary of the restoration of diplomatic relations between the Republic of China and Burkina Faso. Three years ago, to the day, the Chinese State Councillor and Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Mr WANG Yi and his Burkinabè counterpart H.E. Mr Alpha BARRY signed the joint communiqué marking the resumption of Sino-Burkinabè diplomatic relations. Since then, that date has been inscribed and engraved in the history of Sino-African relations.” ; “I have now been living and working in Burkina Faso for three years. Here, it is like a great construction site where everything is moving forward step by step... I am delighted and at the same time galvanised by the wisdom, tolerance, perseverance and dynamism of Burkina Faso, advancing along its own path of development, and by the patriotism, bravery, diligence and optimism of the Burkinabè people.”

acts.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
acts.speech: On the results of Sino-Burkinabè cooperation: said cooperation has yielded fruitful results in health, education, agriculture and infrastructure, that the 113 school complexes financed by China have been fully completed, that the Chinese side is coordinating the final technical aspects of the Bobo-Dioulasso hospital project, that 5,331 tonnes of rice in emergency food aid will shortly be handed over in full, and that the “Smart Burkina” project is expected to start very soon ; “Rest assured that on Burkina Faso’s path of socio-economic development, China will never fail to be present and to provide its support accordingly.” ; said Chinese technical cooperation missions (medical, agricultural, vocational training and the millet project) have worked hard down to distant villages and fields, and that under the “Brightness Action” some twenty Chinese ophthalmologists from a hospital in Wenzhou performed free cataract operations on more than 400 Burkinabè in 2018 and 2019 with a 100% success rate ; said that in 2020 China launched a mechanism exempting customs duties on 97% of Burkinabè products exported to China and that trade volume reached 400 million dollars in 2020, up 24.5% on the previous year, a new record.

acts.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
acts.speech: On Covid-19 cooperation: said that as soon as the first confirmed case was notified in Burkina Faso, China mobilised on a large scale, bringing in by special flights more than a million masks, some ten thousand protective suits, some twenty thousand PCR reagent tests and about a hundred ventilators and oxygen machines; that China financed the rehabilitation of two isolation buildings at the Yalgado Ouédraogo University Hospital and the emergency department of the Koudougou Regional Hospital; and that in April 2020 the Chinese government sent a team of doctors specialised in fighting Covid-19 ; “We must therefore continue to remain vigilant and united, to deepen our cooperation in the field of health and to constantly improve our capacities in human resources, infrastructure and equipment in order always to be able to meet long-term challenges.”

acts.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
acts.speech: On China’s development model and poverty reduction: said this year marks the centenary of the founding of the Chinese Communist Party, which is leading 1.4 billion Chinese and in 100 years has built a moderately prosperous society enabling 800 million Chinese to emerge definitively from absolute poverty ; “China has succeeded in finding its own path of development, and the development miracle in China shows the whole world, especially developing countries and African countries, that it is entirely possible for a country, previously oppressed and underdeveloped, to rise again with sovereignty, dignity, independence and the satisfaction of its people.” ; “China has the will, the experience and the capacity to help Burkina Faso achieve this objective and win victory over poverty” ; said more than 800 professionals have travelled to China for training or seminars, about a hundred Burkinabè students have received Chinese scholarships, and more than 20 online seminars are planned this year for 500 professionals.

acts.speaker: Li Jian, Ambassador of China to Burkina Faso
acts.speech: Called on the international community to increase its investments and support for Africa in general and Burkina Faso in particular: “Efforts must converge towards Burkina Faso to help the country recover as soon as possible from the negative effects of the Covid-19 pandemic and to return to its momentum of growth” ; expressed his sincere thanks to all those who support the development of Sino-Burkinabè relations, and said: “I am firmly convinced that, with the continued deepening of Sino-Burkinabè cooperation, we will open a golden period of the new era for the development of our two countries and for the happiness of our two peoples.”

acts.speaker: Adama Compaoré, Ambassador of Burkina Faso to China
acts.speech: Noted in an interview that China has played an important and constructive role in the economic and social development process of Burkina Faso.

acts.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese State Councillor and Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Affirmed in a full session of the UN Security Council, during the Chinese presidency in May, that as a brother, friend and partner China will always defend the interests of African countries and will not hesitate to undertake all useful actions for the benefit of African peoples ; at the celebration of Africa Day, reaffirmed that strengthening unity and cooperation with African countries constitutes the constant priority of Chinese diplomacy.

acts.speaker: Christophe Joseph Marie Dabiré, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
acts.speech: Stressed in his State of the Nation Address that one of the main objectives of the Burkinabè government for the next five years is the reduction of poverty.

title: Gestion des forêts en Afrique de l’Ouest: Des experts font le point des actions menées

acts.speaker: José Tonato, Minister of Living Environment and Infrastructure, in charge of Sustainable Development (Benin)
acts.speech: Said the ambition by 2040 is for Benin's forest areas to be better managed for their multiple functions.

acts.speaker: Representative of Sweden, financial partner on the project
acts.speech: "We hope that this project will be implemented successfully for the well-being of the communities."

acts.speaker: Ange Obama, FAO Resident Representative
acts.speech: Said that wetland forests constitute an important source of fuel and food but are extremely affected by degradation, meaning that the implementation of specific actions under the project 'Global Forest Transformation for People and Climate: Focus on West Africa' will benefit communities and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: HCB investing 100 million dollars in road rehabilitation

acts.speaker: José Munice, HCB executive administrator for Production, Energy Transmission and Procurement
acts.speech: Said, speaking to reporters, that the initiative to rehabilitate National Road N 301 is part of the 10-Year Vital Capex Project, which is aimed at developing a series of structural projects for the rehabilitation, modernization, and expansion of the HCB power plant, and that the investment aims to make the road robust enough to support the heavy vehicles that will transport equipment for the rehabilitation and modernization: "HCB, which celebrates its 50th anniversary this year, is developing a series of structural projects for the rehabilitation, modernization, and expansion of its power plant. The 10-Year Vital Capex Project is aimed at reversing the negative impact caused by the frequent maintenance of obsolete equipment."

acts.speaker: José Munice, HCB executive administrator for Production, Energy Transmission and Procurement
acts.speech: Said the 10-Year Vital CAPEX programme arises from a technical analysis of the equipment, after the infrastructure completed 50 years: "It was found that a significant portion of the equipment has been in operation for about 50 years, a fact that poses operational risks and so investment projects were developed to mitigate the risk."

acts.speaker: José Munice, HCB executive administrator for Production, Energy Transmission and Procurement
acts.speech: Highlighted the rehabilitation of the South Bank Power Station and the Songo and Matambo substations: "With the rehabilitation of the plant, the company foresees an increase in production capacity of 90 MW. With five generating units, we will replace the alternators, the turbines, the control systems, and the auxiliary systems, among others" ; on the Matambo Substation, responsible for distributing the energy generated by HCB to the central and northern regions of the country: "Here, we will also invest in modernizing and replacing some equipment that is already beyond its useful life" ; he also mentioned the proposed North Bank Power Station, which will be built alongside the existing power station, generating an additional 1,245 megawatts ; and on the solar project: "Among the projects is the construction of a 400 MW solar power plant planned for Matambo, Changara district, also in Tete province. The main objective of the solar power plant is to supply the energy deficit during the repair of the five turbines installed at HCB, one per year. Pre-feasibility studies for the project's implementation are already under way."

title: VIDEO: Rwandan President praises ‘unconventional’ Trump's USAID shutdown

acts.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
acts.speech: "President Trump has an unconventional way of doing things," Kagame said in an interview with CNN reporter Larry Madowo. "I completely agree with him on many things." ; when pressed by a CNN reporter to explain how the shutdown of USAID might negatively affect Rwanda, said that the country might actually benefit from the cessation of USAID funds: "I think from being hurt, we might learn some lessons."

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Has repeatedly signaled that the US Agency for International Development (USAID) should be shut down and cease to distribute taxpayer funds around the world to aid and relief projects; previously told reporters on Sunday that USAID is "run by radical lunatics" ; has also signaled that DOGE, which is tasked with eliminating government spending and waste and streamlining operations, will investigate the Education Department and the Pentagon.

acts.speaker: U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols (court ruling)
acts.speech: A Trump appointee, agreed to block an order that would have given just 30 days for the thousands of overseas USAID workers the administration wanted to place on abrupt administrative leave to move their families back to the U.S. at the government's expense.

acts.speaker: Larry Madowo, CNN reporter (@LarryMadowo, post on X)
acts.speech: "President Paul Kagame says he 'completely agrees with President Trump on many things' after he froze US foreign aid and closed USAID. The Rwandan president tells me that African countries must wean themselves off aid."

title: Communiqué du Cabinet Royal: Visite d’Emmanuel Macron au Maroc

acts.speaker: Royal Cabinet of Morocco (communique)
acts.speech: Announced that “His Majesty King Mohammed VI, may God assist Him, held talks today at the Royal Palace in Rabat with the President of the French Republic, H.E. Mr Emmanuel Macron, who is making a State Visit to Morocco from 28 to 30 October at the invitation of the Sovereign”, and that the talks concerned the transition to a new era in relations between Morocco and France, within the framework of a renewed Exceptional Partnership and a strategic roadmap for the years to come.

acts.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and Emmanuel Macron, President of France (joint position in the communique)
acts.speech: The two Heads of State intend, through this renewed partnership, to give a decisive impetus to the multidimensional relations of excellence between Morocco and France ; agreed to work together to strengthen the Euro-Mediterranean, African and Atlantic projection, in a common approach in favour of prosperity and human and sustainable development ; stressed the importance of renewing, in depth, the partnership between the two shores of the Mediterranean, in order to build a more stable, sustainable and prosperous future for the whole region, while responding to current socio-economic and environmental challenges.

acts.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
acts.speech: Hailed the constructive role of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, in the service of peace in the Middle East.

acts.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and Emmanuel Macron, President of France (joint position in the communique)
acts.speech: Called for an immediate cessation of the attacks in Gaza and Lebanon, while stressing the priority of protecting civilian populations, and the importance of guaranteeing and facilitating the delivery of sufficient humanitarian aid, while putting an end to the regional conflagration ; recalled the urgency of reactivating the peace process, within the framework of the two-State solution, with an independent Palestinian State, on the borders of 4 June 1967, with East Jerusalem as its Capital.

acts.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
acts.speech: Extended an official invitation to His Majesty King Mohammed VI to make a State visit to France.

acts.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
acts.speech: Accepted the invitation, whose date will be agreed through diplomatic channels.

title: Al-Shabaab eases smartphone, internet ban in newly-captured Somali towns | Somali Guardian

acts.speaker: Analysts
acts.speech: View the development as a calculated attempt by the group to counter the federal government's narrative that paints the militants as barriers to modernization and technological advancement. The strategic loosening of restrictions may be intended to portray Al-Shabaab as more tolerant and in tune with younger generations, particularly in contrast to the government's perceived failures.

acts.speaker: International observers
acts.speech: Warn that the country – particularly the capital Mogadishu – risks following an "Afghanistan-style" trajectory.

title: Cabo Verde e a nova ordem mundial

acts.speaker: Fareed Zakaria, columnist (article in the Washington Post)
acts.speech: Underlines the idea that we are witnessing the formation of a new world order, in which the predictability and multilateralism that marked the second half of the twentieth century are being put to the test.

acts.speaker: World Bank report “Cabo Verde - Navigating Rough Seas”
acts.speech: Emphasises the need for the country to reinforce its resilience and accelerate its pace of growth, as a response to the increased vulnerability generated by the international context.

acts.speaker: World Bank
acts.speech: Highlights that Cabo Verde’s institutional stability is one of its greatest assets.

acts.speaker: World Bank report “Cabo Verde - Navigating Rough Seas”
acts.speech: Warns of the importance of strengthening climate resilience, at a time when environmental and sustainability issues remain a priority for the survival of small island States.

title: Gambia-Senegal Agree to Address Trade Barriers

acts.speaker: Report of the Trade Committee of the Gambian Parliament
acts.speech: Contains the development that Gambian authorities and their Senegalese counterparts have agreed to address issues affecting transit traders, such as the exorbitant and unnecessary charges and delays that traders from the two countries are faced with ; one of such issues highlighted in the report is the payment of exorbitant escort charges which traders are obliged to pay to avert unnecessary delay at borders ; according to the report, the National Assembly is responsible for performing oversight of the activities of the Trade Ministry and its satellite institutions or agencies.

acts.speaker: Hon. Kebba Jallow, Chairperson of the Trade Committee of the Gambian Parliament
acts.speech: “This mandate is vested on the committee by the National Assembly under Section 109 of the 1997 Constitution and Standing Order 97. In addition, the committee has the power under Section 109 subsection 2 (B), to investigate any matter of public interest,” he said, reminding his colleagues that during the Fifth Legislature, the committee embarked on a countrywide tour, to both official and unofficial border posts, to assess and generate firsthand information on the implementation of the ECOWAS Protocol and Conventions for the transit of goods across the country’s borders ; “In this regard, GRA officials informed the committee that their Senegalese counterparts do not implement the ECOWAS Inter State Road Transit Convention (ISRT)” ; he said the committee learned that transit goods from the Gambia are being charged prohibitive or double escort fees, to the extent of making “transit trade in the Gambia unattractive, which in turn affects custom revenue” ; “In the same vein, the Gambian traders in transit trade across the border expressed similar concern,” he said ; he said customs officials on the borders subject transit traders to unnecessary charges that contravene the provisions of the ISRT Convention “by imposing unnecessary and multiple escort fees, leaving the traders without choice but to pay, to avert unnecessary delay.” ; he said that after the meeting the authorities of the two states agreed to dedicate their efforts to engage all the relevant authorities in their respective countries on the matter; and to ensure that trade and other border-related issues are addressed ; “There is a need to interconnect the two countries’ customs IT systems (GAINDE and ASYCUDA) in order to harmonize procedures and thus solve the problem of transit documents. The committee also recommended that GRA through the relevant Ministry, engage ECOWAS to operationalize the Interconnected System for the Management of Goods in Transit (SIGMAT) between the two countries,” he said.

acts.speaker: GRA (Gambia Revenue Authority) officials
acts.speech: Informed the committee that their Senegalese counterparts do not implement the ECOWAS Inter State Road Transit Convention (ISRT), and later informed the committee that the situation remains the same, “because their counterparts are not implementing this convention.”

acts.speaker: Senegalese authorities (met during the visit)
acts.speech: “The authorities emphasized the importance of the visit as the two states are inseparable and share the same people, culture, social values, and economic activities among others,” he said. He reiterated among others “that the bond between the Gambia and Senegal makes the countries as one, only to be divided by the West for their own interest.”

acts.speaker: Gambian delegation / members of the Gambia’s Trade Committee
acts.speech: Highlighted the need for collaboration between the two states, as they are all part of ECOWAS and subjected to the convention and protocols of the regional bloc ; “The Gambian delegation informed their Senegalese counterparts that the non-trade barriers that transit traders experience from one border to another is exorbitant and therefore there is a need for dialogue to address these challenges,” he said ; told their Senegalese counterparts that the proper implementation of the convention is beneficial to the two states and therefore the need for them to come together for the smooth implementation of the convention.

acts.speaker: Gambian traders in transit trade
acts.speech: Expressed similar concern about prohibitive or double escort fees charged across the border.

title: US funding pause: UNAIDS warns of HIV infections in Ethiopia

acts.speaker: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
acts.speech: Warned that recent decisions by the United States to suspend funding to Ethiopia's national HIV response will be "particularly severe", affecting more than 270,000 beneficiaries across the country's Oromia and Gambella regions, as well as Addis Ababa ; In a statement released on Thursday said the "pause of U.S. assistance to community programs and drop-in centers serving women, young girls, and priority populations at higher risk of HIV infection means tens of thousands of individuals will no longer be able to access critical services." ; The agency further noted that "the closure of many drop-in centers and the termination of outreach workers' and peer educators' contracts will effectively shut off support to vulnerable groups."

acts.speaker: Ethiopia's Ministry of Health (MoH)
acts.speech: On Wednesday instructed health bureaux to halt all activities and payments related to employees hired under the U.S. government budget support, citing the termination of funding from the USAID.

acts.speaker: USAID
acts.speech: Said the disruption of service in Addis Ababa, Oromia, and Gambella will put 235,560 people at risk of new HIV infections and sexually transmitted diseases.

title: Mozambique: US Ambassador Peter Vrooman presents farewell greetings to President Daniel Chapo

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
acts.speech: Reaffirmed on Wednesday (30-04) in Maputo that the country intends to consolidate bilateral relations with the United States of America (USA).

acts.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
acts.speech: Said the US administration will strengthen the partnership between the two countries, in the search for new opportunities in the private sector and US investments in strategic areas, citing the example of gas, health and infrastructure ; “There are 50 years of cooperation and partnerships between Mozambique and the United States of America” ; He stressed the importance of the US investing almost five billion dollars in the natural gas sector ; “Investment in roads, bridges, and other infrastructure areas is very important for the country’s economic growth.” ; Highlighted the importance of the Mozambican private sector in working together with the American private sector and other countries, as a basis for sustainable economic growth.

acts.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
acts.speech: “We talked about the possibility of continuing some projects, the importance of the US President’s AIDS Relief Program (PEPFAR), a program that saves the lives of many people in the country.” ; Guaranteed the continuity of this initiative, which has benefited many Mozambicans ; “I also mentioned the continuation of some programs that we have in the area of humanitarian assistance, which continues, but we also talked about the challenges.”

acts.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
acts.speech: Encouraged the Mozambican Head of State in his optimism, vision and resilience: “I think his optimism is very important, as the national anthem says, stone by stone building the new day. And this idea, I think we will work towards this and we are together.”

acts.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
acts.speech: Said that his mission as a diplomat was over, but relations between the two countries would continue.

title: PR da Nigéria remodela Governo no meio de crise gerada pelo elevado custo de vida

acts.speaker: Nigerian presidency (official statement/communiqué)
acts.speech: According to the statement, Tinubu appointed new ministers for humanitarian aid and poverty reduction, trade and investment, labour and livestock development, as well as deputy ministers for Foreign Affairs, Education and Housing; the ministers of Education, Tourism, Women's Affairs and Youth Development and the deputy minister of Housing were dismissed.

title: KOICA launches maiden ICT project in Eastern Region

acts.speaker: Dong Hyun Lee, Country Director of KOICA
acts.speech: Launching the programme in Koforidua, stressed the critical role being played by ICT in economic growth to facilitate national development ; Citing Korea's example, indicated that in the 1990s, the country's strategic integration of ICT into its educational system laid the foundation for its success ; Stated that Korea's ICT sector had contributed $224 billion in exports, employing over 1.7 billion people ; Added that Korea's deployment journey, which was supported by foreign aid, had inspired the country's commitment to give back to other developing countries such as Ghana, by sharing its expertise in ICT.

acts.speaker: Dong Hyun Lee, Country Director of KOICA
acts.speech: Highlighted Ghana's potential to bridge its ICT education gap through collaborative efforts and was hopeful that the project would foster long-term positive impact to empower local communities and build self-sufficiency ; Indicated that the first batch of KOICA's volunteers had already been grouped into three teams to ensure its successful implementation.

acts.speaker: Dr Ivy Asantewaa Owusu, Eastern Regional Education Director
acts.speech: Outlined the importance of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education, which, to her, should be prioritised for both individuals and national development.

acts.speaker: Dr Ivy Asantewaa Owusu, Eastern Regional Education Director
acts.speech: Asked school heads and teachers from the beneficiary schools to actively take part and collaborate effectively with the volunteers to ensure the long-term sustainability of the benefits to be derived ; Stated that the partnership between KOICA and her outfit was a promising step to empower the next generation of Ghanaian students with ICT skills ; Added that by improving infrastructure and providing quality training, it would foster a collaborative learning environment to drive innovation and growth, paving the way for a brighter digital future for the country.

title: Validation de trois documents stratégiques à l’IGN: Pour disposer d’un outil stratégique de gestion performante

acts.speaker: Noël Fonton, Minister responsible for Urban Planning, Housing and Sanitation of Benin
acts.speech: In his opening remarks, recalled the importance of the various documents to be validated during the session: "Through a strategic plan with deadlines and resources, a formalised decision-making procedure must, from now on and once validated, guide the Institute's various actions up to 2019," the minister stated; for him, results cannot be achieved in an organisation without qualified human resources, and he remains convinced that IGN's training plan for the period 2015-2017 will allow it to improve its performance and better serve the population.

acts.speaker: Noël Fonton, Minister responsible for Urban Planning, Housing and Sanitation of Benin
acts.speech: Speaking of the document on the audit of the photovoltaic installations of Benin's permanent stations, recalled that they are a legacy of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) and that their management is entrusted to IGN: "These installations deserve our attention because they constitute the support network that ensures the reliability of data for sound and secure land management and, beyond that, for harmonious development of territorial planning," the minister stressed; he specifies that one of the important challenges of the continued operation of these permanent stations is energy, and that the audit will make it possible to rethink the photovoltaic installation arrangements in place today. The minister expressed the wish that, at the end of the proceedings, IGN's performance would improve and that it would have strategic management tools of the greatest importance.

acts.speaker: Roch Abdon Bah, Director General of the Institut national géographique (IGN)
acts.speech: Expressed to the authority the gratitude of all the staff for his leadership, then returned to the importance of the various documents to be validated for his organisation: "Without all this, it would just be flying blind. That is something IGN could not do," he concluded.

title: Waathirika USAID wasimulia machungu uamuzi wa Trump

acts.speaker: USAID project worker (anonymous, asked not to be named; health worker with wife and three children, Makongo Juu, Dar es Salaam)
acts.speech: Told Mwananchi that he never thought he would fall into the disaster of losing his job, since he had a long-term contract, and that he is going through hardship after missing his January salary because of President Trump’s order: “In January we did not get a salary, so we had to keep going to work as usual. But later we were told to stand down to allow for the 90 days.” ; “I paid the house rent at the beginning of January for the whole year, school fees for the children and other important things, and I was left with no money. My expectation was that the January salary would help me run the family.” ; “For now I have asked the landlord for help to find another tenant so that he can return that rent to me, so I can look for a cheaper house and get some capital for whatever business I can do. I have no certainty of returning to employment, so I am looking for an alternative early.”

acts.speaker: Another worker at another organisation (anonymous)
acts.speech: “We started working from home, and when the end of the month came we were not paid the January salary. We have already begun to taste the hardship because, as you know, January has many demands, and to also miss a salary — we are going through a very hard time.”

acts.speaker: John Ambrose, psychology expert
acts.speech: Said these workers will be affected psychologically because they do not accept what has happened, explaining that the person concerned may experience anger, blame and recrimination and so may do things that are not right; advised them to come to terms with the situation and let life go on.

acts.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
acts.speech: Called on the Government to make sure it finds a quick solution in order to protect the skills and remove the disruption to citizens: “We recommend urgent steps to rescue this situation; we cannot dodge that responsibility. The Government should go on carrying out an assessment of the impacts and confront them scientifically.”

acts.speaker: Alexander Baluhya, President of the Tanzania National Nurses Association (TANNA)
acts.speech: Said the departure of many workers at the same time from health facilities is a major challenge that has come at a time when the Nation was not prepared and the workers were not prepared, and that the Government may come up with a plan to rescue the shortfall: “The Government must take responsibility; there was already a shortage, so it will increase. Those affected are not the nurses left with a heavy workload, but the citizens who will not get their services on time. I believe the Government must have an alternative way to see how to reduce this challenge.” ; said the workers are not at fault in any way, so their entitlements must be looked at carefully and administered in line with their contracts.

acts.speaker: Fadhili Hezekiah, President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Tanzania (PST)
acts.speech: Said statistics are important for the country to know how many have been affected, and that many pharmacists were in HIV/AIDS projects: “The Government should know how big the shortage is. A thorough assessment of what should be done at this time. Perhaps there are those who were paid 50 per cent by the Government and 50 per cent by the organisations — we should also know this. Perhaps the impact may not be seen directly in research and empowerment, but I believe it will be seen in services.”

acts.speaker: Regnant Kivinge, chairman of Mafinga Town Council
acts.speech: Said the Councillors’ Council has set aside 15.6 million shillings for the payment of workers who were being paid by the Benjamin William Mkapa Foundation and the USAID Afya Yangu Programme: “We have made monthly arrangements; after seeing that these organisations had issued a letter of suspension, so that our citizens would not be affected, we had to make the decision to pay from our own internal funds — out of 73 workers we have retained 26 who were working in essential areas.” ; said they chose eight essential areas, especially HIV/AIDS, cervical cancer, family planning and other important ones.

acts.speaker: Dr Hamad Nyembea, Director of the Curative Services Department, Ministry of Health
acts.speech: Told Mwananchi on February 12 that an analysis had already been done regarding the shortage that will arise and that facilities had already made adjustments by looking at alternatives: “Whether it is a hospital or a health centre, they have already looked at the areas that will have a shortage and been able to redistribute those workers who are employed by the Government so that they can fill those positions and services are not shaken.”

acts.speaker: Paschal Mbotta, Siha District Medical Officer
acts.speech: Answering a question from the council chairman Dancan Urasa, said six workers were the ones affected by that decision and that their jobs have been stalled: “The impact that exists is that six workers at Siha District Hospital have had their contracts terminated after that announcement, but there are others whose number I have not yet obtained; we will follow up in various places including Ashengai and Ngarenairobi in order to get the exact number of workers who will be affected.” ; said those workers have been retained so that they can continue to help patients living with HIV whom they have been following up at their homes and treating.

acts.speaker: Mark Masue, Acting Executive Director of Siha District Council
acts.speech: Said the director’s office has not received any instructions from the Government: “We are continuing with this arrangement while we await the Government’s instructions on their matter.”

title: MENACE DE FERMETURE DE CAMPS DE REFUGIES PAR LE PAM AU SOUDAN : L’avenir de l’aide humanitaire en pointillés ? - Editions Le Pays

acts.speaker: Cicero
acts.speech: "Pecunia nervus belli (money is the sinew of war)."

title: US funds mobile ICU for Walvis Bay

acts.speaker: Tiffany Miller, acting deputy chief of mission of the US embassy
acts.speech: Explained at the official handover ceremony that the mission of the OHDACA is to fund humanitarian assistance activities and enhance the capacity of partner nations to prepare for and respond to humanitarian crises ; “This fully equipped five-bed intensive care unit is a mobile and self-sufficient system. It provides the ministry of health and social services with a resource that can be used to support the local population in Walvis Bay or can be disassembled, transported and reassembled in a matter of days to respond to a crisis in the most remote locations” ; explained that the unit is self-sufficient with dual generator power, water and sewage systems, and air conditioning, allowing it to operate autonomously in the field ; “It is also stocked with N$600 000 worth of medicine to ensure the ICU is immediately ready for operations. A team of Namibian personnel, including doctors and nurses from the ministry, were trained in all aspects of the ICU set-up as well as the individual pieces of medical equipment within the ICU.”

acts.speaker: Tiffany Miller, acting deputy chief of mission of the US embassy
acts.speech: Further stated that this is the first of four donations that will be installed across Namibia in the coming months: “These donations include a second five-bed ICU in Otjiwarongo, as well as two field hospitals in Outapi and Katima Mulilo, each including a 30-bed negative pressure isolation facility and a UN Level I Urgent Care Clinic. These donations will total over N$128 million in value and represent the largest single DoD humanitarian assistance donation to the Namibian people to date.”

acts.speaker: Ben Nangombe, executive director of the health ministry
acts.speech: Explained that the addition of this state-of-the-art mobile intensive care unit comes at a crucial time as the ministry is enhancing capacity at public health facilities nationwide to provide services to the people ; “Following Covid-19, we had about 23 ICU beds in Onandjokwe, Oshakati, Katutura Hospital and Windhoek Central Hospital. There were no other ICU beds in state health facilities, and we realised that there was a serious gap.” ; said the ministry, in order to address the shortfall in ICU beds at all 34 district hospitals, is going to get ICU capacity funded by the Namibian government ; “By the completion of this project, we will have no fewer than 200 ICU beds. We know that we need to bring services closer to the people, and we are truly grateful for all the support we are receiving to increase that capacity.”

acts.speaker: Ben Nangombe, executive director of the health ministry
acts.speech: Explained that in terms of Walvis Bay, it will not only have ICU capacity funded by the government but will also have an additional mobile ICU facility: “In recent years, the demand for ICU services has grown significantly. Many patients requiring intensive care have had to be transferred to Windhoek. The long distances present considerable risk. The long-distance transfers not only strain our healthcare resources but also place additional stress on patients and their families. The establishment of a fully equipped ICU facility here in Walvis Bay will mitigate these challenges, ensuring that critical care is accessible in a timely manner.”

title: Mozambique: President Chapo concludes two-day visit to Rwanda - Photos

acts.speaker: Rwandan Presidency
acts.speech: Hailed Chapo's visit — the first to Rwanda since he was elected president in October 2024 — saying it “reaffirmed the shared commitment to further strengthen the existing fruitful bilateral collaboration for the benefit of the people of Rwanda and Mozambique.” ; posted: “This afternoon at Kigali International Airport, President Kagame bid farewell to President Daniel Francisco Chapo at the conclusion of his two-day working visit to Rwanda. The visit reaffirmed the shared commitment to further strengthen the existing fruitful…”

acts.speaker: President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and President Daniel Chapo of Mozambique
acts.speech: The two Presidents reaffirmed their commitment to bilateral cooperation in various areas, including peace and security as well as in trade and economic development.

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique (post on X, August 28, 2025)
acts.speech: “We have concluded our working visit to the Republic of Rwanda, marked by productive meetings and by the strengthening of the bonds of friendship and cooperation between our countries. Among the main gains, the Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) and the Memorandum of… stand out.”

title: Tourism and sustainable transformation: Important points to ponder - Daily News

acts.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
acts.speech: Stresses: “Strengthening multilateralism through tourism will deliver results in socio-economic inclusion, sustainable development, peace and understanding.” ; Addressing G20 Tourism Ministers, he commended the South African Presidency’s focus on inclusion and sustainability: “More than a motto, the theme for South Africa’s G20 Presidency ‘solidarity, equality, sustainability’, reminds us that Equality and Sustainability can only be achieved through targeted policies, unified efforts and mutual support among countries – a recognition that in an interconnected world, the challenges faced by one country can have ripple effects globally.”

acts.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
acts.speech: Reaffirms the critical importance of progressing digital transformation, financing for development, investment and resilient ecosystems in tourism, stressing that there will be no resilience without sustainability ; Calls for supporting innovation and stressed that emerging technologies can transform tourism MSMEs, which are the backbone of tourism, but only with adequate financing and programmes to close the digital divide and promote inclusion.

acts.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
acts.speech: Noted that though “for many developing countries, including Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States, tourism is a major source of employment, foreign exchange and tax revenues. Yet, the sector continues to be overlooked as a tool for development, with the total Official Development Assistance disbursements for tourism remaining below 0.11 per cent of total ODA.”

acts.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
acts.speech: Highlights South Africa’s G20 Presidency as a show of the continent’s leadership in the global agenda. He recalled that Africa is home to 19 per cent of the world’s population, with 70 per cent of sub-Saharan Africa under the age of 30. “The opportunities the continent offers in tourism are many” he said and “unlocking tourism investment and development for jobs and inclusion is a core priority of the UN Tourism Agenda for Africa.”

acts.speaker: World Tourism Barometer (report)
acts.speech: According to the latest World Tourism Barometer, international tourist arrivals increased 5 per cent in the first half of 2025.

title: US Women’s equal pay claim dismissed by court

acts.speaker: Molly Levinson, the players’ spokeswoman
acts.speech: Said that they planned to appeal against the decision: “We are shocked and disappointed. We will not give up our hard work for equal pay. We are confident in our case and steadfast in our commitment to ensuring that girls and women who play this sport will not be valued as lesser just because of their gender.”

acts.speaker: Federal judge Gary Klausner
acts.speech: Allowed the players’ case for unfair treatment in travel, housing and medical support to go to trial, which is set for 16 June in Los Angeles.

acts.speaker: The court (ruling)
acts.speech: Giving its ruling, the court said: “The women’s team has been paid more on both a cumulative and an average per-game basis than the men’s team over the class period.”

acts.speaker: Megan Rapinoe, US striker
acts.speech: Tweeted after the equal pay claim was dismissed: “We will never stop fighting for equality.”

acts.speaker: Alex Morgan, US striker
acts.speech: “Although disappointing to hear this news, this will not discourage us in our fight for equality.”

acts.speaker: US Soccer Federation (USSF)
acts.speech: Said it wanted to work with the team to “chart a positive path forward to grow the game both here at home and around the world.”

acts.speaker: US men’s national team (statement)
acts.speech: Issued a statement in February criticizing the governing body, saying that “the federation continues to discriminate against the women in their wages and working conditions.”

title: African Guarantee Fund Launches $5 billion Mission 300 Local Currency Guarantee Facility to Accelerate Energy Access Across Africa

acts.speaker: African Guarantee Fund (AGF) (announcement)
acts.speech: announced the launch of its Mission 300 Local Currency Guarantee Facility, a groundbreaking initiative to mobilize $5 billion to support energy access projects across Africa, targeting financing for small and medium-sized enterprises in the Distributed Renewable Energy sector.

acts.speaker: Wale Shonibare, Director for Energy Financial Solutions, Policy and Regulations at the African Development Bank
acts.speech: said: “The Mission 300 Local Currency Guarantee Facility will encourage collaboration with African governments whilst leveraging concessional financing from the African Development Bank, the World Bank Group, and other development partners to scale the involvement of local banks in financing Distributed Renewable Energy solutions.”

acts.speaker: Jules Ngankam, AGF Group CEO
acts.speech: said: “AGF’s leadership in driving financial innovation for SMEs aligns seamlessly with the goals of Mission 300. By addressing financing gaps and fostering public-private partnerships, AGF plays a crucial role in driving inclusive energy solutions, accelerating the energy transition, and reducing carbon emissions across the continent.” ; “We have successfully implemented the Green Guarantee, which has facilitated progress toward national commitments under the Africa Energy Declaration, the African Union’s Vision 2063, and the global Sustainable Development Goals, fostering inclusive growth and climate resilience.”

title: Mali and IOM collaborate on migration management

acts.speaker: Malian government and the International Organization for Migration (IOM)
acts.speech: Have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation on migration management. During a recent meeting between Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maiga and IOM Deputy Chief of Staff Mohamed Abdiker, the two parties discussed key areas of collaboration, including revising the National Migration Policy to address current challenges and promote safe, orderly, and regular migration; IOM continuing to provide humanitarian assistance to Malian migrants in distress, including repatriation and reintegration programs; and exploring ways to harness the potential of the Malian diaspora to contribute to the country's development. Both parties agreed to work closely to address integrated border management and civil status modernization and ensure the protection of vulnerable migrants.

title: Guterres réitère son inquiétude face à la situation à Tindouf

acts.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
acts.speech: has once again expressed his deep concern about the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in the Tindouf refugee camps; in his latest report he said he was worried about the serious consequences of the surge in food prices, which disproportionately affects the Sahrawi populations ; “This situation, combined with extreme climatic conditions and a lack of economic opportunities, is plunging many Sahrawis into a state of malnutrition and great vulnerability.”

acts.speaker: UN Secretary-General's report
acts.speech: highlights serious human rights violations, including malnutrition, which causes illnesses such as anaemia among children, pregnant women and other camp inhabitants.

acts.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General (2024 report)
acts.speech: noted that the food security assessment reported a “deterioration of conditions in the camps”, due to a 30% reduction in dry food rations attributable to the rise in prices; according to this assessment, more than 80% of camp inhabitants now depend on food aid.

acts.speaker: Former members of the Polisario Front (testimonies)
acts.speech: indicate that only 20% of camp residents are of Sahrawi origin, while the rest would be made up of people from various tribes, notably Algerian.

acts.speaker: Sahrawi NGOs
acts.speech: have documented cases of mismanagement and diversion of resources, implicating Polisario officials in collaboration with the Algerian authorities.

title: Après le succès de «Vrais amis» : le créateur de «Tchèmin» prépare son 2ème album

acts.speaker: Beninese public / listeners (testimonies)
acts.speech: "He is an artist steeped in talent. He is a Beninese star in the making. With support, he will be a complete musician artist like certain great figures of African music." ; "All the songs, added to the rhythms performed, are evocative and draw everyone's attention to the advantages of Beninese culture. This new album by Fifido is a rich cocktail for the greats." ; According to the testimonies gathered, this artist now known to the Beninese public is full of talent and deserves support.

acts.speaker: Fifido (Fidele Dovenon), Beninese artist, creator of the "Tchemin" rhythm
acts.speech: Said that all these descriptions are no illusion since he took all his time to prepare this record ; Said the album "Vrais amis", which addresses several themes of life including love, courage and hope in God, is the fruit of several years of hard work ; Said that for him culture is the driving force of all development, and that much more is to come from him in the promotion of his country's culture ; "I ask all people of goodwill to come and support what I am doing."

title: Siri maambukizi ya VVU Kigoma kupungua
