acts.speaker: Dk Frederick Ndossi, Director of Treatment and Care Services at Tanzania Health Promotion Support (THPS) through the 'Afya Hatua' project, on behalf of THPS Executive Director Dr Redempta Mbatia
acts.speech: Released statistics showing HIV infections in Kigoma region fell from 3.4 percent in 2013 to 1.7 percent in 2023, equal to a 50 percent decline. He said the drop in HIV infections and the increased willingness of people living with HIV to join treatment and care services in the region is the result of the efforts of THPS in collaboration with stakeholders and the Government to build understanding, an enabling environment and community awareness. "Currently, many service recipients are in good health and are continuing to build our nation through various activities. Had there not been treatment as was the case in past years, many would be spending much of their time in bed suffering from illnesses," said Dr Ndossi.

acts.speaker: Dk Frederick Ndossi, Director of Treatment and Care Services at THPS
acts.speech: Said the 40 motorcycles, worth more than Sh141 million, were provided through the 'Afya Hatua' project implemented by THPS with funding from the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (Pepfar) through the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). He said they will be distributed to HIV treatment and care centres and clinics in the councils of Buhigwe (5), Kakonko (4), Kasulu (9), Kibondo, Kigoma (2) and Uvinza (11). "These motorcycles aim to enable essential HIV-related services, including transporting HIV viral load (HVL) test samples to the laboratories," said Dr Ndossi. He also said they will enable follow-up of clients who missed clinic appointments and encourage adherence to services, follow up on reports and contact tracing of sexual partners so that they can be reached by HIV testing services, and support community services such as the distribution of drugs that reduce the risk of HIV infection (PrEP) and the promotion of condom use.

acts.speaker: Thobias Andengenye, Kigoma Regional Commissioner
acts.speech: Speaking after receiving the motorcycles, urged health service providers at treatment and care centres in the region to respect the purpose for which the support was given, warning that those who divert them to other uses will not be overlooked. "The aim of these motorcycles is to build a friendly environment for the provision of treatment and care services for people living with HIV, so I urge service providers to use them to reach the vulnerable who need services delivered to them and who cannot afford to reach the centres," said Andengenye.

acts.speaker: Dk Damas Kayera, Kigoma Regional Medical Officer
acts.speech: Supported Andengenye's statement, saying he believes that after health service providers have been handed these motorcycles, they will fight and reduce HIV infections in the region from the current 1.7 percent to zero (0) percent by 2030.

title: USAID staff will be put on leave starting on Friday

acts.speaker: USAID (statement on its website)
acts.speech: The agency said in a statement on its website that thousands of employees will be placed on leave from Friday night. In the announcement, USAID said all "direct-hire personnel" will be placed on leave at the end of this week except those on "mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs". USAID said it would work with the State Department to arrange and pay for return travel for its many personnel posted outside the US within the month. Those employees who are part of the exceptions will be told by 15:00 EDT on Thursday. The statement concludes with the message: "Thank you for your service."

acts.speaker: USAID (email to staffers, obtained by BBC News)
acts.speech: Many USAID staffers received an email notifying them they had been placed on paid administrative leave. The email told employees they must remain "available" by telephone and email during business hours but are not allowed to enter USAID buildings.

acts.speaker: Congressional Research Service (report/data)
acts.speech: According to the Congressional Research Service, the agency, which provides humanitarian aid to more than 100 countries, employs 10,000 people worldwide and two-thirds of those people work overseas; USAID managed more than $40b (£32.25b) in fiscal year 2023.

acts.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire Tesla CEO appointed to run a new agency to identify US government spending cuts
acts.speech: Has said USAID should be shut down as it is "beyond repair".

acts.speaker: Andy Kim, New Jersey Senator
acts.speech: "[USAID is] a foreign policy tool with bipartisan origins that is critical in this dangerous global environment," Kim wrote on social media. "Gutting it means gutting our ability to compete and keep America safe."

title: Kenyan khat farmers halt exports to Somalia, demand higher prices - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: Kenyan khat farmers
acts.speech: Frustrated with what they describe as exploitative pricing, demand that exporters pay an additional 300 Kenyan shillings (Ksh) per kilogram and enforce a minimum payment of Ksh 200,000 per bag for the premium "Grid" variety of khat ; argue they receive Ksh 300 - an imbalance they say enriches intermediaries and transporters at their expense ; have vowed to continue their protest, even as negotiations unfold.

acts.speaker: Kenyan khat farmers
acts.speech: Point to an illegal levy of USD 4.5 per kilogram allegedly imposed by a "cartel" at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA); they claim this hidden cost is undermining farm-gate prices while inflating Mogadishu's retail rates.

acts.speaker: Somali traders
acts.speech: Accuse the government of maintaining policies that favour select importers while leaving local sellers to grapple with soaring costs.

acts.speaker: Somali female traders
acts.speech: In mid-January staged protests in Mogadishu against high taxation on Kenyan khat, claiming it was eroding their profits.

acts.speaker: Kenya's Agriculture and Food Authority (AFA)
acts.speech: Has acknowledged the farmers' grievances; the agency's Khat Pricing Committee has met with industry stakeholders and is weighing a revised pricing framework.

acts.speaker: James Mithika, Chairman of the Khat Pricing Committee
acts.speech: Confirmed that discussions include the introduction of a guaranteed minimum price of Ksh 700 per kilogram in the dry season and Ksh 500 per kilogram in the rainy season.

title: IOM Launches Islamic Philanthropy Fund to Aid Displaced Communities

acts.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (press release)
acts.speech: Announced that it today launched its Islamic Philanthropy Fund, a new initiative that aims to harness the power of Islamic charitable giving to support some of the world's most vulnerable people; said the Fund is an important milestone for IOM as global crises worsen and human displacement increases, and that in its inaugural year the Fund is prioritizing the Sudan Emergency Response by delivering cash to displaced families, those stranded at borders, and communities in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.

acts.speaker: Amy Pope, IOM Director General
acts.speech: “With today’s complex crises displacing record numbers of people and causing immeasurable suffering, it’s critical to harness the spirit of Islamic charity to help alleviate suffering, empower communities to rebuild and thrive, and protect the dignity of people in need” ; “We are both honored and excited to announce IOM’s Islamic Philanthropy Fund as a means to help us engage Muslims around the world and channel their contributions through a trusted and efficient platform, maximising their positive impact.”

title: Fears grow that US may pull funding for South African medical research | News24

acts.speaker: Professor Ntobeko Ntusi, CEO of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
acts.speech: Told GroundUp that "we were alerted on Thursday last week that the NIH is considering imminently terminating all grants to South Africa… many of us believe these are likely to be announced in the coming days" ; previously told Spotlight that US grants make up 28% of the SAMRC's funding.

acts.speaker: University of Cape Town (UCT) (email to the health faculty)
acts.speech: Warned on Sunday that while they still didn't have confirmation, "developments over the last two days indicate that the termination of US federal funding to South Africa appears to be imminent"; the email states that UCT has established a task team to "plan mitigation measures" if US-funded research projects are terminated.

acts.speaker: Science Magazine
acts.speech: Reported on Friday that the acting director of the NIH had sent an email to staff earlier that week asking them to compile a list of NIH grants for projects in South Africa; the email reportedly contained "similar wording" to a previous request for information about NIH grants related to transgender health and vaccine hesitancy.

acts.speaker: Associate professor Sean Wasserman, infectious diseases, University of Cape Town
acts.speech: Told GroundUp that at present the primary concern is that the grant could be cancelled at any moment; explained that the current treatment duration "keeps people in clinics and in contact with the healthcare system for a long time, which is a real cost to people. [For instance] It makes it difficult to maintain a job… And that also leads to treatment fatigue".

acts.speaker: Associate professor Sean Wasserman, infectious diseases, University of Cape Town
acts.speech: Said that although all the participants would still be able to get treatment in the ordinary health system in South Africa, they wouldn't necessarily be managed correctly: "They're on experimental drug regimens" ; "Transitioning them back to routine care is not ideal because the [experimental regimens] can have effects for weeks or months, which need to be monitored, which routine care isn't set up to do."

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of 7 February)
acts.speech: States that the US would not provide "aid or assistance" to South Africa due to its alleged persecution of Afrikaans people and "racially disfavoured landowners".

acts.speaker: US Secretary of State
acts.speech: Over 80% of all USAID agreements have been terminated globally, according to the US Secretary of State.

title: AfDB powers agriculture sector with K75bn grant - Nation Online

acts.speaker: McMillan Anyanwu, African Development Bank (AfDB) country manager for Malawi
acts.speech: Said the $23 million (about K40 billion) agriculture-based budgetary support programme is designed to unlock the agriculture sector's potential as a catalyst for economic transformation: "The direct budget support will target key reforms to protect the well-being of people in rural and vulnerable communities. We believe that these reforms will help Malawi realise its dream of becoming a net-exporter of value-added products."

acts.speaker: McMillan Anyanwu, African Development Bank (AfDB) country manager for Malawi
acts.speech: Said the Africa Disaster Risk Financing (Adrifi) programme is designed to strengthen the country's resilience by improving disaster planning and crisis response capabilities, particularly for rural farming communities that are most at risk.

acts.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
acts.speech: Commended AfDB for providing the support, saying it complements the Malawi 2063 long-term development plan which earmarked agriculture productivity and commercialisation as key pillars for promoting economic transformation: "This budgetary support will help create an enabling economic and regulatory environment for agricultural transformation by promoting agricultural productivity, commercialisation and market access to help our farmers increase their output and connect to better markets."

title: Vor 50 Jahren

acts.speaker: Government of Owambo
acts.speech: Is surprised that the four churches made the statement on the reasons for the emigration of Ovambos available to the press; it was under the impression that the memorandum continued to serve as a basis for discussion and would not be published unilaterally, and for this reason has so far refrained from issuing a statement of its own.

acts.speaker: Government of Owambo
acts.speech: Has issued no statement on yesterday's talks. (non-response)

acts.speaker: Church leaders of ELOK, the Roman Catholic Church, the Anglican Church and the Baptist congregation (joint memorandum)
acts.speech: Presented the Commissioner-General with a memorandum on the reasons why the Ovambos are leaving their country; they thank the Commissioner-General for having invited them “in these difficult times” to talks with the leaders of the government on the question of why people are leaving the country, and ask him to see to it that the talks of 27 June and 6 August “may bring not mistrust, hatred, persecution and misunderstanding, but good fruits of peace.”

acts.speaker: African Party for the Independence of Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde (PAIGC)
acts.speech: Wishes for a link between Bissau and the Cape Verde Islands.

acts.speaker: Richard Nixon, President of the United States
acts.speech: Has declared anew that he will not resign, although strong pressure is now being exerted on him to avoid a conviction by the Senate.

acts.speaker: Senator Barry Goldwater
acts.speech: Even Senator Goldwater, who is highly regarded by Nixon, has now come out in favour of Nixon's resignation; as a member of the Senate's political committee, which sent a delegation to the White House to tell the President that he was in danger of being convicted if he did not resign beforehand.

acts.speaker: South African Council of Churches (SACC) resolution
acts.speech: In the resolution the member churches are called upon to urge all their members to consider “whether the call of Christ to take up the cross and follow him, and in doing so to identify with the oppressed, does not in our situation mean the refusal (of military service) on grounds of conscience”.

acts.speaker: Major-General J. A., Chaplain-General of the South African armed forces (statement)
acts.speech: Said in a statement that the English-speaking clergy had taken note with dismay of the Council of Churches' resolution encouraging South Africans to refuse military service; the chaplains, familiar with the aims and methods of the communist-inspired terrorists “who want to penetrate our country through murder and violence”, call on all church members, and especially young men, to make their personal contribution to the defence of the country; the chaplains remained loyal to South Africa and expressed their thanks to the army for the opportunity to realize their calling as proclaimers of the Gospel.

title: Forécaria : plusieurs boutiques réduites en cendres à Maférinya

acts.speaker: Concordant witness accounts (local residents)
acts.speech: According to concordant testimonies, several shops as well as their contents were entirely destroyed by the flames.

acts.speaker: A local authority (anonymous)
acts.speech: According to a local official, a short circuit is said to be the cause of the disaster.

acts.speaker: Monsieur Baldé, one of the victims
acts.speech: "We were taken by surprise by a fire, and the flames spread quickly, consuming our goods and the buildings."

title: Mali’s Choguel Maiga charged with embezzlement, remanded in custody

acts.speaker: Choguel Maiga, former Prime Minister of Mali
acts.speech: publicly denounced the military for a lack of clarity over when it would hand over power to a civilian government, before being sacked in November 2024.

acts.speaker: Cheick Oumar Konare, Choguel Maiga’s lawyer
acts.speech: told the AFP news agency that no date has yet been set for the former leader’s trial ; “We believe in justice, we are calm while awaiting the trial,” explaining that Maiga would remain in prison for the trial.

acts.speaker: Public prosecutor of Mali (statement)
acts.speech: said the charges against Maiga involve “money laundering equal to many billions of CFA francs”, or several million US dollars.

acts.speaker: AFP news agency
acts.speech: reported that the former prime minister was arrested one week ago, days after Mali’s military leaders carried out dozens of arrests to quash an alleged plot within the army’s ranks to topple the government; reported, citing a judicial source, that nine of Maiga’s colleagues from his time as prime minister also appeared before the court on Tuesday, with two being charged, some acquitted and others still awaiting their hearing.

acts.speaker: Moussa Mara, former Prime Minister of Mali (social media post)
acts.speech: was imprisoned after tweeting his support for jailed critics of the military.

acts.speaker: Human Rights Watch
acts.speech: according to it, up to 350,000 people are currently displaced by the fighting in Mali.

acts.speaker: Choguel Maiga, former Prime Minister of Mali
acts.speech: previously said he believed the military would safeguard the country’s democracy: “We must refound the Malian state, so that no political power can ever again create the conditions for a return to an unconstitutional order!” he told Al Jazeera in an interview in 2023.

acts.speaker: Choguel Maiga, former Prime Minister of Mali
acts.speech: since his dismissal has become one of the military’s fiercest critics, accusing it of weaponising the courts to silence dissent.

acts.speaker: Alioune Tine, former United Nations rapporteur on Mali to the Security Council
acts.speech: said “If the most prominent opposition leaders are arrested and imprisoned, including Choguel, who once gave the junta credibility, then I believe today the junta credibility is greatly weakened.”

title: Venezuela acusa EUA de mandar navios para usurpar recursos - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Nicolas Maduro, Venezuelan President
acts.speech: Accuses the United States of America of sending warships to the waters off Venezuela and says the United States wants to appropriate the country's natural resources ; announced, at an event broadcast by the state channel Venezuelan Television, that the United States had sent eight warships and 1,200 missiles to the country's coast ; rejected Washington's argument that this is an operation to combat drug trafficking, describing it as a story ; accused the US of wanting to appropriate oil, gas and gold, after reiterating that his country holds the fourth largest gas reserves in the world and one of the largest global reserves of gold.

acts.speaker: Washington (US government)
acts.speech: Argues that it is an operation to combat drug trafficking.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Announced on social media that the US Armed Forces had carried out a strike against a group of narcoterrorists from Tren de Aragua, a terrorist organization involved in drug trafficking, human trafficking, acts of violence, homicide and terror in the US, which according to Trump were in international waters transporting illegal narcotics on their way to the United States.

title: Validation des appuis aux communes pour les programmes sociaux

acts.speaker: Prefect of Oueme/Plateau
acts.speech: Stressed the agricultural potential of the Oueme valley and underlined how important it is to secure land in order to foster sustainable and risk-free investment; urged the competent authorities, especially the heads of land affairs services, to support the vision of MCA-Benin's “Access to Land” project.

acts.speaker: Moukaram Oceni, Mayor of Porto-Novo
acts.speech: Insisted that the workshop will make it possible to identify vulnerable groups and establish a new relationship with local elected officials; for him this vision is crucial for the fight against extreme poverty; praised the American government, which has enabled Benin to take new measures to raise the population's standard of living somewhat through the financing of MCA-Benin's activities.

acts.speaker: Lee Roussel, Resident Representative of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
acts.speech: Took the opportunity to recall the objectives of the United States through the MCA initiative; underlined that land tenure is one of the problems hindering the emancipation of countries, especially developing ones.

acts.speaker: Simon Pierre Adovelande, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
acts.speech: Said this workshop is proof of the implementation of the commitments set out in Benin's memoranda of understanding on land tenure, under which communes have been provided with office furniture and rolling stock enabling them to support the Programme in its policy of securing land through Rural Land Plans (PFR).

acts.speaker: Alassane Seidou, Minister of Decentralisation, Local Governance, Administration and Territorial Planning
acts.speech: Officially opening the workshop, recalled the importance of the document and thanked the United States for their assistance.

acts.speaker: MCA-Benin (general context of the workshop, as set out by MCA-Benin)
acts.speech: Sets out that the government of Benin and the government of the United States, acting through the Millennium Challenge Corporation, concluded an Agreement to provide technical assistance to Benin to improve citizens' access to land, whose general objective is to stimulate investment growth and promote Benin's private sector as fundamental conditions for economic growth and poverty reduction; that specific project objectives include support for a land policy and land legislation reform, formalisation of land ownership rights, support to communes in managing a new land regime, improvement of the land information registration and management system, and information, education and communication activities; and that support to communes addresses two crucial land-policy problems — migrants in rural “host” zones whose land rights are precarious, limited and revocable at any time, and growing numbers of “landless” peasants settling in peri-urban areas who lack assets and professional qualifications, increasing poverty levels in peri-urban communes.

title: Businesses urged to tap into AfCFTA, energy partnerships

acts.speaker: The Journal of African Business (September/October/November 2025 issue)
acts.speech: Outlines key continental initiatives with implications for Eswatini's private sector, from trade reforms to infrastructure and water partnerships, signalling new opportunities and challenges for local enterprises. Notes that regional partnerships are becoming critical as climate variability, ageing infrastructure and urbanisation increase pressure on water resources. Emphasises the growing role of the African Private Sector Hearings (APSH) in shaping trade policy under the AfCFTA framework, and points to rising opportunities in renewable energy and environmental, social and governance (ESG) compliance across Africa.

acts.speaker: Magalies Water (South African water utility)
acts.speech: Revealed that its Scientific Services Division has conducted benchmarking sessions with the Eswatini Water Services Corporation (EWSC) as part of a regional effort to strengthen laboratory services and water quality management standards across the Southern African Development Community (SADC).

acts.speaker: Industry experts
acts.speech: Argue that ESG compliance is becoming a key requirement for accessing international financing and export markets, meaning Eswatini's businesses will need to align with these standards to stay competitive.

title: Chapo diz que Governo não vai ceder à pressão da Mozal - O País - A verdade como notícia

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
acts.speech: Says that the tariffs proposed by Mozal for the consumption of energy from the Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric plant would lead the power generation company to collapse; guaranteed that talks are under way to find fairer tariffs; said that Mozambique will not give up the survival of what he called the "goose that lays the golden eggs." "Mozal is proposing its tariffs and the Government, through the state-owned company HCB, which supplies, sells and exports electricity to Escom - this needs to be made clear - is at this moment discussing the tariffs, because on the basis of the tariffs that Mozal is proposing at the moment, if those tariffs were accepted, HCB could collapse," said the President. "What we are doing at this moment is defending the national interest and the interests of the Mozambican people. We have an added responsibility as a government; we cannot accept tariffs that will lead HCB to subsidise Mozal and cause HCB to collapse. So the talks continue and if we reach a consensus on the tariffs there is no problem," he declared.

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
acts.speech: On the 45th SADC Summit: "The other positive aspect emerging from this summit was the adoption of the budget that will allow the full operationalisation of the Humanitarian Emergency Operations Centre based in Nacala, in the Republic of Mozambique, specifically in Nampula province, at a time when member states face countless financial difficulties. It is a budget that we think will be important, around 3.5 million dollars, which will help us maintain the work at the level of Nacala and also of the region (...)," he shared.

title: M’membe proposes reforms in mining, tax policy changes in face of aid freeze

acts.speaker: Fred M'membe, Socialist Party President (Zambia)
acts.speech: Called for urgent reforms in the country's mining sector to mitigate the economic impact of aid cuts by the United States and Switzerland; urged President Hakainde Hichilema's administration to reconsider mining tax waivers and concessions that he believes are depriving the nation of crucial revenue; and warned of the significant fiscal challenges the country was expected to face.

title: SADC to host virtual public lecture on regional integration

acts.speaker: SADC secretariat (statement on its X handle)
acts.speech: Said AfDB director for regional integration coordination Dr Joy Kategekwa will deliver the public lecture, which will start at 1400 hours: “The public lecture offers a unique platform for engaging and promises to be an insightful forum for dialogue and knowledge exchange among leading think-tanks, policymakers, practitioners, non-state actors, development partners and the public, including the youth and influential voices driving Africa’s integration agenda.” ; said the lecture also offers an opportunity for networking with other stakeholders who are committed to realising the continent’s development aspirations.

acts.speaker: SADC secretariat (statement on its X handle)
acts.speech: Said Dr Kategekwa is a respected international trade and investment lawyer who has dedicated her career to structuring Africa’s trade policy, negotiations and industry landscape for sustainable development, and to ensure that Africa’s integration into global trade is beneficial and wealth creating ; said Dr Kategekwa is passionate about building the next generation of Africa’s trade law/policy practitioners and has spent over 15 years offering guest lectures on international trade, investment, regional integration and development at leading global centres of learning.

title: Ministry of Health launches major recruitment to fill 408 vacancies

acts.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
acts.speech: Emphasised the necessity of this move, positioning the restoration of the health sector as an imperative for achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and securing the nation's human capital for future prosperity.

acts.speaker: Ministry of Health 2025/26 Second Quarter (July to September) Performance Report
acts.speech: Details the specific cadres being prioritised for recruitment and deployment, including 104 nursing roles slated for immediate filling, the urgent recruitment of 115 Pharmacists and 37 Pharmacy Technicians to be completed by October 2025, and funding for 123 support staff positions.

acts.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
acts.speech: "The current recruitment and deployment strategy is not an isolated measure; rather, it is anchored in the newly launched Human Resources for Health (HRH) Strategy 2025-2030. This long-term, comprehensive policy is designed to address the root causes of the health workforce crisis" ; "Continuous professional development and aligning local training institutions with national health needs are key to ensuring a sustainable supply of qualified health professionals for the future."

acts.speaker: Mduduzi Matsebula, Minister of Health of Eswatini
acts.speech: Confirmed that contractual terms strictly mandate suppliers to either replace or reimburse the cost of any recalled or substandard pharmaceuticals and medical supplies, and that should a supplier fail to honour this within 60 days, the Ministry can legally withhold equivalent funds from other outstanding payments to that supplier.

title: UAE ambassador and SoDMA chairman discuss aid and resilience projects in Somalia

acts.speaker: Ahmed J. Al-Rumeysi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates, and Mohamud Ma'allin Abdulle, Chairman of the Disaster Management Authority (SoDMA)
acts.speech: The two leaders agreed that emergency aid should be delivered to the affected areas before the beginning of Ramadan, and also agreed that important dams should be repaired to reduce the risk of floods caused by the spring rains, which are expected to start in April.

acts.speaker: Ahmed J. Al-Rumeysi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates
acts.speech: Updated the chairman on the progress of the UAE-funded wells project, which aims to provide clean water to the communities in need; said that the first phase of the project, which involved drilling 100 wells, has been completed and the second phase, which will drill another 100 wells, is underway.

acts.speaker: Mohamud Ma'allin Abdulle, Chairman of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
acts.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the UAE government for its unwavering support with the Somali government and the Somali people; said that the UAE is a true friend and partner of Somalia, and that the cooperation between the two countries will enhance the resilience and development of Somalia.

acts.speaker: Joint statement by the UAE ambassador and the SoDMA chairman
acts.speech: The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the bilateral relations and cooperation between the UAE and Somalia, especially in the areas of humanitarian assistance, disaster management, and resilience projects.

title: Namcor takes charge of oil storage facility

acts.speaker: Jenny Comalie, Namcor board chairperson
acts.speech: Announcing the official handover of the facility, noted that while construction of the facility, situated in Walvis Bay, commenced in January 2015, the corporation had foresight to recruit and train competent Namibian staff, who, in the process, also assisted the government with the completion and commissioning of the facility.

acts.speaker: Jenny Comalie, Namcor board chairperson
acts.speech: Further indicated the facility will not only be used for Namcor's trading purposes but also to host other international oil marketing companies such as Vitol and Gunvor, Vivo and Total to ensure it is utilised optimally and that Namibia becomes a strategic gateway through which neighbouring African states are supplied.

acts.speaker: Jenny Comalie, Namcor board chairperson
acts.speech: Added that the first shipment of commissioning stock arrived on 1 December 2020, valued at N$407.3 million, which heralded the testing and commissioning of the facility ; “Namcor has already begun to successfully sell the commissioning stock to its retail, commercial, bunkering and export customers, as well as other local marketing companies with success.”

acts.speaker: Immanuel Mulunga, Namcor managing director
acts.speech: Explained commissioning the facility meant bringing in fuel equivalent to the capacity of the terminal to test the operation of the entire system ; assured the nation that the commissioning has so far been a resounding success and that the fuel is safe and clean for use.

acts.speaker: Immanuel Mulunga, Namcor managing director
acts.speech: Stated that even though Namcor owns and operates the massive facility, this does not give them any right to influence fuel and pump prices in Namibia.

acts.speaker: Immanuel Mulunga, Namcor managing director
acts.speech: Said that, according to Namcor's mandate, the corporation looks forward to rolling out more service stations in the coming months in a bid to take services closer to people across the country; explained the target is about 33 service stations to be completed by 2024, and that by end of June this year (2021), eight Namcor service stations, currently under construction, are expected to be operational.

title: Negotiators seek to finalize Gaza ceasefire deal after ‘breakthrough’ in Doha

acts.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
acts.speech: Said a ceasefire and hostage release deal he has championed was on “the brink” of coming to fruition ; “The deal ... would free the hostages, halt the fighting, provide security to Israel and allow us to significantly surge humanitarian assistance to the Palestinians who suffered terribly in this war that Hamas started,” he said in a speech on Monday to highlight his foreign policy achievements.

acts.speaker: An official briefed on the negotiations (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said mediators gave Israel and Hamas a final draft of a deal on Monday, after a midnight “breakthrough” in talks attended by envoys of both the outgoing US president and President-elect Donald Trump; said the text for a ceasefire and release of hostages was presented by Qatar to both sides at talks in Doha, which included the chiefs of Israel’s Mossad and Shin Bet spy agencies and Qatar’s prime minister.

acts.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
acts.speech: Said the sides were “closer than we’ve ever been” to a deal, and the ball was in Hamas’ court.

acts.speaker: Hamas
acts.speech: Said it was keen on reaching a deal ; has always insisted a deal must lead to a permanent end to the war and Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.

acts.speaker: Hamas delegation in Doha (statement)
acts.speech: Issued a statement on Monday after a meeting with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani saying talks were progressing well.

acts.speaker: An Israeli official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said negotiations were in advanced stages for the release of up to 33 hostages as part of the deal.

acts.speaker: Israeli authorities
acts.speech: Ninety-eight hostages remain in Gaza, according to Israeli authorities.

acts.speaker: Israel (government position)
acts.speech: Has said it will not end the war until Hamas is dismantled.

acts.speaker: Israeli tallies
acts.speech: Hamas fighters stormed across Israel’s borders in October 2023, killing 1,200 people and taking more than 250 hostages, according to Israeli tallies.

acts.speaker: Palestinian health officials
acts.speech: More than 46,000 people have been killed in Gaza, according to Palestinian health officials.

title: US cuts visa validity for most Nigerian applicants - Daily News

acts.speaker: US Department of State
acts.speech: Says that from 8 July nearly all non-immigrant and non-diplomatic visas issued to Nigerian citizens will now be single-entry and valid for only three months; says this is part of a global reciprocity realignment ; says visa policies remain “subject to ongoing review” and may change depending on evolving diplomatic, security, and immigration benchmarks.

acts.speaker: US government (statement)
acts.speech: Said it was working closely with Nigerian authorities to ensure the country meets key international standards, including issuing secure travel documents, managing visa overstays, and sharing security or criminal data for public safety purposes ; ordered that the social media accounts of all foreigners applying for visas, including from Nigeria, would be vetted for “any indications of hostility toward the citizens, culture, government, institutions, or founding principles of the United States”.

acts.speaker: Nigerian government
acts.speech: Has not yet commented.

acts.speaker: 2024 Open Doors report on international education exchanges, published by the US Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs
acts.speech: According to the report, Nigeria was the seventh largest source of international students to the US, and the highest in Africa, showing a 13.5% increase from 2023.

acts.speaker: Bashir Ahmad, aide to former Nigerian President Muhammadu Buhari
acts.speech: Said he believed the US was not reciprocating but showing its displeasure with Nigeria, posting on X that President Bola Tinubu's recent visit to Brazil for the Brics gathering was behind the move ; “This is not solely about reciprocity. Rather, it appears to reflect growing US discomfort with Nigeria's increasing global realignment, particularly the warm reception we are receiving from the Brics.”

title: Matarajio ya Watanzania bajeti ya afya ikisomwa leo

acts.speaker: 2007 Health Policy Statement (Tamko la Sera ya Afya ya Mwaka 2007)
acts.speech: Requires that there be sufficient skilled staff in various professions at all levels of service delivery in the country.

acts.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
acts.speech: Said that knowing the fate of health facilities, health workers and the assurance of medicines is the biggest issue, especially at this time when USAID funding has gone: "We are all eagerly waiting to hear the plans. We think the budget will fill the budget deficit after America reduced aid; many expect to see plans that will let them see the future of their health" ; said Tanzanians want to see strategies for controlling epidemic diseases, non-communicable diseases and accidents.

acts.speaker: Dr Ali Mzige, public health expert
acts.speech: Said he is not sure whether the Ministry of Health's budget has reached 15 percent of Government spending, as required since the Abuja agreement that a country should spend at least 15 percent of its revenue on health; secondly said development must always target the population segment that is most affected: "For example small children under five years and pregnant women; there is still a problem in areas that grow food in abundance, but still have stunted children. If you take areas like Katavi, Njombe, Iringa, much of the food grown is sold but stunting is high; it should have been directed to the community" ; said it is important to tell mothers and fathers about children's health and the importance of eating leafy vegetables and fruits, and to remind the community to clean their mouths twice a day and avoid smoking, with that education starting in schools.

acts.speaker: Another health-sector stakeholder who did not want his name mentioned / one of the workers in public hospitals (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said health insurance had not been well planned from the time it started because it focused more on treatment and not on prevention: "If there is a disease that has high costs it is kidney dialysis, diabetes and blood pressure; beneficiaries are not educated on what to do, they come when they have already fallen ill" ; "The budget has never allocated for the presence of these specialists in district areas; there is no balance between Tamisemi and the Ministry of Health; a patient has to travel 90 kilometres to the region and if he is overwhelmed he dies on the way before reaching the hospital." ; "Ambulances carry many patients, they use fuel and they are bought expensively; if you look at a driver's salary and the high cost of fuel, the money exceeds what it would take to employ a specialist doctor in the district."

acts.speaker: Hafidh Omary, resident of Tegeta, Dar es Salaam
acts.speech: Said the Government has made purchases of equipment that are many, countless and without good direction: "An MRI sells for two billion; you could employ 199 doctors for a year and pay them well. Equipment and a person are two different things; you cannot provide a car without a driver."

acts.speaker: Hawa Mwinjuma, trader at the Feri fish market in Dar es Salaam
acts.speech: Said the problem of accidents in the country is big so the budget must look at ways to reduce them, while criticising the country for growing more tobacco, which has harmful effects: "In Tanzania we lead in growing tobacco; I think while other ministries count it as bringing in income, let us look at how patients are increasing. Also, we mothers should be provided with essential services there in our village in Mtwara; there the situation is not good, we do not even have a specialist doctor for women's diseases, you have to travel far to find one."

title: Understanding the cost of affordable financial inclusion

acts.speaker: World Bank
acts.speech: Financial inclusion as defined by the World Bank refers to the share of individuals and firms that use financial services such as transactions, payments, savings, credit and insurance.

acts.speaker: The African Banking Survey, 2016, a report by PwC
acts.speech: Pointed to the fact that bank CEOs’ priority is to secure and increase market share in the domestic regions.

acts.speaker: Likhit Wagle, a former PwC partner
acts.speech: Quipped that ‘the real key problem in financial inclusion today is not so much in opening accounts-that’s happening fairly successfully-but we get stuck with the fact that these are very low balance accounts that are not very profitable’.

title: Afrique centrale : HRW dénonce une répression généralisée

acts.speaker: Human Rights Watch (World Report 2025)
acts.speech: Paints an alarming picture of the human rights situation in Central Africa, highlighting a significant deterioration of fundamental freedoms in the region over the course of 2024 after examining human rights practices in more than 100 countries in its 546-page report; says wartime abuses are commonplace and testify to a lack of accountability in the region; reports that in Rwanda and the Central African Republic the authorities orchestrated “politically motivated prosecutions” to silence dissenting voices; that in Chad and Rwanda the general elections took place in a climate that was “neither free nor fair”; that in Burundi, ahead of the 2025 elections, “the authorities restricted the political space of the opposition”; that clashes in North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of Congo caused the massive displacement of “2.5 million people”; that in Chad “more than 700,000 people have fled to the country to escape the armed conflict in Sudan”, with belligerents systematically hindering the delivery of humanitarian aid; that a historic trial in Rwanda led to the conviction of prison officials for acts of torture at Rubavu prison; and that in Chad the security forces “killed at least 11 people in a post-election shooting in May”.

acts.speaker: Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at Human Rights Watch
acts.speech: “Governments across Central Africa have repressed basic rights and freedoms, notably during elections and referendums, which raises concerns about governments' efforts to monopolise power.”

acts.speaker: Tirana Hassan, executive director of Human Rights Watch (introductory essay)
acts.speech: Stresses that the regional situation forms part of a worrying global context, describing a world in which “governments have repressed, arrested and wrongfully imprisoned political opponents, activists and journalists”, while armed groups and government forces have multiplied abuses against civilian populations.

acts.speaker: Human Rights Watch (call to governments)
acts.speech: Calls on the governments of Central Africa to honour their international commitments and to take concrete measures to protect fundamental freedoms, particularly in election periods; also insists on the need to strengthen the protection of civilians in conflict zones and to prosecute those responsible for abuses, regardless of their position in the hierarchy.

title: Finance Minister Ngafuan Holds Meeting with MCC Vice President on Liberia Compact Development - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
acts.speech: Reechoed President Joseph Nyumah Boakai’s appreciation to the CEO and the Senior Management of the MCC and the American Government for the country’s selection. He recalled the transformative impact the first MCC grant has had on Liberia through the restoration of the Mont Coffee Hydro dam, the setting up of the Liberia Electricity Regulatory Commission, and support to the LWSC for restoring water pipes to Monrovia, among others.

acts.speaker: Kyeh Kim, MCC Vice President for Compact Operations
acts.speech: Expressed her enthusiasm for continuing the partnership, saying, “We’re excited to continue working with Liberia.” ; was happy to reveal that there was strong enthusiasm for Liberia among MCC Board members at their last board meeting, where the country was selected for the second compact ; informed that Mr. Small will visit Liberia to be followed by Vice President Kim to engage with the Minister of Finance and other senior government officials and stakeholders on the Liberia Compact.

title: Baking industry optimistic as local investments drive growth

acts.speaker: Elvis Ncube, National Bakers Association of Zimbabwe president
acts.speech: Said recent commissioning of plants and ongoing investment in local production signal a positive outlook for the sector: “What we are witnessing in the baking sector is very encouraging. Local bakers and producers are commissioning new plants, and we anticipate more facilities coming online in the near future. This clearly shows that the industry is on a growth trajectory.” ; “These are Zimbabweans, living and investing here, and they deserve support and appropriate incentives to continue driving industrial growth. Too often, discussions about investors focus on international players, yet we have local entrepreneurs who are building this country’s future.”

acts.speaker: Elvis Ncube, National Bakers Association of Zimbabwe president
acts.speech: Said one of the key priorities for the industry remains ensuring bread remains affordable for the average Zimbabwean, and urged the government to consider reinstating zero-rated tax status on bread to achieve more growth: “It is our plea that bread be made tax-exempt again. This will help us stabilize prices and ensure the product stays within reach of all Zimbabweans, provided other input costs remain stable. The outlook is generally good. What we need now is to protect and sustain the gains being made so that every Zimbabwean continues to benefit.”

title: 1 mln people experiencing food insecurity in Kenya: authorities - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA), Kenya
acts.speech: Said Monday that at least a million people in Kenya are struggling with food insecurity and in need of humanitarian assistance ; noted in a report released in Nairobi that the affected people are in 23 out of the country's 47 counties, which are classified as arid and semi-arid ; revealed that households sold their harvests to cover other costs, often at the expense of maintaining healthy eating and chronic challenges associated with stunting.

acts.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) report
acts.speech: Noted in July that the number of food-insecure people in the Horn of Africa stood at 66.7 million, among them 39.1 million from six of the eight IGAD member states, namely Djibouti, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

title: Public Hearing On Disability Rights, Anti-Trafficking, Step To Entrenching Social Justice In Taraba – Ade

acts.speaker: Adinya Arise Foundation (AAF)
acts.speech: Said the public hearing by the State Assembly marks a significant step towards ensuring the entrenchment of social justice and human rights in the state.

acts.speaker: Mabel Adinya Ade, Executive Director, Adinya Arise Foundation (AAF)
acts.speech: Describing the public hearing on the two Bills as "ground breaking", stated that the development promises to transform the lives of countless residents in Taraba state, and expressed her profound gratitude to State Governor Agbu Kefas and the State House of Assembly for their leadership and responsiveness to the issues at stake. "The passage of these bills represents not only a historic moment for Taraba but a commitment to restoring dignity, rights, and justice to those most affected by discrimination and trafficking." ; "Through our advocacy efforts, we strive to ensure that every citizen of Taraba is protected, empowered, and provided opportunities for a life free from exploitation and marginalization."

acts.speaker: Mabel Adinya Ade, Executive Director, Adinya Arise Foundation (AAF)
acts.speech: Observed that although the USAID project has officially come to a close, AAF has continued to push for the passage of the bills, underlining the unwavering commitment of AAF to the advocacy and protection of human rights; also expressed the hope that as the bills are on the verge of being passed, the leadership in Taraba state would continue to set the precedence for other states, reinforcing a commitment to human rights, equality, and justice for all.

acts.speaker: Speaker, Taraba State House of Assembly
acts.speech: Had recently announced the commitment of the state government to enact the Anti-Trafficking Bill at the just concluded Conference in Abuja on September 25, 2024, and reaffirmed the Assembly's support alongside that of the state governor; he explained that the collaborative resolve of the legislative and executive arms of government signals a shift in the government's desire to counter the activities of human trafficking and ensure the dignity, rights, and resources for persons with disabilities.

title: Exit strategy 5

acts.speaker: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”, publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert
acts.speech: Cited as the source for the definition that a program “exit” refers to the withdrawal of all externally provided program resources from an entire program area, and that a program Exit Strategy is a plan describing how the program intends to withdraw its resources while ensuring that achievement of the program goals (relief or development) is not jeopardized and that progress towards these goals will continue; it sets out three basic approaches to Exit Strategies — phasing down (a gradual reduction of program activities, utilizing local organizations to sustain program benefits while the original sponsor deploys fewer resources), phasing out (a sponsor's withdrawal of involvement in a program without turning it over to another institution), and phasing over (a sponsor transfers program activities to local institutions or communities, with emphasis on institutional capacity building).

acts.speaker: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”, publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative (an initiative by CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
acts.speech: Cited as the source for the criteria used to determine when to exit programs, grouped into three general categories — time limit, achievement of program impacts, and achievement of benchmarks — and for the recommendations that establishing an exit timeline linked to the program funding cycle and clearly communicated to the community is essential, that the exit plan remain flexible, that exit plans be implemented in a gradual, phased manner, that continued contact with communities after phase over or phase out helps support sustainability of outcomes, that ongoing and timely monitoring of benchmarks is critical and should be integrated into the overall program's monitoring and evaluation plan, and that an evaluation should be conducted after a period of time has elapsed following the program exit.

title: Taxes américaines : la BAD craint une crise économique en Afrique

acts.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
acts.speech: Warned, in an interview with Christiane Amanpour on CNN, of the serious economic consequences of the new US trade policy for Africa, stressing that "47 of the 54 African countries would be directly affected," leading to a "potential decline in export revenues and foreign exchange reserves" ; "when these currencies weaken, two things will happen: first, most of these countries, being import-dependent, will face high inflation; second, the cost of servicing debt denominated in local currency but contracted in foreign currency will increase."

acts.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
acts.speech: Insisted on the importance of avoiding a trade confrontation with Washington: "Africa cannot afford a trade war with the United States," recalling that the continent represents only "1.2% of American world trade, about 34 billion dollars, with a surplus of 7.2 billion."

acts.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
acts.speech: Proposed a three-pronged strategic response: "flexible and constructive trade negotiations with the United States; a diversification of export markets; and the acceleration of the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)."

acts.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
acts.speech: Rejected the idea of an exclusive realignment of Africa towards China, declaring that "the United States is a key ally of Africa, just like China. Africa builds bridges, it does not isolate itself" ; recalled the continent's desire to build "balanced, transparent and mutually beneficial partnerships" with all its partners, including the European Union and the Gulf states.

acts.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
acts.speech: Denounced the paradigm of aid dependency, affirming that "the era of aid as we have known it is over," and argued for "bold investments in domestic resource mobilisation, infrastructure and value-added industrialisation."

acts.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group
acts.speech: Stressed that the AfDB had already invested more than 55 billion dollars in infrastructure and that its "High 5" flagship initiatives had reached more than 565 million people; highlighted "Mission 300," a joint initiative with the World Bank to connect 300 million people to electricity by 2030: "Without electricity, what can one do? It is impossible to industrialise, to create added value, to be competitive in the dark."

title: Adopt Regional Govt To Accelerate Devt, Ex-Rep, Faparusi Tells Tinubu

acts.speaker: Bamidele Faparusi, chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and former member of the House of Representatives (statement by his Media Office)
acts.speech: Has opposed the proposal for the creation of more states, describing it as a ruinous action that will create chaos and economic woe ; vehemently opposed the creation of more States, saying such arrangement would cannibalize the governance structure further ; stated that adopting such strategy under an economic situation, whereby only a few states could operate frictionlessly without federal allocation would further create more economic crises like poverty, unemployment, and inability of states to provide expected social services and infrastructures ; “The National Assembly should jettison the idea of creating more states, because it will simply weaken the existing states further, polarize the country the more and increase the cost of governance” ; averred that with more states in existence, the government will be burdened financially through election of more governors, National Assembly members and appointments of more citizens that will increase the cost of governance ; “Creating more states at a time people are calling for reduction of cost of governance will be implausible With more states, you will have more governors, National Assembly members, State assembly members, Ministers, commissioners, and more Special Advisers” ; “I think it’s completely a bad idea that will create jobs for only politicians and make the citizens poorer.”

acts.speaker: Bamidele Faparusi, chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and former member of the House of Representatives
acts.speech: Backed a structural devolution of powers that will fortify the already existing states, local governments and regional commissions, signed into laws by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to drive regionalism ; was thrilled by the creation of regional development commissions and granting of financial autonomy to the 774 local governments by President Tinubu, branding this as a game changer that will bring gradual and seamless devolution of power to states and possibly the regions ; warned Nigerians against paying lip service to the concerning issue of restructuring of governance in the country, saying the steps being taken by the current APC-led federal government should be fully supported, rather than being sabotaged ; “With the trend of things in Nigeria, what we need now is regional integration, which the Development Commission Bills signed into laws by President Bola Tinubu can easily propel, because most of the states are struggling, without the federal allocation, how many of them can survive?” ; “We should use the template of regional development commission to developing a regional governance structure that will allow for devolution of powers from the central government to the regions” ; “Everyone has been calling for restructuring and this is the time for it” ; “We fashion our own democracy after the United States of America. One state in America, like Texas, is a size of Nigeria, aside the issue of population. So, the idea of state creation is a misplaced priority, instead we should create regional government that will allow for regional integration which will accelerate our development.”

title: Une délégation djiboutienne assiste à la cérémonie de commémoration du 124e anniversaire de la bataille d’Adwa en Éthiopie

acts.speaker: Sahle-Work Zewde, President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
acts.speech: Welcomed the efforts undertaken to further strengthen the unique, long-standing relations between the peoples of Ethiopia and Djibouti, while receiving the delegation from Djibouti made up of Djiboutian diplomats, former Ethio-Djibouti Railway staff and young Ethiopians born in Djibouti; during the meeting, stressed the need to intensify collective efforts in the areas of public diplomacy in order to further maximise the untapped opportunities in the fields of culture, tourism and history.

acts.speaker: Members of the Djiboutian delegation
acts.speech: After a warm welcome, expressed their deep gratitude for the warm reception given to them.

acts.speaker: A former Ethio-Djibouti Railway official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Nicknaming the century-old railway an "umbilical cord" that links the two brotherly peoples, insisted on the need to speed up the creation of the former Ethio-Djibouti Railway staff associations in order to further invigorate the historical ties.

title: WHO calls for research-driven health financing in Nigeria

acts.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
acts.speech: Has called on the Nigerian government to strengthen the use of research and evidence in designing health financing policies that can accelerate progress towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

acts.speaker: Robert Marten, Unit Head at Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research, WHO
acts.speech: Said Nigeria faced peculiar challenges in health financing that required domestic solutions: “We are interested in reframing health financing as an investment and mobilising domestic resources to achieve UHC here in Nigeria” ; “This is not a unique goal as many countries are looking at it, but what is unique is Nigeria’s particular challenges” ; highlighted the urgent need to raise primary healthcare spending from $7 to $30 per person and to increase government health allocations from eight to 15 per cent of national expenditure ; stressed the importance of reducing out-of-pocket health spending by scaling up enrolment in the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) ; stressed that while there is consensus on what needed to be done, the how remained unclear, which is where health policy and systems research is crucial.

acts.speaker: Robert Marten, Unit Head at Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research, WHO
acts.speech: Cited global examples, including India’s rollout of the world’s largest tax-funded health insurance scheme, which now covered 500 million people, and reforms in countries such as Rwanda, Mexico, Ghana and Taiwan that had embedded research into policy cycles ; said Nigeria could adapt lessons from those countries by prioritising local research capacity, fostering partnerships between policymakers and researchers, and institutionalising evidence-based decision-making ; said reforms succeed when they are backed by credible local institutions, measurable quick wins, multisectoral collaboration, and sustained trust between government, academia, and development partners ; “This is a moment in time for Nigeria to step up. Global health financing commitments are shrinking, but Nigeria has world-class expertise and leadership.”

acts.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Announced plans to enrol at least 44 million Nigerians into the National Health Insurance Scheme by 2030 as part of new measures to expand financial protection and reduce out-of-pocket spending on healthcare ; added that the ministry is considering legislation to double BHCPF funding from one to two per cent of consolidated revenue, alongside efforts to enrol 44 million Nigerians into the National Health Insurance scheme by 2030.

acts.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Said President Bola Tinubu has directed policies to strengthen domestic financing and protect vulnerable Nigerians; noted that the President has continued to emphasise that a strong health system is vital for national growth and has therefore directed the implementation of several interconnected policies to achieve universal health coverage: “The government has consistently funded the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) and introduced emergency allocations to cushion the suspension of foreign aid.”

title: EUTM help build capacity of the Mozambican forces while delivering on EU integrated approach

acts.speaker: Charles Fries, Deputy Secretary General of the European External Action Service for Common Security and Defence Policy and Crisis Response
acts.speech: Highlighted during his visit to Mozambique the European Union's commitment to a solid partnership with the country, and commended the role of EUTM-Mozambique in training and building capacity of the national forces to address security challenges and protecting the population in the north of the country.

acts.speaker: Antonio Sanchez-Benedito Gaspar, EU Ambassador to Mozambique (@SBeneditoEU, social media post)
acts.speech: "Reiterated #EU commitment to supporting #Mozambique, at the same time helping each other tackle common challenges. @EUTMMozambique well coordinated with other agencies & Member States on efforts in Cabo Delgado."

acts.speaker: Charles Fries, Deputy Secretary General of the European External Action Service for Common Security and Defence Policy and Crisis Response
acts.speech: In his meeting with the Defence Minister, General Cristovao Chume, on EU-Mozambique cooperation, particularly on defence and security, emphasised the EU's important objectives at the end of the EUTM 2-year mission, i.e. to ensure that Mozambican forces are well trained, equipped and operate autonomously under international standards on humanitarian and human rights laws.

acts.speaker: EUTM brigadier-general Lemos de Pires
acts.speech: Briefed Mr Fries on the priorities of EU support in the context of the Training Mission, namely, helping Mozambican forces' capabilities and equipment provision, protecting the civilian population, fighting terrorism, and coordination.

acts.speaker: Charles Fries, Deputy Secretary General of the European External Action Service for Common Security and Defence Policy and Crisis Response
acts.speech: Left the recommendation to EUTM on the importance of getting all the training equipment sooner for a smooth mission as well as the need for an effective use of those materials.

acts.speaker: EUTM Mozambique (@EUTMMozambique, social media post)
acts.speech: "#EUTMMOZ received a visit from Charle Fries Deputy Secretary General of the European External Action Service for Common Security and Defence Policy and Crisis Response yesterday. Mr. Fries visited the Katembe training Camp and the EUTM HQ."

title: Djibouti condamne fermement l’occupation israélienne

acts.speaker: Republic of Djibouti (official statement)
acts.speech: Condemns in the strongest terms the decision of the Israeli occupation authorities to fully invade the Gaza Strip, considering this measure a grave escalation that adds to a series of crimes and flagrant violations committed against the brotherly Palestinian people, including policies of blockade, starvation, systematic destruction and forced displacement.

acts.speaker: Republic of Djibouti (official statement)
acts.speech: Calls on the international community to assume its legal, moral and humanitarian responsibilities, and to act urgently and decisively to put an end to this escalation, prevent new crimes against the defenceless Palestinian people, guarantee the protection of civilians, and ensure the safe, sustained and unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.

title: Cabinet approves appointment of KwaZulu-Natal MEC in national Cogta dept | News24

acts.speaker: Mondli Gungubele, Minister in the Presidency
acts.speech: made the announcement on Thursday morning that Cabinet has approved the appointment of KwaZulu-Natal Cogta MEC Siphosihle Hlomuka as the national Cogta department's deputy director-general of local government support and interventions management, confirming this when he briefed the media on the outcome of a Cabinet meeting on Wednesday ; said Cabinet also approved a host of other appointments, subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.

acts.speaker: Cabinet (South Africa)
acts.speech: commended the swift arrests made in connection with the murder of Hillary Gardee, the daughter of former EFF secretary-general Godrich Gardee ; also condemned the killing of six people in Khayelitsha, Cape Town.

acts.speaker: Mondli Gungubele, Minister in the Presidency
acts.speech: added that senseless murders were a reminder that more must be done to end gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF); he said Cabinet urged all people in the country to work with the government in the fight against crime and GBVF because a united front was the only way the country could put an end to such heinous crimes: "Together, we can ensure that our communities and streets are safer for all people, including the elderly, women and children."

acts.speaker: Whistleblower (anonymous)
acts.speech: raised allegations of corruption, collusion and interference with supply chain management processes concerning acting HDA CEO Daphney Ngoashen with HDA board chairperson Tshilidzi Ratshitanga and Human Settlements Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi in January.

acts.speaker: Cabinet (South Africa)
acts.speech: expressed condolences to those who lost loved ones in the floods, particularly those in KwaZulu-Natal.

acts.speaker: Mondli Gungubele, Minister in the Presidency
acts.speech: said the declaration of a national state of disaster and socio-economic relief interventions President Cyril Ramaphosa recently announced sought to ensure an effective and coordinated response across all spheres of government through the National Disaster Management Centre; he added that the R1 billion that the government made available was already in use to support relief and recovery efforts, restore basic services and provide humanitarian assistance in the form of food, water, shelter, sanitation and clothing ; "The process to rebuild affected areas has already started as the people of our country unite in their determination to assist those who have lost their homes and possessions."

acts.speaker: Mondli Gungubele, Minister in the Presidency
acts.speech: urged all citizens to take precautionary measures to protect themselves against Covid-19, especially during winter: "The virus is still a constant threat, and vaccination remains the most effective weapon to protect ourselves. The Cabinet is pleased that more people continue to choose vaccination as their first line of defence against Covid-19 after recent statistics showed that we had reached the milestone of over 50 percent of adult vaccinations in five provinces."

acts.speaker: South African Government (@GovernmentZA), social media post
acts.speech: "Join Minister Mondli Gungubele as he briefs media on outcomes of the cabinet meeting held on the 11th of May 2022.... #PostCab" (May 12, 2022).

title: واردات الصين من النفط الكويتي تتراجع بنسبة 7.4% خلال مايو الماضي - إتحاد وكالات أنباء دول منظمة التعاون الإسلامي

acts.speaker: Chinese government data (General Administration of Customs)
acts.speech: Showed that China's imports of Kuwaiti crude oil fell in May by 7.4 percent year-on-year to 318,000 barrels per day, and stated that China's imports of Kuwaiti oil exceeded 300,000 barrels per day for the third consecutive month; added that China's crude oil imports in the first five months of the year rose 5.6 percent over the same period of 2016 to 326,000 barrels per day, and that total Chinese crude imports rose 15.4 percent year-on-year in May to 8.8 million barrels per day, with Russia first (up 9.4 percent to 1.36 million bpd), Angola second (1.32 million bpd, up 79.2 percent), Saudi Arabia third (up 8.6 percent to one million bpd), and Oman and Iraq fourth and fifth.

title: Soudan : 50 morts dans une attaque (groupe prodémocratie)

acts.speaker: Local pro-democracy group in Sudan
acts.speech: said on Saturday that at least 50 people were killed in central Sudan in an attack by the paramilitaries of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), who besieged entire villages in the area ; 50 people were killed and "more than 200 wounded" on Friday.

acts.speaker: AFP
acts.speech: recalls that since April 2023 the country has been the scene of a war between the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), led by General Mohamed Hamdane Daglo, and the army led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhane, the country's de facto ruler, one of the poorest countries in the world.

acts.speaker: Doctors (unnamed)
acts.speech: according to doctors, the war has left tens of thousands dead, with estimates ranging from 20,000 to 150,000, most of the victims going unrecorded.

acts.speaker: Hasaheisa Resistance Committee, pro-democracy group organising mutual aid among residents
acts.speech: told AFP: "The villages of al-Sariha and Azraq (located in Al-Jazira State) are under attack" ; in al-Sariha, 50 people were killed and "more than 200 wounded" on Friday, and it was impossible "to evacuate the wounded (...) because of the shelling and snipers" of the RSF ; no toll could be given for the neighbouring village of Azraq, but the Committee said it was under "total siege, suffering the same violations as al-Sariha."

acts.speaker: Sudanese doctors' union
acts.speech: on Friday called on the United Nations to press for safe humanitarian corridors to the villages "that are facing genocide at the hands of the militia" of the RSF, rescue operations having become impossible.

acts.speaker: Medical sources in several villages
acts.speech: according to medical sources in several villages, almost all emergency care centres have been forced to close.

acts.speaker: United Arab Emirates
acts.speech: denies the allegations that it supports the RSF.

acts.speaker: Minni Arcou Minnawi, governor of Sudan's Darfur region, a former rebel leader now close to the army
acts.speech: accused neighbouring Chad of arming the paramilitaries.

acts.speaker: Abderaman Koulamallah, Chad's Minister of Foreign Affairs and government spokesman
acts.speech: Chad insisted on Thursday that it was not arming the paramilitaries: "Chad has no interest in amplifying the war in Sudan by supplying weapons, we are one of the few countries where this war has significant repercussions."

acts.speaker: Catherine Pattillo, Deputy Director of the Africa Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
acts.speech: told AFP this week that the war in Sudan risked causing serious economic damage to its already struggling neighbours: "Many of these neighbouring countries are already fragile and have their own challenges to meet. Now they face an influx of refugees, security issues, trade difficulties, which represents a real challenge for their growth."

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: according to the UN, the conflict has displaced more than ten million people.

title: US govt ends 83 per cent of USAID programmes, cancels 5,200 contracts

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (post on X)
acts.speech: Announced that the US Department of State, along with Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), made this decision after a six-week review of the agency's activities ; "The 5,200 contracts that are now cancelled spent tens of billions of dollars in ways that did not serve, (and in some cases even harmed), the core national interests of the United States" ; "In consultation with Congress, we intend for the remaining 18% of programmes we are keeping (approximately 1,000) to be administered more effectively under the State Department."

acts.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA), Nigeria
acts.speech: Earlier announced its plan to strengthen its domestic HIV response and produce HIV-related medical tools, including test kits and antiretroviral drugs.

acts.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier reports)
acts.speech: Reported that intervention programmes were abruptly suspended, community health workers lost their jobs, and USAID health workers deployed to hard-to-reach areas were recalled.

acts.speaker: Wale Edun, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy of Nigeria
acts.speech: Disclosed that FEC also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment.

title: LPP Speaks Against ‘Redundant Wastes’ at NPA -Urges Boakai to Stop Providing Support to Two Separate Boards - Analyst Liberia

acts.speaker: Liberian People's Party (LPP) (press release / party statement)
acts.speech: Has spotted what it considers "redundant wastes" at the National Port Authority and is urging President Joseph N. Boakai to cease the expenditure of public funds that result from maintaining two separate boards of directors and two executive teams for the management of the Free Port of Liberia. The party says this redundant structure wastes resources and complicates the management of port operations. The LPP advocates for APM Terminals to continue its management of the Free Port of Monrovia, adhering strictly to the terms outlined in the 2011 concession agreements, and calls for APM Terminals to reimburse the Government of Liberia for all operational costs incurred on its behalf, including salaries of $13 million and $14 million that the NPA paid for 2023 and 2024 respectively. The party noted that the NPA, as landlord and regulatory authority, did not invest in purchasing or maintaining essential equipment or employing a significant workforce to manage daily operations at the port. The LPP also called on the Boakai administration to demand that APM Terminals publish comprehensive financial statements, urged APM Terminals to explain the recent increase in costs associated with NPA services and to undertake a comprehensive removal of debris and sedimentation, and stressed the importance of establishing a transparent and accountable process for the selection of inspection consultants, stating that the government exists to serve the interests of its citizens, not to exploit them through mismanagement or lack of accountability.

acts.speaker: J. Yanqui Zaza, Chairman of the Liberian People's Party (quoted in a party release)
acts.speech: Said that in this revised governance structure, the National Port Authority (NPA) would take on the role of both regulator and landlord, aligning with Landlord Port Governance principles, as the World Bank outlined in 2017. "What exactly is Landlord Port Governance? This model is characterized by a blend of public and private interests in port management. Specifically, the port authority assumes dual responsibilities: acting as both a regulator and a landlord. Meanwhile, operational activities, especially those related to cargo handling, are executed by private firms—in this instance, APM Terminals. This structure encourages collaboration and efficiency while allowing the private sector to leverage its expertise in port operations (as defined by the World Bank in 2007). How does the National Port Authority generate its revenue under this governance model? Consistent with Landlord Port Governance principles, the NPA generates income through various channels: first, it receives concession fees from APM Terminals; second, it collects maritime fees, which include rental income from piers and non-roofed accessories; and third, it earns rental income from storage facilities..."

acts.speaker: World Bank (2007 and 2017 definitions of Landlord Port Governance)
acts.speech: Outlined the Landlord Port Governance model, in which the port authority acts as both regulator and landlord while operational activities, especially cargo handling, are executed by private firms.

acts.speaker: President Joseph N. Boakai of Liberia
acts.speech: On August 5, 2024, reaffirmed a significant transition in the management of the Free Port of Monrovia, confirming the transfer of this vital asset from the state-owned National Port Authority to APM Terminals during a meeting with Mr. Igor van den Essen, Regional Managing Director of APM Terminals; Mr. Clay Crain, Managing Director of APM-Liberia; and Mr. Sekuu H. Dukuly, Managing Director of the NPA. The party quotes President Boakai as expressing a firm commitment to uphold the binding 2011 agreement, emphasizing the importance of safeguarding the interests of the Liberian people. He highlighted that this transfer is intended to bring about improved efficiency and operational effectiveness at the Free Port of Monrovia, ultimately benefiting the nation's economy.

title: Why Ghana has been excluded from US Millennium Challenge list for 2026

acts.speaker: MCC Candidate Country Report for Fiscal Year 2026 (Millennium Challenge Corporation)
