acts.speech: Said the country is investing in the revitalization of primary healthcare, pooled procurement systems, phytomedicine development, and wider coverage under social health insurance schemes ; “We are placing greater emphasis on domestic resource mobilization and increasing our capacity to produce pharmaceuticals and critical health inputs.”

acts.speaker: Dr. Salako, Nigerian Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Highlighted Nigeria’s achievement in rolling out the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine: “As of May 2025, we vaccinated over 14 million girls. This represents the highest number of HPV vaccinations in a single round globally.”

acts.speaker: Dr. Salako, Nigerian Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Disclosed that, in a move to reduce donor dependence, Nigeria budgeted an additional $200 million in 2025 to sustain its AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Programmes in response to declining Official Development Assistance (ODA).

acts.speaker: Dr. Salako, Nigerian Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: “We are addressing Sickle Cell Disease, Type 1 Diabetes, Rheumatic Heart Disease, and Childhood Cancers through the PEN-PLUS strategy. Nigeria currently leads implementation in the African region.”

acts.speaker: Dr. Salako, Nigerian Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Announced that the country will host the next high-level Ministerial Conference on Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) in June 2026 in Abuja.

acts.speaker: Dr. Salako, Nigerian Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Called for increased collaboration within BRICS on pharmaceutical and biomedical research: “We welcome opportunities to collaborate with BRICS countries on pharmaceutical and biomedical research on NCDs, phytomedicine development, and academic exchanges.” “We are also open to partnerships to strengthen our domestic capacities to produce drugs, medical devices, and vaccines.”

acts.speaker: Dr. Salako, Nigerian Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
acts.speech: Said the BRICS bloc has a critical responsibility to lead the global health agenda, stressing that cooperation among its members will drive progress toward achieving SDG 3: “Our collective efforts at addressing global health challenges would not only complement individual country efforts but serve as impetus to ensure SDG Goal 3 is achieved without leaving anyone behind.” “In the context of our shared humanity, we must work together. Humanity is one.”

title: Conferência da ONU para relançar ajuda ao desenvolvimento arranca hoje em Sevilha

acts.speaker: “Seville Commitment”, UN declaration (document)
acts.speech: States that the aim is to “renew the global development financing framework”, at a moment of “serious geopolitical tensions and conflicts” and when the objectives agreed by the international community in the 2030 Agenda “are seriously behind schedule” ; “We are running out of time to reach our goals and to confront the adverse impacts of climate change. (...) The gap between our sustainable development aspirations and the financing to achieve them has continued to widen, particularly in developing countries, reaching an estimated value of 4 trillion dollars a year” ; across 68 pages it also emphasises that only the strengthening of multilateralism can respond to the urgent need to eradicate poverty and to confront the impacts of climate change, and recognises the sovereign debt of vulnerable and developing countries as one of the great obstacles to sustainable development.

acts.speaker: United Nations (calculations/data)
acts.speech: According to UN calculations, the current shortfall in development aid is 1.5 trillion more than ten years ago, and in 2024 official development assistance fell for the first time in six years, with a further 20% drop forecast for 2025.

acts.speaker: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General
acts.speech: Said recently that the Seville conference “is a unique opportunity to reform the international financial system”, which is today obsolete and dysfunctional.

title: Russia inches ahead in eastern Ukraine as Trump warns of aid cuts to Kyiv - The Ghanaian Chronicle

acts.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine
acts.speech: Sharply raised his demand for air defence systems, saying on Tuesday that Ukraine needed a dozen additional Patriot systems to insulate its economy from the war. In April Zelenskyy had said Ukraine needed a minimum of seven Patriot systems to provide air cover.

acts.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine
acts.speech: Said that last week Russia used almost 500 glide bombs, whose warhead ranges from 250kg (550lbs) to three tonnes, more than 400 strike drones, and almost 20 missiles of various types against Ukraine's front lines and civilian infrastructure.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
acts.speech: Told NBC in an interview that he was open to reducing military aid to Ukraine and pulling the US out of NATO. "Possibly," he said, when asked if Kyiv should prepare for less aid from the US.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
acts.speech: Has previously pledged to end the Ukraine war quickly, but unlike US President Biden has not upheld Ukraine's territorial integrity as a priority.

title: Corte do financiamento dos EUA na luta contra a SIDA ameaça milhões de vidas

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
acts.speech: Stated that HIV infections have been declining in recent years, with only 1.3 million new cases recorded in 2023, a 60% decline since the peak of the virus in 1995.

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
acts.speech: Said that with the US President's announcement freezing all foreign assistance for 90 days, authorities estimate that by 2029 there could be 8.7 million people infected with HIV, a tenfold increase in disease-related deaths (to 6.3 million) and 3.4 million more orphaned children: "We will see an increase in this disease", speaking from Uganda ; "It will cost lives if the United States Government does not change its mind and maintains its leadership", adding that it is not her place to criticise any government policy.

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
acts.speech: Pleaded with the Trump administration not to cut the funding abruptly, which she said resulted in "panic, fear and confusion" in many of the African countries hardest hit by AIDS; recounted that in one county in Kenya 550 HIV professionals were immediately dismissed, while thousands of others in Ethiopia were dismissed, leaving health authorities unable to track the epidemic; observed that the loss of United States funding for HIV programmes in some countries was catastrophic, with external funding, mainly American, representing around 90% of their programmes; detailed that almost 400 million dollars go to countries such as Uganda, Mozambique and Tanzania ; "We can work with the Americans on how to reduce their contribution, if that is what they want."

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
acts.speech: Described the American withdrawal from global efforts against HIV as the second biggest crisis the sector has ever faced — after the years of delay it took for poor countries to obtain the life-saving antiretrovirals long available in rich countries.

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
acts.speech: Noted that the loss of American support comes at another critical moment, with the arrival of what she called "a magic prevention tool" known as lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection shown to offer complete protection against HIV in women and which worked almost as well for men; said widespread use of it, in addition to other interventions to halt HIV, could help end the disease as a public health problem within the next five years; said it is sold as Sunlenca and was developed by the American company Gilead ; said international aid "helped an American company innovate, to create something that will earn them millions and millions, but at the same time will prevent new infections in the rest of the world", stating that the funding freeze makes no economic sense ; "We appeal to the United States Government to review this, to understand that this is mutually beneficial", noting that foreign assistance represents less than 1% of the overall United States budget: "Why would it need to be so disruptive for that 1%?"

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
acts.speech: Said that so far no other country or donor has come forward to fill the void that will be left by the loss of American aid, but that she plans to visit several European capitals to speak with global leaders: "People will die because life-saving tools have been taken away from them" ; "I have not yet heard of any European country that has committed to stepping in, but I know they are listening and trying to see where they can step in, because they care about rights, about humanity."

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Announced that the United States would freeze all foreign assistance for 90 days.

title: Affliction Amid Wheat Export Narrative

acts.speaker: Teyba Jemal, 36-year-old maid queuing for bread in the Lafto neighbourhood
acts.speech: "Either I buy this or not eat," Teyba told Fortune.

acts.speaker: Adamu Mulat, Sheger Bread distributor
acts.speech: "I don't blame them. The bread is not enough for all." ; On the volume of bread received at his outlet: "It all depends on the supply."

acts.speaker: Hussien Ahmed, significant shareholder of Mizan Flour & Biscuit Factory
acts.speech: Was in despair about the meagre wheat supply that has led the factory to operate at 20pc of capacity, saying he had to let go of seven of his 47 employees and had to source wheat with the help of intermediaries, paying an additional price of up to 5,000 Br: "Consumers shoulder the burden."

acts.speaker: Muluneh Lema, head of the Ethiopian Millers' Association
acts.speech: Said the Association's leaders tried to commission a survey of the millers but many declined to participate for fear of consequences: "The scarcity is not recent."

acts.speaker: Endeshaw Legesse, director of procurement, Ethiopian Industrial Inputs Development Enterprise (EIIDE)
acts.speech: Attributed the challenges to farmers' unions directly supplying the government and cutting the cord of the distribution chain.

acts.speaker: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD) and Shimelis Abdisa, head of the Oromia Regional State
acts.speech: Announced two weeks ago the first batch of 1.2 million quintals harvested in the Bale Zone.

acts.speaker: Oromia Regional State officials
acts.speech: Claim to have 2.8 million hectares of land cultivated in the region, and continue to aspire to ensure 15 million quintals of wheat are shipped to East African markets such as Kenya, Djibouti, and Somalia.

acts.speaker: Study commissioned by the USAID Ethiopia office on the wheat market
acts.speech: Concluded that Ethiopia would be unlikely to achieve a seven million tonnes harvest in five years; the study says Ethiopian farmers will find it difficult to plough over 2.1 million hectares of land.

acts.speaker: Report by the Foreign Agricultural Services Bureau of the US Department of Agriculture
acts.speech: Has projected Ethiopia's wheat production for the current year at 5.5 million tonnes, a volume three times lower than what Ethiopian agriculture authorities wanted to see.

acts.speaker: Mohammed Amanalo, 37, farmer in the Bale zone
acts.speech: Said he sold 420Qtl of wheat for 3,200 Br a quintal under the pressure of the local authorities: "We can't say no to the government."

acts.speaker: Alemu Tesema, 50, farmer near Bishoftu (DebreZeit) town, Oromia Regional State
acts.speech: Was discontented with the regional bureau selling price officials set at 3,200 Br for a quintal, saying the price fails to consider the production costs, such as pesticides and labour put in during harvest, and that during several meetings with local authorities farmers' complaints have fallen on deaf ears: "No one wants to get less than what they spent."

acts.speaker: Beriso Feyisa, deputy head of the Oromia Agriculture Bureau
acts.speech: Claims the farmgate price exceeds production costs, describing the margin for farmers as "reasonable", crediting the Bureau for supplying agricultural inputs with loans, and disclosed the current export generating 50 dollars from a quintal, revealing a 700 Br loss from the farmgate price: "The forex would be used to buy agricultural inputs."

acts.speaker: Officials of the Ministry of Trade & Regional Integration and the Ethiopian Trading Businesses Corporation
acts.speech: Have declined to comment on this story.

acts.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Minister of Finance
acts.speech: Hoped to see the country generate 200 million dollars from its first wheat export.

acts.speaker: World Bank
acts.speech: Estimated Ethiopia's average fertiliser use at over 36Kgs per hectare.

acts.speaker: World Food Program (WFP)
acts.speech: Reveals that more than 20 million people require food assistance, of which 7.9 million are under productive safety net programs.

acts.speaker: Esayas Lemma, head of the crop development directorate under the Ministry of Agriculture
acts.speech: On officials offering aid organisations the option of buying wheat from the domestic "surplus" with foreign currency: "They can source it from the local market."

acts.speaker: Esayas Lemma, head of the crop development directorate under the Ministry of Agriculture
acts.speech: Attributed the boost in demand to a change in lifestyle and urbanisation, and said most farmers consume 60pc of what they produce during the Meher season.

acts.speaker: Adane Tufa, agricultural economist
acts.speech: Is one of the experts who, while applauding the efforts to become self-sufficient in wheat, question the wisdom of exporting wheat before ensuring local demands are fully covered; he believes the market reflects the gap in the wheat supply chain.

acts.speaker: A macroeconomist requesting anonymity
acts.speech: Said that export should not be a priority in a country where inflation has diminished household incomes. He argued the country would not be competitive in the international market without lowering its price, noting top wheat-exporting countries like Ukraine compete in the global market with lower prices as they do not import agricultural inputs like fertiliser.

acts.speaker: Netsanet Tesfaye, corporate communications manager, Ethiopian Commodity Exchange (ECX)
acts.speech: Said the plan forwarded by the federal and regional authorities to export wheat to neighbouring markets is separate from the ECX.

title: US donates two boats to improve health access for remote communities in the Western Region

acts.speaker: Kimberly Rosen, USAID/Ghana Mission Director
acts.speech: “The United States is proud to partner with the Ghana Health Service to bring health services to remote communities,” said at the handover ceremony. “The boats will improve medical outreach, providing immunizations, maternal and childcare, malaria, nutrition, and other health services to you—the people of Jomoro.”

acts.speaker: Gabriel Yengliereh, Jomoro District Director of Health Services
acts.speech: emphasized the importance of the boats, noting, “None of the communities along the lagoon have a health facility, and reaching them by road is nearly impossible. With these new boats, we can now bring critical health services directly to these remote communities.”

title: Bruxelas aprova ajuda humanitária de 21,5 milhões Ásia-Pacífico

acts.speaker: European Commission (EU executive, press statement)
acts.speech: According to a statement from the EU executive, an air bridge is being launched to take essential goods to the victims of Typhoon Yagi, with a flight expected to arrive in Laos in the coming days.

title: ‘Govt should be extra transparent in the 2025 General Elections process to avoid any suspicions of rigging’—AACC accountability champion Rev. Maulidi

acts.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) economic justice & accountability champion in Malawi
acts.speech: Advised that, ahead of the 2025 General Elections, the State authorities be extra transparent in the electoral process to avoid any suspicions of rigging; faults the State authorities for lack of continuous update of the Kanengo operations ; “It was not wrong for the Leader of Opposition to visit the place as probably a whistleblower alerted him and the other opposition MPs about some suspicious activities there. Whistleblowers are needed in order to make things right” ; “It is clear, based on the reaction of the rest of the members of the public after the MPs visit to the warehouse, that the majority of people are not aware of this arrangement with NRB at Kanengo. Ahead of the General Elections, all stakeholders are bound to be sensitive to the whole electoral process. All eyes are on the voter registration process and that calls for continuous update for transparency and accountability.”

acts.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) economic justice & accountability champion in Malawi
acts.speech: Said the transparency and accountability should also go along with security of every electoral process, saying the warehouse at Kanengo should have been well secured by the country’s law enforcement agency, the Malawi Police Service ; “Part of transparency and accountability in the electoral process is security. It is apparent that the opposition MPs did not find any, thus they can make as many accusations they might make, which unfortunately can be misleading due to lack of security transparency. There have been many other instances where the NRB has been accused of not providing the right services in as far as voter registration is concerned — with many of the issues being controversial and conflicting on the suspicion of rigging of the elections. The State authorities, therefore, must be transparent at every stage of the electoral process by updating the nation of every development because every activity is going to raise eyebrows. For the case of the Kanengo controversy, the State authorities should have come out in the open, along with their development partners, to explain the arrangement and dispel any suspicions of vote rigging instead of letting loose a one-sided version of the event. The nation needs to know all these things. I mean, very few knew of the arrangement between the government, the UNDP and other development partners at Kanengo — thus there was need to keep updating the public of the progress that this system has achieved so far.” ; concluded by saying that while whistleblowing on wrong electoral process is very important, it should also be done in good faith having established all elements of evidence to avoid creating a state of panic among all stakeholders.

acts.speaker: George Chaponda, Leader of Opposition in Malawi
acts.speech: Accused the government of using the National Food Reserve Agency (NFRA) warehouse in Kanengo, Lilongwe in collaboration with the National Registration Bureau (NRB), to compromise the ongoing voter registration exercise ; told the august House that the opposition MPs’ visit was initially intended to assess the availability of maize at the warehouses but claims they stumbled upon thousands of national IDs scattered on the warehouse floor, with some packed in sacks; asserted that the NRB’s operation at the NFRA warehouse raised serious questions about the integrity and security of its operations and questioned why the institution, that is critical to electoral processes, was operating from a warehouse rather than its official premises at the Office of the President and Vice-President.

acts.speaker: National Registration Bureau (NRB) officials
acts.speech: Hit back by accusing the MPs of deliberately scattering the items they found before capturing the place on camera strewn with IDs and papers.

acts.speaker: Junior staff / interns at the Kanengo warehouse (interviewed in the MPs’ video clips)
acts.speech: Explained that their job as interns was to sort out the cards according to each registration centre and pack them for distribution, and that their seniors were somewhere else on other duties to do with their processes.

title: The Struggle of Displaced People in Mogadishu Amidst Aid Diversion

acts.speaker: Disaster Management Agency (DMA), Somalia
acts.speech: Has reported that approximately 6 million people, including entire families, are at risk of famine unless immediate humanitarian assistance is provided.

acts.speaker: Displaced families in Mogadishu
acts.speech: Have claimed that the aid intended for them is frequently stolen, leaving them to fend for themselves.

acts.speaker: Yusuf Luqmaan, father displaced from Lower Shabelle due to drought
acts.speech: "I've moved from several camps, and each time I saw the route of aid deliveries, whether food or materials like shelter and mattresses, they were redirected. After several days, we see the same supplies being sold in the markets." ; Explained that his daily work involves digging holes and burying rubbish, for which he earns a mere dollar per day, but that he often goes home empty-handed: "Sometimes, I don't get work at all."

acts.speaker: Small business owner at Hamarweyne market (anonymous)
acts.speech: Revealed that he buys ready-to-use therapeutic food with the logos of international aid groups from individuals who obtain the supplies from humanitarian agencies, and emphasised that he does not have a direct connection with the original suppliers; the therapeutic food items, typically meant for malnourished children, are being sold for $30-$35 per carton.

acts.speaker: Sahro Sharif Mohamed, mother of nine displaced from Jowhar
acts.speech: "My child was supposed to receive 35 pieces of biscuits per week, but I only get 9. Four or five of them I sell to feed the rest of my family, leaving my child with just 4."

acts.speaker: Anbiya Isaac, displaced woman
acts.speech: "There was a time I went for three days without food, and I did not receive any form of assistance - not even water."

acts.speaker: Mohamud Ma'alin Abdulle, Chairman of the Disaster Management Agency
acts.speech: Confirmed that aid diversion is a known issue and that investigations are currently underway: "We are aware of this issue, and it's a possibility since aid passes through many hands. We are conducting a large-scale investigation into the situation."

acts.speaker: Aid agencies (non-response)
acts.speech: Attempts to contact aid agencies for comment on the diversion issue were unsuccessful, as they were unable to speak with the reporters.

acts.speaker: Shafi Sharif Mohamed, researcher and chairman of the Somali Researchers Association
acts.speech: Warned of the disastrous consequences that could unfold: "The situation could worsen beyond expectations if the aid does not reach the people. This could lead to a greater need for food and resources, further exacerbating the situation, with devastating consequences for the Somali population."

title: WHO working to address funding gaps left by USAID

acts.speaker: Chikwe Ihekweazu, WHO Africa acting regional director
acts.speech: Says that with strategic investment and governance, African nations can fund their health priorities effectively; speaking during a press briefing in Kigali, Rwanda ahead of AHAIC 2025, said there is need to map funding gaps and work closely with African governments to find sustainable solutions for areas that were being sponsored by USAID: “The focus must shift towards internally driven strategies while remaining open to strategic collaborations.” ; said this entails African governments prioritising internal revenue generation for healthcare, reducing out-of-pocket costs, and expanding universal healthcare coverage.

acts.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa Group chief executive officer
acts.speech: Urged African leaders and global stakeholders to rethink health investments to build resilient and sustainable health systems; said Africa’s economic and population growth challenges are deeply linked to healthcare financing: “Sub-Saharan Africa is facing an economic crisis, and the lack of fiscal space is a major issue” ; “Investing in health must be tied to population development, ensuring that every girl and woman have the right to make informed reproductive health choices.” ; called for investment shifts towards primary healthcare, warning that disproportionate funding for tertiary care leaves millions without access to essential services.

acts.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa Group chief executive officer (on USAID-funded programmes)
acts.speech: Said Amref had significant programmes worth about US$28 million in Kenya, Malawi, Zambia and Ethiopia that were being sponsored by USAID, the core of which was around maternal and child health and prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission: “So, as we speak, we are working with the governments to ensure that no child is going to be exposed to HIV because we are not protected during the mother’s pregnancy. That’s a risk. We had programmes on HIV prevention testing. For example, we had programmes on what you may call running care treatment centres for HIV, what we call the comprehensive care clinics that have stopped.” ; said Amref had health workers across Zambia, Malawi, Ethiopia and Kenya actively involved in care and treatment for prevention of mother-to-child HIV and tuberculosis who are now out of the health system though still trained.

acts.speaker: Claudia Shilumani, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention director of external relations and strategic management
acts.speech: Called for sustainable financing for African healthcare; said leaders across the continent should look at the need to explore alternative funding models, including public-private partnerships, to ensure long-term sustainability of health programmes and the continued progress made in improving public health.

title: Brussels Airlines launches “Read to Succeed” Literacy Program in Liberia

acts.speaker: Dorothea von Boxberg, CEO of Brussels Airlines
acts.speech: Extended her greetings and congratulations to the participants.

acts.speaker: Marjolein Six, Country Manager Liberia, Brussels Airlines
acts.speech: "At Brussels Airlines, we are committed not only to serve Liberia as an airline, with regular flights between Monrovia and Brussels. We want to go further. We want to be partners for the Liberian people. Learning to read and to write is for life. By partnering-up with read-to-succeed, we can plant a seed for many young Liberian people that will allow them to blossom for a very long time."

acts.speaker: Ama Harris, Rosetta Steps Education Foundation
acts.speech: "Our organization is founded on the belief that education is a human right and the best means of combating inequality, poverty, and discrimination. Less than half of Liberians are literate. Inspired by the legacy of one of the country's most dedicated educators, Rosetta Benson, we consider it our mission to empower and educate as many Liberian youth and families in need as we can, and we're happy to do this with the support of Brussels Airlines and help alliance."

title: Millennium challenge Account Bénin II: Le Conseil d'administration installé tient sa première session

acts.speaker: Lionel Zinsou, Prime Minister of Benin
acts.speech: Revisited bilateral cooperation between the United States and Benin to stress that the first compact had shown convincing results for the national economy, citing the performance of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou as an example, and said he hoped the cooperation would continue.

acts.speaker: Lionel Zinsou, Prime Minister of Benin
acts.speech: Dwelt on the importance of the second compact for Benin, accompanied by good-governance conditionality, in order to improve people’s daily lives through energy: “It is an important factor of development,” he reminded them. He also drew the board members’ attention to the task before them: “Benin is among the privileged countries with respect to the Compact II investment,” and urged them to succeed in their mission: “Doing so will make you fighters on the front line of the country’s development. Your responsibility is great in the face of this envelope destined for Benin for the happiness of our compatriots.”

acts.speaker: Lucy Tamlyn, U.S. Ambassador to Benin
acts.speech: Praised the head of state’s commitment and the dynamism of cooperation between the two countries, and recalled that Compact II is an opportunity Benin must seize to improve the business climate and the daily lives of Beninese people.

acts.speaker: Fulbert Gero Amoussouga, Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
acts.speech: Insisted that together with his colleagues they grasp the significance of their appointment, and promised not to disappoint: “Our responsibility and our duty are great. They match the expectations of the people.” Speaking of Compact II, he praised it and revealed that it would contribute to improving the living conditions of several thousand of our compatriots, and said he hoped to count on everyone so that the set objectives are achieved.

title: Stakes Unite in Solidarity on Humantrian Day, Celebrating Global Resilience, Compassion

acts.speaker: Darren Welch, British Ambassador to Ethiopia
acts.speech: Urged all stakeholders to redouble efforts towards the humanitarian cause of the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS), underlining that the humanitarian effort needs more support from ambassadors, humanitarian leaders, government officials and members of the civil society ; "This year we'll give perhaps 80 million pounds in support of humanitarian relief in Ethiopia as part of our desire to remain a steadfast and strong partner of the Ethiopian and the UN humanitarian system in the country," Welch pledged during an exclusive interview with EBC World.

acts.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
acts.speech: Underscored that efforts should be redoubled to commit to the people, who are vulnerable around the world and here in Ethiopia.

acts.speaker: Abera Tola, President of the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
acts.speech: “Our volunteers have been with communities in their most difficult times—offering help, hope, and healing” ; “Their courage and compassion reflect the very essence of this year’s theme. Today’s celebration is not just ceremonial, it is a recognition of their daily sacrifices” ; called on development partners, supporters, and the public to renew their commitment by backing the Society’s fundraising drives, ensuring the safety of humanitarian workers, and expanding outreach to vulnerable populations.

title: “É fundamental fazer renascer o processo de atracção do investimento directo estrangeiro”

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said Cape Verde's GDP growth rate, regardless of declarations that express wishes rather than facts, has been low (below 8-9%) and shows a tendency towards stagnation around 4-5%; that the levers of growth have been foreign aid, emigrants' remittances and revenues from tourism and related activities; that at this rate only in 20-25 years will the country reach an income of 10,000 USD per capita while other Small Island Developing States reach 25-30 thousand; that the much-vaunted creation of platforms or hubs and the International Business Centre "are resounding names, but they have not brought the expected results", and that the strategies and their monitors must be revisited.

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said national aviation, or rather air connectivity, internal or external, "has not been a success" and much more was expected; that there has been no courage to tackle the real problems with competent and experienced people; that TACV remains a fragile and loss-making company while TAP Air Portugal has been filling the gaps and reinforcing Cape Verde's connectivity via Lisbon, so that "from the much-vaunted hub in Sal, it is we who are being benefited by the Lisbon hub"; that internal air transport needs a complete overhaul; and that the maritime sector has also not been successful, being a drain on public resources because of badly negotiated agreements.

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said the privatisation of the Caixa is in fact a reprivatisation, because the shares already belonged to GEO-CAPITAL in the past; that reducing the direct presence of the state in a highly regulated sector is a good signal to the market; that it would be desirable for a foreign bank or financial institution to appear among the new shareholders alongside INPS; and that "the transfer of shares from state ownership to the private sector is always a good sign."

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said that from the point of view of financial proceeds the Public Sale Offering does not change much for the state, involving only about 14 million euros, but that a large public turnout at the Stock Exchange would signal confidence in the country's economy and a change of attitude among Cape Verdeans in placing their savings, while warning "we should not expect a miracle as a result of that" ; said the operation could strengthen the business environment because "it stirs people and can induce a new dynamism in business", since "it is people who make the economy."

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said the amount involved (14 million euros) is small for foreign investment and, given that FDI flows over the last 6-7 years have not performed well, the operation will not have much impact; that it is necessary to analyse what is going well and badly in attracting foreign direct investment and to revive the process.

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said Emprofac is perhaps a company with potential for sale if well negotiated and if it effectively reduces medicine prices, but that he would immediately exclude ENAPOR from the published privatisation list; that one should speak not of privatising the ports or their management but of internationalising the ports of Sao Vicente and/or Praia, discussing directly with the 3-5 largest container operators in the Mid-Atlantic region and requiring investments to be at the risk of the candidate.

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said the world is passing from a unipolar world dominated by the USA to a multipolar one without clear contours; that by blindly following the USA in its hybrid war against Russia through the instrumentalisation of Ukraine, Europe miscalculated and showed too much subservience and is now suffering the consequences; that Cape Verde, "a passive and confused element in the Western world", suffers from the effects of recession in Europe; that ECOWAS is not and cannot be an alternative for insertion into the world economy; that Cape Verde must remain aligned with and strengthen relations with the USA and the European Union rather than believing China or other Global South countries can leverage its development; that NATO must review its expansionist ambition and concentrate on security in the North Atlantic, where Cape Verde will play an important role at the southern vertex; and that on emigration the country must toughen conditions of establishment and residence and deter clandestine emigrants using Cape Verde as a corridor to Europe.

acts.speaker: Unnamed interviewee (Cape Verdean economist with experience in tourism, aviation and banking), interviewed by Expresso das Ilhas
acts.speech: Said 2024 will be strongly marked by the shock of the third revolution of Social Security (INPS), which by ending the idle and improper exploitation of its unremunerated deposits by part of the national banking sector has awoken to its real mission; that the new policy will improve and increase social benefits and pensions and raise workers' real wages, reducing union pressure for nominal wage increases; and that the INPS positions itself as the central institution on the Cape Verdean economic chessboard, with its helmsman Mario Rui Lopes Fernandes being "the figure of the year".

title: How will the Iran crisis impact Africa?

acts.speaker: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Egyptian President
acts.speech: advocating for de-escalation.

title: A delicate truce in Uganda-Rwanda relations

acts.speaker: Bank of Uganda (data)
acts.speech: According to data from Bank of Uganda, Uganda's export earnings have dropped from as high as an average of US$15.6 million monthly in January to an average of US$0.68 million as at the end of December last year.

acts.speaker: National Bank of Rwanda (statement)
acts.speech: According to the National Bank of Rwanda, in January 2020, the Rwandan urban consumer price index increased by 0.6% month-to-month, higher than a decrease of 0.3% achieved in the previous month; year-on-year inflation stood at 7.3% for January 2020 compared to 6.7% reached in December 2019. ; "On monthly basis, the inflationary pressures were due to food and non-alcoholic beverages whose prices increased by 0.6% in January from a decrease of 0.3% recorded in the previous month." ; "Prices increased particularly for food products including Irish potato, fermented sorghum, sweet potato, sorghum, palm oil, taro, local rice, live chicken among others. Overall, there was an increase in prices of fresh products (0.3% in January compared to a decrease of 2.8% realized in the previous month)." ; The central bank of Rwanda noted that there would be a "continuing rise in prices of alcoholic beverages and tobacco (21.1% against 20.6% in December) and the uptick in prices of housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels (2.4% after 2.2% in December 2019)."

acts.speaker: A Rwandan citizen who preferred anonymity
acts.speech: Told The Independent in November 2019, "Price hikes every now and then. You can imagine the price of 1 kilogramme of beans has doubled its period in a price of three months."

acts.speaker: A site that aggregates exchange rate movements in the world (data)
acts.speech: Data from the site shows that the Rwanda Franc has weakened against the US Dollar; from July 2019, the Rwanda Franc steadily loses ground against the US Dollar in the period up to January and the trend had not relented till February.

title: Burundi/Humanitaire : Environ 1,5 million de personnes ont besoin d’aide humanitaire d’urgence

acts.speaker: Official humanitarian response plan of the government and the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: States that roughly 1.5 million people will need humanitarian assistance in 2023, of whom 1.1 million of the most vulnerable are targeted for aid.

acts.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: Says that mobilising resources remains a challenge, and the UN warns that the lack of funding could have “serious consequences,” leaving vulnerable populations exposed to climate risks and disease and without protection, jeopardising repatriation efforts and livelihoods ; “Breaking the cycle of epidemics will be difficult without an emergency health response and strengthened access to water, sanitation and hygiene.”

acts.speaker: John Agbor, interim United Nations Resident Coordinator in Burundi
acts.speech: Said in a statement: “Our humanitarian response for Burundi in 2023 is the result of an in-depth analysis of the needs and challenges facing the most vulnerable populations.” He stresses that together with the government and humanitarian and development partners, “we can work towards durable solutions to improve the quality of life of these populations and build a more resilient future. We are all united by a common cause: saving lives and doing everything to leave no one behind.”

acts.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: Says Burundi is highly vulnerable to climate change and that natural disasters have led to significant internal displacement, and considers coordination essential to responding to the humanitarian crisis, with UN agencies continuing to support the humanitarian country team, partners and the government through needs assessments, monitoring and reporting ; “Promoting a well-funded response and a dignified return of refugees will also continue to be a priority.”

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: According to the UN, nearly 675,000 people received humanitarian aid last year, or 70% of the initial target, an achievement resulting from joint efforts by humanitarian partners, the government of Burundi and donors.

title: Titukulane Resilience Food Security Activity hailed for improving coverage of safe, clean drinking water in Mangochi - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Communities in Traditional Authorities Chamba and Ntonda, Mangochi district
acts.speech: Have commended the Titukulane Resilience Food Security Activity for constructing new and rehabilitating existing, but dysfunctional, boreholes in the two areas.

acts.speaker: Village Head Chiyambeni, under T/A Ntonda
acts.speech: Said the problem of lack of safe and clean drinking water negatively affected the social and economic development of his area, and stated that the high levels of destitution and poverty in the area are a result of lack of water, observing that without safe and clean drinking water the possibility of breaking out of the cycle of poverty is incredibly slim: "Lack of water and poverty are inseparably linked because where there is no water, able-bodied members of a community are forced to spend hours searching and transporting water instead of working on their farms. Additionally, poor access to water and insufficient sanitation affect the health of the poor, their food security, and their prospects for making a living."

acts.speaker: Village Head Chiyambeni, under T/A Ntonda
acts.speech: Emphasized that the construction and rehabilitation of the boreholes have reduced cases of waterborne diseases in the targeted areas: "We will now actively participate in the social and economic activities taking place in our communities."

acts.speaker: Theresa Kananji, 50, a widow from Chiyambeni Village who lost her husband to cholera
acts.speech: Said her spouse would not have died if the village had access to safe and clean drinking water, and described the construction of the borehole as a great relief and salvation not only to her family but also to the entire village: "I am very excited with the coming in of a borehole in our village. We used to walk long distances to fetch water from unsafe sources. It would take three hours for someone to walk to and from the water source." ; "This borehole will significantly reduce cases of cases of cholera and other waterborne diseases thereby saving lives. We're very grateful to Care International in Malawi and its partners for giving us this precious gift."

acts.speaker: Solomon Chirwa, WaterAid Malawi Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) specialist
acts.speech: Said the project has helped significantly in improving knowledge, attitudes, skills and norms related to essential sanitation and hygiene behaviors, and stated that there is now increased availability of basic safely managed facilities and consumables necessary for essential sanitation and hygiene practices: "Through the same project, we also provided technical assistance in WASH policy review, WASH planning including integrated planning and performance review with other sectors especially at policy and district levels. We also advocated for increased funding for the WASH sector that recognizes and promotes complementarity with other sectors such as health, education and gender."

title: Tremblements de terre meurtriers en Turquie et en Syrie

acts.speaker: President of Turkey (Recep Tayyip Erdogan)
acts.speech: Requested international assistance in the face of the scale of the tragedy.

acts.speaker: United Nations (UN)
acts.speech: Announced a grant of 25 million dollars to help launch the humanitarian response.

acts.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
acts.speech: Said that nearly 40 international rescue teams should soon be on the ground to assist Turkish rescuers ; that the UN and its partners are monitoring the situation on the ground, while information flows are limited because of chronic telecommunications disruptions and power cuts.

acts.speaker: Carsten Hansen, Middle East regional director of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
acts.speech: "The earthquake struck at the worst hour of the night, at the worst time of the year."

acts.speaker: International Federation of the Red Cross (IFRC)
acts.speech: Declared that it had observed "significant damage to infrastructure in the governorates of Aleppo, Latakia, Hama and Tartous (in the large cities but also in the countryside). The extent of the damage is being assessed." ; According to its latest figures, 1,509 people have died and 3,548 have been injured, a number expected to rise considerably over the next 24 hours ; Launched a total emergency appeal for 200 million Swiss francs (about 215 million US dollars).

acts.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
acts.speech: Said the UN was counting on the international community to help the thousands of people affected by the disaster, "many of whom were already in urgent need of humanitarian assistance in areas where access is difficult."

title: Principaux événements dans le monde ce 20 février au matin:

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Hopes the Ukrainian conflict will be resolved within a year, otherwise there could be a third world war.

acts.speaker: Zenon Mukongo Ngay, Permanent Representative of the DRC to the UN
acts.speech: Told Sputnik that Kinshasa is concerned about the situation with laboratories sponsored by the American USAID in the DRC.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Stated that President Emmanuel Macron could travel to Washington as early as “Monday perhaps.”

acts.speaker: Russian Ministry of Defence
acts.speech: Said Russian air defences destroyed four Ukrainian drones overnight over Crimea and the Bryansk region.

acts.speaker: Head of the Africa Partnership Department at the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Told Sputnik that because of Western sanctions, Russia was unable in 2024 to send money for food aid to African countries such as Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan.

title: Taxpayers owe ZRA K100BN

acts.speaker: Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA)
acts.speech: The authority has revealed that it is currently recording huge fraud in Value Added Tax (VAT) claims, describing it as a scam.

acts.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
acts.speech: Announced yesterday at a Stakeholder Engagement on Tax Administration Performance during the first quarter of 2023 in Lusaka that taxes worth K99.9 billion were being owed to the Authority as at December 2022, and explained that this was one of the reasons the authority was supporting the tax amnesty initiative to encourage taxpayers to commit to their dues; "We have a challenge of escalating debt. Our debt, which are taxes owed to ZRA, now stands at K99.9 billion as at end of 2022 and that is one of the many reasons that we have been supporting implementation of the tax amnesty. We have also started withholding tax liabilities for suppliers to Government. This is a very important reform." ; "What we are saying is that if you want to do business with Government, you must also be a tax payer and if you are not compliant, what we will do is that before Government pays you for the goods and services, we will advise Government to hold a portion of that. We started this in February this year and this is actively in place now so take note."

acts.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
acts.speech: Pointed out that ZRA had continued to record VAT fraud, with taxpayers using fake import certificates, described the current fraudulent VAT as a scam which ZRA had taken aggressively to close, and said Zambia had a huge problem of fraudulent VAT claims; "We also have intensified our investigations on suspected VAT fraud. VAT is a fundamental problem in Zambia. We have a challenge as a country for fraudulent VAT claims. We have heard about supplying air so they claim VAT from air where no goods and servces are provided but someone wants to claim VAT. It is a major scam and we have taken it aggressively as ZRA to make sure that we close it. This is an area we are looking at to seal VAT leakages."

acts.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
acts.speech: Said ZRA collected gross revenue of K27.3 billion during the first quarter of 2023, and announced that K4.1 billion was refunded during the same period with ZRA paying out K1.35 billion per month, compared with K26.5 billion collected during the same period in 2022.

acts.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
acts.speech: Pointed out low payment compliance by withholding VAT agents, with over K13.8 billion cumulatively withheld but not paid, as one of the factors leading to low revenue collection this year; "Other factors are lower than projected profitability of major mining companies in 2022. that led to downward adjustment of the fourth quarter of 2022 provisional tax payment as well as lower metal production and ore grade than forecasted, which affected mineral royalty tax as well as," he said.

title: Fristival en hommage à « Chef Galé » : les organisateurs annoncent les couleurs de la 9e édition

acts.speaker: Macka Traoré, Commissioner General of the Fria Festival (Fristival)
acts.speech: At the outset, the Commissioner General of Fristival explained the reason for the choice of Chef Galé. According to Macka Traoré, this choice is explained by the years of sacrifice and the instilling of the true values of scouting, but beyond that, of true values in the children of Fria. ; "We said to ourselves that instead of always paying tribute to people posthumously, it is better to pay tribute to them while they are still here, so that their families can be even prouder of them. Everyone agreed that Chef Galé should be honoured."

acts.speaker: Macka Traoré, Commissioner General of the Fria Festival (Fristival)
acts.speech: Returning to the 9th Fristival itself, the Commissioner General hammered home what makes this year special: "This year, Father Christmas will walk through Fria like when we were little. In every neighbourhood of Fria, we will give gifts to the children. We will bring that back to life. Because there are children of ten years ago who do not know that this used to happen here. The Feu de Caen, we started it last year. So we will continue the Feu de Caen this year. There are also the former Syli players who will play a gala match. We will put the schools in competition. The winners will get tablets and everything."

acts.speaker: Macka Traoré, Commissioner General of the Fria Festival (Fristival)
acts.speech: "This appointment of hope offers not only humanitarian aid but also an exceptional programme with artists such as Singleton, Fishkiller, Sheba Queen, Koury Simple and many others on stage. These artists, also present at this conference, each promised the best of themselves," Macka Traoré listed, in conclusion.

title: As Somali court draws up lawsuit on human rights violations, ex-spy chief flees the country

acts.speaker: Security sources privy to the matter (anonymous)
acts.speech: Told Horn Observer that Mr. Fahad, who recently changed his name into Fahad Ahmed Dahir, has covertly travelled to Doha, Qatar on a flight via Addis Ababa, Ethiopia on Saturday.

acts.speaker: An officer at the Somali military court (anonymous)
acts.speech: "We can confirm that ex-NISA commander, Fahad Yasin had left the country. We have no further details," said one officer at the military court.

acts.speaker: Supreme Court of Somalia (court record)
acts.speech: Declined an application filed by Fahad's lawyers seeking the top level court to overturn a suspension decision on his parliamentary seat; the court found no reason to overturn the suspension decision issued by the electoral commission which refused to accept the initial victory claimed by Mr. Fahad for the seat number 086.

acts.speaker: Hassan Mohamed, member of parliament from Jubbaland State
acts.speech: "Having lost in the court application followed by the defeat recorded in the recent parliamentary leadership election, I think he senses the dangers unfolding. If Farmaajo loses the [presidential] race. That would mean less protection for him."

acts.speaker: A lawyer working on the case (anonymous, due to security concerns)
acts.speech: "The charges we are filing against Mr. Fahad include the disappearance and the murder of Ikran Tahlil Farah as well as several charges related to attacks, unlawful detentions, torture and injuries against journalists and members of the opposition politicians."

acts.speaker: The Military court and the Banadir regional court
acts.speech: Did not comment on the matter.

acts.speaker: Lawyers working on the case
acts.speech: Say prosecution against the pair (Kulane Jiis and Yasin Farey, both members of the new Somali Parliament) will require the court to write to the new Speaker of the Parliament.

acts.speaker: Abdullahi Jimale, criminal law professor at the Somali university
acts.speech: "Being a member of the Parliament gives you an immunity that provides a shield against criminal charges but that immunity can be revoked because this is the interest of the nation and it is the interest if the justice."

title: Mali-Usa : L'argent de tous les soupçons !

acts.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali
acts.speech: Says it followed with surprise the publication by the United States Department of Government Efficiency, on 15 February 2025, on social media, citing Mali among the countries whose American grants have been cancelled.

acts.speaker: United States Department of Government Efficiency (social media publication, 15 February 2025)
acts.speech: Cited Mali among the countries whose American grants have been cancelled, concerning a supposed grant in favour of Mali of 14 million US dollars (about eight billion eight hundred million CFA francs) in support of social cohesion.

acts.speaker: Government of Mali
acts.speech: Recognises itself in the new orientation of the American authorities aimed at cleaning up and humanising their grants, and welcomes this awareness of the reality of their “public aid” and the actions undertaken against its subversive use that does not conform to the essential needs of the beneficiaries.

acts.speaker: Government of Mali
acts.speech: Invites the American authorities to initiate legal proceedings against the persons who diverted the said funds to finance international terrorism, of which Mali and the other States of the AES Confederation are victims; says it should be recalled that Mali, in its quest for sovereignty, has never ceased to denounce, well before the installation of the new American administration, the danger of the diverted use of official development assistance.

acts.speaker: Malian authorities
acts.speech: Hold that international aid is often used as an instrument of destabilisation and subversion of countries through the financing of terrorist networks and as a means of violating the sovereignty of our States; say that in line with the vision of the President of the Transition, Mali has placed all of its cooperation relations within the framework of respect for the sovereignty of the State, the sovereign choices of the Malian people and the defence of their interests.

title: Va pewa ombautu youhaku

acts.speaker: Dr Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
acts.speech: Said the boat is intended to deliver health services in the region, especially at times when the water is high. “The boat is worth about N$600,000. The boat was built to transport doctors, nurses and patients to health facilities, especially to places that are usually flooded, as well as to Impalila Island,” Shangula said. ; Shangula said that providing the boat demonstrates the ministry’s commitment to ensuring that every Namibian receives quality health care with dignity. ; “The situation of the Zambezi region makes it difficult for the ministry of health to treat citizens at certain times of the year because places become surrounded by flood water. This problem has been solved by the donation of this boat,” Shangula said. ; Shangula added that what is called the Universal Health Coverage Service Coverage Index currently stands at 63%. ; “Flooding does not only disrupt everyday life, it also obstructs health work. The boat will help children and women during difficult times, and also make it possible to respond to places where a particular disease has broken out,” Shangula said.

title: IN FULL | Omri Sender tells the ICJ it is Israel that faces irreversible harm from SA's Gaza action | News24

acts.speaker: Omri Sender, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Told the International Court of Justice that South Africa's claims of genocide in Gaza did not meet requirements for urgency and irreparable harm - and that only Israel would suffer harm that could not be reversed if the court granted the interim order SA seeks ; "It falls to me to address the condition of risk of irreparable harm and urgency. This third condition is, of course, dependent on the two preceding ones... It follows that the irreparable consequences cannot, in the present case, be caused by the alleged disregard of rights under the Genocide Convention." ; "the conclusion is that the condition of irreparable prejudice and urgency cannot be met. It is Israel and its citizens who would risk irreparable harm if the Request of South Africa were to be granted."

acts.speaker: Omri Sender, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Argued that the Applicant's factual account is "entirely one-sided" and makes "hardly any mention of the extraordinary efforts undertaken by Israel - and by a host of other States and international actors - to improve the humanitarian situation" ; said Israel has taken "concrete measures aimed specifically at recognizing and ensuring the right" of the group in question to exist, "facilitating the provision of more and more humanitarian assistance for people in need throughout the Gaza Strip", including the re-opening of a dozen bakeries with the capacity to produce more than two million breads a day, an average of 109 food trucks a day over the last two weeks compared with 70 before the war, water supplied by two pipelines and a new pipe from Egypt, four field hospitals and two floating hospitals, 180 000 litres of fuel a day and an average of 90 tonnes of cooking gas per day ; said "A great effort is indeed invested in eliminating bottlenecks so as to improve the entrance and distribution of aid - notwithstanding Hamas constantly stealing it."

acts.speaker: Omri Sender, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Said civilians "have been severely affected by the hostilities instigated by Hamas", whose "systematic strategy of prosecuting war from under, and within, the civilian population exposes civilians to great risk - and it has brought about great suffering", while "Israel has done - and is doing - a great deal to alleviate this suffering in very challenging circumstances."

acts.speaker: Omri Sender, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Said that "the scope and intensity of the hostilities has been decreasing", and that the United Nations Security Council had only recently adopted resolution 2720 for the specific purpose of alleviating the humanitarian situation; contrary to what was heard the previous day, "this resolution does not 'remain unimplemented'. A Senior Coordinator has been appointed and indeed began her work; the Council remains actively seised of the matter." Israel is already working with the Senior Coordinator and has co-ordinated the entrance of a United Nations delegation into northern Gaza.

acts.speaker: Omri Sender, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
acts.speech: Said "the lack of urgency within the meaning of the Court's case law is further demonstrated by assurances provided before you today by Israel's Co-Agents", that "Israel remains bound, at all times, by its international legal obligations", and that "your consistent case law suggests that assurances of the kind offered by Israel may well render the indication of provisional measures unnecessary."

acts.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw and Galit Raguan, counsel for Israel
acts.speech: "have already shown that the provisions relied upon by the Applicant do not afford, even prima facie, a basis on which this Court's jurisdiction could be founded. They also showed that the rights asserted by the Applicant cannot be regarded as plausible."

acts.speaker: World Food Programme
acts.speech: "has said that the delivery of flour, salt, sugar and yeast continues, so as to enable more bakeries to re-open, 'increasing accessibility and affordability' for thousands of families."

acts.speaker: Israel's Defence Minister
acts.speech: "said last week that Israeli forces would be shifting from the 'intense maneuvering phase of the war' toward 'different types of special operations'." (statement made in an interview to international media, at tab 16-A of the Volume submitted)

acts.speaker: Spokesperson for the Israeli military
acts.speech: "confirmed that the Israeli campaign had already started a transition to fewer ground troops and fewer airstrikes. 'The war shifted a stage', he said... he spoke of a new and less intense phase of fighting. He specifically mentioned that Israel will continue to reduce the number of troops in Gaza."

acts.speaker: United Nations Security Council (resolution 2720 of 22 December 2023)
acts.speech: "the Council demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, as well as the delivery of humanitarian assistance at scale directly to the Palestinian civilian population throughout the Gaza Strip... the Council requested the Secretary-General to appoint a Senior Coordinator in order to establish a United Nations mechanism for accelerating the provision of humanitarian relief consignments to Gaza."

acts.speaker: South Africa (the Applicant in the ICJ case)
acts.speech: "mentioned yesterday the number of trucks entering Gaza each day before and after the war" and argued that Security Council resolution 2720 "remains unimplemented", that the multilateral large-scale humanitarian effort is lacking and that scaling up access of humanitarian relief to Gaza would be of no avail.

acts.speaker: COGAT, the unit in the Israeli Ministry of Defence in charge of monitoring the humanitarian situation (official data/website)
acts.speech: Cited as the source for daily updated details concerning the various ongoing humanitarian efforts, including official data that from 8 December the amount of fuel entering Gaza has doubled and currently stands at 180 000 litres a day.

acts.speaker: Government of Israel (decision of 15 December)
acts.speech: "Israel decided to open its crossing at Kerem Shalom with the express intention to 'improve and upgrade' the delivery of humanitarian assistance to Palestinian civilians in Gaza."

title: PDS Scandal: Akufo-Addo’s “corrupt, cronyistic actions” cause of $190m compact loss – Mahama

acts.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, former President of Ghana and 2024 NDC flagbearer (Facebook post)
acts.speech: Expressed deep disappointment and worry at the loss of $190 million meant for private sector participation in Ghana's electricity distribution under the US Millennium Compact, saying the "corrupt, 'yenkyendi', and cronyistic governance practices" spearheaded by President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo and Vice President Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia led to the loss: "It's disheartening to learn that the $190 million we negotiated for private sector participation in electricity distribution under the US Millennium Compact has been lost due to Nana Addo and Bawumia's corrupt, 'yenkyendi', and cronyistic governance practices. This is unacceptable, and we deserve better as a people."

acts.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, former President of Ghana and 2024 NDC flagbearer (Facebook post)
acts.speech: Pledged that he "will work diligently to enhance private sector efficiency in the electricity distribution system, including metering, revenue management, and fault response" when re-elected president, and promised to "ensure a thorough investigation of the PDS [Power Distribution Services] scandal to hold those involved accountable" ; "My administration will prioritise accountability... We can work together to build a brighter future for Ghana's power sector that benefits citizens and businesses. Let's stand together, fight against corruption and cronyism, and work towards building the Ghana we want."

acts.speaker: US government
acts.speech: Halted the transfer of the funds, stating that private sector participation was a central reform under MCC's Ghana Power Compact.

title: How APD is shaping Pan-African development

acts.speaker: Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first President (speech at the founding of the Organization of African Unity, Addis Ababa, 1963)
acts.speech: Emphasized the urgency of African unity and the need for collective economic planning to effectively harness the continent's potential resources. He warned that without such unity and concerted effort, Africa would struggle to progress at the necessary pace, and its challenges could become chronic, making it too late for Pan-African unity to ensure stability and prosperity.

acts.speaker: Africa Prosperity 2024 Presidential and Business Executive Dialogue Peduase Compact 2024 (joint declaration presented by Africa-America Institute President Kofi Appenteng)
acts.speech: Committed business leaders, elected officials and social impact leaders to advancing the African Continental Free Trade Area Agreement with the goal of empowering African nations in their pursuit of prosperity: "We emphasised that the primary goal of the Africa Prosperity Network is to shift the narrative in African countries from 'poverty reduction' to one that empowers nations in their pursuit of prosperity." ; "We believe that it is both necessary and urgent for Africa's private sector, from large-scale to small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs), to own and drive the continent's single market agenda." ; committed the business community to interoperable payment systems, value-added manufacturing, digitalisation and agri-technology; governments to public-private infrastructure partnerships, trade facilitation, visa-free arrangements among all African countries, investment in agriculture and value addition of natural resources, and to advocating the creation of a reparation infrastructural fund; the AfCFTA Secretariat to supporting non-ratifying member States; and development partners including the UN, UNDP, UNECA, WFP, AfDB, Afreximbank, BADEA, BOAD and EBID to coordinated support and technical assistance ; "We commit to meet annually, under the Africa Prosperity Dialogues, to take stock of the progress of Africa's Prosperity Agenda" ; "We thank H.E. Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo and the government of the Republic of Ghana for spearheading the Africa Prosperity Dialogues."

acts.speaker: Award recipients of the Africa Prosperity Champions Awards
acts.speech: Registered their pleasure to Mr. Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko, the founder and executive chairman of the Africa Prosperity Network, for the honour done them, and pledged to continue in their various endeavours which led to the recognition and to continue to spearhead the transformation agenda of the African continent in their individual sectors of activity to achieve the prosperity of Africa and all her peoples.

acts.speaker: Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma, former Chairperson of the African Union Commission and Chairperson of the Africa Prosperity Network Advisory Council
acts.speech: Remarked in her welcoming address at the official opening ceremony of the Africa Prosperity Dialogue on Monday, January 30, 2025, that the "APD is like Africa's magnetic force, and the time for talk is over; now is the moment for decisive action."

acts.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
acts.speech: Said in his remarks at the 2025 Africa Prosperity Dialogue on February 1, 2025, at the Accra International Conference Centre: "Ghana is proud to be the host of this important dialogue series, and it will continue to enjoy my full support to make subsequent events even greater. This congress is a testament to our collective commitment to unlocking Africa's full potential and ensuring that our continent takes its rightful place in the global economic system."

title: Conseil des ministres : nominations à la Présidence et dans trois ministères

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué signed by Eugène Dossoumou, Secretary General of the Government)
acts.speech: Records that the Council of Ministers met in ordinary session on Wednesday 28 September 2011 and observed a minute of silence in memory of seven deceased persons, including Dah Djihossonou H. Michel Ahanhanzo-Glele, relatives of several members of the National Assembly, and Georges N. Timanty, former Ambassador of Benin to Havana.

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Announced the adoption of several draft decrees, notably on the creation, powers, composition and functioning of the ad hoc Committee to conduct the process of creating Benin's Court of Auditors; granting approval to “Elavagnon et Fils” Sarl under regime “A” of the investment code for a pipe factory at Bazounkpa; granting approval to the Société des Huileries du Bénin - Bohicon under regime “B” for the extension of its edible oil factory at Bohicon; and on the conditions for the 2011-2012 shea nut marketing campaign.

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Set the conditions of the 2011-2012 shea nut campaign - a floor producer price of 70 CFA francs per kilogramme, opening on 1 September 2011 and closing on 31 May 2012 - and highlighted the serious depredations of shea that risk penalising future production, namely the absence of a shea sector, the uncontrolled felling of trees and poor preservation of nuts causing excessive acidity ; instructed ministers to ensure strict compliance with the campaign conditions, to continue awareness-raising and training of women marketing and processing shea nuts on better storage, and to undertake a bold reform of the Directorate of Forests and Natural Resources to strengthen protection of shea and néré.

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Examined and approved several reports, including a joint report by the Ministers of the Interior and of Foreign Affairs on a ministerial delegation's working visit to Iran; a report by the Minister of Economy and Finance on the 2nd review of the economic and financial programme supported by the IMF; a report by the Minister of Nursery and Primary Education on the Ifadem financing agreement signed in Paris; a report by the Minister of Decentralisation on the Decnet 2011 forum in Bujumbura; a report by the Minister of Foreign Affairs on the Bamako workshop on ratification of the African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance; and a report by the Minister Delegate for the Maritime Economy on steps to finance consolidation works on investments financed at the Port of Cotonou by the Millennium Challenge Corporation.

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Examined and approved a communication from the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research on creating new faculties at Savè, Tchaourou and Natitingou for the 2011-2012 academic year, responding to the Government's concern to decongest the overcrowded Universities of Abomey-Calavi and Parakou.

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Authorised, among others, approval of a cooperation agreement with Complant International for bioethanol production from cassava at Savè; the working visit of Ibrahim Assane Mayaki, Director General of the Nepad Planning and Coordinating Agency, for Benin's National Agricultural Investment Programme; Benin's participation in the 13th meeting of States parties to the convention against torture in Geneva, in the 8th Science and Technology in Society forum in Kyoto and in the 62nd UNHCR executive session; the hosting in Cotonou of the 10th Annual General Assembly of the Association of African Road Maintenance Funds; the working visit to Benin of Daniel W. Yohannes, CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation, from 9 to 12 October 2011; and the 6th edition of the Civil Society Organisations Days in Cotonou.

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Pronounced appointments and returns to availability, including a Technical Adviser for Social Affairs at the Presidency of the Republic and directors at the Ministries of Justice, of Higher Education and Scientific Research, and of the Family, Social Affairs, National Solidarity, the Disabled and the Elderly.

title: Central Bank Loosens Credit Reins But Stops Short of Bold Overhaul

acts.speaker: Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank of Ethiopia (statement)
acts.speech: Ironically, the statement from the Monetary Policy Committee sounded as if it were reporting on two different economies: on the surface, headline inflation cooled to 13.6pc in August, down from 18.8pc a year earlier; food prices eased, helped by a decent harvest; buoyant coffee and gold exports replenished reserves; and Treasury-bill yields slipped to 15pc in August from 17.6pc in June. Beneath that veneer, non-food inflation was stuck at 15.1pc, the Birr's weakness feeds into rents, transport and every imported good, liquidity pressures are biting at banks, and the policy rate, currently at 15pc, offers no relief to borrowers. ; For now, the Monetary Policy Committee's message appears plain: it prioritises price stability, and growth is secondary.

acts.speaker: Bankers (unnamed)
acts.speech: Eyob's decision produced cautious optimism, and a fair bit of scepticism, among bankers who have watched the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) tighten and loosen the taps for years without ever daring a wholesale overhaul; the Governor's latest move, they suspect, is another exercise in fine-tuning rather than a bold leap.

acts.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (Central Bank data)
acts.speech: Central Bank data from the fourth quarter of 2023/24 show commercial banks' liquidity ratio - actual reserves plus net foreign assets relative to demand deposits - was 13.8pc in June 2024; reserves on hand or parked with the Central Bank totalled 263.1 billion Br, while foreign assets were a further 143.9 billion Br. System-wide deposits reached 2.5 trillion Br in June 2024, up 15.3pc on the year, while outstanding credit, including corporate bonds, rose 10.1pc to 2.1 trillion Br, leaving the aggregate LDR at 60.5pc. ; Broad money grew by 23.1pc year-on-year, while base money expanded by a startling 70.7pc.

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
acts.speech: Pegs global growth at three percent for 2025.

source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
title: FEMAFOOT : Démarrage du championnat national le 23 novembre prochain - amap

acts.speaker: Sports source (anonymous), cited by AMAP
acts.speech: AMAP learned from a sports source that the Malian Football Federation (Femafoot), after a series of postponements, has set the start of the national football championship for 23 November for the 2024-2025 season.

title: Siguiri : des élèves dans la rue après des heurts près de leur école

acts.speaker: Official of the Ousmane Doussou Camara school complex (unnamed)
acts.speech: Explains: “it was the security forces who came and attacked a petrol station located near the school. Then they turned against the pupils. The situation is really tense.”

acts.speaker: Parents of pupils
acts.speech: Many parents say they have still not found their children at the time the dispatch was put online.

title: Reclaiming reality: Africa’s fight to correct its shrinking map

acts.speaker: African Union (AU)
acts.speech: Has formally endorsed the "Correct The Map" campaign, which calls for the replacement of the Mercator map with the Equal Earth projection. According to the AU, Africa's true size is 30.37 million square kilometres (11.73 million square miles) and is big enough to fit Europe, China and the United States combined, with space left over. The AU has pledged to advocate for wider adoption of Equal Earth and discuss collective action with its 55 member states.

acts.speaker: Selma Malika Haddadi, AU Commission Deputy Chairperson
acts.speech: "It might seem to be just a map, but in reality, it is not." ; She argued that when Africa is misrepresented in size, the world's perception of the continent is also distorted – in media, education and policy.

acts.speaker: Campaigners ("Correct the Map" campaign)
acts.speech: Argue that this visual misrepresentation reinforces colonial-era narratives that portray Africa as marginal, underdeveloped and peripheral to global affairs.

acts.speaker: Carlos Lopes, professor at the University of Cape Town and proponent of the "Correct the Map" campaign
acts.speech: "Maps shape how we see ourselves and how others see us." ; "If Africa appears smaller than it is, so does its weight in the imagination of citizens and decision-makers. Correcting the map is not vanity – it is reclaiming reality."

acts.speaker: Fara Ndiaye, Speak Up Africa co-founder
acts.speech: Noted the psychological impact of distorted maps on African children. "They grow up thinking Africa is modest in size when, in reality, it's gigantic—larger than the US, China, India, Japan and much of Europe combined. Perception translates into confidence and confidence into action."

acts.speaker: Fara Ndiaye, Speak Up Africa co-founder
