acts.speech: Emphasized that while leaders are looking for external investment, much should be based on practical and valuable investment, and that Africa needs to improve its economy and look towards attaining economic sovereignty.

acts.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
acts.speech: On food security and food sovereignty, said "While the principle of African Solutions to African Problems is widely raised in the scope of conflict, it is imperative that we begin to extend this principle to a wide range of peace and security issues. Our continent is not only well able to feed itself, but can become a bread basket of the world. With 65% of the world's remaining uncultivated arable land in our backyards, we need to critically assess why one third of the hungry people in the world are in our continent." ; called upon the African Union and development partners to offer investment support in unleashing this potential ; "Sadly, the principle of African Solutions to African Problems is not a silver bullet to address all challenges, because not all our problems are the products of our own making."

acts.speaker: 2023 Dakar Declaration on Food Sovereignty and Resilience
acts.speech: Acknowledged the continental awakening that 'it is time for Africa to feed itself and fully unlock its agriculture potential to feed the world'.

acts.speaker: Macky Sall, Senegalese President and Former AU Chairperson; Moussa Faki Mahamat, African Union Commission executive leader; and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed
acts.speech: Have strongly been advocating Africa's inclusion on foreign bodies, lending their voices yet again for Africa to be represented on the UN Security Council with at least one permanent seat and double non-permanent seats, and for proportionate representation at the G7, the G20 and similar international institutions.

title: Opinion - Deliberately targeting UN missions, civilians are war crimes

acts.speaker: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
acts.speech: Under the Rome Statute, "intentional attacks against personnel, installations, material, units or vehicles involved in a humanitarian assistance or peacekeeping mission in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations" that are entitled to civilian protections are war crimes in both international and non-international armed conflicts ; Article 87(7) provides: "Where a state party fails to comply with a request to cooperate by the court contrary to the provisions of the statute, thereby preventing the court from exercising its functions and power under the statute, the court may make a finding to that effect and refer the matter to the assembly of state parties or, where the Security Council referred the matter to the court, to the Security Council."

acts.speaker: Law of treaties
acts.speech: The law of treaties obliges these states to refrain from "acts which would defeat the object and purpose of the treaty until they declare they do not intend to become a party to the treaty."

acts.speaker: Satellite imagery analysis (5 October 2024)
acts.speech: On 5 October 2024, satellite imagery analysis found that new Israeli military activity was visible near UNIFIL position 6-52 where at least 30 military vehicles of the Israeli Defence Force (IDF) were present near the UNIFIL position.

acts.speaker: United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL)
acts.speech: On 6 October, UNIFIL publicly raised concerns regarding Israel's military activities immediately adjacent to its mission's position southeast of Maroun el-Ras in Lebanon.

acts.speaker: Israeli military
acts.speech: Made a request to UNIFIL to relocate more than five kilometres from the Israel-Lebanon border "as soon as possible, in order to maintain their safety".

acts.speaker: UN peacekeeping chief
acts.speech: Totally refused the Israeli military request that UNIFIL relocate more than five kilometres from the Israel-Lebanon border.

acts.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
acts.speech: As of 11 October 2024, the CPJ preliminary investigation showed that at least 128 journalists and media workers were killed in the West Bank, Gaza, Israel and Lebanon since the war began.

acts.speaker: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
acts.speech: On 19 July 2024, the ICJ found that: "It is plausible that Israel's actions amount to genocide, and Israel's occupation and annexation of Palestinian territories are unlawful, and its discriminatory laws and policies against Palestinians violate the prohibition and racial segregation and apartheid."

title: Gvt holds consultations with the country’s diplomats to redefine foreign policy - Lesotho Times

acts.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Principal Information Officer of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Told the Lesotho Times that former ambassadors had been invited to participate in the workshop "to share their expertise, experiences, and ideas with the current envoys" ; "They have been on this journey and know better, so they can provide guidance on how to successfully execute their roles."

acts.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Principal Information Officer of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: When quizzed on the rumours of reshuffling of the ambassadors after the workshop, said that had not been the primary reason for the consultations; however, he acknowledged that "reshuffling can happen at any time".

acts.speaker: King Letsie III of Lesotho (Speech from the Throne, November 2022)
acts.speech: Placed emphasis on the importance of Lesotho "deploying diplomatic professionals who can secure lucrative benefits for the country when they are deployed to foreign missions."

acts.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Emphasized the importance of this initiative during his opening remarks: "Under the new leadership (of Prime Minister Sam Matekane's coalition administration), we have not had sufficient time to consult on the new vision that the government has for Lesotho" ; said the workshop was meant to "equip diplomatic representatives with the knowledge and strategies necessary to promote international trade, enhance tourism, and improve productivity in the energy sector, among other priorities."

acts.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Noted the urgency of addressing the country's high unemployment rates and the interconnected issues of crime and corruption that stemmed from low productivity levels: "One of our key goals is to increase productivity, particularly in agriculture, with the support of our diplomatic missions and international partners" ; further underscored the need for skills exportation as one of the ways to address the high unemployment in Lesotho.

acts.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Highlighting Lesotho's abundant natural resources, said the country's potential to produce and export electricity to meet the growing demands in the Southern African region was one of its low hanging fruits to be plucked to improve prosperity levels for citizens.

acts.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Reiterated a significant policy shift aimed at boosting tourism by offering visa-free entry to European Union citizens: "This decision is expected to foster unparalleled growth in tourism and international relations."

acts.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Expressed the need to revise Lesotho's foreign policy "in light of evolving geopolitical realities": "We must work together with you, our diplomatic missions, to navigate this changing landscape," he urged, revealing plans to establish the Lesotho Institute of Diplomacy, which he said aims to fortify the diplomatic profession and better address the challenges it faces.

acts.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
acts.speech: Addressed the impact of external factors on Lesotho's economy, particularly recent developments regarding U.S. aid, and stressed the necessity for a strategic government vision to build Lesotho's economic resilience: "The current environment necessitates a transformative approach to promote trade, investment, and tourism, which hold the keys to our economic diplomacy."

title: AfDB approves $46m to transform Healthcare in Nigeria's Sokoto State

acts.speaker: Abdul Kamara, Director General of the African Development Bank's Nigeria Office
acts.speech: "This investment illustrates our commitment to continue working with the Government to fill critical infrastructure gaps in Nigeria's health system while building resilient, climate-adapted healthcare facilities." ; "By strengthening healthcare infrastructure in Sokoto State, we are building hope and creating pathways to better health outcomes for millions of Nigerians."

acts.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the African Development Bank Group (AfDB)
acts.speech: According to it, the African Development Bank Group remains committed to enhancing the quality of life for Africa's people through targeted investments in resilient health infrastructure that drive inclusive growth and sustainable development across the continent.

title: Out of 14K Customers, Less than 5K Pay Bills

acts.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
acts.speech: Explained on OK FM’s afternoon show that if people paid for the service, much work would be done and more people would have access to water compared to the low percentage currently recorded by the company: “We have begun a massive disconnection exercise. We started off today (Monday February 11, 2024) around the Duport area and that will continue until we can collect more than 50 percent of our debt. Just for this year, from January to October, there is uncollected debt of nearly one million United States Dollars. We have 14,000 customers but less than 5,000 of this number pay bills” ; noted that the failure on the part of the majority of the customers to pay bills continues to deny the company sufficient funds to underwrite costs for maintenance, extension of service to communities yet to have access, as well as providing security and other services.

acts.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
acts.speech: “We do not have the money to pay for the extension of the main pipe into the communities. We understand that access to water is a fundamental human right but in order to continue having it, it is good that people pay. Water bills are not that high. An average home uses less than 5,000 gallons per month and it costs around US$10. A single individual using water pays US$5 or even less than, depending on the usage” ; “There are some communities that are just using water without paying and when there is no water supply they can be the loudest in criticizing” ; admonished all interested in having and using water to visit the company’s website, download a form, register and proceed to its office for connection after paying about US$200, and appealed to all to pay for water and connect legally.

acts.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
acts.speech: Noted that the construction of a dosing unit to effectuate the application of chlorine into the water for its purification has been completed, and said powder chlorine is being used instead of liquid chlorine due to the many security conditions associated with its importation: “The chlorine dosing unit will transform the powder into a liquid form and it will be used into the clear water wells. The dozing chlorine unit will determine the exact quantity of chlorine that is required to disinfect any given quantity of water, even millions of gallons.”

acts.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
acts.speech: “The second development is that we now have a booster station at Caldwell Junction. It got burned in 2021. The water is pumped from the treatment plant in Caldwell and before it reaches Duala, the pressure drops. If functioning, it helps to pump water all the way to St. Paul Bridge and also towards town” ; explained that since the booster got burned, residents in Duala and central Monrovia have not been receiving water but the problem has been resolved and the dedication of the facility will take place before this month; “We have just completed that and are now installing the electrical facilities.” He put the cost for the booster construction at US$136,000 while the chlorine unit costs US$82,000.

acts.speaker: Mohammed Ali, Managing Director of Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
acts.speech: “We just signed a contract for the construction of a water supply system in Bopolu City. It is the same thing we have in Kakata and Robertsport. We will run pipes to government offices and hospitals and some other buildings. When people want water they can pay for connection to their homes. That is expected to be completed in February” ; named Greenville in Sinoe, Pleebo in Maryland and subsequently Zwedru in Grand Gedeh County as cities that will benefit from the first plan which is expected to run up to 2026; disclosed that the sum of US$60,000 has been secured through the Ministry of Finance to conduct a feasibility study in the counties.

title: Apprentissage des opérations de vote, la centralisation et la transmission des résultats au cœur d’une formation des membres des Cepi et Ceci

acts.speaker: Prosper Ntahorwamiye, President of Burundi's Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI)
acts.speech: Said that CENI judged it appropriate to combine the CEPI and the CECI so that the members of these commissions would receive the same content at the same time and under the same conditions, and that these members would in turn train the polling-station members to be recruited shortly for the operationalisation of the electoral process; he indicated that overall, preparations for the 2025 elections are going well and are advancing properly. ; Stressed that to assign voters to polling stations, CENI has taken the figure of 500 voters as the reference figure for each polling station, with a special derogation for people who vote in places where they did not register, for example journalists, security agents accompanying the authorities, and observers; he added that in such cases the list must not exceed 25 voters at each polling station. ; Advised the members of these commissions to prepare well because the elections are very close; urged them to avoid favouritism in recruiting polling-station members, saying they must recruit those who are capable instead of considering existing affinities; and reminded them that well-prepared elections are the source of lasting peace, which is why they must work in the interest of the nation.

title: Nigerian Senate Summons NSA Ribadu, DSS Boss Over Alleged Boko Haram Funding

acts.speaker: Scott Perry, U.S. Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
acts.speech: Alleged during a congressional hearing that USAID had indirectly financed terrorist activities across the world, including in Nigeria ; accused USAID of inadvertently supporting extremist groups through its annual budget of $697 million ; cited concerns over cash flows to Islamic schools (madrasas), which he claimed had facilitated terrorist training.

acts.speaker: Gen Christopher Musa, Nigeria's Chief of Defence Staff
acts.speech: Had raised concerns about terrorist groups in the country receiving funding and training from international organisations.

acts.speaker: Senator Ali Ndume
acts.speech: Raised a motion calling for an urgent investigation into the claims, after which Nigerian lawmakers on Wednesday issued summons.

title: Mozambique: Meet the Sustainable Livelihood Development Program for Communities in the Gorongosa National Park Sustainable Development Zone

acts.speaker: Elsbeth Akkerman, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands
acts.speech: present at the event stated that “the Dutch Government’s development strategy is based on the following pillars: Sustainable Development, Gender Equality, Youth Support, Food Security, Water and Climate and all of them are clearly aligned with the development strategy of the Government of Mozambique”.

acts.speaker: Mike Marchington, Director of Finance & Planning, Gorongosa Restoration Project (GRP)
acts.speech: On behalf of the GRP, Mike Marchington stated that “the Program we launched today is yet another affirmation of our commitment to combine conservation and community development. Biodiversity protection, to be successful, must be an inclusive process, with the participation of all, where community participation must result in tangible benefits for them, making communities the greatest guardians of the ecosystem. Finally, we want to state that, as a team, we are committed to the objectives of this program and to the rational use of the resources allocated to the SLDP by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands”.

acts.speaker: Stella da Graça Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for the Province of Sofala
acts.speech: At the end of the ceremony, the Secretary of State for the Province of Sofala affirmed the Government’s commitment to the success of the Program, recognizing that the Program is part of the Government’s Plan and the Sustainable Development Objectives of the United Nations that the Government of Mozambique has ratified.

title: Chief Matipa tells investors to prioritise locals

acts.speaker: Chief Matipa of the Bisa people, traditional leader
acts.speech: Said it was important for investors to employ local people and to help develop his chiefdom; said he could not allow investors to bring in expatriates when the locals were able to do the work ; "I want my people to benefit from the investment being brought in the chiefdom. I want to see my people's welfare change" ; said he was open to work with investors that would enhance economic activities in his chiefdom and that he wants to see to it that the welfare of the people in the area improves.

acts.speaker: Wang Haipeng, vice president of the China Asia Economic Development Association
acts.speech: Said the cassava processing plant will have the capacity to process 100,000 metric tonnes of cassava for export.

title: Moçambique e China reforçam cooperação

acts.speaker: Mozambique and China (joint expression at an audience in Maputo)
acts.speech: Expressed their interest in strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two countries, particularly in the industry and trade sectors, and congratulated themselves on the excellent Sino-Mozambican relations, with a visible impact on the continued strengthening of political, economic and social exchange.

acts.speaker: Maria Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
acts.speech: Praised the growth of political-diplomatic cooperation embodied in the exchange of visits at different levels, especially presidential ones ; "We are going to continue working, as we were already saying, but just to say that this year we are celebrating 50 years of Mozambique's independence" ; "We will have a celebration here in Maputo, but in China there will also be a big celebration" ; mentioned that President Chapo is already preparing the visit for 2026, adding "So, there is much celebration, and that is why your coming here, your arrival here, is very welcome by the government, by the party, but also by the Mozambican people."

acts.speaker: Maria Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation
acts.speech: Acknowledged the continued support China has given Mozambique in various sectors, with emphasis on humanitarian assistance, food security and infrastructure, and thanked China for the support provided for the realisation of the President's First 100 Days Plan ; "His Excellency the President, Daniel Chapo, asked me to convey the welcome to Mozambique to our special envoy and also to inform him that he is visiting Gaza province, and also to inform him that his 100-day plan was successful because of the support that China gave" ; "Besides the support that China gave, in relation to financial support for various areas with humanitarian aid, we also laid the foundation stone for the construction of the Surgical Centre of Mozambique, which will be the largest in Mozambique."

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique (message conveyed by Maria Lucas)
acts.speech: Asked the minister to convey a welcome to Mozambique to the Chinese special envoy and to inform him that the President is visiting Gaza province and that his 100-day plan was successful because of the support China gave.

title: Après sa démission de l’Umpp

acts.speaker: Yacoubou Malêhossou, Beninese deputy (Honourable)
acts.speech: Refused to follow Kindjanhoundé in his defection, finding the enterprise unhealthy, stating on a local radio station that he is a religious preacher and that, as such, he cannot betray.

title: Djibouti salue la décision de la CIJ contre Israël

acts.speaker: Republic of Djibouti / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI communiqué)
acts.speech: Welcomes the historic decision handed down by the International Court of Justice in the case brought by South Africa against Israel ; states that the decision, although it does not immediately impose a ceasefire under the provisional measures, "constitutes a decisive victory for humanity, for the international rule of law and for non-impunity" and a significant turning point in the quest for justice for the Palestinian people ; stresses the imperative of implementing fully and immediately the measures set out in the ruling, calls on the international community to assume its responsibilities to achieve a complete and comprehensive halt to Israeli aggression, and insists on the need to ensure immediate and sustained humanitarian aid in the Gaza Strip.

acts.speaker: Republic of Djibouti / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI communiqué)
acts.speech: Expresses its profound gratitude to the Republic of South Africa for its honourable stance in favour of human rights and justice, and for having decided to bring this case before the International Court of Justice.

title: Coopérative des entreprises de transformation d'ananas du Bénin: Muhammadou Alidou prend les rênes pour une nouvelle ère de croissance

acts.speaker: Albertine Houessou, local coordinator of the CBI project
acts.speech: Presented the results of the evaluation of Cetrab's strategic plan (2022–2024), conducted by Resilience Consultancy in collaboration with CBI and Economic Sense; the evaluation highlighted the progress made while identifying persistent structural challenges, notably the cooperative's financial autonomy.

acts.speaker: Cyrille Adjahouinou, outgoing president of Cetrab
acts.speech: Presenting his end-of-term report, recalled the path travelled over the past six years to structure the processed pineapple sector. He praised the collective efforts and the support of technical and financial partners, notably Defia-Enable (today Parsad), Pfd/Pinex and Atda Pôle 7, as well as the new collaboration with the Centre for the Promotion of Imports (CBI) of the Dutch government through its gender-transformative project in the dried pineapple sector in Benin.

acts.speaker: Muhammadou Awêlou Alidou, incoming president of Cetrab
acts.speech: Presented his roadmap, centred on resource mobilisation, the professionalisation of member enterprises and strengthening the visibility of the body, which is still too little known nationally and internationally: “We will go looking for partners to support member enterprises, especially the smallest ones, so that they can meet the quality standards required by the markets,” he declared ; Cetrab, according to him, aims in the coming years to become a strong umbrella organisation, representative of all the country's pineapple processors, capable of exporting high-quality products to regional and international markets.

title: Choguel Maïga : Les raisons d’une posture téméraire - Mali 24

acts.speaker: Choguel Maïga, Malian Prime Minister and chairman of the strategic committee of the M5-RFP
acts.speech: In a thunderous outburst on Saturday 16 November, at the rally commemorating the recapture of the capital of the Ifoghas from the CMA, did not mince his words, castigating his employers without restraint.

acts.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
acts.speech: According to our sources, his departure, announced and postponed many times, is this time well and truly settled; from the same sources, the head of state had even informed him of it the day after his elevation to the dignity of Grand Officer of the National Order of Mali, a distinction which, our source adds, was only a way for the head of state to pay tribute to him for the three years spent at the head of the Government; he is protected, according to our sources, by one of the Generals.

acts.speaker: Associates of Choguel Maïga
acts.speech: maintain that, just like the military, he has not been unworthy and played a leading role in the coming of the Transition, and that it is therefore unacceptable that he should step aside in favour of eleventh-hour performers.

title: Aterian lance des opérations commerciales élargies au Rwanda avec sa première livraison de coltan

acts.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
acts.speech: Announced the launch of expanded commercial operations in Rwanda, marked by the transfer of the first delivery of responsibly sourced tantalum/niobium concentrate, also known as coltan, to its global trading partner.

acts.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
acts.speech: Said that its partnership with a major international metals and minerals trading company provided it with a well-established global trading and marketing platform, and that the agreement allowed Aterian to access a network of downstream buyers and accelerate the development of its activities.

acts.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
acts.speech: Explained on 15 September that, before commercial sales began, its partner had carried out extensive due diligence and testing to check product quality and compliance with a group of artisanal and small-scale mining suppliers in Rwanda that comply with OECD standards; following the success of this process, Eastinco, Aterian's wholly owned Rwandan subsidiary, activated its responsibly sourced tantalum and niobium supply chain and began trading.

acts.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
acts.speech: Confirmed that a $250,000 mezzanine loan obtained to support its expansion had already been fully drawn and invested in trading operations, notably the acquisition of mineral concentrates from Rwanda.

acts.speaker: Simon Rollason, CEO of Aterian
acts.speech: "The successful completion of testing and supplier compliance checks, combined with the injection of new trading capital, now allows us to move forward at a sustained pace. We anticipate a significant increase in trading volumes over the coming weeks, thanks to the activation of multiple supply relationships and the strengthening of sourcing operations with our financial partners." ; "This is a pivotal moment for our trading business, which lays the commercial foundations for our growth in the region." ; "With our operations, our risk management systems and our partnerships now in place, we are confident in our ability to demonstrate full traceability compliance while building a robust supply chain with integrity, capable of supporting substantial volume growth and sustaining long-term revenue generation for the group."

acts.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
acts.speech: Said that all of its mineral supplies came from the International Tin Supply Chain Initiative and were fully compliant with OECD due diligence guidelines, involving rigorous on-site audits, verification of mine of origin and conflict-free checks to guarantee the legitimacy and integrity of the supply chain; it also stressed that every supplier underwent a detailed onboarding and audit process covering operational, legal and ethical standards, and said these checks would continue and were essential to maintaining a regular supply of materials.

acts.speaker: Aterian (London-listed company)
acts.speech: According to the company, the partnership with its trading house validated its business model and opened a clear commercial path to establishing a vertically integrated exploration and trading platform for critical minerals across East Africa; Aterian confirmed that container-scale export sales were now ready to begin.

title: Court Fixes May 20 To Hear Contempt Case Against MDS Of GHL, Century Energy, Others

acts.speaker: Federal High Court, Port Harcourt (court record)
acts.speech: Has fixed May 20, 2025, for the hearing of contempt proceedings filed against the Managing Directors of General Hydrocarbons and Century Energy Limited and others, over alleged disobedience to the orders of the court.

acts.speaker: Justice A.T. Mohamed, Federal High Court (court order of December 18, 2024)
acts.speech: Ordered the arrest and detention of 150,000 barrels of Crude oil which belongs to GHL on board an oil tanker, M.T. Tamara Tokoni, as security for the plaintiff's claim: "an order is hereby made directing the admiralty marshal with the assistance of the Nigerian Navy, and the Harbour Master of Nigerian Ports Authority to arrest and detain the Cargo of 150,000 barrels of Crude Oil herein sued as 1st defendant respondent and currently onboard MT. Tamara Tokoni IMO: NO 8302131 ... be arrested and remain under arrest pending further orders or further directions of this Honourable Court." ; "An Order is hereby made directing that the Cargo of 150,000 Barrels of Crude Oil ... be released from arrest only upon payment of all sums claimed in the writ of summons into Court or pending the provision of an acceptable Bank Guarantee, to the Deputy Chief Registrar of this Honourable Court, in the sum of: A total sum of USD$1,647,975 ... being unpaid Hire due to the plaintiff from the 2nd defendant for the Hire of the plaintiffs Ships: MV DONNY & MV OCEAN MERIT ... The sum of USD$60,000.00 ... Cost of redelivery of vessel ... The sum of USD$50,000 ... on the footing of General damages, to be issued by First Bank of Nigeria Plc, Zenith Bank Plc, United Bank for Africa Plc or any other First-Class Nigerian Bank acceptable to the Applicant."

acts.speaker: Godpower Anuba, Plaintiff's Operations Supervisor (affidavit of facts and urgency)
acts.speech: "that I know as a fact that, on the 18/12/2024, sequel to the originating processes filed in this suit together with a motion Exparte for the arrest and detention of the 1st defendant, this court directed the admiralty marshal with the assistance of the Nigeria Navy, and the Harbour Master of the Nigeria Ports authority to arrest and detain the 1st defendant pending the provision of an acceptable bank guarantee to secure plaintiff's claim as writ of summons"

title: Lesotho farmers left stranded as US ends poultry project

acts.speaker: Rural Self-Help Development Association
acts.speech: said the termination of the aid jeopardised Lesotho's food security and economic prospects.

acts.speaker: Estimates (unattributed trade figures)
acts.speech: say the country imported more than 80 percent of its chickens and eggs.

title: Initiative for compliance with Int. Humanitarian Law

acts.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
acts.speech: According to the ICRC, International Humanitarian Law “protects persons who are no longer participating in hostilities and restricts the means and methods of warfare.”

acts.speaker: ‘Mabataung Khalane, Principal Secretary, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Office (opening remarks)
acts.speech: Emphasized Lesotho’s dedication to IHL, stating: “The Government of Lesotho understands that IHL applies only in armed conflict, offering two systems of protection – one for international conflicts and another for non-international conflicts. It strikes a balance between humanity and military necessity.” ; highlighted key IHL principles that focus on distinction, protection and compliance, saying parties in conflict must differentiate between civilians and combatants and that Lesotho recognizes the binding nature of these IHL instruments and customary law ; said the project underscores Lesotho’s commitment to strengthening legal frameworks for conflict mitigation, enhancing humanitarian diplomacy through cross-sector collaboration and promoting accountability in warfare to protect vulnerable populations ; described customary law as formed when “state practice is sufficiently dense – widespread, representative, frequent and uniform – and accompanied by a belief among states that they are legally bound to act – or prohibited from acting – in certain ways.”

acts.speaker: Sarah Mabeza, Regional Legal Advisor of the Pretoria Delegation of the ICRC
acts.speech: Stated that ICRC is a neutral, impartial and independent entity that is able to reach those in need when others cannot, and said this is done through providing humanitarian assistance, protecting lives, upholding rights and relieving the suffering of people around the world whose lives have been torn apart by armed conflict and violence ; pointed out that the ICRC is operational in 90 countries across the globe, that over 90 percent of donations received go directly to the field, and that ICRC is the oldest organisation in the world with a lifespan of 160 years ; “Humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity and universality: these are fundamental principles that guide and define not only our work, but also the work of National Red Cross Societies worldwide, including the LRCS.” ; stressed that the ICRC operates in accordance with the principles of IHL based on the Geneva Conventions of 1949, their Additional Protocols, the Statutes of the international Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and the resolutions of the international Conferences of the Red Cross and Red Crescent ; “We take action to assist the victims of armed conflict and other violence, and at the same time promote respect for the IHL and implementation in domestic law.”

title: Dr EFFI YAMIEN

acts.speaker: The widow, children, grandchildren and allied families of Dr Effi Yamien (death/thanksgiving notice)
acts.speech: Deeply touched by the many marks of compassion and support shown at the time of the death of their beloved brother, brother-in-law, uncle, friend, colleague, father, father-in-law, grandfather and husband, Dr Effi Yamien, and unable to reach each of you individually, express their profound gratitude and their most sincere thanks to Minister Kandia Camara, Adama Coulibaly, Ida Camara, and Senator Boby Assa Eminiene, with particular thanks to the various Pastors, to the king of Moronou, to the traditional and cantonal chiefs and to the order of pharmacists of Côte d'Ivoire. "A year already, wow! How time flies... Your smile, your calm and your voice, although engraved in us, are terribly missed!"

title: Elevados custos de eletricidade e de água têm condicionado competitividade da economia

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: "The joint importation by the two operators that act in the fuel sector has not structurally changed this situation, so the cost of electricity continues to be one of the highest in the world and the ship and aircraft supply sector (bunkering) is less competitive than the Canary Islands and Dakar, notwithstanding that Cabo Verde's geostrategic situation is better than that of its competitors."

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: Has no doubt that the long-term evolution of the cost of energy is also a great threat to Cabo Verde's future competitiveness: "With the annual increase in energy demand of around 7-8%, combined with the increase in fossil fuel prices, above 10%, the cost of fuel imports has seen galloping increases, of about more than 12 times" ; stresses that if energy demand and fossil fuel prices continue at the same level this decade, import expenditure could increase around 20 times more, strongly pressuring Cabo Verde's balance of payments and the competitiveness of the national economy.

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: "In this sense the initiatives of successive governments to work towards increasing the penetration rate of renewable energies by 50%, and studies towards an option using 100% Renewable Energy by 2050, as well as the identification of energy efficiency measures, seem very well judged."

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: Observes that water and energy costs represent on average around 40 to 45% of production costs in Cabo Verde, with water for agriculture at around 19 to 22% and energy for catering, services and manufacturing at around 25 to 30% ; reiterates that irregularity of access, high costs and precarious availability of these two essential goods impact the whole economy, blocking production and distribution and affecting the competitiveness of products and services as well as the attractiveness of the economy as a whole.

acts.speaker: Continuous Multi-Objective Survey (IMC-2024)
acts.speech: 43.9% of households in Cabo Verde had access to insufficient quantities of water to satisfy their needs in 2024; the same source indicates that 52.3% of the rural population felt the need for water, a larger proportion than in urban areas.

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: "The water problem constitutes one of Cabo Verde's greatest challenges. About 80% of the water for domestic consumption in Cabo Verde is desalinated and with a high cost of energy, with a direct implication for the water tariff, considered one of the highest in Africa."

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: Stresses that the country has made significant progress in promoting access to drinking water, having reached the Millennium Development Goals on that matter in 2007, ahead of the 2015 target: "And we are on a good pace as regards the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals 2030, in this case SDG 6 - Clean water and sanitation... and SDG 7 - Affordable and Clean Energy" ; but says those advances mask the challenging reality of the water sector, concealing disparities between rural and urban areas: "The reality is that per capita water consumption in Cabo Verde is still below the minimums globally recommended by the WHO. It is estimated that around 30% of the country's population still does not have access to the public water supply network. On the other hand, the population that obtains supply outside the network pays a price far higher than the average price charged on the network."

acts.speaker: Jose Agnelo Sanches, economist and consultant
acts.speech: Admits that everything has already been identified and turned into specific programmes, such as the National Strategic Plan for Water and Sanitation (PLENAS) of 2015 and 2025, the Master Plan for the Electricity Sector, and the project "Access to Sustainable Energy for the Management of Water Resources: Energy-Water Nexus", but concludes that there remains the "enormous challenge" of timely delivery, implying an acceleration in planned investments and policy measures.

title: Bank Of Afrique dans l’espace UEMOA : Un résultat net de 92,9 milliards de FCFA en 2022

acts.speaker: Abderrazzak Zebdani, Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
acts.speech: Presented the 2022 financial results of the Group's six listed UEMOA subsidiaries at an online press conference on Wednesday, April 12, 2023, showing a total balance sheet of 4,540 billion CFA francs and a net profit of 92.9 billion CFA francs ; "With the exception of BOA-Ghana, the results of all our subsidiaries are beyond our targets," he said with satisfaction.

acts.speaker: Abderrazzak Zebdani, Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
acts.speech: Stressed that these results are the outcome of the group's strategic vision, broken down into three strategic pillars: digital transformation; balance-sheet transformation, which has translated into colossal investments in networks and staff training and a reorientation of the portfolio towards individuals and SMEs, with more than half of outstanding loans now coming from individuals; and trade finance. He indicated that for SMEs the Group has developed a package of specific services made up of advisory support, technical assistance and training in cash and stock management and in mastering import/export processes ; "We cannot be a Group with a significant and varied presence and not be a major player in international trade."

acts.speaker: Abderrazzak Zebdani, Deputy Managing Director of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group
acts.speech: Responding to journalists on the question of the BCEAO's call to commercial banks for prudence in the distribution of dividends, said that beyond this directive from the regulator, the sharing of dividends at BOA obeys three fundamental principles: ensuring its growth from its own funds independently of shareholders, complying with the various regulatory ratios, and maintaining a harmonious level of dividend distribution.

acts.speaker: BCEAO (Central Bank of West African States)
acts.speech: Invited commercial banks to exercise prudence in the distribution of dividends.

title: Free carry shareholding in the spotlight

acts.speaker: Fraser Institute
acts.speech: Said it contributed to Namibia's score in its annual Policy Perception Index for 2023 decreasing 20 points from 87.22 in 2019 to 68, dropping Namibia from position 14 out of 76 jurisdictions, down to 33 out of 86.

acts.speaker: Isabella Chirchir, mining commissioner, and Erasmus Shivolo, deputy mining commissioner
acts.speech: According to them, the suggestion is still in development, and discussions with the ministry of finance are ongoing.

acts.speaker: Erasmus Shivolo, deputy mining commissioner
acts.speech: Made reference to Epangelo, the government's mining enterprise, which enjoys preference for strategic mineral licences and holds 10% of the massive Husab uranium mine, and 7.5% of Navachab gold mine, among others.

acts.speaker: Veston Malango, Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
acts.speech: Said the policy proposal is on the table, and the chamber has been engaging the minister and the mining ministry since it was introduced. Further clarity is needed, he said, adding that the chamber is working on models to present to government, which will detail the consequences of a free carry policy for mines. "We have highlighted that free carry is an additional cost. The final decision should be informed by well-researched models. The objective is obviously more benefits from the mineral resource coming to government. The question comes in: Will you have more with that scenario than what you are getting right now?"

acts.speaker: Veston Malango, Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
acts.speech: Recently told parliament that in the last five years, the industry paid close to N$9.7 billion in royalties to government, export levies worth N$1.32 billion, dividends of N$3.4 billion and corporate tax of N$11.44 billion, all amounting to N$25.84 billion in government income.

acts.speaker: Veston Malango, Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
acts.speech: "Our minister has proposed to us, and we have accepted, that these discussions must firstly be at a technical level, between the executive director of the ministry of finance, the executive director of ministry of mines and ourselves, and that is where we are," he said. ; "Hats off to our government that they don't just come and decree, but it is a proposal that has been put on the table, and now it is subject for engagement," he said.

title: LPM expresses dissatisfaction with Namibia’s decentralisation progress

acts.speaker: Landless People’s Movement (LPM)
acts.speech: Is dissatisfied with the level and progression of decentralisation in Namibia; the party claims that the Ministry of Urban and Rural Development, which is responsible for the decentralisation function, is delaying the transfer of power to local authorities and regional councils.

acts.speaker: Ivan Skrywer, LPM Councillor
acts.speech: Said the government must empower local authorities to drive development and build lasting resilience against the challenges facing citizens; noted that while there has been a lot of talk in public forums, there hasn’t been much action on the ground.

acts.speaker: Ivan Skrywer, LPM Councillor
acts.speech: Expressed dissatisfaction with the proposed amendments to the Regional Councils Act, which govern the appointment of Chief Regional Officers. “He stated that appointments now require prior written approval from the minister based on recommendations from the PSC, as the president may resolve disputes. Now, all of a sudden, consultation with the minister is replaced with prior written approval, totally taking away the power of elected officials. Who, by the way, are paying these officials?” ; “You can’t appoint somebody that you’re not paying; that is the order of the day, and it should be the order of the day, and that is not the case with the current proposed amendments.”

acts.speaker: Evelyn Nawases-Taeyele, Deputy Minister (of Urban and Rural Development)
acts.speech: Stated in her speech during the Decentralisation Day that the government worked towards empowering Regional Councils and Local Authorities through legislative reforms and reviews, capacity building and fiscal resources, but said there is still a need to enhance the capacity of local institutions to manage resources effectively and transparently.

title: 300 die of tuberculosis in Ogun

acts.speaker: Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN)
acts.speech: Disclosed that 300 patients died of tuberculosis out of over 6,000 cases recorded in Ogun State in 2023.

acts.speaker: Florinda Olawusi, Senior Programme Officer, Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN)
acts.speech: Expressed concern over a 100% rise from 2019, adding that 3,000 cases were recorded in 2019, and noted that 95% of patients were already placed on treatment: "Since the inception of TB long 3 project in Ogun state which started in 2019, Ogun state was diagnosing a little over 3,000 cases annually but presently from 2019 till now for example last year in 12 month they were able to diagnose over 6,000 cases which is a huge increment. Its over a 100% increase in the number of cases diagnosed." ; "The treatment lasts for six months. So, what that means is that after six months once the duration of the treatment is complete the patient leaves the program. As at last year, we were able to identify 6,000 cases and 95% of them were placed on treatment." ; responding to questions on the number of deaths: "Yes, there have been some TB related death in the past year, a little over 300 patients died from TB related causes last year in Ogun state."

acts.speaker: Data from the IHVN and USAID TB-LON 3 project for Ogun State
acts.speech: According to the data, 3,000 cases were recorded in 2019.

acts.speaker: Olusola Taiwo, State Programme Manager for TB and Leprosy Control
acts.speech: "One of the predisposing factors for TB infection is staying in over crowded environment, so people should stay where there is good ventilation, indiscriminate pit, they should try put on their coughing etiquette to prevent the spreading of TB germs."

title: Beyond the triumphalism of Trumpism, By Simbo Olorunfemi

acts.speaker: Lao Tzu
acts.speech: “What is soft is strong.”

acts.speaker: Nicolo Machiavelli (advice to “The Prince”)
acts.speech: “it is better to be feared than to be loved if one cannot be both.”

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
acts.speech: Has consistently accused Canada and Mexico of being ‘’bad trade partners” who have not treated America right; complained that the “unfair” trade deficit with Canada is between $200 billion and $250 billion ; speaking recently at the World Economic Forum in Davos, made it clear that he doesn’t “need Canadian cars, lumber or oil”.

acts.speaker: Pierre Trudeau, former Prime Minister of Canada
acts.speech: Said in 1969 of relations with the US, “Living next to you, is in some ways, like sleeping with an elephant. No matter how friendly and even-tempered is the beast, if I can call it that, one is affected by every twitch and grunt.”

acts.speaker: analysts
acts.speech: Say that much of the deficit was “caused by the U.S. importing Canadian oil, which keeps costs at the pump down for Americans.”

acts.speaker: Trump’s aides
acts.speech: Argue that tariffs are either being used as a “negotiating tool” or a “means of raising taxes on foreigners to pay for retaining low tax rates on Americans.”

acts.speaker: Stephen Miran, previous senior Trump adviser nominated to chair the Council of Economic Advisers (paper)
acts.speech: In a paper touted to serve as a blueprint for Trump 2.0, anchors a proposal to reform the global trading system on the proviso “that access to the U.S. consumer market is a privilege that must be earned, not a right.”

acts.speaker: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, WTO Director-General
acts.speech: Has called for dialogue and restraint among members in response to the Trump phenomenon; drawing parallels to the 1930s Smoot-Hawley Act, warns that retaliatory trade wars could have catastrophic consequences for global growth.

acts.speaker: Giulio Gallarotti
acts.speech: Argues that unilateralism “can be especially debilitating, because in an interdependent and globalised world, unilateral solutions to international problems are often inferior to collective solutions” ; submits that “…forsaking erstwhile allies and international commitments in favour of unilateral solutions produces a maverick image that compromises traditional sources of power embedded in multilateral support networks. Without such networks, even preponderant national resources will fall short of the effectiveness of multilateral solutions in attending to foreign objectives, thus creating an unsupportable burden for the maverick nation.”

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
acts.speech: On the withdrawal of the United States from the World Health Organization: “World Health ripped us off, everybody rips off the United States. It’s not going to happen anymore.”

acts.speaker: Lawrence Gostin, professor of global health at Georgetown University
acts.speech: “This is the darkest day for global health I have ever experienced…Trump could be sowing the seeds for the next pandemic.”

acts.speaker: The White House
acts.speech: Celebrated the “victory” in the standoff with Colombia as evidence that the US is “respected again”.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
acts.speech: Describing DeepSeek: “…a wake-up call for our industries that we need to be laser-focused on competing”.

acts.speaker: Mike Johnson, House Speaker
acts.speech: DeepSeek is “a serious threat” from China, which is a “terrible trading partner.” “They abuse the system. They steal our intellectual property. They’re now trying to get a leg up on us on AI, as you’ve seen the last day or so… It’s a serious threat to us and to our economy and our security in every way.”

acts.speaker: Joseph Nye Jr.
acts.speech: Explains, “…in a world where borders are becoming more porous than ever to everything from drugs to infectious diseases to terrorism, nations must mobilize international coalitions and build institutions to address shared threats and challenges. In this sense, power becomes a positive-sum game. It is not enough to think in terms of power over others. We must also think in terms of power to accomplish goals that involves power with others. On many transnational issues, empowering others can help us to accomplish our own goals. In this world, networks and connectedness become an important source of relevant power”.

acts.speaker: An Australian Senator (placard)
acts.speech: “…if you respect the world’s laws, the world will respect you.”

title: Court jails trafficker 2 years

acts.speaker: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
acts.speech: has secured the conviction of human trafficker, Fasa Sandra, over trafficking of persons for prostitution; had arraigned Fasa Sandra, 35, and Omengor Chinoso, 26, before a Federal High Court for exportation of persons for prostitution and tampering with evidence and witness in 2021.

acts.speaker: Federal High Court (court record)
acts.speech: Sandra was sentenced to two years jail term with an option of N250,000 fine; the court reserved judgment on Omengor Chinoso, who had jumped bail, pending when she was brought back to the court.

title: No Disparity In Crude Oil Production Figures, Says NNPC

acts.speaker: Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd)
acts.speech: Has clarified that there is no discrepancy between its crude oil production figures and those supplied by the regulatory agency, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Company (NUPRC).

acts.speaker: Olufemi O. Soneye, Chief Corporate Communications Officer, NNPC Ltd. (statement)
acts.speech: According to a statement, the seeming disparity is as a result of the difference in the period of coverage in the reports – whereas the NNPC Ltd's figure was the peak production for October 2024, the NUPRC's figure was the average production for September 2024.

acts.speaker: Gbenga Komolafe, Chief Executive Officer of NUPRC (represented by Enorense Amadasu, Executive Commissioner, Development & Production)
acts.speech: Disclosed that Nigeria's crude oil output, including condensate, increased by 16.56 percent to 1.8mbpd in October 2024, from 1.54 million bpd in September 2024: “This represents an increase of 253,710bpd to reach 1.8 million bpd in October, up from 1.54 million bpd in September 2024, representing 16.56 percent month on-month rise”.

acts.speaker: Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Company (NUPRC)
acts.speech: Also confirmed at the NAPE event that the 1.8mbpd feat pushed Nigeria's production beyond the 1.5mbpd quota of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

title: School Feeding begins restructuring - 31-day arrears for caterers cleared

acts.speaker: Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) Secretariat (press statement)
acts.speech: “The GSFP Secretariat, under the supervision of the MoGCSP, has commenced a restructuring of the programme to fulfil the government’s commitment to decentralise its operations, improve the quality of food served and ensure consistency in the payment of caterers,” the secretariat said in a statement. The statement further announced that the government, through the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP), had paid the 31 days’ arrears owed to caterers under the GSFP for the first term of the 2024/2025 academic year.

acts.speaker: Hajia Fati Forgor, National Coordinator of the GSFP Secretariat (press statement)
acts.speech: thanked the government for the release of funds for the payment of the outstanding arrears. “The GSFP Secretariat extends its appreciation to the government for the timely release of funds for the payment of outstanding arrears owed to the caterers,” the statement read.

acts.speaker: Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) Secretariat
acts.speech: expressed gratitude to the programme’s donor partners for their support, indicating that such collaborations remained vital to the sustainability of the initiative. “We thank our donor partners for their continuous support and collaboration with the Government of Ghana to sustain the programme,” it said.

acts.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Finance Minister (Ghana)
acts.speech: Presenting the Budget Statement to Parliament on March 11, 2025, announced an increase in the feeding grant per child from GH¢1.20 to GH¢1.60. He explained that the increment was necessitated by rising food prices and the need to sustain the programme to ensure that pupils in public basic schools continued to receive nutritious meals.

title: Suspension de 90 jours des financements américains par le Président Trump : Enjeux et conséquences sur les programmes en cours au Mali

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
acts.speech: Announced a temporary 90-day suspension of certain international funding, a measure described as a "period of strategic evaluation" of international priorities.

title: Taxes douanières américaines: Les implications économiques pour le Bénin

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said the resurgence of protectionism by the United States since President Donald Trump's return to power constitutes a major economic event, and that the decision can be considered a calling into question of the tariff preference granted by the United States to certain countries, including Benin, through AGOA; although the share of the United States in Benin's exports is still fairly low (a little less than 2% between 2021 and 2023), it shows a very marked upward trend; "The abandonment of AGOA and the imposition of a 10% customs duty will inevitably lead to increased competition for the products we export to that country. This may contribute to a reduction in our exports to the United States. The consequence must be a worsening of the deficit in Benin's trade balance, which is structurally in deficit."

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said that despite the relative weakness of the share of Beninese products sold on the American market, the measure could have notable repercussions on several macroeconomic indicators: "one can expect a contraction of investment in sectors oriented towards exporting to the United States, a fall in the incomes of the producers concerned, as well as a decrease in the volume of goods transiting through Benin bound for the American market," which could also negatively affect the country's port activities.

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said it is too early to have a precise estimate of the impact on the textile factories installed at the Glo-Djigbe Industrial Zone (Gdiz), but that since conquering the American market is among the investors' objectives there is a risk of a slowdown in foreign investment, while adequate trade facilitation measures could improve competitiveness and attract investors; "From my point of view, the situation should not be dramatised... our capacity to react can spare our economy a significant slowdown in its rate of growth."

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Argued that the response must not be limited to seeking a short-term readjustment, since obtaining new unilateral preferences through bilateral renegotiation would always expose Benin to an abrupt reversal in the future; urged continuation of the policy of diversifying export products and markets and the elimination of all practices and measures that obstruct competitiveness, saying such an option should make the country more resilient to the trade policy shocks of its partners.

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Said the question of AGOA's fate remains entirely open since the United States has taken measures, since President Trump's return, suggesting it is no longer in a logic of special and differentiated treatment for developing countries: "I am referring to the suspension of the programmes managed by USAID. In my opinion, as to the fate that will be reserved for AGOA until September 2025, clarifications must be given by the American side." Said what is most worrying is what happens to the instrument after September 2025, and proposed that the authorities assume AGOA will not be renewed and begin taking measures so as not to be excluded from the American market because of the lack of competitiveness of Beninese products.

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, economist
acts.speech: Argued that shocks of this nature create the conditions for a readjustment of economic strategies and that countries must avoid building an entire strategy on preferential agreements; said it is now time to put in place strategies for improving the competitiveness of export products and to diversify export destinations, relying on other mechanisms such as the AfCFTA, which "should allow us to have better access to the African market"; added that Benin's membership of regional organisations such as WAEMU, ECOWAS and the AU requires a concerted approach in trade policy, and that the regional approach increases negotiating power, "which, even at that scale, is still very weak."

title: State Department refugee office to assume USAID’s disaster aid role, says cabl

acts.speaker: Internal State Department cable (ALDAC) excerpts reviewed by Reuters
acts.speech: Under the new arrangement, all U.S. overseas missions should consult with PRM on foreign disaster declarations, said the cable. "With approval from PRM based on established criteria for international disaster assistance, up to $100,000 can be issued to support the initial response," it continued. "Additional resources may be forthcoming based on established humanitarian need" in consultation with other State Department offices. ; One cable excerpt said that in the event of an overseas disaster, PRM may call on what's left of USAID's Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance to mobilize the remnants of its staff "to provide the most efficient and effective response."

acts.speaker: State Department (non-response)
acts.speech: The State Department did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

acts.speaker: Source familiar with the matter (anonymous)
acts.speech: confirmed on condition of anonymity the authenticity of the excerpts. Only 20 experts out of the roughly 525 who did the work at USAID's Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance and its Office of U.S. Foreign Disaster Relief are being hired by PRM, the source said. But, the source continued, the number is far from adequate and the PRM leadership has "no concept of how to" mount responses to major overseas disasters. "They do not understand disaster response," said the source.

acts.speaker: Jeremy Konyndyk, former director of the Office of U.S. Foreign Disaster Relief and president of Refugees International
acts.speech: "It's a joke. It's ridiculous. PRM is not an operational entity. They do important stuff but this is not what they do." ; Konyndyk warned that with the approaching Caribbean hurricane season the U.S. can no longer mobilize the world-leading Disaster Assistance Response Teams (DARTs) it once could to help with serious disasters on this side of the globe. "The mechanics of how DARTs work cannot be replicated in PRM. They are just trying to create a Potemkin DART."

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
acts.speech: has rejected criticism of the administration response to the earthquake in Myanmar. He said it was a difficult place to work, the military junta does not like the U.S. and it was unfair that the U.S. has provided most international humanitarian aid.

acts.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
acts.speech: say the Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration lacks the knowhow and personnel for the role; USAID's gutting has already led to what many experts called the administration's late and inadequate response to a serious earthquake in Myanmar on March 25.

title: Nigerian Senate increases country's health budget to address US aid freeze

acts.speaker: Nigerian Senate
acts.speech: Has allocated additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 approved budget to bridge the gap created by the United States government's freeze on foreign aid; the Senate said the funds would support health interventions and address challenges previously financed by US government foreign aid before its suspension.

acts.speaker: Health experts
acts.speech: Worry that Nigeria's health sector could face significant challenges without US foreign aid.

acts.speaker: Nigerian government
acts.speech: Had pledged to strengthen the health sector and intensify domestic funding to ensure ownership and sustainability of the country's HIV/AIDS response; announced it would begin producing tools such as test kits and antiretroviral drugs locally.

acts.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
acts.speech: Said the US executive orders had made the re-evaluation of the country's dependence on foreign aid a necessary move.

acts.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier reporting)
acts.speech: PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the government had pledged to strengthen the health sector and intensify domestic funding to ensure ownership and sustainability of the country's HIV/AIDS response; this paper also reported that the government had announced it would begin producing tools such as test kits and antiretroviral drugs locally.

title: Former President Sharif meets U.S. ambassador to discuss political stability and state-building - Hiiraan Online

acts.speaker: Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, former Somali President
acts.speech: Thanked the United States for its continued support in security, counter-terrorism, and humanitarian assistance efforts in Somalia.

acts.speaker: The United States
acts.speech: Has reiterated its commitment to backing Somalia's efforts to build effective governance institutions despite persistent political and security challenges.

title: “Si nous sommes attaqués par l’Iran, l’armée américaine répliquera avec toute sa force”, prévient Trump

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (post on Truth Social)
acts.speech: Warned Iran on Sunday that the American army would respond with "all its force" if it attacked the United States: "If we are attacked in any way by Iran, the full strength and might of the US armed forces will come down on you at levels never seen before." He reaffirmed on Truth Social that Washington "had nothing to do" with the ongoing Israeli attacks against Tehran.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: "We can easily reach a deal between Iran and Israel and end this bloody conflict" ; he had said he was aware of the Israeli operation before it began early on Friday.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: On Friday, the American president had urged Tehran to conclude a deal or face "even more brutal" attacks from Israel.

acts.speaker: Tehran (Iranian authorities)
acts.speech: According to Tehran, the Israeli operation targeted Iranian nuclear and military sites, killing dozens of people, including senior army commanders and atomic scientists.

acts.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
acts.speech: Promised to strike "all the targets of the ayatollahs' regime".

title: Prime Minister Hamza Receives Chinese Ambassador to Somalia

acts.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
acts.speech: Expressed gratitude to China for its continued support to Somalia, particularly in the areas of politics, security cooperation, economic development, and humanitarian assistance.

acts.speaker: Wang Yu, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Somalia
acts.speech: Highlighted the longstanding partnership between Somalia and China and reaffirmed his country's commitment to further supporting the Somali people and government.

title: Nigeria and the transition to a cleaner energy mix, By Haruna Momoh

acts.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA), 2015 report
acts.speech: According to a 2015 report by the International Energy Agency, the world may need to do away with 80 per cent of coal deposits, 50 per cent of oil reserves and 40 per cent of gas deposits without extraction in order to reduce carbon emissions to tolerable levels.

acts.speaker: United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
acts.speech: Defined climate change as “a long-term change in the average weather patterns that have come to define Earth’s local, regional and global climates.”

acts.speaker: UNICEF Report (2022)
acts.speech: Cited that about 1.5 million children needed humanitarian assistance due to devastating floods that affected 34 out of 36 states.

acts.speaker: Reuters (13 November 2024 report)
acts.speech: Reported that heavy rains and floods ruined more than 1.5 million hectares of farmland in Nigeria.

acts.speaker: Member of the Nigerian Delegation at COP29 (unnamed)
acts.speech: Informed an audience that more than 40 million people in the Niger Delta had been adversely affected by sea level rise with a huge chunk of land lost.

acts.speaker: Rural Electrification Agency (REA)
acts.speech: According to the REA, about 86 million Nigerians lack access to grid electricity, one of the highest numbers by global standards.

acts.speaker: Governor of Oyo State
acts.speech: During the inauguration of the first phase of the 11 megawatt Ibadan Hybrid Power Plant Project, stated that the state was aiming at a 500 megawatt solar power generation project to meet domestic needs and sell to neighbouring countries.

acts.speaker: Kashim Shettima, Nigerian Vice President
acts.speech: Stated on 19 March 2024 that the Nigerian Sovereign Wealth Fund planned to build a 20 megawatt solar power plant, a first step towards an ambitious 300 megawatt project.

acts.speaker: ThisDay (review report, June 2024)
acts.speech: Indicated that the Nigeria Sovereign Insurance Authority had completed the development and construction of a 10 megawatt solar energy project in Kumbotso Local Government Area in Kano State; the report also highlighted several ongoing solar energy projects, including the 5,600 megawatt Argungu Solar Energy Park in Kebbi State, expected to come on stream in 2027, the 1,000 megawatt Jigawa Solar Project and the 350 megawatt Lafia Solar Project.

acts.speaker: Studies (unspecified)
acts.speech: Studies have shown that projects associated with renewable energy are projected to create more jobs than fossil fuel energy sources.

acts.speaker: Gulf Times (3 November 2024 report)
acts.speech: Posited that Qatar’s LNG production will rise by 35% in 2027, as additional demands from Europe are expected, which would raise the per capita income of the Gulf country in excess of $80,000.

acts.speaker: Reports (unspecified projections)
acts.speech: Reports project that lithium demand will rise from 720,000 metric tonnes in 2022 to 3.2 million metric tonnes by 2030.

acts.speaker: Bloomberg (21 November 2024 report)
acts.speech: Highlighted that Kuwait proposed to spend over $33 billion to ramp up oil production capacity, placing a bet on increased demand for decades to come.

title: Over Bloated Civil Service: NGF Boss Urges States To Deploy Workers To Areas Of Need

acts.speaker: Abdulateef Shittu, Director General of Nigeria Governors Forum (NGF)
acts.speech: Has called on States with overbloated Civil service to take proactive steps by deploying some of the workers to areas where their services are highly needed for optimal performance ; Pointed out that some States have overbloated Civil service, adding that States do not need overbloated Civil Service to guarantee efficient service delivery ; "I want to throw a poser to all the Heads of Service here. You should start thinking about the overbloated Civil Service in your States. You have to start thinking of the major reforms across the bureaucracy in the Service. I know that a country is as great as its civil service. The states are as strong as their civil service. When the Civil service is not working for the overall development of States, then we will be having issues. As we speak today, there are many challenges in the workforce. I will not mention states. We have some states that have 50,000 workforce. Some have 52,000. You don't have to sack them, you can deploy them to the areas of need to optimise resources."

acts.speaker: Irene Karimi, State2State Chief of Party
acts.speech: Explained that in the past four years, the USAID State Accountability, Transparency and Effectiveness (State2State) Activity has invested in various interventions across the seven partner States ; Reaffirmed that these interventions that have resulted in governance, public financial management and citizen engagement reforms should be sustained beyond State2State ; Revealed that one of the sustainability and institutionalisation vehicles introduced by State2State across the partner states is the State Transformation Committee (STC), with the Offices of the Head of Service in the States playing crucial roles in the successes recorded by the STCs.

acts.speaker: Irene Karimi, State2State Chief of Party
acts.speech: On the essence of the Community of Practice, explained that it would serve as an avenue that facilitates and promotes quality conversations and peer-learning among actors and stakeholders within the office of States Head of Service to engender and sustain a stronger civil service, delivering quality service within the Activity's priority sectors such as basic education, primary health care and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services in the seven partner States.

acts.speaker: Dr. Joe Abah, DAI Nigeria Country Director
acts.speech: Blamed some Governors for overbloated Civil service, adding that some governors often employ civil servants on political exigencies, rather than on the basis of needs ; Called for strong collaboration, experience sharing and best practices between the Federal and States Civil Service.

acts.speaker: Stanley Achonu, Deputy Chief of Party, USAID State2State Activity
acts.speech: In an interview with Daily Independent, explained that in the last four years the organisation has funded extensive reforms in the partner States of Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Bauchi, Ebonyi, Gombe, Kebbi, and Sokoto ; Stated that institutional capacities of these States have been built towards effective utilisation of resources, improved laws and policies as well as deployment of resources to the priority sectors of education, healthcare, water, sanitation and hygiene ; Noted that many civil servants in these States have been trained in planning, procurement, internal audit, financial control, internally revenue generation and improvement ; Pointed out that these reforms would be sustainable if those who have been trained by USAID State2State are allowed to use their training and capacities to implement these reforms ; "What we are doing with CoP is to make sure that those who are custodians of the deployment of servants and human resources within the states are aware of the capacity which these people have received as well as the need to keep them in the relevant MDAs where they will continue to use the skills that we have given them to drive the reforms."

title: Journée Mondiale de l’Action Humanitaire : “Agir pour l’humanité”, thème retenu pour l’édition 2025 - Agence Nigérienne de Presse

acts.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: Launched on Tuesday 19 August 2025 the activities for the celebration of World Humanitarian Day under the theme "Act for Humanity", paid tribute to the resilience of affected communities and sought to raise public awareness about humanitarian activities ; said this year's theme "calls on decision-makers to use their influence to put an end to atrocities and human suffering" ; "this day, instituted in 2008 by the United Nations General Assembly, commemorates the attack on the United Nations house in Baghdad on 19 August 2003", the aim of the commemoration being to recall the significant challenges facing humanitarian actors, notably the climate emergency.

acts.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: Addressed the security and humanitarian situation in Niger, marked by the actions of terrorist groups, and assured that "the government is committed to restoring security and peace throughout the territory".

acts.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity of Niger
acts.speech: "This event that we are celebrating together is an opportunity for us to recall that humanitarian action must align with the ideals of the Refoundation" ; "communities must be at the heart of humanitarian action" ; "humanitarian aid accompanies, but it is the communities that initiate, guide and shape the responses to their challenges" ; "it is important to respect dignity, beyond relief, and every humanitarian intervention must preserve the dignity of the women, men and children who resist crises every day."

acts.speaker: Issoufou Soumana, representative of the NGOs
acts.speech: In his address paid tribute to humanitarian actors and underlined the crucial role of national and local organisations in assisting populations affected by climate and security challenges in Niger ; "despite the decline in funding, NGOs have maintained their assistance; this collective effort has translated into daily assistance to millions of people in Niger."

acts.speaker: Issoufou Soumana, representative of the NGOs
acts.speech: Insisted on the need to guarantee safe and regular humanitarian access to populations in need, while ensuring the protection of populations and humanitarian actors ; said coordination mechanisms between humanitarian actors and State services "must be strengthened", specifying that "continuous engagement and dialogue between these two parties is essential in order to ensure an effective humanitarian response, from planning to the monitoring of interventions" ; added that humanitarian work requires the contribution and collaboration of all actors — State, NGOs, communities — and that "it is together, respecting our respective roles, that we will continue to act for humanity."

acts.speaker: Nena Lafuente, representative of the technical and financial partners (PTF)
acts.speech: Stressed that "humanitarian work is a collective responsibility, framed by humanitarian principles and international humanitarian law", adding "that it requires collaboration between governments, communities and humanitarian organisations, respecting the fundamental role each one plays" ; noted that in 2024, 383 humanitarian workers were killed, the deadliest year ever recorded for humanitarian personnel, and that in 2025 to date 265 humanitarians have lost their lives, which "puts us on track to exceed this grim record".

acts.speaker: Nena Lafuente, representative of the technical and financial partners (PTF)
acts.speech: Insisted on the protection of civilians and humanitarian workers against dangers linked to conflicts and disasters, and called for "respect for international humanitarian law, particularly with regard to the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel in times of armed conflict", while stressing the need to hold accountable those who violate international humanitarian law, ensuring that the perpetrators of violence and attacks are brought to justice.

acts.speaker: Kinday Samba, acting Humanitarian Coordinator for Niger
