acts.speech: Clarified changes regarding the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), noting that its functions would now be overseen by the U.S. State Department, a transition consistent with her long-standing view that U.S. development assistance, funded by taxpayers, should serve as a foreign policy instrument and be administered accordingly: “The functions of USAID will now be run by the State Department, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and that is something, to be honest, I have advocated for decades. I don’t think that will cause any difference in focus or in effect.” ; Reassured that the U.S. remains firmly committed to its development partnership with Ghana and emphasised that the change in administrative oversight will not impact the effectiveness or direction of American assistance ; Reaffirmed Ghana’s continued significance in U.S. foreign policy.

title: Journées portes ouvertes sur la ‘’Gire’’: Un nouvel élan vers une gestion concertée des ressources en eau

acts.speaker: Hounkponou K. Saïd, Director of Water (Bénin)
acts.speech: IWRM promotes the coordinated development of water, land, and related resources for equitable economic and social well-being, while ensuring the sustainability of ecosystems.

title: Akatswiri Mineral Resource rolls its Mulanje Bauxite Project: Over 1300 jobs created, to generate forex, create wealth - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Akatswiri Holdings
acts.speech: Has committed to minimizing ecological damage through Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) to ensure sustainable operations; reforestation and land reclamation to preserve Mulanje Mountain's biodiversity; and integration of renewable energy solutions to reduce the carbon footprint of the mining process.

acts.speaker: Hilton Banda, Managing Director of Akatswiri Holdings
acts.speech: "This project is about more than mining—it's about building a brighter, self-reliant future for Malawi."

title: Rebasing Economy Without Growth Is Economic Deception — Onuesoke

acts.speaker: Chief Sunny Onuesoke, Environmentalist, Political Commentator and Former Gubernatorial Aspirant, Delta State
acts.speech: “You do not project or rebase your economy using random databases and speculative figures. Economic rebasing must reflect real growth and measurable activities. You do not borrow to rebase — that is economic deception.”

acts.speaker: Chief Sunny Onuesoke, Environmentalist, Political Commentator and Former Gubernatorial Aspirant, Delta State
acts.speech: Argued that Nigeria’s 2014 rebasing, which overnight made it Africa’s largest economy, was “a paper gain — one that brought prestige without progress,” and set out conditions for legitimate rebasing: it must be based on verifiable economic activities rather than donor-driven data modeling, must reflect real sector performance, “must not be funded through loans or foreign aid meant to decorate statistics,” and must be part of a broader structural reform agenda rather than an isolated PR move.

title: Trump calls his own foreign aid cuts at USAID 'devastating'

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
acts.speech: said on Wednesday that his administration's cuts to the U.S. Agency for International Development and its aid programs worldwide have been "devastating." "It's devastating, and hopefully a lot of people are going to start spending a lot of money." ; "I've talked to other nations. We want them to chip in and spend money too, and we've spent a lot. And it's a big - it's a tremendous problem going on in many countries. A lot of problems going on. The United States always gets the request for money. Nobody else helps."

acts.speaker: U.S. State Department
acts.speech: The State Department, which manages USAID, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

acts.speaker: Trump administration
acts.speech: has repeatedly defended the cuts, saying they were focused on wasted funds.

acts.speaker: U.S. government data
acts.speech: The United States disbursed $61 billion in foreign assistance last year, just over half of it via USAID, according to government data; the U.S. spent half a billion dollars on South African aid in 2023, mostly on healthcare, the most recent data shows.

acts.speaker: Reuters
acts.speech: has reported that in the months since the cuts, testing and monitoring of HIV patients across South Africa has decreased.

title: Port autonome de Cotonou : tonneau des danaïdes ou corvée de Sisyphe ?

acts.speaker: The Americans / US international partners
acts.speech: had threatened to downgrade and declassify the port of Cotonou; now they applaud the new import verification reforms with both hands.

acts.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account (MCC)
acts.speech: had warned that it would withdraw if the port continued to be a cesspit; according to certain leaks, it is said to have given Benin Controle a clean bill of health.

title: Collaborate for sustainable water access - Water sector stakeholders urged

acts.speaker: Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources of Ghana
acts.speech: Has called on stakeholders in the water sector to strengthen collaboration and create synergies in their operations for efficient delivery of water services to Ghanaians ; stressed that there was a need for synergy between both state and non-state water sector institutions and agencies because if they did not shake each other, their investments could be duplicated and, therefore, counterproductive ; said in an era when the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) had ceased its investment across the world, affecting some water projects, the state and private sector needed to work closely together to prudently channel resources into water systems that would be of utmost benefit to the people ; "However, we recognise that the government alone cannot solve all the challenges in the water sector. Partnerships with non-state actors such as Safe Water Network, other members of the Safe Water Enterprises (SWE) Alliance, the private sector and development partners are not only welcome but essential."

acts.speaker: Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources of Ghana
acts.speech: Described the theme of the forum as apt and timely because the country was at a critical point where access to water had become a critical development challenge ; said in furtherance of the commitment made by President John Dramani Mahama in his maiden State of the Nation Address to Parliament to expand water access for all Ghanaians, the Works and Water Resources Ministry would implement policies that would accelerate access to the resource, that ongoing water projects would be completed and new ones initiated at both the urban and rural levels "to ensure that every Ghanaian, regardless of where they live, enjoys the right to safe and reliable water" ; stressed that there would be more targeted investment in infrastructure, institutional reforms and digital innovation to drive progress.

acts.speaker: Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, Deputy Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources of Ghana
acts.speech: Said one of the most challenging issues to access to quality water was the galamsey scourge: "Galamsey has taken over our water quality, and it is pathetic to see how people suffer for water in communities and regions where the menace is rife. We are at a crisis point now, and all of us must play our roles as expected to help save our water bodies." ; touching on the Blue Water initiative in which 400 water guards were deployed to protect rivers, said it was a great move to help bring back heavily polluted water bodies, and contrary to criticisms that the initiative would not make any impact on the galamsey fight, said "the people are taken from the community and they can help to fight galamsey if there is political will to do so" ; "Inter-ministerial and inter-development partner collaborations are key in all of these."

acts.speaker: Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, Deputy Minister of Works, Housing and Water Resources of Ghana
acts.speech: Said as a government that just took over a couple of months back, they were currently assessing water sector projects that had stalled and water systems that were malfunctioning, and collaborating with other state institutions to halt galamsey and other human activities that polluted water sources.

acts.speaker: Charles Nimako, Country Director of Safe Water Network Ghana and Lead for Africa initiatives
acts.speech: Highlighted that over the past year, the entity had expanded to an additional 55,000 people in 10 communities across the country, taking their total coverage to 504,000 people in 158 communities ; said when that number was added to what had been achieved by other implementers of water services, particularly Safe Water Enterprise Alliance, then more than two million Ghanaians would be reached with safe and affordable water ; stressed that although that achievement was a key milestone, it was not "the finish line" ; "In the coming months, we will continue to build on the progress we have made by strengthening the technical and financial resilience of our model, equipping local operators and field support teams, and aligning with government priorities as articulated in the President's State of the Nation Address and the 2025 Budget that was delivered in Parliament."

title: African Union adopts Akufo-Addo’s proposal for mobile money interoperability across Africa

acts.speaker: African Union (AU)
acts.speech: has adopted President Akufo-Addo's proposal for mobile money interoperability across Africa. The reports — “Establishment of the African Union Financial Institutions (AUFIs)” and “Scaling up Interoperability for Economic Integration: Using Mobile Money to Buy and Sell Across Africa” — were endorsed by the AU, paving the way for implementation of mobile money interoperability across Africa.

acts.speaker: GSMA
acts.speech: The total value of mobile money transactions was recently estimated to be over $1.26 trillion, according to GSMA, that is around 40% of Africa's GDP.

acts.speaker: Nana Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana and AU Champion on Financial Institutions
acts.speech: emphasized the importance of mobile money interoperability, stating that while creating business opportunities and helping to tackle unemployment among the youth, continent wide interoperability will also make it easier for SMEs to conduct business and expand their reach.

acts.speaker: African Union (AU)
acts.speech: has called upon member states, regional economic communities, and relevant stakeholders to commit to achieving mobile money interoperability by 2027. This includes bringing all member states on board the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), allowing cross-border mobile money interoperability, and developing a continental regulatory framework for mobile money operations.

title: Aids Commission calls for political commitment - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
acts.speech: Calls for bold political commitment and increased domestic resource allocation to support the country's HIV response amid global donor funding challenges: "The fight against the spread of HIV remains a national priority that requires our collective efforts, partnership, and collaboration; we call for a united front to address structural barriers such as stigma and discrimination that impede access to HIV testing and treatment services." She notes that inadequate domestic resource allocation for HIV response in Liberia continues to undermine efforts to sustain gains beyond 2030, stressing that it is time now to own and sustain these achievements as a country. She explains that this year's World AIDS Day is globally themed, "Collective Action, and Sustain and Accelerate HIV progress," which aligns with Liberia's commitment to ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

acts.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
acts.speech: Announced that with support from UNAID, NAC has initiated the development of a National HIV Sustainability Roadmap to transform Liberia's HIV response into a more self-reliant system, and that the roadmap will prioritize increased domestic financing, as outlined in the updated National HIV and AIDS Strategic Plan (2021-2026).

acts.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
acts.speech: Acknowledges partners' contributions, including PEPFAR, the Global Fund, UN agencies, and civil society organizations, for their unwavering support in combating HIV in Liberia: "We also recognize the efforts of civil society organizations that continue to stand up for the voiceless and the donor community for their commitment to the national HIV response."

acts.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
acts.speech: Appeals to policymakers, private sector actors, and community leaders to play active roles in sustaining gains made over the years ; "Community outreach will engage opinion leaders to reduce HIV-related stigma and discrimination while creating demand for HIV testing" ; urges Liberians to rally behind the national theme: "We want to humbly appeal to all state actors, policymakers, and the private sector to get involved."

title: Embaixadores condenam Israel nas Nações Unidas

acts.speaker: Ambassadors of 105 countries to the United Nations in New York, including Mozambique (joint letter of 10 October)
acts.speech: Signed a letter expressing their “profound concern” at the recent statements by Israel’s minister of foreign affairs declaring Secretary-General António Guterres persona non grata; condemned them and consider that such statements and other actions may undermine the capacity of the United Nations to carry out its mandate, which includes mediation in conflicts and the provision of humanitarian aid; hold that Israel’s actions can only contribute to delaying the end of hostilities in the Middle East and efforts to establish a roadmap leading to the two-State solution ; “In moments of heightened tension, the role of the Secretary-General is essential for the promotion of dialogue and understanding between parties in conflict” ; “We are confident of his commitment to peace and security, and alignment with International Law, including in promoting respect for international humanitarian law and the relevant United Nations resolutions on the situation in the Middle East” ; “constructive engagement with the United Nations is vital for overcoming the challenges we face and achieving a future of peace.”

acts.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Israel
acts.speech: Made recent statements declaring the Secretary-General of the United Nations, António Guterres, persona non grata.

title: Formation, recherche de pointe… : L’Ens réceptionne des équipements scientifiques

acts.speaker: Bamory Kamagaté, Director General of the École normale supérieure (Ens), Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Said that alongside the rehabilitated and equipped laboratories, four rooms equipped with 25 computers each were also received, three at the Ens and one at the Jean Piaget application school. Said "A fifth, larger room is equipped with 45 interconnected desktop computers and a Vestel [interactive display]. In addition to all this, we also have laptops, electronic tablets, video projectors, cameras and multifunction printers, to name just a few." Recalled that this important equipment will help improve the quality of teaching, learner training, and research activities. Recalled that another important component of the collaboration with Mca-CI concerns the construction and equipping of Ens branches in San Pedro and Bouaké. Said "The next step will be to carefully consider the choice of application schools that will support these branches. The idea is to rely either on the schools of excellence built precisely by the Mca in these two regions, or on the public institutions located there. On this matter, an imminent meeting is planned between Mca-CI and Ens experts. A report will be submitted to the minister following this meeting."

acts.speaker: Adama Diawara, Ivorian Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research
acts.speech: Expressed satisfaction at the successful completion of the rehabilitation and equipping of the school with scientific and educational material by the Mcc and the Mca. Noted that this donation is only part of the broader Employability and Productivity Project (155 million USD) aimed at improving the employability of Ivorians and the productivity of the private sector by improving the quality, supply and access to technical and basic skills, in response to private sector demand. Said "We remain convinced that this will significantly improve the working conditions and quality of training at this school, whose primary mission is to train the trainers of our education system."

title: Mozambique: Regulation for the leader of 2nd party approved - Notícias

acts.speaker: Notícias (newspaper report)
acts.speech: Reports today that the Council of Ministers yesterday approved regulations concerning the leader of the opposition, instituted through Law number 33/2014 of 30 December.

acts.speaker: Armindo Tiago, Minister of Health of Mozambique
acts.speech: Explained at the scheduled post-session press conference that only the evolution of the coronavirus in Mozambique would determine the extension or not of the state of emergency decreed on April 1 by the President of the Republic, and scheduled to end on 30 April: “Besides, it is not up to the Ministry of Health to decide on this. One thing is certain: many factors will be considered in taking this decision, especially the number of cases and the effective implementation of preventative measures so that we do not have more people infected.”

title: Don de matériels informatique et bureautique pour renforcer les capacités techniques du conseil régional de Dikhil

acts.speaker: Hassan Abdi Robleh, Prefect of Dikhil
acts.speech: After a welcome message, gave an overview of the various projects carried out by USAID in his region before speaking of the region’s tourism opportunities.

acts.speaker: Nancy Ostrowski, USAID Representative in Djibouti
acts.speech: Emphasised the commitment of the American people to supporting the development process of the regional local authorities.

acts.speaker: Abdallah Mohamed Hassan, interim President of the Regional Council of Dikhil
acts.speech: Thanked the American people and USAID for the valuable donation and in particular for their support to local development initiatives: “This equipment is of crucial importance in strengthening our capacity to serve the community,” he declared. It is, he continued, “another step towards a better future for our region, where civil society will play a key role.”

title: 20ème anniversaire de carrière musicale: La gratitude de King Mensah au public béninois

acts.speaker: King Mensah, Togolese music star
acts.speech: Testified that he had received a great deal of support from the Beninese public in his musical rise in Africa. "I am an empty bag and it is you who have kept me standing since the beginning of my career," King Mensah declared on stage.

acts.speaker: King Mensah, Togolese music star
acts.speech: Returned to the dream that is dear to his heart, helping orphaned children: "Even if I am not a billionaire, I believe that what I have will be enough to realise this dream that is dear to my heart," he said. He explained that he was only 13 when life took his father from him, and that having managed to make a name for himself despite many difficulties, he decided to help children in a similar situation to get ahead in life ; as founder of a humanitarian aid centre for children in Togo, he promises actions in favour of Benin's orphans.

title: AfDB forecasts $40bn global aid cut, Zambia hit

acts.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
acts.speech: Has projected that global aid from the world's 17 largest donors will decline by US$39.84 billion in 2025, driven mainly by reduced contributions from the United States and Germany; cautioned that modest increases from Japan, South Korea, and Italy would not be enough to offset these losses.

acts.speaker: African Development Bank, African Economic Outlook 2025 (report)
acts.speech: Warned that if Africa's current 18 percent share of aid holds, the continent could lose US$4.2 billion next year, posing a serious funding risk for low-income countries: "If this share holds in 2025, Africa would face a nearly 12 percent drop in aid from the 17 largest DAC donors compared with 2023. This would translate into a seven percent decline in total aid inflows, equivalent to US$4.2 billion, if aid from all other donors remains relatively stable. To put this into perspective, the projected decline exceeds the combined GDP of Comoros, Guinea Bissau, and Sao Tome and Principe in 2023. These developments heighten the risk of a funding squeeze for many of Africa's low-income countries, which remain heavily dependent on external aid to finance their national budgets. Aid cuts will especially affect Africa's low-income countries, where ODA contributes significantly to financing the budget."

acts.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
acts.speech: Noted that although external financial flows to Africa rebounded in 2023, persistent global uncertainty and aid cuts threaten to reduce inflows in the short to medium term.

acts.speaker: African Economic Outlook 2025 report
acts.speech: Revealed that while most financial flows declined in 2023 due to global economic challenges, portfolio investments rebounded strongly, with net portfolio flows reversing from outflows of US$23.1 billion to net inflows of US$322.9 million.

title: Burkina Faso : La Russie livre 700 tonnes de pois pour l'aide d'urgence

acts.speaker: Igor Burkin, Chargé d'Affaires a.i. of the Russian Federation in Burkina Faso
acts.speech: "This donation was motivated first of all by the situation currently prevailing in Africa, and more particularly in the Sahel. There are currently displaced people as a result of terrorist actions, and it is precisely these displaced populations who are destitute and in need. Russia is here to help African countries, and Burkina Faso in particular." ; He recalled that since 2003 his country has paid out more than 430 million dollars to support WFP humanitarian operations around the world, placing it among the UN agency's 20 main donors. ; He said that hunger and food shortages in Africa, particularly in the Sahel region, are exacerbated by the security crisis, and that the humanitarian aid, sent by the Russian Ministry of Civil Defence and Emergency Situations, had successfully reached Burkina Faso: "This gesture underlines the traditionally friendly character of relations between the Russian Federation and Burkina Faso."

acts.speaker: Sory Ouane, WFP Representative and Country Director in Burkina Faso
acts.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the donor: "This donation testifies to your strong commitment to supporting humanitarian efforts in a particularly difficult context." ; He highlighted the role of WFP's logistics and recalled that the Burkinabè government has made food security a priority, and that WFP, aligned with the Sustainable Development Goal, must support Burkina Faso in its efforts to eradicate hunger and improve nutrition.

title: DUEL ENTRE HARRIS ET TRUMP, VU D’AFRIQUE : Pour qui bat le cœur des Africains ? - Editions Le Pays

acts.speaker: A specialist well versed in American affairs (anonymous)
acts.speech: Affirms that "A return of Trump would mean a reduction in American involvement in everything to do with multilateralism, such as the climate issue, and possibly a reduction in development aid."

acts.speaker: Many analysts (unnamed)
acts.speech: Announce that a return of Trump to power would bring a new springtime of dictatorships on the black continent, considering that "African authoritarian regimes will be able easily and openly to renew ties with Russia and China."

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, former US President and Republican candidate
acts.speech: During his first term showed little interest in African countries, which he weaned off American aid through the withdrawal of the USA from numerous funds or projects, and which he above all described as "shithole countries."

acts.speaker: General Charles de Gaulle (quoted)
acts.speech: "States have no friends, they only have interests."

title: Accusation de financement du terrorisme à l’USAID : le Mali demande des poursuites judiciaires

acts.speaker: Trump administration / new US administration
acts.speech: Revealed that USAID had financed terrorism with development aid and suspended Mali from its aid programme; in Mali, the diverted amount comes to 14 million dollars (8 billion FCFA).

acts.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali (communique)
acts.speech: “The ministry invites the American authorities to initiate judicial proceedings” - proceedings, the communique details, to be brought against the persons who diverted the said funds in order to finance international terrorism, notably in Mali and in the other AES (Alliance of Sahel States) countries.

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs (head of Malian diplomacy)
acts.speech: Said Mali “recognises itself in the new orientation of the American authorities aimed at cleaning up and humanising their subsidies”; also welcomed this awareness of the reality of their “public aid”; and encouraged the actions undertaken against the subversive use of aid and its non-conformity with the essential needs of the beneficiaries.

acts.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Revealed that Mali had already refused an American grant: for the past two years the government has “refrained from signing the five-year Development Objective Grant Agreement with the United States concerning the financing of USAID projects”, and also postponed the implementation of certain activities, including those relating to social cohesion.

acts.speaker: Government of Mali
acts.speech: Said these measures were aimed at requiring respect for Mali's sovereignty and priorities, and at ensuring respect for national implementation procedures in matters of development aid.

title: Pour noyer Talon, le pouvoir l’accuse de complot

acts.speaker: Beninese government
acts.speech: Accuses Patrice Talon, promoter of the company Benin Control, of seeking to destabilise the institutions of the Republic, presenting him as a stateless man who has made an attempt on the life of the institutions of the Republic

acts.speaker: Eugene Dossoumou, Secretary General of the Government of Benin (formal notice letter No. 233/PR/SGG/SGAG3/C)
acts.speech: “In the hope that you will comply with this formal notice, the government assures you that it is in the name of democracy that it wishes to send it to you in a spirit of adversarial debate, because increasingly you appear as a citizen determined to defy and humiliate a government and to make the suicidal choice of destabilising the institutions of the Republic.” ; “This is an inadvisable option to which an absolute end must be put because it carries the seed of endangering the peace, stability and security that have always characterised our dear homeland.”

title: Government proclaims it does not need a “baby-sitter”

acts.speaker: Ethiopian government
acts.speech: Announced it has completed its military offensive after taking the town of Mekele from the so-called criminal group of the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF); announced that the TPLF group had attacked the North National Defense ; said on Tuesday that 44 truckloads of food aid had been delivered to Shire, the main town near the refugee camps.

acts.speaker: Sekoture Getachew, veteran TPLF politician
acts.speech: Publicly justified the November 4th military attack against the Northern Command of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) as an anticipatory self-defense.

acts.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
acts.speech: Told reporters that Ethiopia will invite others for assistance only if it feels that it failed to investigate: "Ethiopia is led by a government which knows how to govern a nation. Ethiopia doesn't need a baby sitter."

acts.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
acts.speech: Confirmed that Ethiopia's security forces shot to the air and detained United Nations staffers as they tried to reach parts of the embattled Tigray region that they were not supposed to go: "They broke two checkpoints to drive hastily to areas where they were not supposed to go, that they were told not to go." ; "They were told in some areas they were not supposed to move. And when they were left alone they broke two checkpoints, and when they were about to break the third one, soliders shot to the air and detained them. Now, of course they are free."

acts.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
acts.speech: On humanitarian access: "No entity, multilateral or unilateral, is supposed to supplant the government. We, the government, would call the shots." ; "Humanitarian assistance must be escorted by defense forces." ; "The government will give allowance on where to go and where not to go. There are some forces who have not surrendered. They may not have some regular leadership and command and supply of resources but they can still keep on shooting until they run out of their arms. Thus, we are saying our humanitarian assistance has to be escorted with the military."

acts.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
acts.speech: On casualties from the operation: "Just because we completed the operation in three weeks it doesn't mean we are in a picnic it was a very tough assignment it was completed successfully because the government was very much conscious about its people. Any life that dies during the operation is a lose to Ethiopia, but we are not hiding anybody killed by the government defense but because there was none there is no one to be accountable other than Ethiopians. It doesn't matter if they were killed by government force or TIgray forces all are Ethiopians, we are not fighting with a foreign enemy it was a family feud."

acts.speaker: United Nations
acts.speech: Has openly sought unfettered and neutral access according to international principles; announced a deal with the Ethiopian government, saying it was signed on November 29, a deal that allows aid only in areas under Ethiopian government control.

acts.speaker: Mitiku Kassa, Commissioner of the National Risk and Disaster Management
acts.speech: Said the commission is working to address humanitarian assistance to 1.8 million people in the region; however, with the fear of the number increasing, the commission is working to do a rapid assessment to capture additional numbers of beneficiaries, since between 22-30 percent of the urban population may need relief assistance for a short period of time.

title: Diocese builds 4 teachers ’houses in Chitipa District - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Teachers at Kawale Primary School, Chitipa District
acts.speech: Have thanked Karonga Diocese of the Catholic Church for constructing four teachers' houses.

acts.speaker: Vincent Munyimbiri, head teacher of Kawale Primary School
acts.speech: Said only five out of 36 teachers had houses at the school: "With the additional four houses, it means we now have nine teachers residing at the school. This will enhance efficient delivery of lessons. We appeal to other stakeholders to help construct more houses."

acts.speaker: Ethel Kayuni, a beneficiary teacher
acts.speech: Said she used to spend K3 000 daily on transport to school: "Preparation of lesson plans was difficult due to long distances and fatigue. Now, that is history. I am able to plan well and deliver lessons efficiently" ; also said the houses will motivate teachers to work hard.

acts.speaker: Lino Nyirenda, diocesan education desk officer
acts.speech: Said the diocese received funding from United States of America-based Cross Catholic Outreach and constructed two duplex staff houses at K163.4 million and two classroom blocks with desks, toilets and textbooks at K122.2 million: "The construction of these classroom blocks mean that children who were learning under trees have extra space and desks to sit at, thereby increasing performance while the four houses can now accommodate four more teachers who will have more time to prepare for lessons."

title: ANALYSIS | South Africa’s Covid relief measures mostly excluded refugees: a neglect of duty | News24

acts.speaker: Callixte Kavuro, Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Public Law, Stellenbosch University
acts.speech: Writes that South Africa's Covid-19 relief measures, and constitutional socio-economic protections in general, need to be harmonised with the Refugees Act to promote access by formally recognised refugees to state relief programmes ; "The interests of asylum seekers, who are not fully protected by the act, also need to be considered as they too have socio-economic rights."

acts.speaker: Callixte Kavuro (study on socio-economic rights of refugees and asylum seekers during the pandemic)
acts.speech: "My study examined the protection of the socio-economic rights of refugees and asylum seekers in the country during the pandemic. It also considered the impact of non-citizenship on the protection of these vulnerable people." ; "I found that although refugees and asylum seekers are protected in law, this is not always the case in practice. Asylum seekers' interests are rarely considered when it comes to socio-economic protections. They must fend for themselves."

acts.speaker: Callixte Kavuro, Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Public Law, Stellenbosch University
acts.speech: Concludes that the South African government has, over the years, displayed an ambivalent attitude towards the protection of refugees and asylum seekers, evident in its adoption of socio-economic laws which do not speak to the Refugees Act, and that this ambivalence stems from the notion among some within government that most asylum seekers and refugees are not "genuine"; "That's why the government did not fully meet its commitment to treat refugees and asylum seekers with dignity and humanity."

acts.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
acts.speech: On 15 March 2020 stated that his cabinet was finalising a comprehensive package of interventions to mitigate the expected impact of Covid-19 on the economy, and that such interventions would prioritise protecting the health and well-being of "all South Africans".

acts.speaker: 2019 UN report
acts.speech: According to the report, the country had 89,285 formally recognised refugees and 188,285 asylum seekers.

acts.speaker: Scalabrini Centre (NGO, in litigation)
acts.speech: Successfully argued that the exclusion of asylum seekers from the R350 Social Relief of Distress grant was arbitrary and unreasonable, and that it also violated their constitutional rights to equality, dignity and access to social security.

acts.speaker: Department of Employment and Labour
acts.speech: Argued that its computer system was not designed to capture the numbers appearing on the refugees and asylum seekers' status permits.

acts.speaker: Equality Court (2017 order)
acts.speech: Ordered the department in 2017 to fix its computer system to capture the numbers appearing on refugees' and asylum seekers' status permits.

title: Rencontre avec Mohamed Guirreh Galab, formateur sur le Social Business Camp

acts.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
acts.speech: “The objective of this training is to create innovative social enterprises with positive impacts in our community” ; said the training week is entitled GO, to welcome the participants of the first phase, Know, and that it was six days of training on putting together their business model dossier.

acts.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
acts.speech: On the objective of the training, said it was first necessary to clarify the semantics of social entrepreneurship, recalling that Cantillon, a forerunner of the theory of entrepreneurship, affirmed in 1755 that the entrepreneur is an important actor who influences the economic market, and that Schumpeter defined, in 1911, the entrepreneur as a person who innovates and creates new combinations, new products or new processes; said that today both researchers and economists consider entrepreneurial activity to be essential to a country's economic vigour, that social entrepreneurship is the action deployed by an entrepreneur to find innovative solutions to social problems, and that “the objective pursued is to support project holders in order to create social enterprises with a positive impact in Djibouti.”

acts.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
acts.speech: On difficulties encountered, said: “The main challenge was to gather fifty entrepreneurs and project holders coming from all six regions of our national territory in one and the same place, ‘Sunny Hill’. It was a first, in order to develop the entrepreneurial spirit, create a network and a favourable environment outside their comfort zone.”

acts.speaker: Mohamed Guirreh Galab, president of the young entrepreneurs' club and trainer on the Social Business Camp
acts.speech: Said the participants had very interesting ideas in different sectors such as agriculture, fishing, industry or training.

title: Les ministres de la santé de l’IGAD appellent à l’action pour combattre le COVID-19

acts.speaker: Sarah Abdelazem Hassana, Deputy Minister of Health of Sudan
acts.speech: Welcomed "the swift action taken by all IGAD Heads of State and Government to contain and fight the spread of the Corona virus"; on behalf of the Minister of Health of Sudan and chair of the IGAD ministerial health committee, Dr Akram Ali Eltom, she conveyed Sudan's commitment to mobilise national resources in the fight against the Corona virus; she urged the IGAD Secretariat to speed up the process of deploying response teams in member states and to facilitate a coordinated partnership.

acts.speaker: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of IGAD
acts.speech: Recalled that the main objective of the meeting was to discuss the current needs of member states, to fight the coronavirus collaboratively and to provide projections of the infrastructural, technical and material capacities urgently needed for the duration of the epidemic, through a response strategy to fight COVID-19; he also reiterated his call for protection from the pandemic for vulnerable populations such as displaced persons, refugees and migrants in the region.

acts.speaker: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of IGAD
acts.speech: Highlighted the serious disruption of "livelihoods, social and economic security" for the region's 270 million people that the disease could cause ; "If we do not act quickly to stop it and minimise its impact, the virus has the potential to turn into a social and economic catastrophe," said Dr Workneh before presenting a draft call to action for deliberation and adoption.

acts.speaker: IGAD health ministers
acts.speech: Discussed, on the guiding principle that "no country is safe until every country is safe", ways of operationalising the outcomes of the 30 March IGAD summit, including the development of an IGAD regional response strategy for COVID-19, the creation of an emergency fund for COVID-19 and other disease outbreaks and the strengthening of national response systems; they approved the outlines of a regional response plan (RRP) presented by the IGAD Secretariat and created a regional expert working group to coordinate and monitor the regional response, and issued a call-to-action document at the end of the meeting.

acts.speaker: Ibrahim Elbadawi, Minister of Finance of Sudan
acts.speech: Expressed his own and his country's determination to ensure that "COVID-19 does not translate into a recession curve" for the region and its people; he stressed that the IGAD region "cannot afford to be complacent" in the face of the current threat; he welcomed the initiative of a regional response in the context of promoting cooperation and ensuring that work is carried out not only at country level but also on a regional basis to mitigate the potential fallout and impact of COVID-19 on the region's economies.

acts.speaker: Jutta Urpilainen, European Union Commissioner for International Partnerships
acts.speech: Welcomed the fact that IGAD had held a summit, a meeting of health ministers and a meeting of finance ministers when she joined the conversation; the Commissioner announced the establishment of an EU financial package comprising "immediate humanitarian aid" and "support for strengthening health systems and mitigating the economic crisis."

title: Relation bilatérale: Diomaye Faye en visite de travail à Cotonou

acts.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
acts.speech: "Mr President, I would first like to thank you for all the marks of hospitality and the warm welcome extended to me here on the African soil of Benin, and to my delegation, and also to thank you for the quality of the exchanges we have had, with a wide-ranging tour of all the subjects of bilateral cooperation, but also and above all on the multilateral level, with the challenges confronting our sub-region today." ; "I will end my remarks by reiterating my thanks to President Talon and to the brotherly Beninese people, wishing you and all Beninese men and women a happy independence day in advance. Thank you very much."

acts.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
acts.speech: "As soon as I took office, I had undertaken a tour to pay my respects to my brother heads of State, and Benin figured very prominently in the calendar of those visits. Unfortunately, scheduling constraints and constraints external and internal to Senegal, but also scheduling constraints on your side, did not allow the visit to take place when I wanted it to, but I had nevertheless insisted on calling you on the telephone and telling you how impatient I was to meet you." ; "That telephone call obviously triggered much friendship between us, because you picked up that telephone with great warmth. We had at that moment a very fruitful discussion, which we have continued on the rare occasions when we have met."

acts.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
acts.speech: "We of course discussed the relations of friendship and cooperation between Benin [and Senegal], which are cordial and very convivial, even though both of us noted that today, given the quality of the relationship, we can do much more and much better in terms of trade."

acts.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
acts.speech: "We also spoke about the situation of the sub-region, both at the ECOWAS level and at the UEMOA level, but also about the security situation in the sub-region, which is very worrying. I took the opportunity to express all my solidarity with President Talon and with the brotherly Beninese people regarding the painful events that have occurred in the framework of the fight against terrorism, and to convey to him Senegal's support in those moments, by which we too are just as affected." ; "We also spoke about UEMOA which, as we know, is going through a somewhat difficult situation that we must address quickly, and President Talon and I agreed, in the very near future, to undertake steps to work on revitalising the organisation, to give it a new breath, of course with the support of the other fellow member States of the union." ; "As for ECOWAS, we have not long ago returned from a summit which was nonetheless a moment of constructive exchange among heads of State, and I recalled a short while ago to President Talon all the importance of the subjects we discussed and the challenges facing the organisation, which must, as in the case of UEMOA as well, obviously reform itself in order to be able to take on the challenges of our era."

title: CNG demands release of detained #EndBadGovernance protesters

acts.speaker: Daily Trust (report)
acts.speech: Had reported how 76 protesters who were arrested during the August 1 to August 10 #EndBadGovernance demonstration were brought to a Federal High Court in Abuja, on Friday.

acts.speaker: Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), statement by national coordinator Comrade Jamilu Aliyu Charanchi
acts.speech: Said the “detention and arraignment of those frail, malnourished and hapless children have exposed the government as a desperate entity that is determined to de-market and embarrass Nigeria before the international community while presenting its credentials for medals in gross inhumanity.” ; “The continued detention and mistreatment of these minors is a gross violation of their basic rights, including the right to freedom of expression and assembly. CNG strongly condemns this abuse of power and the blatant disregard for the welfare and dignity of young citizens.” ; “The treatment these children are receiving highlights a troubling failure of state actors to prioritize the welfare and rights of its most vulnerable citizens, children, especially when their ‘crime’ was to demand better governance and accountability.” ; “It is disheartening that in a country with a history of resilience and promise, minors are being made to endure starvation and harsh conditions while awaiting trial for daring to speak up for their future. This is not only a violation of domestic law but also contravenes international human rights principles protecting children from harm and unlawful detention.” ; “Ideally, those children are supposed to be treated first as victims of state abuse and deprivation whose leaders have failed to provide the necessary leadership that can mold them into better members of the society as they are a direct outcome of our decayed system.” ; “It is shamefully despicable that criminals and bandits that are holding the entire country to ransom do not face such stringent consequences for their actions.”

acts.speaker: Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), statement by national coordinator Comrade Jamilu Aliyu Charanchi
acts.speech: On government economic policy: “Evidently, the Government has consistently proven that people’s problems and deteriorating situations are not part of its priority because of its disregard for the daily hardships of its citizens. Increasingly, frequent blackouts have become a norm across the country, severely impacting homes, businesses, and essential services which became worse with the recent blackout.” ; “The elimination of fuel subsidies and constant raising of fuel prices have pushed the cost of living to record highs, making basic necessities even harder to afford. Instead of prioritizing the welfare of the populace by providing feasible alternatives or relief, the government’s priorities appear to be detaining, abusing and crushing the vulnerable children that need support and protection to grow into responsible adults.” ; “Unfortunately, hunger and starvation have become weapons against defenseless and malnourished teenagers. It is clear that the government’s neglect of essential services and its catastrophic economic policies have strangulated millions in a state of uncertainty, desperation, and disillusionment in which these minors belong. These children must not be targeted as the scapegoat for expressing their frustrations as Nigerians have never gone through such dehumanizing and cruel policies that this administration promotes.”

acts.speaker: Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG) (statement)
acts.speech: Called for the immediate and unconditional release of all the minors detained for participating in the protests: “We demand that the government prioritize dialogue and constructive engagement over intimidation, especially with young citizens who represent the future of this nation.” ; “In the interim, we urge relevant agencies and civil society organizations to provide immediate humanitarian assistance to these detained children to mitigate further health risks. The protection of children is non-negotiable, and we implore the authorities to treat these young citizens with the compassion and respect they deserve.”

title: Pour une éducation préscolaire de qualité, inclusive et équitable

acts.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
acts.speech: In her speech, emphasised the importance of preschool education as an essential foundation for children's futures. She further highlighted the multiple benefits that allow pupils to develop early skills, to be better prepared for primary school, and to significantly reduce the risks of dropping out of school.

acts.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
acts.speech: Addressing in particular the children who had just started school: "I am delighted by the adventure you are embarking on. School is a place for fun, for making friends, for singing songs, and for learning about your country and the world. You have the support of your parents, your teachers, your communities, the government and USAID," she declared, before praising the efforts of the 'Play to Learn' programme teams and of the actors involved, affirming that their dedication is a source of inspiration for building a promising future for the children of Djibouti.

acts.speaker: Lauren Greubel, Deputy Representative of USAID in Djibouti
acts.speech: "The Djiboutian government is making considerable efforts to offer every child the right to a quality education." ; "USAID's project 'Play to Learn' aims to increase the number of children benefiting from a quality education. A quality, inclusive preschool education can have a significant impact on children's learning outcomes for the rest of their lives. Preschool programmes offer many benefits to pupils, their families and their communities. Pupils develop early academic skills and are better prepared to enter primary school. The data has shown that when children attend preschool, they are more likely to complete secondary school, their dropout rate is reduced, and their learning outcomes are better. Through the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training and the Ministry of Women and Family, the Djiboutian government is making considerable efforts to find lasting solutions to offer every child, and particularly children in vulnerable situations, the right to a quality education."

acts.speaker: Fozia Ibrahim, Head of the Preschool Service of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
acts.speech: For her part, highlighted the importance of this partnership for strengthening the capacities of private preschool establishments, but also reminded parents of the importance of monitoring their children's attendance.

title: Trump administration proposes scrapping UN peacekeeping funding

acts.speaker: Internal planning documents seen by Reuters
acts.speech: According to internal planning documents seen by Reuters, the White House budget office has proposed eliminating funding for United Nations peacekeeping missions, citing failures by operations in Mali, Lebanon and Democratic Republic of Congo.

acts.speaker: Tammy Bruce, State Department spokesperson
acts.speech: "There is no final plan, final budget," she told reporters on Tuesday when asked about the OMB proposals.

acts.speaker: Office of Management and Budget "Passback" document
acts.speech: Proposed ending Contributions for International Peacekeeping Activities (CIPA): "For example, Passback provides no funding for CIPA, ending contributions for international peacekeeping due to the recent failures in peacekeeping, such as with MINUSMA, UNIFIL, and MONUSCO, and the disproportionately high level of assessments."

acts.speaker: Office of Management and Budget "Passback" document
acts.speech: Proposed the creation of a $2.1 billion America First Opportunities Fund (A1OF), which it said would be used to cover a limited set of foreign economic and development assistance priorities: "Should the Administration seek to pay any assessments for the United Nations Regular Budget or peacekeeping assessments, we would look to provide that funding from the A1OF."

acts.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, U.N. spokesperson
acts.speech: On Tuesday declined to comment on "what appears to be a leaked memo that is part of an internal debate within the U.S. government."

acts.speaker: Antonio Guterres, U.N. Secretary-General
acts.speech: Last month said he is seeking ways to improve efficiency and cut costs as the world body turns 80 this year amid a cash crisis.

title: Challenges Facing Nigeria’s Oil And Gas Industry Are Multifaceted – Osifo

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said on accountability and divestment that “Accountability is a basic principle of good governance. We are redefining our approach with International Oil and Gas companies, including governments, the private sector, to become less bureaucratic and more agile, effective and efficient”, that the major task before PENGASSAN leadership was how to protect the jobs of members and the existing collective bargaining agreement, and that the association has concluded agreements covering the NAOC–Oando divestment, the Mobil Producing Nigeria–Seplat divestment and the Equinor–Chappal Energy divestment, while stopping all conversations with Shell over the SPDC–Renaissance sale because government declined approval.

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said the leadership of the association across all levels has been engaging different managements at all sub-sectoral levels in negotiating new collective bargaining agreements, and that “We have been able to secure a cumulative increase of 150% to over 200% increment for our members in some branches.”

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said the oil and gas sector faces immense challenges that threaten not only its sustainability but also the prosperity of the nation, that “the challenges facing Nigeria’s oil and gas industry are multifaceted and deeply intertwined with our social, economic, and environmental fabric”, but that these challenges can be turned into opportunities through a commitment to transparency, inclusivity, and innovation.

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said on host communities that harnessing Nigeria’s environmental protection regulations requires a multi-faceted approach focusing on regulatory enforcement, community engagement, proactive environmental management and legal framework enhancement, so that regulations translate into tangible improvements and end youth restiveness and communal conflicts, and called “for a 100% implementation of the provision of host communities in the Petroleum Industry Act.”

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said on the tax reforms that tax relief exemptions given to those earning minimum wage and businesses should be expanded, that clarity must be provided regarding revenue collection processes from oil and gas companies because some provisions could negatively impact members in branches like NUPRC and NMDPRA, and called on the National Assembly “to conduct a proper public hearing session where different views will be collated to amend the provisions in the bill and not just to tick the box.”

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said Nigeria faces a looming food crisis of immense proportions and that PENGASSAN demands the government support both commercial and smallholder farmers through access to credit, improved seeds, fertilisers and technology, strengthening farmer cooperatives and market linkages, investing in roads, storage facilities and irrigation to reduce post-harvest losses, and providing a secure environment enabling farmers who abandoned their farms to return.

acts.speaker: Cadre Harmonisé Report for October 2024
acts.speech: Recently projected that at least 33.1 million people in 26 states and the FCT will face a food and nutrition crisis between June and August 2025.

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said on the power sector that Nigeria’s continuous decline in power generation and transmission is profoundly disappointing and a significant cause of the terrible quality of life and economic downturn, that despite tariff increases “we have witnessed the national grid collapse over 6 times this year alone… the worst frequency in our country’s history”, and that the union advocates decentralising power transmission and involving state governments and private sector players, citing Abia State as a good example.

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said on economic policy that there must be information-sharing with stakeholders, especially civil society organisations working on financial management, criticising that countries go to the IMF and World Bank for loans approved without details or oversight of implementation; called for serious reforms for economic stability, noting corruption-driven backsliding, factory closures, failure to collect revenue from multinational corporations and wealthy individuals, absence of property taxation, and dilapidation of health, education and physical infrastructure through diversion and theft of public funds, and said it is important that the IMF/World Bank democratise information and create opportunities for interaction.

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said investment and employment in Nigeria are constrained by high cost and difficulty of accessing credit, problems securing property rights and enforcing contracts, weak energy, transport and communications infrastructure, business registration delays, lack of transparency in regulation and deficiencies in education and skills; that most Nigerian enterprises, many operated by women, remain trapped in the informal economy; and that Nigeria needs a strategy for sustainable enterprise development and decent work including an enabling environment, a better investment climate, macroeconomic stability, respect for workers’ rights, good governance and particular attention to MSMEs and women’s entrepreneurship.

acts.speaker: Festus Osifo, National President of PENGASSAN and President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC)
acts.speech: Said the urgency of the ‘Africa Solution To African Problems’ quest comes from optimism that Africa’s growth can be led by young people, that timely investment in education and health can spur a demographic dividend since by 2075 one-third of the world’s population and working-age population will be African, that Africa’s Heads of State need to accelerate human capital accumulation, leverage the youth bulge and create jobs, and that Africa is battling a learning crisis with the percentage of 10-year-olds unable to understand a simple text projected to approach 89% after the COVID pandemic.

title: South Africa's Ramaphosa to lead HIV/AIDS Global Fund replenishment

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
acts.speech: Announced South African President Cyril Ramaphosa’s agreement to take charge of the upcoming three-year funding cycle of the Global Fund at a press conference in Johannesburg on Friday: “The Global Fund replenishment is critical and it’s great that South Africa has offered to lead that.”

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
acts.speech: Told reporters that AIDS “is very much an African disease now, with 75% of people living with HIV being on this continent.”

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
acts.speech: Said that a smaller amount of foreign aid means a plan to end the disease as a public health threat by 2030 “will get more and more off-track” ; said that while poor African countries are working hard to fill the sudden gap created by President Donald Trump’s decision to halt US aid, they are going to have to do more with less, and added that there was also an urgent need to restructure their debts to cut debt-service costs that can be many times larger than their healthcare budgets.

acts.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the Joint United Nations Program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
acts.speech: “South Africa is a leader and the region itself has been making progress and can continue making progress in spite of the funding freeze by the American government”, but it “needs to move faster on reducing new infections”, and on ensuring key at-risk communities including migrants, men who have sex with men, sex workers and drug users have appropriate services.

title: Lutte contre l’hémorragie post-partum : L’Unfpa apporte un soutien de 80 millions de FCfa au gouvernement

acts.speaker: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), through the "Safe Birth Africa" project
acts.speech: Holds that no woman should lose her life while giving life.

acts.speaker: Diene Keita, Executive Director of UNFPA
acts.speech: Said the gesture goes well beyond a simple handover of medicines, that it embodies a collective promise: to do everything possible so that every Ivorian woman has access to quality care allowing her to give birth safely; and that her organisation reaffirms its determination to support the government and all its partners in building policies and programmes guaranteeing universal access to safe, equitable and quality maternal health services. "Together, let us continue our efforts to build a future in which motherhood will never again be synonymous with danger, but will remain what it must be: a moment of life, joy and fulfilment."

acts.speaker: Charles Aka Koffi, Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Welcomed the implementation of the Safe Birth Africa project: "Thanks to this investment, access to health services for pregnant women will be markedly improved, particularly in the Gbeke and Gontougo regions, and, on the other hand, the infrastructure and skills of health personnel will be strengthened." ; "The Safe Birth Africa project will be an opportunity for Côte d'Ivoire to further consolidate its gains in maternal and child health."

acts.speaker: Charles Aka Koffi, Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Hailed the inclusion of reproductive health among development priorities and the support of the African Development Bank (AfDB), which aims to strengthen reproductive health services, including family planning, maternal and child care, and the fight against sexually transmitted diseases, with the aim of improving quality of life in Africa.

acts.speaker: Clarisse Kayo Mahi, Chair of the Board of Directors of the New Public Health Pharmacy of Côte d'Ivoire (NPSP-CI)
acts.speech: Stated that the gesture highlights the fruitful partnership between Côte d'Ivoire and UNFPA, supported by the AfDB, recalling that since 2014 the partnership between NPSP-CI and UNFPA has made it possible to manage, on behalf of the National Mother and Child Health Programme, at least 1 billion CFA francs of health products per year for reproductive health and family planning. "It is therefore a pleasure for me to welcome this partnership of more than ten years in the field of mother and child health, which will continue with the recent signing of the tripartite agreement between the Ministry of Health, UNFPA and NPSP-CI for a renewable period of 12 months."

acts.speaker: Irchad Ramiandrasoa Razaaly, Representative of the European Union in Côte d'Ivoire
acts.speech: Reaffirmed the Union's commitment to strengthening the Ivorian health system to promote a better quality of life for all the women and young people of the country.

title: Atupele Muluzi Warns of Growing Threat to Democracy in Malawi - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
acts.speech: Raised alarm over what he describes as a growing threat to democracy in Malawi, warning that the country is on a dangerous path toward autocratic rule and internal decay; told fellow leaders at the Platform for African Democrats (PAD) conference in Angola that Malawi is experiencing a rollback of democratic principles amid rising global instability and weakening international cooperation: “We are witnessing a dangerous shift: a retreat from the principles that have long underpinned democratic governance. Truth itself has become a casualty, with disinformation distorting the foundations of informed political discourse.” ; Pointed to the consolidation of power by autocratic regimes across the continent, adding that such trends have emboldened leaders who undermine democracy through coercion rather than consent ; Accused several African governments of falling prey to kleptocracy, describing them as “government by the corrupt, for the corrupt,” where leaders prioritize personal enrichment over public service.

acts.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
acts.speech: Accused the current administration of using undemocratic tactics to cling to power: “The current administration has failed to deliver on its economic and social promises. Facing near-certain electoral defeat, it is resorting to undemocratic means to maintain control” ; urged Malawians to resist any attempts to subvert democratic norms and called on Malawians to speak with a united voice to defend the country’s democracy: “This is our moment to stand firm for democracy. We cannot allow our democracy to be stolen.”

acts.speaker: Atupele Muluzi, United Democratic Front (UDF) leader
acts.speech: Highlighted the impact of shrinking international support, citing the scaling back of donor agencies such as USAID, and warned that Africa is being left to tackle economic stagnation, agricultural insecurity, corruption, and poor governance largely on its own: “Yet, this is precisely when we need greater collaboration to tackle Africa’s pressing challenges.”

acts.speaker: Malawi government officials
acts.speech: Did not immediately respond to Muluzi’s claims.

title: EFF Condemns President Ramaphosa’s ‘Reckless’ Interaction with Elon Musk Over Diplomatic Protocol Breach - Malawi News | Breaking News, Politics, Business & Sports | Nyasa Times

acts.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
acts.speech: Sharply criticized South African President Cyril Ramaphosa for allegedly breaching diplomatic protocols after contacting billionaire Elon Musk regarding the recently enacted Expropriation Act; labeled Ramaphosa's actions as "reckless," accusing him of compromising South Africa's sovereignty to appease U.S. interests; expressed dismay over Ramaphosa's direct engagement with Musk, an unelected U.S. business figure. "This breaking of diplomatic protocol should never be taken lightly" - describing it as symptomatic of a "dependency syndrome" on Western influence.

acts.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
acts.speech: Accused Musk of exploiting his ties with former U.S. President Donald Trump to pressure South African authorities into easing regulatory barriers for his satellite company, Starlink, saying Musk's push undermines South Africa's Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) policy, which mandates that foreign-owned satellite firms allocate at least 30% ownership to historically disadvantaged South Africans.

acts.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
acts.speech: Criticized Ramaphosa's inconsistency, noting that just days earlier the government reprimanded Minister Gwede Mantashe for diplomatic missteps when he threatened to restrict mineral exports to the U.S. over foreign aid disputes.

acts.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
acts.speech: "The President's conduct risks opening the door to state capture" - drawing parallels to South Africa's troubled past with the Gupta family during Jacob Zuma's administration; urged Ramaphosa to avoid relying on foreign billionaires to shape national policy, stressing the importance of upholding diplomatic protocols and protecting South Africa's sovereignty.

title: Guerre au Liban : le Maroc appelle à un cessez-le-feu immédiat

acts.speaker: Kingdom of Morocco (official position at the Paris conference)
acts.speech: Morocco called on Thursday for an immediate and complete ceasefire in Lebanon, at an international conference in Paris, calling for respect for the nation's sovereignty and the dignity of its people.

acts.speaker: Fouad Yazourh, Morocco's ambassador and director general of bilateral relations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Speaking on behalf of Morocco, stressed that Lebanon should not continue to suffer from conflicts fuelled by regional agendas ; "Lebanon cannot and must not continue to bear the burden of conflicts taking place elsewhere," adding that these conflicts have exhausted the country ; expressed Morocco's support for immediate international action, calling on the United Nations to supervise a ceasefire and facilitate the return of displaced persons with guarantees of protection ; stressed the need for the Lebanese authorities to manage humanitarian aid, alongside international efforts to rebuild the country ; reiterated Morocco's solidarity with Lebanon, calling for "reason and diplomacy to prevail," and called for a simultaneous political approach, alongside the ceasefire, to establish a just and stable peace in the Middle East.

acts.speaker: Fouad Yazourh, Morocco's ambassador and director general of bilateral relations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
acts.speech: Recalled that Morocco, led by King Mohammed VI, has advocated a comprehensive solution to the region's crisis; stressed that the Palestinian question was at the heart of the broader Middle East conflict, reiterating Morocco's long-standing position that a two-State solution is essential for lasting peace ; "An independent Palestine, with Gaza as an integral part and East Jerusalem as its capital, is necessary for any lasting security in the region."

acts.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
acts.speech: His constant message that without a resolution of the Palestinian question, tensions will persist.

title: Vinodia Janete

acts.speech: Considers that the pressure exerted on the Indian Ocean by Illegal and Undeclared Fishing may be coming to an end. Nyusi was speaking in the context of the start of construction of the SADC Fisheries Monitoring and Surveillance Centre, whose foundation stone was laid on Monday in the Ka-Tembe Municipal District, in the city of Maputo.

acts.speaker: Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade of Mozambique
acts.speech: Presented a new proposal to the Vice-Minister of Commerce of the People's Republic of China, on the sidelines of the Sixth Macau Forum Conference, for Chinese government financing of the construction of the new infrastructure for the Maputo International Fair site at Ricatla, in Marracuene District.

title: Seeking Local Sustainable Funding Source For Development Work In Nigeria

acts.speaker: Sir Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
acts.speech: Has recently announced a boost to the UK defence spending, with the increase coming at the expense of the aid budget; explained that the increase will see an additional 13.4bn pounds on defence every year from 2027, but that it will be paid for by cutting development assistance aid.

acts.speaker: Government of the Netherlands

acts.speech: Cited the BOTA Foundation as one of the most effective and successful examples of asset return administration.
