title: Primature : Retour du Premier ministre burundais en provenance de la Tanzanie

acts.speaker: Gervais Ndirakobuca, Prime Minister of the Republic of Burundi
acts.speech: "We discussed the security situation prevailing in eastern DRC in order to find the necessary solutions for the restoration of peace and security," the Burundian head of government indicated ; added that he had shown the heads of state and government of the two Communities that the insecurity prevailing in the DRC disrupts regional security, including that of Burundi, especially with the presence of the terrorist group Red Tabara present in that region ; went on to say that during these meetings measures were taken for the restoration of peace and stability in eastern DRC, citing in particular the immediate cessation of hostilities in order to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of the wounded and the dead.

acts.speaker: Joint SADC-EAC Summit of heads of state and government
acts.speech: also concluded that the Rwandan troops supporting the M23 have no reason to be on Congolese soil and must return home, and likewise that the other foreign troops on Congolese soil that were not invited by the Congolese government must leave the country; an unconditional ceasefire, support in humanitarian aid to the victims of the hostilities, the repatriation of the wounded, etc. It was also agreed to establish protection of Goma airport and its surroundings, the roads of the city of Goma, and the opening of the airport and Lake Kivu to facilitate movement; the immediate resumption of dialogue within the framework of the Nairobi process and the Luanda protocol was addressed and the presidents of the two Communities were asked to seek mediators.

title: Public outcry against Minister’s absence - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Citizens of Maryland County speaking on a local radio talk show
acts.speech: Speaking on a local radio talk show in the county, many citizens, in anger, wondered whether the Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Public Works, is concerned about Liberians' safety and free movement. According to them, such a great occasion that will bring relief to peoples of both countries, attended by representatives from ECOWAS, SHAANXI Construction Engineering Corporation LTD, and Engineers from Côte d'Ivoire, was held without the presence of Minister Giddings or any representative of the Ministry of Public Works ; the citizens termed Minister Giddings's response embarrassing because they were looking forward to seeing him perform at the event, as it would've drawn the attention of ECOWAS and Chinese engineers gearing up for the project ; according to them, despite their excitement and anticipation, the Public Works Ministry was nowhere around, which they described as worrisome and questionable.

acts.speaker: Roland Giddings, Liberian Minister of Public Works (relayed through ECOWAS Project Manager Ashok Maliki)
acts.speech: Contacted during the opening of the program as to why he had not arrived when his Ivorian counterparts were already present at the occasion, responded that he was stuck in the mud near Nimbia County in Liberia.

acts.speaker: Pastor Abraham Togba, resident of Zone 7A and caller on the radio talk show
acts.speech: Laments that the absence of Liberian officials at such a great occasion wasn't only embarrassing but disgraceful to the entire country because President Boakai can't be everywhere and that's why he appointed cabinet ministers to fill such gap, but notes that to have heard the Minister saying he wasn't present because his vehicle stuck in the mud, was a big shame ; adds that such an excuse was very poor, stressing that Giddings had been invited and informed about the event days before the ceremony ; “So the Minister who should've had the roads fixed is crying of being stuck; what happens to ordinary Liberians that use the roads on a daily basis?” ; continues that Liberians will now begin to notice the change they made in the poll, whether it's positive or negative, adding that it's so early for people to start criticizing the government for not attending important events.

acts.speaker: Jerryling Geetah, caller from Zone 11
acts.speech: “I can't believe that the Public Works Ministry or Minister didn't show up. We have been praying tirelessly for years to make this event a success, and he couldn't even spare a few hours to unbrace such a great occasion.” ; explains that there are reasons why such things are happening in Liberia, such as people's unwillingness to correct wrongs; points out that even in the Minister's absence, the County Resident Engineer should have shown up, pointing out that the program wasn't held secretly or behind closed doors ; believes that Liberian officials didn't turn out only because ECOWAS did not bring money to share, noting that had that been the case, the entire place would've been filled with Liberian officials ; calls on President Boakai to take such occasions seriously and take action against officials who downplay them because this could undermine his government's growth and development ; “So to say, we are watching because we will not allow any government officials to stop our progress and developments. Other countries are moving forward, and we are still behind due to some officials' attitudes.”

acts.speaker: Jacob Towliad, supporter of the ruling Unity Party and public school teacher
acts.speech: Criticizes the Public Works Minister's absence: “I thought Minister Giddings would've come for sure because road connectivity has always been his involvement and activities. I can't believe he has made such a statement.” ; maintains that, given the importance attached to the project, it was prudent that the Minister should've taken a flight to Maryland, as he claimed the roads were bad ; “Let me say, it was a failure on the part of the Minister and the local officials of the county because their presence was very important during such an occasion.”

acts.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
acts.speech: Disclosed that official groundbreaking for the project will be done hopefully in November this year and is expected to bring together the Presidents of both countries when the Public Works Minister may attend ; says the bridge project is an ECOWAS Commission's initiative through its President in collaboration with the African Development Bank as a way of giving back to 400 million people living within the West African region.

title: More HIV patients not on treatment – New report reveals

acts.speaker: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC), 2024 national and sub-national HIV estimates and projections
acts.speech: Revealed that more than half of the people living with HIV/AIDS have not sought the life-saving antiretroviral therapy treatment; the commission reports that 334,721 people living with HIV, accounting for 47 per cent of that population, are currently on antiretroviral therapy treatment, with 52.6 per cent without treatment. The commission described the situation as "alarming", warning of its potential to derail national efforts to control the epidemic, and said the current situation had left the lives of the entire population, including non-HIV patients, at risk.

acts.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission
acts.speech: Said the figures fell short of the global 95-95-95 targets set by UNAIDS, for 95 per cent of people living with HIV to know their status, 95 per cent of those diagnosed to be on treatment and 95 per cent of those on treatment to achieve viral suppression.

acts.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission
acts.speech: Explained that 15,290 new HIV infections were recorded in 2024 alone, and that although 12,614 AIDS-related deaths were recorded, an estimated 12,358 deaths were prevented due to access to treatment; he said the data underscored the urgent need to expand access to antiretroviral therapy treatment. He stated that women and children continued to bear a disproportionate burden, with 68.5 per cent (10,303) of new infections occurring in females and 5.4 per cent (1,243) in children under 15; he remarked that although Ghana boasts that 99.3 per cent of HIV-positive mothers now receive prevention of mother-to-child transmission, more needed to be done to ensure effective follow-up and treatment, and added that the records for males were 4,987, while adults aged 15 and older recorded 11,289 out of the 15,290 new cases.

acts.speaker: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo, Deputy Chief of Staff
acts.speech: Said issues such as misinformation, disinformation, stigma, discrimination, individual economic challenges, inadequate lifesaving services and recent funding cuts had contributed to derail progress. "Regardless, we are determined to ensure sustained domestic financing, including the recent suspension of USAID's international funding programme; integrate HIV priorities into broader health and development strategies, and adopt innovative, data-driven approaches to enhance service delivery. No one should be left behind in our HIV response," she emphasised.

acts.speaker: Nana Oye Bampoe Addo, Deputy Chief of Staff
acts.speech: Cautioned that every HIV-positive person who was not on treatment was one step closer to advanced illness and AIDS-related death, which she said was unacceptable, and stressed that especially in present times there should not be such a wide treatment gap; as Ghana prepares to host the 2025 ICASA conference, she called on stakeholders, government institutions, health workers, donors, researchers, community advocates and civil society leaders to reflect deeply on the findings from these estimates and turn them into purposeful action.

title: Au Burkina, des médecins réalisent une exérèse tumorale complexe

acts.speaker: Dr Boa Jacques, doctor (Odontostomatology/Maxillofacial Surgery department, CHR of Fada)
acts.speech: According to him, a significant need remains unmet in the treatment of disfiguring conditions, which are often neglected by traditional humanitarian aid ; "These conditions seriously compromise the social reintegration and psychological well-being of patients. It is therefore essential to mobilise more resources and to raise NGOs' awareness of this problem. The current security context constitutes a major obstacle to access to care. Yet, with appropriate support, significant potential remains untapped to help a greater number of people."

title: This is why Justice Gertrude Torkornoo has been removed as Chief Justice and Justice on Supreme Court bench [FULL DETAILS]

acts.speaker: Committee of inquiry into the petitions against Chief Justice Torkornoo (report)
acts.speech: Recommended her removal from office based on its findings; in the opinion of the committee, the travel expenses which Justice Torkornoo “heaped on the Judicial Service when she travelled on holidays in September 2023, first to Tanzania with her husband and second, to the United States of America with her daughter, together with the payment of per diem to the spouse and daughter of the Chief Justice, constituted unlawful expenditure of public funds”, which it indicated cannot be justified in law or policy; those acts, it said, “constitute avoidable and reckless dissipation of public funds and, in the view of the committee, to have been occasioned by the overall head of the Judiciary and the Judicial Service, whose duty is to guard pubic resources allocated by the Government, is caught within the spectrum of stated misbehaviour.”

acts.speaker: Committee of inquiry into the petitions against Chief Justice Torkornoo (report)
acts.speech: Stated without fear or favour that the Chief Justice unjustifiably breached the provisions in article 295(a) and (b) of the Constitution, 1992, in the way and manner that she transferred one Mr Baiden, a staff of the Judicial Service, and said her conduct amounted to misbehaviour ; Indicated it was of the view that the conduct of Justice Torkornoo falls squarely in the category of conduct described as stated misbehaviour under article 146(1) of the Constitution, and that her action and conduct fell within the meaning and categories of stated misbehaviour as provided under article 146(1) of the Constitution, 1992.

acts.speaker: Committee of inquiry into the petitions against Chief Justice Torkornoo (report)
acts.speech: On the allegation of her request in a letter to former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo for the appointment of more justices to the Supreme Court bench and her recommendation of certain names, said Justice Torkornoo cannot lay claim to ignorance of the nomination process and procedure, notwithstanding that the process is not spelt out in the Constitution but case law, noting that her own appointment as a Justice of the Supreme Court went through the very process set out in the Ghana Bar Association case: “Therefore, to seek, wittingly, to outwit this known process and procedure for appointing Supreme Court Justices amounts to misbehaviour in the eyes of the Committee and the Committee finds it as such.”

acts.speaker: Committee of inquiry into the petitions against Chief Justice Torkornoo (report)
acts.speech: Found, within a four-month period of hearing, that the grounds of stated misbehaviour under Article 146(1) had been established and recommended her removal from office.

acts.speaker: President John Dramani Mahama (instrument of removal)
acts.speech: “Now therefore, know ye all men that I, John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, in pursuance of the said Article 146 (9), do hereby REMOVE the said Chief Justice, Gertrude Araba Esaaba Sackey Torkornoo, from the office of Chief Justice and Justice of the Supreme Court, with effect from the date hereof. In witness whereof, I have hereunto set my hand caused the Presidential Seal to be affixed at Accra this 1st of Sept 2025.”

acts.speaker: Presidency of Ghana (press statement, September 1, 2025)
acts.speech: Said the move was in accordance with Article 149 (9) of the 1992 Constitution: “President John Dramani Mahama has, in accordance with Article 146(9) of the 1992 Constitution, removed the Chief Justice, Her Ladyship Justice Gertrude Araba Esaaba Sackey Torkonoo, from office with immediate effect. This follows receipt of the report of the Committee constituted under Article 146(6) to inquire into a petition submitted by a Ghanaian citizen, Mr Daniel Ofori. After considering the petition and the evidence, the Committee found that the grounds of stated misbehaviour under Article 146(1) had been established and recommended her removal from office. Under Article 146(9), the President is required to act in accordance with the committee’s recommendation.”

acts.speaker: Daniel Ofori, Ghanaian citizen (petition dated March 17, 2025)
acts.speech: Petitioned the President to remove Justice Torkornoo from office on the grounds of misconduct and stated misbehaviour as Chief Justice.

acts.speaker: 1992 Constitution of Ghana, Article 146(9)
acts.speech: Stipulates that “The President shall, in each case, act in accordance with the recommendations of the committee.”

title: Malawian youth ambassador showcases country's culture and tourism potential in Beijing

acts.speaker: Blessings Chiwosi, Malawian youth ambassador and student at China Agricultural University
acts.speech: “I feel it is every citizen’s duty to utilize such opportunities for the betterment of our country’s development,” he said, adding that “Malawi has a lot of resources that can attract noble investors for her economic growth, hence taking part in this cultural event.” ; “I am representing Malawi not only because it is less popular in other parts of the world but also for positioning it for socioeconomic returns to address challenges that people face, which need innovative ways and solutions through tourism.”

title: Bientôt, un premier salon sur les études supérieures en France

acts.speaker: Gilles Ganivet, cooperation and cultural action counsellor of the Embassy of France in Burundi
acts.speech: “A first fair – I repeat it, and I am very happy and proud – a first fair organised in Burundi,” he exclaimed during a press conference on 25 April; according to him, this first fair will be held on Tuesday 2 May 2023, with an institutional session in the morning from 9 a.m. bringing together French and Burundian higher education institutions at the French Institute of Burundi, and the fair open to students at the French School of Bujumbura in the afternoon at 1:30 p.m. and the following day, Wednesday 3 May 2023, from 9 a.m.

acts.speaker: Perrine Chuker, head of Campus France
acts.speech: “Different French higher education institutions will be here in Bujumbura from 1 to 4 May to meet Burundian higher education institutions. The idea is to be able to forge future partnerships between these various institutions.” ; She explains that students will meet the French higher education institutions at their stands: “Students will be able to move freely between the stands and will be able to meet around ten French higher education institutions that will be present at the French School of Bujumbura.” ; “Entry will be free. The exact programme as well as all the schools that will be present will be announced on the website of Campus France Burundi and on social media.”

acts.speaker: The organisers
acts.speech: According to the organisers, students' choice is driven by academic and research excellence, the low cost of higher education and the variety of its higher education offer.

title: USAID implementing partners renew calls to end GBV in South Sudan - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: USAID's implementing partners
acts.speech: Have reiterated calls for an end to violence against women and girls in South Sudan, as the country marks 16 Days of Activism against Gender Based Violence; speaking on Eye Radio's Dawn Show on November 25, the U.S. agency's implementing partners said women and girls should be protected and respected in the country.

acts.speaker: World Health Organization
acts.speech: According to the World Health Organization, globally, one in three women experience either intimate partner violence or non-partner sexual violence during their lifetime.

acts.speaker: Boboya James, senior technical advisor with Sustainable Independent Media Activity (SIMA)
acts.speech: Called for collective efforts to end GBV in South Sudan ; "We need to continue to promote the women voice in South Sudan" ; "We need to continue to build leadership around women-like initiatives, and we should continue to support initiatives like the media, where you produce a lot of content and begin to increase talks, outreach, roundtable discussion of these topics" ; said there should be dialogue with government officials to engage them in taking up their responsibilities of implementing some of the laws and policies ; "Awareness in community level is very important, a lot of funding is going to local organizations to be able to capitalize on this GBV related issues in the communities."

acts.speaker: Gloria George, Gender Based Violence Officer with UNICEF
acts.speech: Says for GBV to end in the country, there is need for collective efforts ; "One hand cannot do it, so everybody needs to come on board and we see how this GBV really comes to an end" ; "We have to create an environment that women and girls, even men and boys are able to move freely, are able to interact, are able to say what is in their mind and have the positive change that we need."

acts.speaker: Caroline Hlatywayo, gender specialist of the Resilience through Agriculture Activity (RASS)
acts.speech: Said communities need to be empowered to do away with cases of GBV in the country ; "Let us work on strengthening local capacity and community engagement. We need to empower communities to identify and address the root causes of GBV and leverage their inside into social, cultural and economic factor."

acts.speaker: Museme Munira, USAID's Gender Specialist
acts.speech: Said realizing the importance of working together and collaborating across different institutions, stakeholders, development partners and women and girls is key to winning the war on GBV ; "This is something that affects all of us, and for many nations that have moved ahead in dealing with issues of reducing GBV and focusing on empowering all sections of society have had very great progress. We would like to see that in South Sudan that we have progress."

title: Réunion virtuelle des chefs d’Etats et gouvernements: Des réformes institutionnelles fortes pour la réalisation de l’Agenda 2063 de l’Union africaine

acts.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
acts.speech: Said the meeting, chaired by Kenyan President William Ruto, the current AU chairman, was held in order to inaugurate the special committee of Heads of State and Government overseeing the institutional reforms of the African Union.

acts.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
acts.speech: In his speech on behalf of the Burundian Head of State: "The will of the Heads of State and Government to reform our African Union in depth reflects a shared aspiration to endow our continent with strong, coherent institutions adapted to the challenges of the 21st century. These reforms are the foundation on which the realisation of Agenda 2063 rests, that of an integrated, prosperous and peaceful Africa, an Africa that we want, an Africa that we must build together."

acts.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
acts.speech: Affirmed that Burundi firmly supports the reform of the African Union's financing system, stating that the organisation's budgetary autonomy is the only key to its independence and credibility, and indicated that the effective implementation of the 0.2% levy on eligible imports is crucial to guarantee the financial independence of the African Union, as well as its political sovereignty and freedom of action ; Mentioned that the main objective of the reform is to ensure the financial sovereignty of the continent in order to build together an African Union worthy of its ideals, at the service of its peoples, an African Union of dignity, results and hope.

acts.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
acts.speech: "Today, our organisation is evolving in a world confronted with multiple crises of political instability, security threats, climate change, economic and social challenges. These trials undermine the resilience and credibility of our organisation. And yet, it is in these moments of challenge that our determination must assert itself. And whatever the situation, we must build a more robust African Union, capable of acting quickly and effectively to defend the principles of its constitutive Charter." ; Insisted that AU member states must rationalise their institutions, eliminate duplication and optimise the use of their own resources, because a Union that depends too much on external financing risks losing its freedom of decision ; "That is why we must redouble our efforts to strengthen our autonomy, while consolidating coordination between the Commission, the Regional Economic Communities and the member states." ; Underlined that the simplification of the AU's structures is an imperative for an African Union worthy of its ambitions.

acts.speaker: Prosper Bazombanza, Vice-President of the Republic of Burundi
acts.speech: "And the government of Burundi, through the leadership of President Evariste Ndayishimiye, commits to contributing actively to this process, convinced that an effective, financially autonomous and strategically coherent African Union is the indispensable condition for our shared ambition, that of a sovereign, respected and influential Africa on the world stage."

title: UN nuclear watchdog board passes resolution criticising Iran

acts.speaker: Three diplomats (anonymous)
acts.speech: Told AFP on Wednesday that the International Atomic Energy Agency's 35-nation board of governors has passed a resolution criticising Iran's lack of cooperation with the UN nuclear watchdog ; told AFP that the resolution was carried by 20 votes in favour -- including the United States, which initially was reluctant for fear of aggravating Middle East tensions -- with 12 abstentions and one country not participating.

acts.speaker: IAEA Board of Governors resolution (confidential document obtained by AFP)
acts.speech: Reiterates it is "essential and urgent" that Tehran provide "technically credible explanations" for the presence of uranium particles found at two undeclared locations in Iran ; states that "A continued failure" by Iran to provide full cooperation on the years-long probe "may necessitate" a comprehensive assessment by IAEA chief Rafael Grossi ; says Iran has to "reverse its withdrawal of the designations of several experienced Agency inspectors", and "without delay" reconnect the cameras used to monitor nuclear activities ; notes the "concerns" surrounding "recent public statements made in Iran... regarding its technical capabilities to produce nuclear weapons and possible changes to Iran's nuclear doctrine".

acts.speaker: Tehran (Iranian government)
acts.speech: Has already threatened "a serious and effective response", and slammed the censure motion as "devoid of any legal, technical and political basis".

acts.speaker: European powers at the IAEA Board of Governors debates
acts.speech: Denounced Iran's expansion of its nuclear programme "to alarming levels" as "unprecedented for a state without a nuclear weapons programme".

acts.speaker: Britain, France and Germany (the E3), separate statement
acts.speech: "Iran's escalating nuclear activities significantly harm international security and undermine the global non-proliferation architecture."

acts.speaker: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)
acts.speech: According to the IAEA, Iran is the only non-nuclear weapon state to enrich uranium to the high level of 60 percent -- just short of weapons-grade -- while it keeps accumulating large uranium stockpiles.

acts.speaker: Tehran, Moscow and Beijing (joint statement quoted by Iran's official news agency IRNA)
acts.speech: Called on "Western countries to show political will... and take the necessary steps to resume the implementation" of the 2015 nuclear deal.

acts.speaker: United States (national statement to the IAEA board)
acts.speech: Rejected that assertion as "a tired and transparent gambit" ; "Iran refused a deal when it was possible, continued with activities that negated the chance for that deal, and now makes baseless statements to obfuscate the history."

title: Paludisme : l’Afrique risque de demeurer le continent le plus touché par la maladie au-delà de la date prévue pour l’éradication en 2030

acts.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
acts.speech: Called for redoubling efforts at all levels in order to achieve the eradication of malaria provided for in the document adopted by the WHO in May 2015, entitled Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016-2030.

acts.speaker: WHO report (published December 2024)
acts.speech: "The African region is the most affected by malaria, accounting for about 94% of global cases and 95% of malaria-related deaths in 2023. Slightly more than half of these deaths occurred in four countries: Nigeria (30.9%), the Democratic Republic of Congo (11.3%), Niger (5.9%) and the United Republic of Tanzania (4.3%)" ; the most recent WHO figures, dating from 2023, report a toll of 597,000 deaths from the disease.

acts.speaker: James Tibenderana, Director General of the British NGO Malaria Consortium (quoted by Le Monde)
acts.speech: Declared: "There are fears that it may not be able to start on time in some West African countries where we operate, when the rains begin in June-July."

acts.speaker: Dorothy Achu, head of the malaria and tropical diseases team at the WHO Africa office
acts.speech: Warned that "malaria can be treated, but in young children this disease quickly becomes fatal when treatment is delayed."

acts.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
acts.speech: According to the WHO, a growing number of countries have made the fight against and elimination of malaria a national priority; no fewer than 11 high-burden African countries had signed the Yaounde Declaration in March 2024.

acts.speaker: Dr Daniel Ngamije, Director of the WHO Global Malaria Programme
acts.speech: Declared: "The ministers committed to strengthening their health systems, increasing domestic resources, reinforcing multisectoral action and guaranteeing a robust accountability mechanism" ; "this is the kind of leadership the world must rally behind."

title: Our Lending Model Is Sustainable, Quota-Blind – Okpanachi

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: Speaks on how the bank has provided long-term finance to support over 60 Primary Financial Institutions (PFIs) since its inception, to address the challenges confronting MSMEs in Nigeria: “It has been interesting coming from strictly commercial focus of profitability to impacting lives through providing access to credit for MSMEs which results in job creation, empowerment, economic growth and diversification.” He described DBN as a wholesale Development Bank with three specific mandates — increasing access to finance for MSMEs by lending to Participating Financial Institutions for on-lending, providing capacity building for PFIs, and providing partial credit guarantees — and said that as at December 2022 DBN had provided N631 billion as financing support to the PFIs, while over 313,000 MSMEs had benefited, leading to the creation of more than 900,000 jobs; women-owned MSMEs accounted for 69 per cent of all businesses financed by the end of the 2022 financial year; N230 billion was channelled to small businesses in trade and commerce, more than N69 billion to manufacturing MSMEs and N27 billion to Agro-MSMEs.

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
acts.speech: According to the IMF, more than 80 per cent of the entire population of Nigeria, which is more than 160 million Nigerians, depends on the informal economy.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On whether development banks in Nigeria are failing in their mandate: “No. This is because the concept of development finance institutions is not a new phenomenon. They have been used all over the world as instruments of economic growth and infrastructural development. What makes development financial institutions (DFIs) succeed or fail is the model — the pattern through which the intervention funds are made available to the sector where they are required.” He said that in the case of DBN there was a very deliberate calibration to avoid the pitfalls of defective DFIs while embracing the principles of successful ones, leading to the creation of DBN premised on the PFI lending model, which offers a more sustainable path to MSME financing through established channels and competitive pricing.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On gender parity: said the Development Bank of Nigeria believes strongly in the importance of creating an ecosystem with gender parity where everyone has an equal opportunity to prove his/her role and contribute to societal development; said Nigerian women have proven over the years how resourceful and dependable they can be, that DBN celebrates its females and remembers fallen heroines such as Dr. Stella Ameyo Adadevoh, Prof. Dora Akunyili, Tolulope Arotile and Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, and that in its bid to comply with the Nigerian Sustainable Banking Principles, which align with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, the DBN is committed to continue to lend its voice to gender equality and empowerment.

acts.speaker: World Bank international debt report
acts.speech: Indicated that developing countries, amid the biggest surge in global interest rates in four decades, spent a record $443.5 billion to service their external public and publicly guaranteed debt in 2022; debt-service payments increased by 5 percent over the previous year for all developing countries, while the 75 countries eligible to borrow from the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) paid a record $88.9 billion in debt-servicing costs in 2022; interest payments by these countries over the past decade have quadrupled, to an all-time high of $23.6 billion in 2022, while overall debt-servicing costs for the 24 poorest countries are expected to balloon in 2023 and 2024 by as much as 39 percent.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On the World Bank debt report: said the increase in costs shifted scarce resources away from critical needs such as health, education, and the environment in developing countries; “We are worried that the record debt levels and high interest rates have set many countries on a path to crisis while every quarter that interest rates stay high results in more developing countries becoming distressed and facing the difficult choice of servicing their public debts or investing in public health, education, and infrastructure.” He said the situation warrants quick and coordinated action by debtor governments, private and official creditors, and multilateral financial institutions, with more transparency, better debt sustainability tools, and swifter restructuring arrangements, as the alternative is another lost decade.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On high interest rates: said surging interest rates have intensified debt vulnerabilities in all developing countries, with 18 sovereign defaults in 10 developing countries in the past three years alone — more than in all of the previous two decades; that about 60 percent of low-income countries are at high risk of debt distress or already in it; that most of these countries face the additional burden of accumulated principal, interest and fees incurred under the G-20’s Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI); that the stronger US dollar is adding to their difficulties; that new external loan commitments dropped by 23% to $371 billion in 2022, the lowest level in a decade; that private creditors received $185 billion more in principal repayments than they disbursed in loans; and that the World Bank and other multilateral development banks stepped in, providing $115 billion in new low-cost financing in 2022, with the World Bank providing $16.9 billion more through IDA than it received in principal repayments and disbursing $6.1 billion in grants.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On MSME financing in Nigeria: said MSMEs are collectively the largest employers in many low-income countries including Nigeria, yet their viability is being threatened by lack of access to risk-management tools such as savings, insurance and credit; noted the exclusion rate reduced from 53 per cent in 2008 to 46.3 per cent in 2010, that the Central Bank of Nigeria launched the National Financial Inclusion Strategy on 23rd October 2012 aimed at reducing the exclusion rate to 20% by 2020, and that DBN was conceived by the Federal Government in collaboration with the World Bank, African Development Bank, German Development Bank (KfW), French Agency for Development and European Investment Bank, obtaining its Wholesale Development Banking licence in March 2017.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On sector focus: said DBN is not status specific, but over time will encourage some growth sectors in line with the development objective; “The key thing for us is that whatever sector of the economy you are, the questions are, are you able to create employment? Are you able to empower people? And all these things will help in diversification of the economy, which are the developmental impact you want to make in the economy.”

acts.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) World Economic Outlook
acts.speech: Said inflation was coming down and acute stress in the banking sector had receded, but the balance of risks facing the global economy remained tilted to the downside and credit was tight; projected global real GDP growth of 3.0% in 2023, up 0.2 percentage point from its April forecast, and left its 2024 outlook unchanged at 3.0%; indicated new technologies could boost productivity but could be disruptive to labor markets; described the outlook as “broadly stable” in emerging market and developing economies for 2023-2024, with growth of 4.0% in 2023 and 4.1% in 2024; noted credit availability is tight and there was a risk that debt distress could spread to a wider group of economies, and that the impact of higher interest rates was especially evident in poorer countries, driving debt costs higher and limiting room for priority investments.

acts.speaker: Dr. Tony Okpanachi, Managing Director/CEO, Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)
acts.speech: On development finance in Africa: said development finance of Africa has its limitations in amounts available, acceptable repayment risk and in some cases financing cost vs project viability, and that such finance often comes with strictures on how African nations should run their economies, so that solutions that are imported rather than developed at home may inadvertently come at a hefty price; said there is no denying that the traditional development finance model has not worked for Africa over the past six decades, that most African nations turn to development aid to survive, which is not a viable model to achieve sustainable economic development, and that since 1990 African countries have received over $1.3 trillion in development assistance while the continent’s financial, societal, and political fabric remains fragile.

title: Mozambique: Private funding is strategic for sustainable development – Chapo

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
acts.speech: Believes that private funding is a strategic imperative for sustainable development, as it is an engine of innovation, growth and value creation for Mozambique and other developing countries, and that leveraging companies and private investment is not an option but an essential condition for boosting Mozambique’s development in an accelerated and sustainable way ; “For this reason, we believe that private financing should seek to establish appropriate solutions, aimed, among other things, at stimulating the development of entrepreneurship, innovation, internationalization and company mobility.” ; gave the example of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which has 1.4 billion consumers, “a fact which will allow for a substantial increase in intra-African trade by 2045.” ; “That’s why governance and transparency, reform of the legal framework, promotion of local content and the development of innovative financing mechanisms are important to us. It is undeniable that public funding alone is insufficient to bridge the vast investment gap needed to achieve the country’s development goals.”

acts.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
acts.speech: Explained that Mozambique’s national agenda consists of economic transformation, reducing poverty, creating decent jobs, especially for young people, and building resilient infrastructure, all in line with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals 2015-2030 ; “In addition to the significant structural challenges, the country’s development journey, like that of many developing countries, is ambitious and full of potential.”

acts.speaker: United Nations (UN)
acts.speech: According to the United Nations, development aid is currently facing a deficit of four billion dollars a year.

title: Mca-Bénin : Lee Roussel et Gloria Peterson reçus dans l’ordre national

acts.speaker: Speakers at the decoration ceremony (Beninese officials, unnamed)
acts.speech: The various speeches all went in the same direction, saying the distinctions came to "attest to the satisfaction of the Beninese people with regard to the work" carried out by Lee Roussel and Gloria Peterson, and praising "the calm and rigour they displayed when it came to recalling the need to respect the agreed management rules."

acts.speaker: Lee Roussel, resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) in Benin, spokesperson for the two recipients
acts.speech: At the podium, was lost for words to express their joy; moved, she dissolved into nothing but thanks.

title: EAC, SADC Leaders Meet in Tanzania to Address DRC Security Crisis - Burundi Times

acts.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya (summit co-chair)
acts.speech: "The situation in eastern DRC is dire. It has led to a humanitarian crisis that has taken countless lives, and we must act now," said President Ruto during the opening session. "Our priority is to bring immediate relief to the people suffering and work toward a long-term peaceful resolution." ; "We are committed to merging the Luanda and Nairobi processes to create a more unified and effective approach," President Ruto added.

acts.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe (summit co-chair)
acts.speech: "We urge the government of the DRC to uphold the principles of peace and security by safeguarding diplomatic missions and ensuring the safety of all international personnel," Mnangagwa said.

acts.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe (summit co-chair)
acts.speech: "The sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC must be respected by all parties," said Mnangagwa.

acts.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania (summit host)
acts.speech: "We cannot allow this crisis to continue unchecked," said President Samia Suluhu Hassan of Tanzania, who hosted the summit. "We stand in solidarity with the people of DRC and will continue to support their efforts toward peace."

title: Israel and Hamas agree to a ceasefire and hostage deal

acts.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
acts.speech: Confirmed the deal, which involves a full and complete ceasefire, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza and the release of all the hostages held by Hamas ; says the first phase will allow Palestinians to return home to their neighbourhoods and let more humanitarian assistance into the Gaza Strip.

acts.speaker: Hamas-run health ministry (Gaza)
acts.speech: According to the Hamas-run health ministry, more than 46,000 Palestinians have been killed during the Israeli offensive on Gaza.

acts.speaker: Israel (government)
acts.speech: Says 94 hostages are still being held by Hamas, of whom 34 are presumed dead.

title: Namibia and USA reaffirm strong bilateral ties

acts.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
acts.speech: "Our elections are over; it was tough, it was complicated, and everybody saw what happened, but now we have a President-elect in the capacity of Dr. Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah. She will have time to organise her things because, according to our rules, having started from the year we gained our independence, we had elections in November 1989, and we needed 3 months to draft the Constitution, and that is why our independence is in March, and because of that we always have elections in November. But the assumption of power is in March. Nevertheless, we are comfortable now that when the dust has settled, everybody will accept what we have gotten from the people of Namibia. We have solid bilateral relations. We are benefiting from PEPFAR in terms of health, AGOA in terms of trade, YALI, and the Peace Corps."

acts.speaker: Randy Berry, US Ambassador to Namibia
acts.speech: Informed President Mbumba: "I also had a chance to discuss with the President how much I believe that is intensifying rapidly. I think all of the elements for closer relationships for increased coordination and collaboration are based on those very items, and when you are talking about democracies, democracies are driven by the rule of law, driven by institutions, and they are driven by elections, and those bring us together in terms of making sure that people's voices are heard. One area where I see a great deal of hope is expanding the economic situation; obviously, Namibians want opportunities; they want an economy that is thriving. We have seen a significant increase in private-sector investment from US firms here."

title: Citizens challenged to own Malawi 2063

acts.speaker: National Planning Commission (NPC) of Malawi
acts.speech: has said inclusive wealth creation is crucial for achieving Malawi's long-term development vision, Malawi (MW) 2063 ; said this approach was essential for the country's prosperity, as it would enable Malawians to create own wealth and reduce reliance on donor support.

acts.speaker: Thomas Munthali, Outgoing NPC Director General
acts.speech: said Malawi must shift focus from relying on foreign aid to creating own wealth: "Our vision is clear; inclusive wealth creation and self-reliance must guide our long-term development. We can no longer rely on donor support. We must create our own wealth. Planning and long-term thinking are important for national development" ; cited several achievements during his time at NPC, including the development of MW 2063 ; urged training institutions such as MSG to align their programmes with goals outlined in MW 2063 ; stressed the need for capacity building to support the national vision, with culture, Tourism, Mining and Manufacturing being prioritized.

acts.speaker: Jessie Kabwila, Higher Education Minister of Malawi
acts.speech: said the MW 2063 vision needed to be discussed and known by everyone: "When Malawians understand a certain issue, they are able to implement it. So, we need to explain to everyone what the Malawi 2063 [vision] entails. Malawians have a lot of ideas; we need to engage them to achieve this vision. When implementing it, we need to decentralise it" ; said underprivileged people had good ideas but that they were rarely engaged.

acts.speaker: Lewis Dzimbiri, MSG (Malawi School of Government) Council Chairperson
acts.speech: said the goal of becoming a self-reliant nation required more people to be trained in requisite areas: "We can also achieve the Malawi 2063 vision through engagement between the private and public sectors; it is not a one-person job."

title: Sécurité sanitaire : l’ONSPA reçoit plusieurs kits d’inspection pour renforcer le contrôle des produits halieutiques

acts.speaker: Fassou Théa, Guinean Minister of Fisheries and the Maritime Economy
acts.speech: welcomed a “strategic” support for the Guinean fisheries sector: “These inspection kits are not simply logistical equipment. They constitute a genuine strategic added value in the service of health and health security. Thanks to this support, ONSPA will be able to effectively fulfil its sovereign mission in accordance with national and international standards.”

acts.speaker: Dr Mamadou Bano Diallo, Director General of ONSPA
acts.speech: recalled the central role of his institution in protecting public health and promoting Guinean exports: “ONSPA works tirelessly to guarantee the quality and health compliance of fishery and aquaculture products intended for local consumption and for export. The success of this mission depends largely on the availability of appropriate logistical and human resources.” ; “ONSPA will make good use of this equipment in a spirit of responsibility and efficiency, in order to strengthen the health safety of fishery products and the competitiveness of our exports.”

acts.speaker: Dr Moustapha Grovogui, National Coordinator of the Regional Health Security Programme
acts.speech: stressed the need for continuous strengthening of institutional capacities to prevent health risks in the food sector: “Our country faces multiple and simultaneous epidemics. This programme aims to strengthen human, animal and environmental health within an integrated ‘One Health’ approach.”

title: Eswatini deploys cops in Somalia

acts.speaker: Manoma Vusie Masango, National Commissioner of Police (Royal Eswatini Police Service)
acts.speech: Called on 32 Individual Police Officers to embody discipline, honour, and respect for human rights as they prepare to join AUSSOM in Mogadishu, and reminded the officers that their role is not only to represent Eswatini but also to safeguard civilians and uphold international law in a conflict-torn region. "You have reflected an earnest intention on the commitment of member states to the contribution of peace and security in the continent," Masango said. "Go with purpose, humility, and the unwavering determination to serve the African people. Your safety, conduct, and discipline will remain our highest priority and concern." ; Emphasized the importance of adhering to International Humanitarian Law and International Human Rights Law while on mission, stressing that the officers must protect civilians and respect the Rule of Law in line with the principles of African Union Peace Support Operations.

acts.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
acts.speech: According to OCHA, over 6.9 million Somalis currently need humanitarian assistance due to conflict, drought, and food insecurity.

acts.speaker: The African Union and its international partners, including the United Nations and the European Union
acts.speech: Have repeatedly stressed that instability in Somalia is a continental concern.

acts.speaker: African Union
acts.speech: Has committed to a gradual transfer of security responsibilities to Somali authorities, with the ultimate goal of allowing Somalia to take full ownership of its peace and security.

title: Presse-Afrique de l'ouest: routes payantes et médecins en exil

acts.speaker: Fraternite Matin (Ivorian newspaper)
acts.speech: Announces the opening of four new toll stations in Cote d'Ivoire.

acts.speaker: Government of Cote d'Ivoire (statement of Monday 10 February 2025)
acts.speech: Specifies that the new toll stations are the Katiola toll station on the Bouake-Katiola axis, that of Ebouassue on the Abengourou-Bondoukou axis, and the Lakota and Eticoon-Tollakro toll stations on the N'Douci-Divo-Gagnoa axis.

acts.speaker: Jeune Afrique (magazine)
acts.speech: Reports that Tidjane Thiam will soon be "freed" from his French nationality, and stresses that becoming exclusively Ivorian is a sine qua non condition for being eligible in the presidential election next October.

acts.speaker: Tidjane Thiam, president of the PDCI
acts.speech: Announced that he had begun the administrative steps to become exclusively Ivorian, nine months before the Ivorian presidential elections.

acts.speaker: Financial Afrik (news website)
acts.speech: Returns to the impact of the halt to USAID funding decided by American President Donald Trump: "Nigeria, Tanzania and Uganda will be the hardest hit by the withdrawal of the main foreign aid of the United States via the American development agency," noting that in 2023 Nigeria received 368 million dollars, followed by Tanzania with 337 million.

acts.speaker: L'Essor (Malian newspaper)
acts.speech: Reports the introduction of new taxes by the transitional government as part of a "citizen contribution", with three adopted texts concerning the tax on access to the telecommunications network paid by operators, the tax on alcoholic beverages, and the levy on top-ups and mobile money transactions.

acts.speaker: Transitional government of Mali
acts.speech: Justifies these measures by the need to stabilize the economy, optimize the management of resources and modernize public infrastructure.

acts.speaker: Le Soleil (Senegalese newspaper)
acts.speech: Questions the capacity of the health system to cope with epidemics and future threats, after having been shaken by "Ebola, Covid-19 and Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever".

acts.speaker: Senegalese doctors
acts.speech: Analyse whether the Senegalese health system is ready to manage a new crisis.

acts.speaker: EnQuete (Senegalese newspaper)
acts.speech: Points to another difficulty, the exodus of health workers: because of "difficult working conditions, derisory salaries and the lack of infrastructure", many Senegalese doctors prefer to resign in order to work abroad, with France at the top of the destinations thanks to a well-organized recruitment.

title: Kiir assures Gituai of 'availability' of resources for peace implementation - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Statement from the Office of the President of South Sudan
acts.speech: "President Kiir expressed his commitment to ensuring a smooth and timely implementation of the extended agreement, noting the availability of resources to support these efforts," said the statement from Kiir's office; it added that the Head of State reassured Amb. Gituai that the country's security situation "remains stable, fostering a conducive environment for the forthcoming general polls." ; according to the statement, the discussions focused on key breakthroughs attained in the ongoing revitalized deal and the preparations for elections in December 2026.

acts.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
acts.speech: Assured the chairperson of peace monitoring mechanism R-JMEC of the availability of resources for the 2018 peace implementation.

acts.speaker: Amb. Charles Tai Gituai, chairperson of the peace monitoring mechanism R-JMEC
acts.speech: Briefed President Kiir on the progress of the agreement implementation, and reportedly highlighted advancements made in the constitution-making process and the security arrangement as critical components of the peace agreement.

acts.speaker: Khartoum (Government of Sudan)
acts.speech: Declared force majeure in March 2024, stating it was unable to facilitate the transportation of South Sudan crude oil through the Jabalayn-Port Sudan Pipeline, citing interruptions from the ongoing conflict.

acts.speaker: Officials from South Sudan and Sudan
acts.speech: Have repeatedly announced that the damaged pipeline had been repaired and is fully ready for resumption of crude export to the Red Sea.

acts.speaker: Dr. Martin Lomuro, Cabinet Minister of South Sudan
acts.speech: Emphasized the importance of regional and international support for South Sudan's peace process; "Minister Lomuro further stated that the government is prioritizing urgent matters to facilitate the onset of a new transitional period."

title: Beyond Perry's Thesis on Terror Financing

acts.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
acts.speech: Stated that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funded terrorist organizations, including Boko Haram.

acts.speaker: Nigerian scholars (Professors Kyari Mohammed, Jibrin Ibrahim, Usman Tar and Chris Kwaja, Dr. Atta Barkindo, Abdulbasit Kassim and others)
acts.speech: Have extensively researched and reported the origins and evolution of Boko Haram.

acts.speaker: Experts on the subject matter
acts.speech: Are sharply divided: some see Perry's thesis as political, while others hold it as something to interrogate.

title: How U.S. cuts in Somalia could imperil the fight against al-Shabab | Somali Guardian

acts.speaker: Matt Bryden, founder of Sahan, a Nairobi-based think tank
acts.speech: "The Trump administration is apparently not convinced that al-Shabab represents a direct threat to U.S. interests," and said further gains by the group "would have far-reaching implications for U.S. policy in Africa and much of the Middle East."

acts.speaker: Former senior State Department official (anonymous)
acts.speech: "I sat down with people from the White House, and they asked: 'What if we just let [Somalia] burn? Can we contain it?' I said, 'No!'"

acts.speaker: Former senior State Department official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said U.S. disengagement could fuel al-Shabab's expansion into neighboring Kenya and Ethiopia and allow the Somali fighters to strengthen fledgling relations with Yemen's Houthi rebels; said the last of two recent al-Shabab-Houthi meetings involved the Houthis sending an explosives expert to Jilib, al-Shabab's de facto capital, citing U.S. intelligence.

acts.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Acknowledged growing frustration with the Somali government, telling the Washington Post: "We are concerned about President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's prioritization of internal politics over counterterrorism efforts, particularly in light of the growing threat from al-Shabab." ; Said American officials have "repeatedly urged" Mohamud "to refocus on security cooperation and regional inclusion, and are disappointed by the lack of progress," adding that his emphasis on centralizing power "is hindering progress on counterterrorism" and "we believe a shift in priorities is essential to address the escalating threat."

acts.speaker: State Department press office
acts.speech: Said the United States "will continue to work closely with Somali and African Union forces."

acts.speaker: Turkish officials
acts.speech: Did not respond to requests for comment.

acts.speaker: U.N. sanctions experts
acts.speech: Documented two recent meetings between al-Shabab and the Houthis.

acts.speaker: Larry Andre, former U.S. ambassador
acts.speech: "Things always start off great with a new president, and then clan politics makes it all fall apart," recalling coordinating outfits with the beleaguered prime minister in 2022 during a joint news conference; their matching sky-blue running suits signaled they were united, Andre said, after political rivalries sparked deadly clan battles.

acts.speaker: Larry Andre, former U.S. ambassador
acts.speech: "Somalia is resource rich, but insecurity has prevented the commercialization of those resources. If we desert our partners, then others will replace us and reap the rewards when Somalia establishes peace and prosperity."

acts.speaker: Hussein Sheikh Ali, Somalia's national security adviser
acts.speech: Said the U.S. helps organize Somalia's seven core security partners, which include Britain, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and the African Union; all are against al-Shabab, Ali said, but sometimes have competing agendas: "On areas of counterterrorism [the Americans] are our lead partner."

acts.speaker: Aldebaran, a risk consultancy company
acts.speech: According to Aldebaran, since February insurgents have taken back dozens of villages, including the strategic town of Adan Yabaal, and regained the ability to operate in nearly a third of the territory they lost to federal forces in 2022.

acts.speaker: U.S. government audit
acts.speech: A U.S. government audit last year found that Danab had padded food and fuel requisitions.

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
acts.speech: Has said the wider freeze on foreign assistance programs under Trump will reduce government bloat and allow the administration to focus on domestic priorities.

acts.speaker: Some former U.S. officials
acts.speech: Say the torrent of international security funds into Somalia only fuels the country's deep-rooted corruption; others contend that continued funding to a small, select unit working alongside U.S. soldiers is the best among bad options.

acts.speaker: Former senior U.S. military official (anonymous)
acts.speech: "If we don't directly sustain the Danab, the Somali National Army is highly unlikely to sustain them to the degree required for them to be most effective."

acts.speaker: Former senior U.S. military official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said that although the fight in Somalia is a grinding and protracted one, AFRICOM has seen the spending and the risk to U.S. forces as an acceptable cost to contain a potential threat; he noted that U.S. access to the Horn of Africa has decreased steadily over the past decade: "The accountant's argument might be we hand [Somalia] off to the Turks and let them handle that security problem, but the cost of reentry is significant, and we lose influence over key geographic terrain." ; "When you sacrifice that and burden-shift it to an ally … it's unlikely your interests and objectives will align."

acts.speaker: Mogadishu-based security expert who works with the Somali military (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said morale within Danab is "not that high"; when the stipends were cut, about 100 soldiers "went AWOL for a bit," he said, and most of Danab's foreign mentors also went home after the U.S. cuts.

acts.speaker: U.S. security officials (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said plans to deploy the roughly 500 U.S. forces in Somalia across the country to better support Danab are also under review now.

acts.speaker: Senior Somali security official (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said an April 16 U.S. airstrike on two unflagged vessels off the Somali coast hit a shipment of surface-to-air missiles from Yemen.

acts.speaker: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
acts.speech: Declined to provide details, but its news release said the boat carried "advanced conventional weapons."

acts.speaker: Western military official (anonymous)
acts.speech: "Airstrikes are only useful if you have good ground troops to hold."

acts.speaker: Berkay Mandiraci, senior analyst for Turkey at the International Crisis Group
acts.speech: "With traditional powers retreating from parts of Africa, Ankara sees an opportunity to step in. Somalia holds strategic value for Ankara, sitting astride key shipping lanes and vital trade routes."

acts.speaker: Other security partners of Somalia
acts.speech: Have said they are often not informed about Turkish operations.

acts.speaker: Mogadishu-based diplomat (anonymous)
acts.speech: "At times you had multiple UAVs over a target."

acts.speaker: Witnesses (to Turkish drone strikes)
acts.speech: Told the Post that Turkish strikes from less-powerful drones have killed at least 40 civilians since late 2022; according to witnesses and a relative, a January 2023 strike on a gathering under a tree killed seven civilians, including an 8-year-old, in the town of Quracley.

acts.speaker: Local doctor (Mubarak, Somalia)
acts.speech: Said eight were killed on Sept. 9, 2022, when a strike hit a group of drivers and hawkers in the al-Shabab-controlled town of Mubarak.

acts.speaker: Mohamed Nur Ahmed, 50, who lost three sons and a nephew in the Quracley strike
acts.speech: "I couldn't even wash my children's bodies according to the Islamic custom," because they were "ripped to pieces."

acts.speaker: Western diplomat (anonymous)
acts.speech: "You've got the Somalis telling the Turks to … save Mogadishu at all costs. This will inevitably lead to further civilian casualties, which can be exploited by al-Shabab."

title: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, président de la CCIB: « Nous devons être en phase avec les normes américaines »

acts.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
acts.speech: On the signing of the 2nd MCA Compact: “I would first like to say that this signing is a complete success. We must salute the work that has been done, and I say congratulations to the President of the Republic for his leadership. You know under what conditions and why we were suspended... We must salute the work of the MCC team and of the MCA-Benin team, on which the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin is represented.” ; “There is no particular expectation. The second compact is simply the continuation of the first... That prepared the ground for the second compact, whose distinctive feature is essentially focused on the energy sector... with the particularity of bringing the Beninese and international private sector into production.” ; “The principle of this second compact launched a call for ideas from users, and so my own group, CDPA-Agrisatch, was approached and we made proposals on how we can contribute to producing solar energy and biomass-based energy... Energy is the engine of development, and without energy you cannot achieve development, still less industrial development.”

acts.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of the Republic of Benin
acts.speech: Says that in view of Benin's needs projected over time, the country must achieve 1,000 MW (of electrical capacity).

acts.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
acts.speech: On partnership with American business: “The presentation records that the compact amounts to about 411 million dollars. These resources will produce 78 MW of electrical energy... And there is even provision inside it for a cost-sharing fund... So it serves as a catalyst to go and seek other investments.” ; “Even before we went there, we had begun a discussion with the officials of the [US] Chamber's Africa department... That is how we discovered the CIP, which is a structure that supports the development of businesses internationally... We plan to sign a partnership with this structure shortly.” ; “The weakness of francophone countries is that we do not have big economic exchange links with the United States. The United States Chamber of Commerce can serve as a support point to strengthen this emerging Africa. We must work to improve our standards in terms of entrepreneurship, to develop our companies to be competitive at the international level.”

acts.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
acts.speech: On AGOA: “AGOA is a law that opens the American market to nearly 6,000 African products. Benin was chosen to take part in it. The first approach of the Chamber's new team is to diagnose the result of this AGOA... There is nevertheless one Beninese company that works with the United States and has stayed the course. It is Natura... But as for everything textile, we have not managed it. Lolo Andoche, who has made enormous efforts, is not yet at the level... what the American market demands... is mass production. Volume is needed.” ; “Over these 15 years the Chamber has worked to meet AGOA's requirements, but it has not worked miracles beyond measure. Fifteen years are in any case not enough to bring oneself up to American standards, to enter into the Anglo-Saxon mentality of entrepreneurship.” ; “Take our sugarloaf pineapples: do they comply with American phytosanitary standards?... We have a great deal of wealth that AGOA can awaken, but we must be in step with American standards.”

acts.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
acts.speech: On the public-private partnership: “We must salute the dialogue that was begun in October 2012 but which did not go to the very end of its completion because there was a bit of exclusion inside it... We came out of those general assemblies with a platform that brings everyone together without exclusion... The public-private partnership (PPP) can only be strengthened. But there was also the problem of the legal framework... The private sector does not feel secure in these investments and is proposing texts. Work has been done, which is now at the level of Parliament... We must create Beninese champions further... The other element is the strengthening of an operational justice system for the cause of the PPP.”

acts.speaker: Jean-Baptiste Satchivi, president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCIB)
acts.speech: On what he expects from government on the business climate: “What we expect from the government is very simple. First, more consideration for the one who undertakes, I mean the business leader whatever his size... What we owe the State is to create favourable conditions as regards the factors of production and raw materials. We must accompany the government so that the government accompanies us. We are not going to ask for exemptions on everything from a State that needs a fiscal budget in order to work.” ; “The only thing lacking today is a fruitful dialogue between the public sector and the private sector represented by a non-exclusive platform. I would like to make an appeal to the President of the Republic to kindly ensure that this platform becomes a reality before his departure. It will be an important element of his legacy... Beninese people must learn to come together in order to win.”

title: USAID places staff on leave, recalls personnel overseas

acts.speaker: USAID (statement on its website)
acts.speech: Said on Tuesday that all direct hire personnel would be put on leave from Friday, apart from "designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs"; said USAID personnel posted overseas will be recalled from their postings within 30 days; said it would consider case-by-case exceptions and extensions based on "personal or family hardship, mobility or safety concerns, or other reasons" ; "For example, the Agency will consider exceptions based on the timing of dependents' school term, personal or familial medical needs, pregnancy, and other reasons. Further guidance on how to request an exception will be forthcoming," the statement said ; "Thank you for your service."

acts.speaker: Congressional Research Service
acts.speech: According to the Congressional Research Service, USAID employs more than 10,000 people, about two-thirds of whom are stationed overseas.

acts.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
acts.speech: Asked by a reporter on Tuesday if he was preparing to "wind down" the agency, Trump said, "I think so."

acts.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
acts.speech: On Monday confirmed that he was serving as acting administrator of USAID.

acts.speaker: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
acts.speech: Has called USAID a "criminal organisation", without substantiation, and claimed the agency is a "viper's nest of radical-left Marxists who hate America".

title: Namibia's beef exports to EU under threat

acts.speaker: EU Deforestation Regulation (text of the regulation)
acts.speech: The regulation prohibits the entry of commodities linked to deforestation after December 2020, including beef, unless stringent environmental standards are met. The regulation stipulates that products including cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, soy, timber, rubber, and derivatives such as chocolate and furniture must adhere to stringent environmental and social standards.

acts.speaker: Carl Schlettwein, Namibian Minister of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform
acts.speech: In his address to the National Assembly, warned that non-compliance could lead to severe penalties: "Non-compliance will result in the following: Fines can reach up to 4% of the operator's or traders's annual EU turnover. Confiscation: Revenues from relevant transactions may be confiscated. Exclusion: Temporary exclusion from public procurement and access to public funding for a maximum of 12 months. Suspension: Temporary suspension from placing or making available on the EU market or exporting relevant commodities/products, along with a prohibition from exercising simplified due diligence."

acts.speaker: Carl Schlettwein, Namibian Minister of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform
acts.speech: Acknowledged that while the regulation presents compliance challenges, it also offers Namibia an opportunity to enhance its forest governance and environmental policies. He called for a multi-stakeholder approach, urging various ministries, agencies, and local farmers to collaborate in preparing for the Deforestation Regulation ; "Preparatory steps may include, but are not limited to understanding and analysing the requirements; identifying relevant state actors concerned by the requirements; reviewing the legal framework and existing national and international approaches to guarantee compliance; developing strategies to consolidate and harmonise legal frameworks, especially through participatory approaches; defining indicators for legal compliance; sensitising local farmers about the content of the legislation and how to comply with it; developing legality assurance systems through auditing, certification, and chain of custody requirements; strengthening compliance with the legal framework's standard operating procedures and law enforcement strategies; and supporting independent forest monitoring to verify compliance."

title: Editorial: Taking jobs from Liberians is counterproductive to economic growth - Liberia news The New Dawn Liberia, premier resource for latest news

acts.speaker: Joint Committee on Investment and Concessions and Transport of the House of Representatives (Liberia)
acts.speech: Last week ordered the suspension of all Liberia Traffic Management (LTM) operations, for failure to appear before lawmakers for an investigative hearing that was scheduled for Thursday, July 31, 2025, effectively returning complete operational control to the Ministry of Transport.

acts.speaker: Commercial drivers / protesters
acts.speech: Staged a mass protest against what they described as inhumane treatment under the new agreement; the protesters decried excessive ticketing and alleged extortion by LTM officers, claiming the company is exploiting drivers under the guise of traffic enforcement.

acts.speaker: Plenary of the Liberian Senate
acts.speech: On Thursday, July 24, 2025, mandated its leadership to request that President Joseph Nyuma Boakai immediately halt the implementation of the Liberia Traffic Management Incorporated (LTM-I) concession agreement until further consultations and clarity provided.

acts.speaker: Employees of the Ministry of Transport
acts.speech: Staged a series of protests calling attention to the fate waiting them, if the Liberia Traffic Management were to take full control of license production and issuance to the public.

title: OPEC daily basket price stood at $74.12 a barrel, Tuesday

acts.speaker: OPEC Secretariat (calculations)
acts.speech: According to OPEC Secretariat calculations, the price of the OPEC basket of 12 crudes stood at $74.12 a barrel on Tuesday, March 18, 2025, compared with $73.65 the previous day.

title: Sign peace pact - US Ambassador to political parties

acts.speaker: Virginia Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
acts.speech: Advised that contesting political parties must commit to a peace pact as soon as possible: "All political parties must sign the peace pact as soon as possible because that is a sure way to signal to the young people on the streets that violence in any form will not be the way to go during the elections" ; touted Ghana's democratic credentials, which she admitted were the envy of the rest of the continent and the world at large, and stressed the need for that to be jealously guarded during and after the crucial December 7 general election ; said elections were not battlegrounds or a period to make enemies but a platform to project ideas to the electorate for them to make a choice.

acts.speaker: Virginia Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
acts.speech: Referenced the just-ended elections in the USA, which was won by former President Donald Trump over Vice-President Kamala Harris, and stated that immediately after the elections there had been business as usual in the US with all citizens living in peace; said no matter how violent the campaigns were, America emerged victorious and peaceful because the people believed it was where their power as citizens lay; urged Ghana to emulate that example as it had always been done since the Fourth Republic, to keep the peace, while remaining the beacon of democracy on the continent and beyond; expressed the hope that just as America had done it successfully, Ghana would also emerge victorious after the elections.

acts.speaker: Joe Biden, US President (quoted by Ambassador Palmer)
acts.speech: "You can't love democracy only when you are winning and you can't love your neighbour only when you agree."

acts.speaker: Ghana National Peace Council (as recalled by Ambassador Palmer)
acts.speech: Had been preaching that elections were not a battle between enemies but a contest of ideas between groups with different ideologies.

acts.speaker: Virginia Palmer, US Ambassador to Ghana
acts.speech: Pledged the continuous support of America to Ghana, both politically and economically, as they strengthened the bond of friendship between the two countries.

acts.speaker: John Agyekum Kufuor, former President of Ghana
acts.speech: Called for greater partnership between Ghana and America in a manner that ensured a win-win for all and not one that was tilted against the other; recalled the enormous support Ghana enjoyed from the United States through the Millennium Challenge Account that resulted in the funding of some major road projects and the energy sector; expressed the hope that the bond of friendship between the two countries would extend way into the future in the interest of their citizens.

acts.speaker: Kimathi Kuenyehia, President of the American Chamber of Commerce (AMCHAM) Ghana
acts.speech: Paid glowing tribute to the founder presidents, directors and patrons of AMCHAM, touting the benefits Ghanaian and American businesses have enjoyed in the last 35 years; said plans were afoot to have AMCHAM move from its rented premises into its own edifice, a project which would soon start.

title: APM warns against over reliance on maize - Nation Online

acts.speaker: Peter Mutharika, former president of Malawi and leader of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
acts.speech: Encouraged Lhomwe people to diversify food choices and move away from reliance on maize to deal with perennial hunger in the Southern Region, saying that in the past Lhomwe people relied on crops such as pigeon peas, cassava, sweet potatoes and millet for food: “These crops are drought resistant as they do not require a lot of rain. Of course, we should grow maize but we need to move to these traditional foods to deal with perennial hunger.”

acts.speaker: Peter Mutharika, former president of Malawi and leader of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
acts.speech: Urged people to register [for the September 16 2025 General Elections] ; spoke against suicide, victimisation of girls, trafficking in persons and attacks against the elderly in the country ; noted that it is common in the Lhomwe belt districts such as Phalombe, Mulanje and Thyolo for people to send children to Mozambique to work in farms: “I appeal to chiefs and all community leaders to ensure that the culture of sending children to other areas should stop.”

acts.speaker: Blessings Makwinja, representative of Lhomwe Paramount Chief Kaduya
acts.speech: Mentioned the continued rise in prices of goods and services, unemployment, natural disasters and hunger as some of the challenges that people are facing, and said people from the Lhomwe belt will register for the 2025 General Elections and vote massively on polling day as a way of resolving these challenges.

acts.speaker: Felix Tambulasi, organising committee chairperson and private practice lawyer
acts.speech: Said they faced many challenges in raising funds because of the poor economic situation in the country: “Despite the challenges, various individuals and organisations contributed and we have raised K180 million which has been used to buy food and cover other costs for this event.”

source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
title: Ramadan : L’État offre 20 tonnes de riz aux nécessiteux à Koulikoro - amap
