acts.speaker: Colonel Lamine Kapory Sanogo, Governor of Koulikoro
acts.speech: Welcomed this active solidarity of the government towards its people.

acts.speaker: Beneficiaries of the rice distribution
acts.speech: Expressed wishes of happiness, prosperity and peace for Mali and for the Transition authorities.

title: Inondations au Niger : La Sous-Administratrice Adjointe du Bureau d'Aide Humanitaire de l'USAID annonce une aide d’un million de dollars - Agence Nigérienne de Presse

acts.speaker: Jacqueline Musiitwa, USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator, Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance
acts.speech: Announced $1 million in aid for people affected by flooding in Niger. Met with USAID staff in Niamey with whom she discussed "the Agency's priorities, as well as development and humanitarian partners." Announced that earlier in the month, the United States committed to providing $1 million to help people affected by the recent flooding in Niger.

acts.speaker: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
acts.speech: Said the visit "underscores the commitment of the United States government to collaborate on shared objectives in Niger."

title: President Tinubu Orders Customs To Return Seized Food Items To Owners On One Condition

acts.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
acts.speech: Has directed the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) to return the food items seized at border communities to the rightful owners, with the caveat that the owners must be willing to sell the items in Nigerian markets.

acts.speaker: Adewale Adeniyi, Comptroller General of Customs
acts.speech: Said that President Tinubu chose to exercise his authority not based on legal criteria, but rather out of a genuine sense of goodwill towards Nigeria ; “In doing so, he has directed that those food items that were going out of the country that have been seized in various border areas should be returned to the owners on the condition that those goods would be sold in the Nigerian markets.” ; “So, we will be monitoring you to know if there is a violation of this. Those food items will be returned, and it is a directive that we will pass them back into the Nigerian markets.”

acts.speaker: Adewale Adeniyi, Comptroller General of Customs
acts.speech: Revealed that President Tinubu will choose to reopen borders very soon and confirmed that the Service will prioritise eliminating barriers that hinder free trade ; “We are conscious of the concerns of the border communities, particularly with regards to the number of checkpoints and the closure of land borders. I assure you that our operations are always guided by law, and we only operate on delegated powers. We have communicated the concerns and complaints by residents of the border communities to the President and because he has listening ears, he directed that we should release confiscated food items, on the condition that they will only be sold in the Nigerian markets.” ; “We know that there are markets around our borders, and we know that not all of them are targeted at taking goods across the borders. We will continue to monitor and ensure that food produced in Nigeria remains and is consumed in Nigeria. This is because we are in a period of national emergency that has to do with food insufficiency. And that is why we must collectively work together to assist the government to enforce the various laws prohibiting exportation of food items at this time.”

acts.speaker: The Sun News (report)
acts.speech: The SunNews reports that President Tinubu chose to exercise his authority not based on legal criteria, but rather out of a genuine sense of goodwill towards Nigeria.

title: L’ONU en crise : António Guterres alerte

acts.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
acts.speech: Before the Fifth Committee of the General Assembly on Friday 17 October 2025, issued an urgent appeal: "if member states do not quickly regularise their contributions, the UN could find itself in a situation of bankruptcy" ; denounces a critical situation in which "credit returns" and budgetary arrears compromise the organisation's operational capacity.

acts.speaker: Former Malian diplomat (anonymous), expert on the UN system
acts.speech: "This is not just a cash-flow crisis. It is the very model of multilateral financing that is faltering. The great powers hesitate to support an institution they consider too normative. But weakening the UN means weakening global dialogue, solidarity and conflict prevention."

title: Maxkamadda CQS oo maanta Dhageysatay kiiska Askari ‘Miino dhigay’

acts.speaker: Tahliil Axmed Fiidow Caraale (also known as Cali Daahir Jimcaale), defendant, former member of the armed forces
acts.speech: Said that 'AS' (Al-Shabaab) cut off his hand after he indicated that he had been accused of theft.

acts.speaker: Office of the Prosecutor of the Military Court (Armed Forces Court)
acts.speech: Requested that a severe sentence be imposed on Tahliil Axmed Fiidow, since the explosion he was accused of caused deaths.

acts.speaker: The defendant and his lawyers
acts.speech: Jointly requested for their part that the punishment be reduced in the cases the prosecution had charged him with, given that he had confessed to part of the crimes he is accused of.

acts.speaker: Chairman Shuute, presiding judge of the Armed Forces Court
acts.speech: Closed the session.

title: Éthique et gouvernance : La Chambre de commerce européenne réfléchit sur la question

acts.speaker: Christian Delmotte, President of Eurocham (European Chamber of Commerce in Cote d'Ivoire)
acts.speech: Stated that good governance is the pillar of economic growth and of corporate social responsibility in Cote d'Ivoire: "This programme, financed by Eurocham in collaboration with Siemens and the World Bank, was therefore designed to raise awareness among and train about one hundred Ivorian companies in adopting and implementing high standards of ethics, good governance and the fight against corruption" ; "Since its launch, the ACCG has made it possible to support some sixty companies, thereby contributing to a more ethical and transparent business environment in Cote d'Ivoire."

acts.speaker: Dr Franck Eba, Regional ESG manager at Hummingbird, and Fabrice Piofret, CEO of Veilleur des medias (panellists)
acts.speech: Shared their experience in matters of ethics and good governance and above all what the programme brought them, in particular regarding internal control mechanisms and the importance of transparency in financial reporting.

title: Diaspora Nationals Celebrate Independence Day Anniversary

acts.speaker: Beyene Russom, Eritrea’s Ambassador to Kenya
acts.speech: Highlighting the deep meaning of Eritrean independence and the heavy sacrifice paid, expressed appreciation to all who contributed to the colorful event.

acts.speaker: Robel Aaron, chairman of the Eritrean community in Finland
acts.speech: Emphasized the heavy sacrifices made for independence and called on nationals to strengthen their organizational capacity and participation in national affairs; he also urged the transfer of noble societal values to future generations.

acts.speaker: Eritrean nationals in Minnesota and Orange County, United States
acts.speech: Expressed their readiness to play their due part in the successful implementation of national development programs.

title: Gestion des forêts en Afrique de l’Ouest: Des experts font le point des actions menées

acts.speaker: José Tonato, Beninese Minister of Living Environment and Infrastructure, in charge of Sustainable Development
acts.speech: Said the ambition for 2040 is for Benin's forest areas to be better managed for their multiple functions.

acts.speaker: Representative of Sweden, financial partner of the project
acts.speech: "We hope that this project will be successfully implemented for the well-being of the communities."

acts.speaker: Ange Obama, FAO Resident Representative
acts.speech: Said that wetland forests constitute an important source of fuel and food but are extremely affected by degradation, and that implementing specific actions under the project 'Global Forest Transformation for People and Climate: Focus on West Africa' will benefit communities and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Dissolution de l’Usaid: Déclic pour des systèmes de financement innovants

acts.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
acts.speech: According to OECD data, sub-Saharan Africa absorbed nearly 40% of USAID's annual budget, with countries such as Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, Senegal and Nigeria among the main beneficiaries.

acts.speaker: The White House
acts.speech: According to the White House, USAID's missions will henceforth be integrated directly into a Directorate-General for Cooperation and Development attached to the US State Department; officially the aim is to streamline the structure, limit administrative duplication and strengthen the alignment between development aid and US diplomatic priorities.

acts.speaker: World Bank
acts.speech: Recalls that the agency was among the top five bilateral donors for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to health, education and gender equality.

acts.speaker: Government Accountability Office (GAO) report
acts.speech: Underlines that USAID managed more than 1,300 projects across 80 overseas missions, with occasional duplication between federal agencies.

acts.speaker: US administration
acts.speech: Defends a refocusing on major diplomatic priorities, in a context of heightened rivalry with China over investments in Africa and Asia; the dissolution is presented as a measure of sound management of public funds.

acts.speaker: Several US officials
acts.speech: Find that USAID's strength lay precisely in its operational autonomy and technical expertise; according to them, the technical expertise accumulated over decades by USAID teams could be diluted, even lost, within a broader diplomatic framework where aid risks becoming a mere instrument of geopolitical influence.

acts.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa
acts.speech: Stated recently at the eleventh session of the Africa Regional Forum on Sustainable Development held in Kampala, Uganda: “Aid can no longer be considered a reliable or sustainable solution. Time is pressing. We must act now, with you, our heads of state, who are leading reforms, creating an enabling environment and mobilising domestic resources. Together, we can deliver on the promise of Agenda 2063 and the SDGs.”

acts.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, statistician-economist, specialist in economic policy management
acts.speech: “Efforts must be made to diversify sources of financing by turning to regional and international financial markets and to innovative financing. The most predictable and most sustainable resources are domestic public resources.”

title: The Global Soft Power Index in the Trump era, By Oluwaseun Tella

acts.speaker: Global Soft Power Index 2025, Brand Finance
acts.speech: One of the most notable findings from the survey is that the US has retained its position as the top-ranked soft power state, as it was in the 2024 edition; the 2025 edition evaluated all 193 United Nations member states, drawing on data from a global sample of over 170,000 respondents across more than 100 markets; China has now risen to second place, overtaking the United Kingdom, with Japan, Germany, France, Canada, Switzerland, Italy and the UAE maintaining their 2024 rankings from fourth to tenth; Egypt, South Africa, Morocco, Nigeria and Algeria are the highest-ranked African states in the index.

acts.speaker: Portland's Soft Power 30 Index (2019)
acts.speech: In 2019, France overtook the US as the leading soft power state.

source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
title: Baréma Koïta, chef du secteur pêche de Ségou : «Il faut favoriser l’accès aux intrants de qualité à un prix raisonnable» - amap

acts.speaker: Baréma Koïta, Chief of the Ségou Fisheries Sector (Mali)
acts.speech: Said fish farming as a fish-breeding technique emerged in Mali through a small experimental station in the San Region, financed under a November 1979 agreement between Mali and the United States with USAID support, leading to an extension outpost being created in Niono ; detailed that the Ségou Circle currently has 131 ponds, 115 above-ground tanks and 2 floating cages, that rice-fish farming covers 7,500 m2 and that there are 31 ponds spanning 51.68 hectares, and that a 144 m3 floating cage produced 2,624 kg from 10,000 fingerlings while a 10 m3 tank with 1,000 fish yielded 369 kg ; stated that Nile tilapia and Clarias gariepinus are the two species studied, and named ongoing initiatives supporting fish farming in Ségou, including the Degraded Land Restoration Project (PRTD), a project supporting sustainable livelihoods for fishing communities adapting to climate change, and Jègè ni Jaba (JNJ).

acts.speaker: Baréma Koïta, Chief of the Ségou Fisheries Sector (Mali)
acts.speech: Said producers' access to inputs remains a concern, that his department lacks enough agents to cover the whole Circle, that growing insecurity hinders access to some localities, and that the service also faces a shortage of financial means ; said: "We must promote access to quality inputs at a reasonable price, have a permanent water source, regularly maintain infrastructure, and secure facilities against theft." Speaking about challenges and prospects, he mentioned reducing input costs, developing fish farming infrastructure, and strengthening producers' capacities.

title: Traffic halted again at Maputo tollgate

acts.speaker: STV (independent television station) report
acts.speech: According to a report on the independent television station STV, the sabotage of the road was spearheaded by drivers of the minibuses, known colloquially as “chapas”, which provide much of the passenger transport in Maputo.

acts.speaker: Chapa (minibus) drivers protesting at the tollgate
acts.speech: They warned the police that, if there was any attempt to disburse the protesters, they would blow up the [hijacked fuel] tanker.

title: Horn Observer

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: Condemns the unlawful arrest and physical assault of woman journalist Anisa Ahmed, who works for the online channel Dalbile TV, by members of the Mogadishu police. Anisa has since been released without charge.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) and Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights (RFKHR) (joint statement)
acts.speech: Strongly denounce the attempts of Premier Bank to silence Abdalle Mumin, a human rights defender and journalist.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: Condemns the harassment and brief detention of Himilo Somali TV journalist Omar Yusuf Mohamed (Omar Guux) by members of the Somali National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) in Mogadishu's Dharkeenley district on Monday, 18 August 2025.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: Calls on Puntland and SSC-Khaatumo (now Northeast Somalia State) to respect freedom of expression and to end intimidation tactics against journalists reporting on issues considered critical by local authorities, including those reporting security matters.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: Strongly condemns the wave of attacks targeting journalists in Mogadishu amid violent evictions and gunfight on Thursday, as the Somali national intelligence and security agency (NISA) intensified its aggressive pursuit of critical journalists.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: Strongly condemns the unlawful arrest of two journalists in Adaado town, Galmudug State, on Tuesday, 5 August 2025, following their reporting on the alleged rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl in Adaado town.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: Strongly condemns the abduction-style arrest of three journalists in Mogadishu on Sunday, 3 August 2025, by armed officers from the Turkish-trained Haramcad police unit.

acts.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) (press statement)
acts.speech: The SJS and its network of members proudly congratulate its Secretary General, Abdalle Ahmed Mumin, for receiving an Honourable Mention at the 2025 Allard Prize for International Integrity.

acts.speaker: Somali Media Association (SOMA) (press statement)
acts.speech: Welcomes the recent high-level meeting between civil society leaders and the European Union Ambassador to Somalia, H.E. Karin Johansson, which focused on Somalia's National Dialogue process and the role of civil society.

title: African leaders entreated to honour 15% health budget commitment

acts.speaker: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa, President of the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA)
acts.speech: called on African heads of state to honour the 15 per cent health budget commitment promised under the Abuja declaration; said the 2030 Millennium Development Goals were five years away and if they did not prioritise health and put it at the forefront of the Africa development agenda, they would not be able to meet the 95-95-95 HIV target ; “We are aware a few of the African countries have already reached that target, but the majority have not yet. There is no way we can make meaningful progress in the fight against HIV and AIDS and other diseases without significant increases in health funding and commitment from African governments.”

acts.speaker: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa, President of the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA)
acts.speech: said health was not a cost but rather an investment in economic and social development, adding that Africa must take its own resources like diamonds, gold and oil and invest them into the health systems of their respective countries ; quoting the World Bank's key demographic projections, said Africa's population would reach a record 1.7 billion by 2040, with 40 per cent being under the age of 15 years, and asked how the continent would ensure that future workforce was productive and able to contribute to the continent's development when the continent did not have at least a basic functional universal healthcare system ; “Let us not wait any longer. It is time we produce our own vaccines and medications. We hope that this will reduce our dependence on foreign aid and pharmaceutical imports.” ; stated that all Africans needed to know their HIV health status, saying this could not be ignored in this era where there had been scientific breakthroughs, including pre or post-exposure prophylaxis access, injectable treatment and all other tools that could be used maximally in every country.

acts.speaker: World Bank key demographic projections
acts.speech: quoted as projecting that Africa's population would reach a record 1.7 billion by 2040, with 40 per cent being under the age of 15 years.

acts.speaker: Dr Hafez Adam Taher, Director of Technical Coordination at the Ministry of Health, Ghana (speaking on behalf of the sector minister)
acts.speech: said Ghana's hosting of ICASA 2025 came at a time when it had made notable strides in its national response to HIV-AIDS; mentioned these to include expansion of access to antiretroviral therapy, reduction of mother-to-child transmission and improving community-based care and support services.

acts.speaker: Dr Kyeremeh Atuahene, Director General of the Ghana AIDS Commission
acts.speech: expressed the readiness of the commission to host the conference, elaborating that they were already setting up a national planning committee in conjunction with the organisers so that they would be driving all the activities in terms of planning, organisation and administration of the conference.

title: OPINION: How Eng. Napoleon Adok transformed ICT sector in South Sudan - Eye Radio

acts.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
acts.speech: Recently during the swearing in of the new Minister of Finance and Planning, quoted as saying: “I am looking for a solution, this is why I bring somebody today and tomorrow I kick him out and bring another person. When I succeed in getting the right person, I will hold him firmly and will not let him go.”

acts.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
acts.speech: In February this year during the swearing-in of the Chairperson of the National Bureau of Statistics, also quoted as saying: “We are trying to promote the young people that will make the real change that we are aspiring for.”

acts.speaker: Eye Radio (editorial note)
acts.speech: “The views expressed in this article are solely those of the writer. The accuracy of any claims made is the responsibility of the author and not of this website. The writer is a researcher and writer on local and international economic and political affairs.”

title: Présidence de la République: Un déjeuner d’au-revoir pour Michael Raynor

acts.speaker: Michael Raynor, United States Ambassador to Benin
acts.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the Beninese government and people for the good times he was able to spend during his three years of mission in Benin: "I am truly honoured to have represented my country here for three years. I had the privilege of discovering the many riches of this country and I was above all impressed by the dynamism of the women and young people of Benin" ; gave assurances that his departure would change nothing in the bilateral cooperation between the United States and Benin, cooperation which he had tried to strengthen during his stay in Cotonou.

acts.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
acts.speech: Saluted "a great friend" of Benin who shares with the United States the values of the free world: "For three years, you accepted our shortcomings, you accompanied us in our reforms" ; said the Beninese people are attached to democracy, which does not go hand in hand with destitution: "We must avoid the gap between destitution and democracy. If destitution is severe, it betrays democracy. Likewise, democracy does not go with a failing education system, a shortfall in health services, or a deficit in infrastructure, primarily energy."

acts.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
acts.speech: Hailed the American diplomat's involvement in securing the second Millennium Challenge Account compact, estimated at 411 million dollars: "It is the first time that a country has received an amount higher than what it had received under the first compact", and assured the United States of his government's determination to improve governance.

title: የጤና ባለሙያዎች ጥያቄና የዘርፉ አጠቃላይ ሁኔታ - ሪፖርተር - Ethiopian Reporter - #1 Reliable News Source In Ethiopia

acts.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
acts.speech: Ministry of Health data for 2024 indicates that 404 hospitals, 3,907 health centres and 15,531 health posts are in service; the ministry, along with international institutions, has testified that Ethiopia registered significant growth in the health sector over the past three decades, raising primary health institution coverage from 50.7 percent in 2000 to 90 percent in 2019.

acts.speaker: International reports
acts.speech: Say the country has 17,534 health posts including those under construction, 3,643 health stations including some 57 under construction, about 3,867 private clinics, and 43 private hospitals.

acts.speaker: Various reports (on the health sector's problems)
acts.speech: Classify the problems of Ethiopia's health sector into five main categories: shortage of doctors and professionals (Limited Number of Medical Graduates), professional migration (Brain Drain), Inadequate Infrastructure, Uneven Distribution of infrastructure, and Financial Constraints.

acts.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
acts.speech: Says the health sector is distinct: "The work is directly connected with human life. It has a high workload, it demands strict ethics and discipline, and it does not allow one to live while doing other additional jobs as in other professions. Because the health sector is complex in its own right, it requires special attention. It is because that has not happened, and because some of the demands we raised earlier were not properly answered, that the demand is now being raised."

acts.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
acts.speech: Explained that medical professionals' demand for salary and benefits should not be seen as a peculiar sin or a luxury, and added that they work facing great danger to serve their country where conditions are not favourable and infrastructure is lacking: "These professionals work by exposing themselves to danger, without excluding patients infected with rapidly transmissible diseases. They have to treat patients with tuberculosis, hepatitis and other diseases while facing danger. Because doctors spend their working day inside a medical institution, they are made more vulnerable than a person who spends the day in an office or a factory. Doctors' protest and demand must be viewed in relation to the overall pressure and nature of the work that the sector demands."

acts.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
acts.speech: Indicated that about 42,000 health extension workers deployed under 15,000 health posts are providing a major service by delivering community-based health care.

acts.speaker: Protesting health professionals (placards at demonstrations)
acts.speech: Carried placards reading "We are hungry" and "We can no longer survive" at peaceful demonstrations in the regions and at health institutions, saying salary and benefits have become difficult for them.

acts.speaker: A doctor, member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
acts.speech: Said that professionals' very existence has today fallen into danger: "It is a problem accumulated and overflowing over the ages that has brought us to this stage. We have been presenting about 12 clearly known demands. Since 2010/11 E.C. we have been presenting our demands clearly, orally and in writing, at the level of the Prime Minister. Of these demands, the main and fundamental one, which could answer 11 of them, is our demand that the medical sector be separated from the civil service and be administered autonomously by a board. Just as it was said that our universities should be organized autonomously, the demand that the health sector too be autonomous and be led by a board managed directly by professionals rather than by politicians has not been answered. It was believed that this would modernize the service and not only satisfy the client but also benefit the professional. The key issue is that an independent board called the Ethiopian National Health Service Board be established. It has also been successful in the experience of Kenya and other countries. If there is a health service not burdened by politics, the suffering and emigration of doctors will stop. Projects come, saying doctors should benefit. Words centred on the professional are promised. It is said you will become a homeowner, there will be money for buying a car, and so on. But nothing ever materializes."

acts.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
acts.speech: Stated that the cancellation of USAID and other foreign funding for Ethiopia's health sector is unrelated to the doctors' protest, saying that although the matter may cause damage, the problem is not beyond the country's capacity.

acts.speaker: A doctor, member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
acts.speech: Gave an idea supporting the view that the USAID cuts are not the cause, noting that Ethiopia has never poured adequate resources into the health sector.

acts.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia (2017 E.C. budget plan)
acts.speech: Ranks the annual budget allocations by sector, with debt payment leading at 139.31 billion birr (18 percent of the total budget), road development 86 billion birr (11.71 percent), education 79.84 billion birr (10.87 percent), defence 65.70 billion birr (about 8.9 percent), and health fifth at about 33.90 billion birr (about 4.62 percent), followed by justice and security (27.64 billion birr, 3.76 percent), water and energy (25.26 billion birr, 3.44 percent), agriculture (22.92 billion birr, 3.12 percent), disaster prevention (11.90 billion birr, 1.62 percent) and transport and communications (11.89 billion birr, 1.62 percent).

acts.speaker: UNICEF (report comparing Ethiopia's 2022/23 and 2023/24 budget performance)
acts.speech: Places the health budget in eighth place, after debt payment, roads, education, defence and other expenditures, and states that Ethiopia allocated 3.4 percent and then 3.9 percent of its total budget to health in the two budget years, a growth of only 0.5 percent.

acts.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (data)
acts.speech: Indicated that community-based health insurance coverage was extended to 1,050 woredas as of last year (2016 E.C.), with about 11.14 million households benefiting, about 73 percent of the population believed to be reachable.

acts.speaker: Girma Ababi (Dr.), chairperson of the founding committee of the 'Family Health and Life Insurance' Share Company
acts.speech: Said the insurance sector accounts for one percent of the country's economy and is still undeveloped: "In Kenya, beyond conventional insurance, they have made the health insurance sector one that moves 66 billion birr in assets. With us, let alone health insurance, the insurance sector as a whole has not yet grown. Health insurance is not given separately on its own by an insurance institution; it is combined with other insurance branches. Although community-based health insurance was started, it has not yet reached everyone. Beyond filling this gap, private health operators need money to grow themselves and for new investment. Therefore, alongside the insurance, we have begun to organize a microfinance bank that provides financial support only to the health sector."

acts.speaker: Doctors / health professional associations
acts.speech: Announced, through various associations, a one-month deadline for staging a general work stoppage ; said that only one day remains before that deadline expires.

acts.speaker: Kasahun Follo, President of the Confederation of Ethiopian Trade Unions (CETU)
acts.speech: Said that the doctors' demand has not come to them and that it does not concern them.

acts.speaker: Civil Servants Proclamation No. 1064/2017 (law)
acts.speech: Provides in Part Three, Sub-part One, Article Nine for how the salary scale is to be revised, and in Article 17 stipulates that a Merit and Salary Board shall be established for this purpose and shall be chaired by the Prime Minister - indicating that the doctors' salary and benefit demand must pass through long legal and procedural chains.

acts.speaker: Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2011 (law)
acts.speech: Provides in Part Nine, Article 137, sub-article two, a list by name of the sectors in which work must not stop whatever the labour dispute: (a) airline services; (b) electric light and power enterprises; (c) water service and urban sanitation enterprises; (d) urban light rail transport services; (e) hospitals, clinics, pharmaceutical distribution enterprises and pharmacies; (f) fire brigade services; and (g) telecommunication services - stipulating that even if doctors have salary and benefit demands, the sector's service should not be interrupted.

acts.speaker: Yonatan Dagnew, President of the Ethiopian Health Professionals Association
acts.speech: Stated that law is made by people themselves so that people may be governed by it; saying the doctors are presenting a peaceful and civilized demand, he said he believes that even if the law prohibits a work stoppage, before it comes to that the government will look at the matter in good faith and resolve the problems through discussion.

acts.speaker: A doctor, member of the Health Professionals Movement association (anonymous)
acts.speech: Noted that the matter is connected with existence and that people give matters of existence precedence over law, and stated that he expects the government to recognize the urgency of the doctors' peacefully presented demand and move to resolve it.

title: Mozambique: 32,000 families face food insecurity in centre of country

acts.speaker: Helder Alberto, director of the district services for economic activities in the Chibabava district of Sofala
acts.speech: Said: ‘At the moment, we have around 32,000 families in a situation of food insecurity who live on remittances and the sale of small animals. The most affected area is the Goonda administrative post, which is our granary in cereal production’ ; According to Alberto, the local government has assisted around 4,100 families affected by the drought, especially those in the Goonda administrative post in the Chibabava district.

acts.speaker: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
acts.speech: Recently estimated that around 4.8 million people need humanitarian assistance in Mozambique, with $64 million (€60.6 million) needed to meet the needs ; ‘The poly-crisis in Mozambique—conflict, drought and public health emergencies—are stretching humanitarian resources. Approximately 4.8 million people require humanitarian assistance (10 per cent persons with disabilities), including 3.4 million children.’

acts.speaker: United Nations (UN)
acts.speech: In September 2024, said that nearly two million people needed humanitarian assistance in the country ; explained: ‘This year, Mozambique was affected by drought induced by the El Niño phenomenon during the 2023-2024 season. It is estimated that around 1.8 million people could face food insecurity between October and March 2025. Faced with this situation, the need for humanitarian assistance for the affected communities has been increasing, especially in Mozambique’s central and southern regions.’

title: Compte rendu du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 27 novembre 2024

acts.speaker: Council of Ministers of Burkina Faso, chaired by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Faso (official communiqué)
acts.speech: Reported that the Council deliberated on the items on its agenda, heard oral communications, made appointments and authorised missions abroad; that it adopted a report on the 2024 specific projects of the National Bureau of Major Projects of Burkina (BN-GPB) totalling 60,824,529,234 CFA francs financed by the State budget; that it adopted decrees on the collection of revenue for certain services of the General Secretariat of the Government, on declaring SONABEL electricity projects to be of urgent public utility, on approving the statutes of the rail company "FASO RAILS", on mining taxes and royalties, and on the conditions for transferring the State's mining assets; and that it examined and agreed to transmit to the Transitional Legislative Assembly a draft law amending the 1997 law on the coat of arms so as to retain "The Homeland or Death, We Shall Overcome" as the country's motto.

acts.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance, acting Minister of Foreign Affairs, Regional Cooperation and Burkinabè Abroad
acts.speech: Reported to the Council on Burkina Faso's participation in the ministerial conference of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum, held from 09 to 10 November 2024 in Sochi, Russia, which was attended by nearly fifty African countries and was marked by exchanges between the Russian Foreign Minister and the heads of delegation as well as by plenary work.

acts.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
acts.speech: Advocated for a multipolar world order free of neocolonialism, in which Africa must play a leading role commensurate with its potential.

acts.speaker: Participants of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum ministerial conference (joint declaration)
acts.speech: Adopted a joint declaration on strengthening the various areas of cooperation - the economy, humanitarian affairs, investment, security, the fight against terrorism, culture and education - accompanied by a roadmap for the period 2024-2026.

acts.speaker: Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity
acts.speech: Presented to the Council an assessment of the multisectoral needs of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) who have returned to their localities of origin in five regions of Burkina Faso (Boucle du Mouhoun, Cascades, Hauts-Bassins, Nord and Sud-Ouest), aimed at targeting and adapting multisectoral actions on infrastructure rehabilitation, access to basic social services and restoration of livelihoods; a survey was carried out among 469,898 returned IDPs from 59,972 households in these five regions, and the assessment made it possible to identify the actions to be implemented for their sustainable reintegration.

title: Young Zesh, Tru Classic wow Sandton crowd

acts.speaker: Stanley Dlamini, Chief Executive Officer of the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC)
acts.speech: Shared how the event showcased a vibrant array of talent, with Eswatini's Young Zesh and Tru Classic delivering electrifying performances that earned a standing ovation from a discerning audience ; Noted that the stage was alive with energy from a diverse line-up of performers, including Mthokozisi Ndaba, Yamke, Don Dada, Kingsmen, and the closing act, Aubrey Qwabe, adding that each artist contributed to a memorable evening, celebrating the richness of regional artistic talent.

acts.speaker: Stanley Dlamini, Chief Executive Officer of the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC)
acts.speech: Expressed appreciation for the warm reception accorded to the Eswatini artists and delegation in Sandton, specifically acknowledging the presence and instrumental role of Eswatini National Arts and Culture Awards (NACA) Chairperson Sipho Makhabane; he reiterated the need for continued collaboration and extended an invitation to South African media to further promote Eswatini talent, highlighting the interconnectedness of the global village.

acts.speaker: Stanley Khoza, AIRCO Deputy Chairperson
acts.speech: Speaking at the event, extended heartfelt gratitude to the ENCAC CEO for facilitating this pivotal collaboration: "This is just the beginning of many more collaborations between our two nations," emphasising the strategic importance of cross-border artistic exchange.

acts.speaker: Stanley Khoza, AIRCO Deputy Chairperson
acts.speech: Formally introduced Young Zesh and South African artist Yamke, confirming that they had entered the studio on Monday to record a collaborative track with a top-tier technical team; according to Khoza, Show Them Flames will oversee the post-production of the highly-anticipated song, with plans to visit Eswatini for its official launch.

title: Companies Recognized for Excellence in Quality Standards During EAC Regional Quality Awards 2024 - Burundi Times

acts.speaker: Hon. Mwebesa Francis, Uganda's Minister of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives (guest of honour)
acts.speech: emphasized the importance of supporting Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as key drivers of economic growth and job creation, particularly for East Africa's youthful population ; "We should be deliberate as the EAC region on boosting the competitiveness of MSMEs to thrive in the marketplace by supporting them to implement quality practices." ; "This will enable us to tap into the AfCFTA continental market valued at a GDP of US$2.9 trillion, with a consumer base of over 1.4 billion people."

acts.speaker: Annette Mutaawe Ssemuwemba, EAC Deputy Secretary General for Customs, Trade and Monetary Affairs
acts.speech: highlighted the vital role of quality in driving regional competitiveness: "Quality lies at the heart of competitiveness." ; "This ceremony is a testament to the diversity and resilience of our community, and we are grateful to the European Union for their continued support of the MARKUP II program. With a collective commitment to a culture of quality, we can unlock the full potential of our region."

acts.speaker: Eng. James Kasigwa, UNBS (Uganda National Bureau of Standards) Executive Director
acts.speech: noted that Uganda is actively supporting MSMEs to meet international standards as part of the country's transition from National Development Plan III to NDP IV: "Our new value proposition for growing quality MSMEs will help enhance the competitiveness of their products in both local and international markets." ; "By supporting MSMEs, we contribute to economic growth and create more employment opportunities for the region."

acts.speaker: Adrian Njau, Executive Director of the East African Business Council (EABC)
acts.speech: emphasized that the EAC Quality Awards represent a shared vision of fostering a robust quality culture across the region: "Studies by EABC show that adherence to quality standards results in increased intra-EAC trade, reduced border clearance time, and greater global competitiveness." ; "These awards offer MSMEs an invaluable opportunity to showcase their commitment to quality and innovation."

title: City lights up over 3 000 homes

acts.speaker: City of Windhoek council
acts.speech: noted that “If the budget allocation is not utilised due to challenges and difficulties on the ground, it is reduced during the city’s budget review period in September-October; a mismatch between the city and national government’s financial years.”

acts.speaker: Financial model prepared under the collaboration agreement between the municipal council and the USAID Southern Africa Energy Programme (SAEP)
acts.speech: shows the city will require over N$700 million over eight years to complete the electrification of Windhoek’s informal settlement areas.

acts.speaker: City of Windhoek (statement released by the city)
acts.speech: “This means that the City of Windhoek needs N$100 million annually over the next eight years. In light of this, the city’s strategic executives for electricity and finance were granted approval to approach financial institutions on behalf of the City of Windhoek for the financing of the electrification in Windhoek’s informal settlements.”

acts.speaker: National Emergency Care Centre (NECC) application dated 5 July 2021
acts.speech: indicated that the applicant will set up a Section 21 entity, and will be filling the gap between public and private healthcare facilities in the quality and cost of services.

acts.speaker: Council documents (conditions of approval)
acts.speech: “The applicant must implement an appropriate healthcare risk waste management system to ensure that all the waste generated at the facility is properly disposed of. The applicant will be responsible for running expenses, including water, electricity and security services. The applicant will not pay rent, as this will be offset as council’s contribution towards the noble project.”

title: Over 5,000 SMEs already covered by Conecta project

acts.speaker: Joel Sauane, expert of the Conecta Negócios project
acts.speech: Speaking to AIM on Wednesday during a supervision mission in Nampula, said the project has already reached important milestones in its implementation: “The training process is progressing in Nampula, Tete and Cabo Delgado provinces, which are the priorities, with the support of the Northern Integrated Development Agency (ADIN) as the project's co-implementing entity.”

acts.speaker: Joel Sauane, expert of the Conecta Negócios project
acts.speech: Explained that the training is aimed at instructing the SMEs on how to establish connections with the megaproject operators and the customers in general: “In the first phase, SMEs receive training in business management, gender inclusion, green competitiveness, and digital skills. In the second phase, they move on to the ISO 9001 certification process, required to supply goods and services to megaprojects, and can then apply for grants.”

acts.speaker: Joel Sauane, expert of the Conecta Negócios project
acts.speech: Revealed that the overall goal is to train 9,000 SMEs, of which 6,000 have already been trained, that the project intends to cover 3,000 SMEs in Nampula and so far 2,900 have been covered, and added: “In order to support these companies financally, 15 million dollars in grants are available, divided equally into 7.5 million for microenterprises and 7.5 million for SMEs.”

acts.speaker: Hegínio Mussequece, business owner in the construction sector, Nampula
acts.speech: “We learned tools focused on results. Our hope is to obtain certification that will allow us to participate in major projects underway in Nampula province and beyond. We intend to apply for the grant to leverage our business with the acquisition of equipment.”

acts.speaker: Linda Nhalate, business owner in the seafood industry
acts.speech: Praised the management skills learned in the training, claiming that they “will help us implement more professional administrative procedures” ; “This will help the company grow. We hope to continue expanding and recruiting more young people as now we are hiring 12 permanent employees and 40 seasonal employees.”

title: Guinée : lancement du 2ème forum PROTECT

acts.speaker: Project head, PROTECT project (OCPH/Caritas Guinea)
acts.speech: "the PROTECT project, launched in May 2023, aims to strengthen prevention, awareness-raising and victim protection actions against trafficking. The project covers the regions of Boké, N'Zérékoré and Kankan, encompassing 7 prefectures and 21 communes, with the ambition of raising awareness and promoting behaviour change within communities. To date, the project has raised awareness among more than 527,000 people, trained community relays and religious leaders, and supported the return to school of 52 at-risk children. These results demonstrate tangible progress, but challenges persist."

acts.speaker: Jean-Louis Maomy, project head and representative of the interim secretary general (OCPH/Caritas Guinea)
acts.speech: Stressed that "the PROTECT project has made it possible to reach a wide audience," while noting that challenges remain, particularly regarding psychological and social support for victims, data collection and expanding awareness-raising nationwide. He therefore insisted on the need for integrated solutions linking the fight against trafficking to key areas such as health, education and social cohesion. He also expressed his gratitude to the partners and urged all actors to continue their efforts to eradicate human trafficking in Guinea.

acts.speaker: Alexious Butler, USAID Country Director
acts.speech: In her speech, welcomed the progress achieved through the PROTECT project and reaffirmed USAID's commitment to supporting Guinea in this fight. She stressed the importance of close collaboration with local partners, including NGOs, religious leaders, civil society and the media, to strengthen prevention, protection and prosecution of traffickers.

acts.speaker: Father Francis Oularé, representative of the Archbishop
acts.speech: Insisted on the importance of the commitment of every individual and every organisation in this fight, calling for new financial and technical support to help Guinea in this effort.

acts.speaker: Sekou Fofana, senior adviser and representative of the Minister for the Promotion of Women, Children and Vulnerable Persons
acts.speech: Highlighted the reforms undertaken by the Guinean government to strengthen the fight against human trafficking, including the creation of an Office for the Protection of Gender, Children and Morals and the establishment of a central service for the protection of vulnerable persons. He stressed the need for a comprehensive action plan to coordinate the efforts of all actors involved, with the support of technical and financial partners.
